## 276. Outside Line — check the selected browser path without turning reachability into delivery

Date: 2026-10-18 (America/New_York). Received archive: `Vibechat-rev0093-2026.10.18-porchlight-builder-handoff.zip`. Received product SHA-256: `19dd065c8a854edcd1d3d282b695ef6c5cb79da4bc8b19d77a2c315381714a65`.

### The ordinary road

**Connection settings → Check this browser’s path → Check meeting service or Check TURN relay → optionally Save redacted result.**

Porchlight completed bounded reader ownership for both first-meeting Beacon and established-friend Homecoming routes, but its next deployment gate could not be answered honestly by another loopback-only automatic test. Outside Line therefore adds an explicit field check to the delivered product. It lets the person or operator exercise the exact service selected in the browser, at the place and time where the result matters, without asking Vibechat to infer delivery, durability, peer presence, or future availability from a reachable endpoint.

Nothing runs merely because Vibechat opens, Connection settings opens, a meeting-service address is selected, or ICE configuration is entered. Each check begins only from its named button. It uses no chat, identity, password, friend key, invitation, accepted room, message, file, saved profile, unfinished writing, or current peer connection. It creates no trust decision, conversation, signaling packet, invitation, room, message, receipt claim from another person, persistent outbox, background worker, or automatic resend.

### Meeting-service check

**Check meeting service** reads the exact normalized service currently selected under **People → Other ways → Meeting & return service**. It creates one fresh synthetic topic of the form `vc_` plus 48 lowercase hexadecimal characters and one fresh synthetic text record beginning `vibechat-field-probe-v1:` followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Those values are unrelated to any invitation, return route, identity, room, or content event.

The browser performs exactly one text `POST` and then one `GET` at the corresponding topic JSON route with `poll=1&since=all`. Every request omits credentials and referrers, disables cache reuse, and refuses redirects. Each complete headers-and-body request is bounded to 15,000 ms; the pair shares one 30,000 ms total budget. A response body is limited to 65,536 bytes and must complete as valid UTF-8. The retrieved service record must match the exact random topic and exact random text. A successful HTTP status without that record is not a pass.

Stopping or replacing an attempt aborts the owned request and cancels an incomplete body. Late success cannot overwrite a newer attempt or a completed earlier result. The check does not leave its random probe capability in the saved field receipt. Service-side retention of the synthetic probe remains governed by that selected service; Outside Line does not claim deletion, restart survival, or retention policy from the round trip.

### TURN relay check

**Check TURN relay** requires at least one current `turn:` or `turns:` ICE entry. It creates two temporary `RTCPeerConnection` objects in the same browser with `iceTransportPolicy: "relay"`, negotiates one ordered data channel, and exchanges a fresh random challenge and response. The whole attempt is bounded to 30,000 ms. A channel opening is insufficient: both selected nominated candidate pairs must report local candidate type `relay`, and the random challenge must return exactly.

The two temporary peers are a local diagnostic pair, not the user’s active chat peers. Completing the check shows only that this browser could allocate and use the supplied relay path at that moment. It does not establish that a second device, another browser, another network, a particular NAT, a captive portal, a proxy, a radio transition, or a future session can use it. The check does not publish signaling, inspect chat data, change the configured policy, or retain TURN secrets after the existing page-memory custody ends.

### One owner, explicit stop, and redacted local evidence

Only one Outside Line job may own the field-check surface. **Stop check**, closing Connection settings, changing the selected meeting service, changing ICE configuration or preset, Lock, and `pagehide` invalidate that owner, abort its requests, close its temporary peer connections and data channels, and fence delayed callbacks. A stopped check does not erase a previously completed result. It also does not silently retry, switch services, weaken relay-only policy, or convert failure into an availability claim.

**Save redacted result** offers a local canonical JSON file only after at least one check has completed. Its format is `vibechat-field-qualification-v1`. It records the Vibechat revision, the browser’s unauthenticated wall-clock timestamp, the normalized meeting-service base where applicable, coarse relay protocol classes, elapsed milliseconds, pass/fail state, bounded failure reason, and the narrow meaning of each result.

The receipt is unsigned. It deliberately omits the random topic, random payload, service cursor, candidate addresses, TURN URLs, TURN usernames, credentials, identity material, keys, invitations, rooms, messages, files, and drafts. Its clock is not a trusted timestamp. It is local operator evidence, not a statement by a friend, service operator, independent monitor, or auditor.

A pass means only that this browser completed that exact narrow round trip at that moment. A failure means only that this attempt did not establish that path. ## 274. Porchlight — retire a silent established-friend reader without inventing presence

Date: 2026-10-18 (America/New_York). Received archive: `Vibechat-rev0092-2026.10.18-watchful-line-builder-handoff.zip`. Received product SHA-256: `0adb86b29fc467e0381c1e56ab3de3f9d2b2e83dd3728bf45dc48889908ee0e7`.

### The ordinary road

**Open an established chat → the retained Homecoming socket silently stops delivering → Porchlight retires that reader → one bounded HTTP reader continues from the exact committed cursor → the same conversation reconnects without another handoff.**

Watchful Line gave the first-meeting Beacon listener explicit liveness, ordered retirement, and cursor-safe HTTP fallback. Homecoming is a separate established-friend state machine: it carries the already-saved encrypted Waystation route and can receive held messages, signed reconnect offers and repair traffic without asking the people to exchange another link. Before Porchlight, that reader could still wait forever when a genuinely upgraded WebSocket remained nominally `OPEN` but no longer delivered frames. It could also reach HTTP fallback through paths that did not share one explicit reader owner.

Porchlight gives each exact Homecoming route one listener owner and one monotonic listener serial. The WebSocket must open within 15,000 ms. Once open, while the document is visible and the browser reports online, each 75,000 ms quiet interval must contain at least one string frame. Any string frame refreshes transport liveness only. It does **not** prove peer presence, identity, message delivery, human reading, remote processing, or durable remote storage.

When the open or quiet bound expires, or the browser reports socket `error` or `close`, Vibechat first retires socket admission. The owned socket is detached and closed, its timer is cleared, and new frames from that socket are fenced. Frames already admitted to the exact listener's ordered processing chain are allowed to settle. Only after that chain drains does the same route start exactly one bounded HTTP polling reader at the last committed service cursor.

HTTP mode is sticky for the remaining life of that listener. It polls on the existing 8,000 ms cadence, with one read at a time and the inherited bounded response handling. A delayed socket callback cannot reopen WebSocket mode, start a second reader, move the committed cursor backward, or take ownership from a newer listener. Retirement itself never publishes signaling and never invents a cursor; only the existing authenticated ordered frame path commits progress.

Hidden or offline time does not by itself condemn the socket. Visibility or online return rechecks the original elapsed liveness clock under the same route and listener ownership. Browser timer suspension is therefore not treated as evidence that a peer disappeared. A wake check can retire an already-overdue reader, but it does not turn elapsed silence into presence, delivery, rejection, or failure of the other person.

### Established-friend ownership and deliberate controls

There is at most one Homecoming reader for an exact active route. Starting a newer listener, replacing the route, clearing the friend flow, deliberate Disconnect, repair pause, expiry where applicable, or Lock invalidates the previous serial, closes its socket, aborts its owned HTTP read, clears timers, and fences delayed callbacks. A late admitted frame may finish only while its original listener still owns the route; post-retirement frames are inert.

An exact already-live RTC peer remains stronger than transport silence. Porchlight does not tear down that healthy connection merely because the rendezvous reader retires or a service response is missing. This safeguard does not override deliberate Disconnect, Lock, or an explicitly paused repair. Existing identity pins, safety words, signed signaling, exact room membership, message signatures, WebRTC validation, encrypted holding, and manual recovery remain authoritative.

No signaling packet is republished by Porchlight. No invitation, compact code, topic, key, connection offer, peer connection, room, conversation, message, trust decision, storage permission, persistent outbox, background worker, or automatic resend is created. The first-meeting Beacon listener and the established-friend Homecoming listener remain separate state machines with separate ownership; their state is not shared by convenience.

### Deliberately narrow scope

Porchlight changes the active established-friend listener in the current unlocked tab. ## 272. Watchful Line — retire a silent first-meeting reader without losing its cursor

Date: 2026-10-18 (America/New_York). Received archive: `Vibechat-rev0091-2026.10.18-same-invitation-builder-handoff.zip`. Received product SHA-256: `9599cb419e0103e194b93f241cf700b94135db00cd07b232e6a0a795746c495b`.

### The ordinary road

**Share one link, QR, or code → the first-meeting socket goes silent without closing → Vibechat retires that reader → bounded HTTP listening continues from the exact committed cursor.**

Same Invitation bounded first-meeting publication and HTTP reply reads, retained exact encrypted setup frames for explicit retry, and preserved a verified live peer when a service acknowledgement went missing. Its WebSocket fallback still depended on the browser reporting `error` or `close`. A TCP path, proxy, radio, or suspended intermediary can leave a WebSocket nominally `OPEN` after frames have stopped arriving. In that state, the first meeting could wait forever even though bounded HTTP retrieval remained available.

Watchful Line gives the **first-meeting reply listener** one owner and an explicit liveness state machine. The socket must open within 15,000 ms. Once open, while the document is visible and the browser reports online, each 75,000 ms quiet interval must contain at least one text frame. Any text frame refreshes transport liveness; it does **not** prove that the peer is present, that a signed setup stage exists, that any chat message was delivered, or that a person read anything.

When the quiet bound expires, Vibechat first retires socket admission. Frames that were already admitted to the listener's ordered decode chain are allowed to finish. New frames from the retired socket are fenced. Only after the admitted chain drains does the same invitation session hand off exactly once to a new bounded HTTP reader, starting at the last committed service cursor. That HTTP mode is sticky for the remaining life of the invitation session: a delayed socket event cannot reopen a second reader, rewind the cursor, or take over a newer attempt.

The liveness deadline is an observation aid, not a peer-status claim. Hidden or offline time does not itself retire the reader. Returning visible or online rechecks the elapsed transport quiet time under the same ownership token. A normal socket `error` or `close` uses the same retirement and drain path. Opening, quiet, polling, replacement, expiry, cancellation, Lock, and friend-flow reset all share the existing invitation generation and admission fences.

No setup frame is republished by this feature. No invitation, code, topic, key, signed offer/reply/ready packet, room, conversation, message, trust decision, storage permission, background worker, persistent outbox, or automatic resend is introduced. Same Invitation's explicit **Try sending setup again** remains the only publication retry. Manual Other ways recovery and the no-service file route remain available.

### Cursor and ownership invariants

There is at most one active first-meeting reply reader. Socket creation receives a listener serial bound to the exact live Beacon session. Its opening timer, quiet timer, message admission, close/error path, and HTTP handoff all recheck that serial and session ownership. Replacing or stopping the session closes the owned socket, clears its timer, aborts an owned HTTP read, and invalidates delayed callbacks.

The service cursor advances only through the existing ordered, authenticated reply-processing chain. Retirement never invents a cursor and never adopts the cursor attached to a late retired frame. The handoff begins from the cursor committed after all already-admitted frames have settled. Bounded HTTP polling retains Same Invitation's 15,000 ms complete-response deadline, 4 MiB response ceiling, redirect refusal, body cancellation, credential/referrer omission, and one-read-at-a-time rule.

A verified signed next stage and the exact expected live peer remain stronger evidence than a missing service acknowledgement, exactly as in Same Invitation. Mere socket activity is not that evidence. The original independent identity comparison, exact pins, safety words, signed setup stages, room membership, and WebRTC validation remain authoritative.

### Deliberately narrow scope

Watchful Line changes only the first-meeting Beacon listener. Homecoming's established-friend listener is a separate state machine and still has its prior `error`/`close` behavior. This release does not claim dead-open recovery for Homecoming, public ntfy or custom-Waystation availability, public TURN/NAT traversal, durable execution while a page is closed, mobile timer precision, or background delivery.

A 75-second application timer is rechecked after awaited work and after visibility/online return. It is not a promise that a suspended browser executes JavaScript on schedule. Silence can result from a healthy but quiet service, a broken path, browser suspension, or absence of traffic; therefore the UI and protocol do not translate it into presence, delivery, rejection, or remote failure.

## 270. Same Invitation — retry the encrypted setup, not the human handoff

Date: 2026-10-18 (America/New_York). Received archive: `Vibechat-rev0090-2026.10.17-invitation-kept-builder-handoff(1).zip`. Received product SHA-256: `a80aa4f7df21d7ca59d23e70b183f9332b41ae16cb0dd35258635e6d195cc6e1`.

### The ordinary road

**Share one link, QR, or code → an interrupted setup send stops → Try sending setup again → continue the same meeting.**

Invitation Kept repaired the receiving side of a first meeting: a stalled lookup can retain the exact invitation in the current tab. Same Invitation repairs the corresponding sending side. The host or guest no longer needs to mint another code, repeat the human handoff, rebuild the signed offer/reply/ready packet, or abandon an already-open exact peer connection merely because the Waystation did not return a publication confirmation.

For each signed first-meeting stage, Vibechat prepares the encrypted chunk frames once and retains them with a confirmed-prefix cursor in the live invitation session. **Try sending setup again** appears directly below setup progress and above the QR/card. Retry skips confirmed frames and repeats the first uncertain encrypted frame byte-for-byte. It then continues the remaining original frames in order. It does not derive another seed, topic, key, invitation, setup ID, connection offer, room, conversation, or message; unfinished writing never enters this path.

The sender-facing recovery is explicit. There is no background publication loop after a failed send. A successful retry resumes the ordinary listener and progress flow. The manual Other ways route remains available with the same original signed setup. A failed service confirmation is described as uncertain because the service may already hold the encrypted part.

This is **same-tab, same-invitation recovery**. Cancel, replacement by a newer setup stage, expiry, Lock, friend-flow reset, or closing the page fences late work and releases the retained publication capability. It is not closed-tab reception, persistent setup recovery, an offline outbox, multi-device signaling, or permission to resend a current draft.

### Bounded first-meeting publication and reply polling

Every first-meeting publication request owns a 15,000 ms allowance. The complete multipart publication shares one 45,000 ms budget. The request uses an AbortController plus an independently settled stop promise, so cancellation and deadline handling do not rely on a Fetch collaborator honoring AbortSignal. The controller immediately observes its own stop promise, including an invitation that is already expired before its first request, so no rejected internal stop can escape as an unhandled rejection.

Publication omits credentials and referrers, disables cache use, refuses redirects, and cancels unused response bodies. HTTP refusal, cancellation, replacement, expiry, Lock, and deadline settlement cannot advance the confirmed cursor. A late confirmation cannot take over a newer attempt. Confirmed progress is retained only inside the current invitation session.

HTTP reply polling now owns the full response, not just response headers. One read has a 15,000 ms deadline covering headers and body, refuses redirects, omits credentials/cache/referrer state, and accepts at most 4 MiB before parsing. Streamed bodies are counted incrementally and cancelled on timeout, oversize, refusal, cancellation, or stale ownership. Text-only adapters are bounded by UTF-8 bytes. One automatic poll/read can exist at a time; stopping the meeting removes its timer, active body read, and listener.

The WebSocket listener is single-instance and falls back to the bounded HTTP path on a reported error or close. **Silent half-open WebSocket detection is not added or claimed here.** A connection that remains open but stops delivering without error/close still needs its own liveness and cursor-continuity design.

### Exact peer proof outranks a missing service acknowledgement

A Waystation acknowledgement is transport evidence, not identity authority. When the next signed first-meeting stage is verified, the prior publication necessarily reached the exact peer that could produce that stage. Likewise, when the exact expected peer, room, and invitation session have already produced a live verified RTC channel, that peer connection is stronger evidence than a missing service confirmation for the final setup frame.

Same Invitation marks the retained publication complete on either proof, aborts the still-waiting service request, and preserves the healthy connection. It does not accept an unsigned outer wrapper, a different identity, a different room, a different invitation, or mere topic possession. Existing source confirmation, safety words, exact pins, signed invite/reply/ready packets, room membership, and WebRTC checks remain authoritative. A late service reply after peer proof is inert.

This does not turn service acceptance or peer proof into human reading, durable remote storage, delivery of later chat messages, or independent evidence that another device saved anything.

### Focused and real-connection regression

`beacon_checks.py --focused-only` runs **92 assertions** on the exact final carrier: the 41 Invitation Kept lookup/controller cases plus 51 publication, retry, polling, listener, expiry, and peer-proof cases. These include real Fetch/Response/ReadableStream and loopback HTTP collaborators where declared, exact-frame identity across retry, shared multipart budgets, body stalls, cancellation despite ignored AbortSignal, duplicate-listener suppression, and the expired-before-first-request rejection edge.

The full Beacon journey runs **150 checks** in Chromium against the exact carrier. Its deterministic Waystation adapter stores the last encrypted ready chunk but withholds that POST confirmation. The recipient reconstructs and verifies the signed stage, both real RTCDataChannels open through the owned loopback TURN relay, the sender uses exact peer proof to stop the pending request, and releasing the late confirmation does not disturb the connection. Encrypted text then travels both ways and a multipart file is recovered byte-for-byte.

The browser journey uses the existing native cryptographic-provider fixture, an explicit cryptography adapter where this host's opaque document lacks SubtleCrypto, controlled camera/BarcodeDetector collaborators, an in-memory adapter for the documented HTTP/WebSocket surface, and an owned loopback relay. It is not public ntfy/custom-Waystation availability, public TURN/NAT traversal, physical camera/clipboard/share behavior, normal browser persistence, mobile suspension, or an independent security audit.

Qualify real navigation, two tabs, restart, eviction/persistence decisions, mobile foreground/background transitions, timer suspension, screen sleep, low-memory termination, and re-unlock. Keep exit 77 or another unavailable result explicit rather than substituting a fixture.

4. **Physical interaction and accessibility.** Test phone camera scanning, native share/clipboard, soft keyboards and IME/composition, focus order, screen readers, reduced motion, zoom, narrow landscape, and interrupted permissions. Existing DOM/layout checks do not establish these behaviors.

5. **Persistent unsent intent only by deliberate protocol design.** Same Invitation deliberately keeps setup recovery in the current tab. Do not quietly serialize signed setup capabilities or restored writing into an automatic outbox. A future persistent intent feature would need encrypted ownership, exact destination and policy binding, expiry/revocation, conflict handling, explicit resume, no automatic resend after uncertain completion, backup/transfer semantics, and multi-tab/device rules.

Do not let first-meeting retry imply those properties.

### Recommended order

The next revision should address **WebSocket liveness and cursor-safe fallback first**, because it completes the bounded first-meeting network state machine without expanding persistence or trust. After that, qualify one real deployment and ordinary browser/mobile lifecycle. Only then decide whether persistent unsent intent is desirable; it should not be smuggled in as a convenience patch.

## 268. Invitation Kept — retry the invitation, not the human handoff

Date: 2026-10-17 (America/New_York; execution receipts cross midnight UTC). Received archive: `Vibechat-rev0089-2026.10.17-clear-wait-builder-handoff.zip`. Received product SHA-256: `16a655b3456cb830bfcf6a3820df508d97a76b4812caf75e7230e37162c72c37`.

### The ordinary road

**Scan or paste once → a stalled check stops → Try this invitation again → review the person → connect.**

Incoming first-meeting retrieval used to wait without a request deadline. Its opening-screen Cancel could discard the result without stopping the underlying HTTP request. This revision adds a bounded lookup and keeps the exact canonical invitation code in the current tab when retrieval is interrupted. The person does not need to fetch the code again, reopen a messenger, or repeat the QR scan simply because the service stalled.

Both the locked opening screen and the unlocked friend guide show **Invitation kept**, with **Try this invitation again** as the primary action. The panel precedes scan/paste controls, so recovery is visible on a narrow screen. The original entry details and any usable staged preview are not discarded by a failed candidate. The retry uses the retained canonical `vibe1:`/`vibe2:` value and selected Waystation, not whatever the person subsequently types into another field.

**Cancel invitation check** aborts the active request while retaining the code. **Forget this code** removes this tab's retained code and cancels its active attempt. Neither action removes saved chats, trusts a person, or destroys an already-established connection. Closing the friend dialog cancels its lookup; reopening can still offer the kept code. Closing/navigating away from the page, Lock, successful adoption, or expiry clears that recovery state. The retention window is at most ten minutes from its first retention; retrying the same code does not extend it. Existing encrypted invitation expiry is still checked independently.

This is explicitly **same-tab recovery**, not saved invitation storage, a permanent invitation, closed-tab reception, or an offline outbox. The host's original live invitation still needs to be open and valid. A retained code cannot revive a closed or expired meeting. The original file, full-text, reusable public-card, and portable-HTML routes remain available under Other ways.

### Bounded incoming I/O

The carried client owns each incoming lookup and each HTTP request. Each request has a 15,000 ms allowance covering headers and the entire response body. The lookup shares one 30,000 ms budget across at most three reads. Only a completed empty mailbox can lead to the next bounded read; a timeout or refusal returns control to the person instead of starting a retry loop. There is deliberately no new online/visibility auto-retry for first invitations.

For a real ReadableStream, the reader counts received bytes and refuses a response above 4 MiB before parsing. The text-only adapter path also checks UTF-8 bytes and remains time-bounded. HTTP refusal does not wait for an arbitrary error body. Unused or oversized bodies are cancelled. Fetch retains credential omission, no cache, and no referrer, and refuses redirects instead of following the private topic request to a substituted destination. The code still selects exactly its original normalized service; there is no automatic service switch.

An AbortController plus an independent stop promise makes cancellation/deadline settlement work even with a collaborator that ignores AbortSignal. A response arriving after timeout is cancelled rather than parsed. Code retention has wall-time and monotonic expiry checks. These are software bounds rechecked after awaited work, not a promise that suspended browsers continue to run their timers.

The scope is **incoming invitation lookup only**. `beaconPublish`, live Beacon polling/WebSocket liveness, and the first signed offer/answer/ready publication path were not redesigned in this cut. They still need their own bounded publication and already-live-channel recovery work. Clear Wait's separate returning-friend request/publication deadlines remain unchanged.

### Own the attempt, not identity authority

Every attempt belongs to the exact retained record, generation, entry operation or friend-dialog selection, and AbortController. Cancelled, forgotten, replaced, expired, closed-dialog, or locked attempts cannot adopt a later response into a newer session. Delayed clipboard success/failure cannot reopen a cancelled intake or replace a more recent code. Invalid replacement input is validated before it can displace the earlier valid kept code.

Cancellation is checked after material derivation, HTTP reading, outer decryption/parser work, and invitation validation. The ordinary `friendRead` receives an optional admission guard and checks it after its asynchronous decode and hash, before changing the friend flow. Its original callers remain compatible. The entry route still returns an unverified preview through the transactional doorway; the unlocked route still opens the exact existing person-review flow. Neither lookup success nor retry bypasses independent source confirmation, safety words, signed signaling, exact recipient/room policy, or WebRTC validation.

The retained recovery record contains only the incoming capability and local lifecycle state. It is not put in profile storage, IndexedDB, localStorage, backup files, Carryover snapshots, browser URLs, or new network payloads. No new protocol format, trust decision, storage permission, key derivation, provider, or service is introduced. Starting an explicit request still exposes the existing service's normal network/traffic metadata; encryption is not traffic invisibility.

### Focused regression and real conversation journey

`beacon_checks.py --lookup-only` runs 41 focused assertions using the exact carried function bodies. Declared DOM, clock, invitation-parser, and selected controller collaborators cover refusal, expiry, replacement, cancellation, body cleanup, and same-code retention. Actual Node Fetch/Response/ReadableStream plus an owned loopback HTTP server separately cover a successful request, redirect refusal without visiting its destination, stalled headers, stalled bodies, and cancellation. Those checks are not browser-native storage or public-service qualification.

The functional `--lookup-regression` fails on the received rev0089 because its stalled lookup never settles, not because it lacks a new label or named helper. It passes on this revision. The receipt records wrong/oversized replies, a total budget not reset by another poll, cancellation during derivation/validation, late response disposal, retained expiry not renewed, invalid paste preservation, and delayed clipboard/closed-dialog fences.

The expanded browser journey contains 52 checks, in addition to those 41 focused checks, for a **93-check Beacon lane**. A locked recipient pastes once, retains entered login details through a real 15-second header stall, retries without another clipboard read, then cancels an outstanding attempt and ignores its late result. An independently unlocked recipient scans a QR once, receives a deliberately stalled body, uses the same-code retry, and opens the exact original unverified friend without a second scan. Late old data cannot replace that review.

The journey then completes original independent identity acceptance, all three encrypted/signed setup stages, actual RTCDataChannels through the owned loopback TURN fixture, encrypted text both ways, and byte-exact multipart-file recovery. The holding-service and camera/detector are controlled collaborators. The actual sealed client, CSP/standards parsing, native cryptographic provider, QR encoding/independent decoding, and owned RTC are exercised within that declared scope. ## 266. Clear Wait — do not leave a conversation waiting on a request forever

Date: 2026-10-17 (America/New_York; execution receipts cross midnight UTC). Received archive: `Vibechat-rev0088-2026.10.17-keep-these-words-builder-handoff.zip`. Received product SHA-256: `14b39eeaff938e3679a19c5d9f7577806d99eb9f40af8f4e07110b0bf2e1fbc1`.

### The ordinary human road

Keep using the existing conversation. If the holding service stalls while accepting a message, the tab now stops saying **Leaving an encrypted copy…** indefinitely. It offers **Holding unconfirmed · retry**. Open that message's status and choose **Try sharing again**. This uses the original encrypted event and the original conversation, not the current composer text. Newer writing is neither sent nor erased. A service may have accepted some or all of a publication before its reply was lost; the interface therefore does not assert that nothing arrived.

There is no new settings page, invitation code, recovery password, contact or message transport. A first meeting still uses one existing link/QR/code. An established eligible friend still uses **Open chat → Connect**. Direct RTC remains preferred, the established held-message path remains secondary, and ordinary exact-event deduplication handles overlapping arrivals. An unconfirmed hold is not a new event, a read receipt, or a promise about the other person's storage.

### Bound the request and the publication

`homecomingRequest` is inside the carried, CSP-bound client. Its 15,000 ms request budget covers response headers and the entire retrieval body. For real streamed Responses it counts actual received bytes, stops above the existing 4 MiB response limit before parsing, and cancels an unused or refused response body. The text-only compatibility path still bounds the UTF-8 byte size and its waiting time. HTTP refusal does not wait for an arbitrary error body. Successful POST status is sufficient for the existing service-acceptance observation; its unused body is cancelled, not read without a bound.

Each multi-part publication also has one 45,000 ms budget shared across its requests. A fresh request cannot reset that whole-publication allowance. These are software deadlines checked again after awaited work, not a promise that a suspended browser executes timers. No request timeout proves non-delivery. An uncertain part can already exist at the service. An explicit retry retains the original inner encrypted event; the existing outer wrapping can be fresh. It does not mint another chat message or bypass current conversation/recipient/policy checks.

Holding fetches continue to omit credentials and referrer information and to avoid response caching. They now refuse redirects rather than forwarding a topic request to a substituted destination. The selected pair's existing Waystation address and the ntfy-only publish query rules are unchanged. No alternate public service is selected automatically.

### Own cancellation and recovery

A lost service confirmation can arrive after the signed exchange already opened an exact peer channel. Both offer and answer controllers now check that observed outcome before dismantling a failed publication. Only the exact currently live, identity-bound link can complete this recovery; a different/replaced link, non-ready channel, cancelled attempt, stopped route or Lock cannot. A healthy peer channel is not torn down merely because its signaling mailbox did not confirm acceptance. A naturally completed attempt also does not turn a late publication callback into a false cancellation warning. This is observed local channel readiness, not proof of human presence or durable remote storage.

Each live return route owns an AbortController. Stopping/replacing the route or locking aborts its outstanding HTTP work. Each pending Homecoming connection owns a separate controller, so cancelling that connection interrupts its signal publication without disabling ordinary held delivery for the friend. Existing key cleanup, signed signaling, exact identity and room policy remain in place.

The timeout/cancel promise settles even when a test adapter ignores AbortSignal. A late response cannot start the next publication part, confirm a stopped event, feed a timed-out body to the parser, advance the resumed retrieval cursor, or repaint a stopped route. Message admission checks the route after asynchronous validation and again inside the existing admission queue, so Lock during either wait does not admit the old result into a later session.

Startup and polling share one in-flight read per route. Repeated socket-fallback notifications cannot spawn extra polling loops while a poll is active. After a failed poll the existing loop schedules another attempt. Coming back online or making the page visible checks an already-active retained route, coalesced with any current read and rate-limited to one wake per two seconds. The hint does not assert service availability or human presence, restore a removed route, start a new friendship, or turn deliberate Disconnect/Lock into automatic reconnect consent. The existing negotiated repair controller still decides whether a fresh signed connection attempt is permitted.

There is deliberately **no new automatic message resend loop or persistent outbox**. Exact-record manual retry remains the ordinary answer to an unconfirmed hold. This feature adds neither durable delivery reports nor closed-tab execution. Existing encrypted saving, file backup, Carryover/Carry Link, signed Arrival, resumable transfers, local draft recovery, conflict review, unreadable-copy consent and whole-envelope draft CAS remain unchanged.

### Exact tests, not caption substitutes

The carried `reunion_checks.py` adds 45 selected-source transport checks and a separately scoped answer-controller regression. They execute the exact client function bodies with declared synthetic route, clock, parser/frame and admission collaborators. Actual Node Fetch, ReadableStream and a separately owned real loopback HTTP server cover successful reading, redirect refusal, oversize streaming, stalled headers and stalled bodies. These are not browser-native persistence or public deployment tests.

The functional stalled-publication regression runs against the received rev0088 too. It fails because the original publication does not settle when its request stalls, not because a new function name or UI label is absent. It passes on this revision. The tests additionally cover cancellation after delayed response headers, release of pending I/O, a late body after a successful new cursor, polling recovery, request coalescing, whole-publication budget, cancelled signal publication with holding still available, and Lock during verification/queued admission.

The full returning-friend journey uses the original native-cryptography/declared browser adapter and real RTCDataChannels through the owned TURN fixture. Its new lost-reply case lets the holding adapter retain **all** first-publication chunks, then deliberately withholds the final HTTP reply. The real client returns to an actionable message status, retries its existing record, keeps newer writing untouched, ignores the late reply, and the independently unlocked friend admits one message rather than two. A second fault retains the complete signed answer while withholding its final service reply. The original two RTC peers stay open after that request deadline and its late reply; subsequent encrypted messages still flow both ways. A 390-pixel status review keeps the existing retry reachable. This is a Chromium geometry/interaction check, not a physical phone or assistive-technology qualification.

### Failed attempts and unavailable lanes are retained separately

A final review found that the earlier deadline candidate could tear down an answerer's already-open RTC channel when the signaling publication lost its confirmation. The exact selected answer-controller regression fails on both the received rev0088 and candidate v2 before the fix, and is carried as a separate one-check lane. Its RTC/provider outcomes are explicitly synthetic; the full RTC lost-answer-reply journey tests the behavior independently. This was fixed before publication by checking only the exact still-live connection, with cancellation, Lock and replacement remaining authoritative.

The v2 Beacon lane also stopped at a static function-signature assertion expecting the old two-parameter `homecomingPublish`; its predicate now requires the new explicit optional pending-connection parameter while retaining the direct-send and bounded-route checks. That fixture failure was not a network or invitation-protocol failure. In-progress v2 broad qualification was stopped when the live-channel race was found; completed v2 receipts remain scoped to v2, and incomplete runs are not passing evidence.

The received strict real-storage lane was attempted before building. Ordinary navigation returned `ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ADMINISTRATOR`; the lane exited 77/unavailable with zero real-storage assertions and no substituted pass. No host policy was changed. This remains a separate browser-device gate from the passing fixture-based writing checks.

The inherited Plainview projection lane stops at `ReferenceError: homecomingCancelHold is not defined` because its selected-function fixture omits a collaborator that the real client has. The same unchanged helper failure was reproduced on the received product. It is not counted as a passing lane. The new full returning-friend journey separately exercises the real status/retry UI, not that incomplete projection fixture.

An early new Node test had a missing closing brace in its fabricated event; that syntax failure was corrected before the meaningful received-versus-final regression. An early UI test incorrectly waited for the retry button to become enabled after successful holding; successful holding correctly disables redundant retry. It now waits for the real successful status, retaining the original retry/delivery assertions. The earlier failed run is not passing evidence.

The first sealed candidate stopped the carrier lane at the combined Arrival metadata check: its compressed status prose no longer began with the prescribed compatibility phrase or contained the prescribed Connect wording. These two metadata phrases were corrected without changing runtime behavior; all 42 individual Arrival predicates were preflighted before final resealing. That failed candidate is not the released carrier. A same-runtime earlier backup run timed out after 120 completed assertions while awaiting an unlock. A v2 run stopped at the combined hosted-link/QR assertion after 71 checks; it did not capture which term differed, so no decoder, timing or product cause is asserted. An unchanged v2 retry completed all 140 checks. Those results remain separate from final-carrier backup qualification. A foreground reproduction tool call also timed out between completed cycles; only subsequently completed, compared cycles count below. No test timeout or unavailable run is relabeled as a pass.

Keep the core goal central: one initial string/QR, no repeated handoff for established friends, one ordinary conversation, and failure states that preserve usable work. Next, address bounded first-meeting Beacon lookup/publication and preserved-code recovery with the entry/Lock/identity barriers intact. Qualify deployed Waystations, silent WebSocket loss and mobile foreground/background transitions, service acceptance followed by browser termination, and persistent unsent-intent semantics before promising a durable outbox. Do not auto-resend restored history. Keep manual signed connection recovery and no-service backup files available.

Actual same-origin browser storage, separate real tabs, process-kill send windows, native phone input/camera/share behavior and accessibility remain distinct qualification work. Fix the omitted Plainview projection collaborator explicitly before calling that old lane green. Advance the supported comparison edition and impact-receipt section with the next revision; preflight status and all brief/Arrival predicates before long journeys.

Implementation references, consulted 2026-10-17: [WHATWG Fetch Standard](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/) for abortable request/body handling and redirect modes, and [HTML Living Standard system state](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/system-state.html#navigator.online) for online/offline hints. These contracts inform implementation; they are not execution receipts, presence proof or public-service qualification.

### The ordinary human road

Default encrypted browser saving still needs no new setup. Write normally. A sound saved draft still returns after unlocking the same identity here. If saved writing has changed, the existing **Saved writing needs review → Review saved writing** route remains.

Previously, an unreadable saved ciphertext could make that review fail every time. The tab retained readable writing, but there was no explicit way to save it past the damaged checkpoint. The new review says **Keep these words**, shows only this tab’s readable text, and explains that the unavailable saved copy might contain different words. It does not display, adopt, compare, or treat unauthenticated contents as a saved draft.

**Leave both unchanged** receives initial focus. Escape, Close, and that action retain the readable text and stored bytes. Replacing an unreadable checkpoint requires checking the initially unchecked choice **“Replace the unreadable saved copy with these words. The unreadable copy will be lost.”** Only then is **Save this tab’s writing instead** enabled. An empty local draft cannot use this route to erase the unreadable copy. There is no Use saved writing action for an unauthenticated copy.

Successful replacement saves a newly encrypted checkpoint of the readable local words. It sends no message and starts no connection. The normal saved indication returns only after the transaction commits and other saving/observation conditions permit it. This is a way to **keep the words still in this tab**, not recovery or decryption of the damaged copy. There is no promise that the unavailable copy is redundant, and no automatic deletion or replacement.

The ordinary two-readable-version review remains available. An authenticated missing checkpoint can still be explicitly recreated, and existing encrypted empty tombstones continue to prevent a stale tab from silently resurrecting cleared writing.

### Check the complete stored copy before every draft write

The second defect was narrower but important: observation compared complete envelopes, while writes compared only the revision label. Same-revision damage could therefore be overwritten by a later automatic save before a focus/hint check noticed it.

All draft writes now compare the complete canonical expected envelope with the copy read in the same `readwrite` transaction as the replacement. A null expectation means the slot must still be absent. This covers ordinary autosave, pending-send checkpoints, clearing, and explicit review choices. A changed cipher, identity, field, or revision cannot pass merely by retaining the old revision string. Comparison is a local precondition, not authentication of damaged data or a guarantee against a later writer.

The unreadable-copy review derives the selected room’s slot through the currently unlocked cryptographic provider; an untrusted row cannot choose its own replacement destination. The existing identity, generation, provider, draft epoch, selected room, complete accepted room object, membership, pending-policy state, and local writing version are checked. Unknown identity, mismatched slot, oversized envelope, another room, changed audience or writing, and superseded review attempts refuse replacement.

The review remembers the complete stored copy being offered for replacement. It checks that copy again at commit, so damage or a different edit arriving after review does not acquire consent. Withdrawing the checkbox while encryption is delayed also refuses replacement. Repeated save actions coalesce. Cancelling or locking aborts pending draft transactions and invalidates late callbacks. Text written after a commit begins is not erased by finishing the older choice. A failed transaction retains the readable local draft and stored copy, leaves saving visibly unresolved, and asks for a fresh review rather than silently retrying destructive consent.

Initial-load authentication failures are tracked by slot only; untrusted rows are not accepted as room mappings. Repair clears only the corresponding unreadable warning. An earlier global observation warning is rechecked rather than automatically cleared as proof that every other slot is sound. The review’s readable fields and replacement consent are cleared on dismissal and Lock.

### Scope and unchanged boundaries

Drafts remain local to default browser saving in `Vibechat-writing-v1`, schema 1, with the existing 32-slot, 33-row overflow, 170,000-byte envelope and eight-second transaction bounds. No schema migration, new key, envelope format, provider operation, package installation, compiler run, network service, permission request, or remote synchronization is introduced. `draft-seal` and `draft-open` are unchanged. Readable drafts are not placed into chat messages, profiles, backups, transfer snapshots, Waystations, the clipboard, or broadcast hints by this feature. Temporary and other storage modes retain their existing behavior.

The optional local BroadcastChannel hint is still the constant `changed`; it supplies neither contents nor authority. Focus and visible-page checks remain the fallback. No claim is made that hints deliver reliably, that a completed transaction survives every device failure, or that the browser can run while closed.

Runtime changes are confined to the draft controller in `client.js`, the recovery controls in the template, and current revision labels. `native.py`, `worker.js`, `worker.ts`, `crypto.ts`, `kdf.ts`, and `vendor.json` are byte-identical to the received carrier. The frame, CSP and finite source-only application copy are resealed from the checked sources. Builder status remains bounded under 32 KiB, current impact receipts point to section 265, and the external/carried drivers match.

First-meeting link/QR/code, independent identity confirmation, exact room policy, automatic returning-friend Homecoming, encrypted holding, negotiated accidental-connection repair, file backup, Carry Link, resumable transfer, signed Arrival, Safe Passage and manual recovery retain their existing implementations. There is still one ordinary conversation, not a new inbox or draft transport.

### A separate real-browser storage gate, with no substituted success

The carried `draftkeep_checks.py` now provides a strict route through `bash test.sh --require-navigation writing` (or its direct `--real-storage` option). It uses ordinary owned-loopback navigation, actual browser Worker/cryptography/IndexedDB/BroadcastChannel, independent same-origin tabs, a persistent browser profile, and a normal browser-process close/reopen. Only the encrypted accepted-room profile is a declared synthetic seed, written through an actual IndexedDB transaction. No storage, digest, provider, channel or DOM implementation is replaced in that strict lane; non-loopback requests are refused.

The intended assertions cover independent-tab draft recovery, real cross-tab conflict observation, atomic refusal of a change after review, explicit readable adoption, unreadable-copy replacement, and recovery after a normal browser restart. A normal restart is not a process kill, power cut, or hardware durability test.

On this host the first ordinary navigation returns `ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ADMINISTRATOR`. The lane therefore exits **77 / unavailable**, with **zero real-storage assertions** and no fallback to the simulation. No browser policy was changed. The separate 119-check writing lane continues to use its declared scoped fixtures; its passing status must not be substituted for the unavailable real-storage result.

The underlying platform references consulted for implementation are the [Indexed Database API 3.0 Working Draft](https://www.w3.org/TR/IndexedDB/) and the [HTML Living Standard local broadcasting section](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/web-messaging.html#broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts), consulted 2026-10-17. Their transaction/channel contracts are not execution receipts or proof of durable storage.

## 262. Same Desk — notice when another tab changes saved writing

Date: 2026-10-17. Input: `Vibechat-rev0086-2026.10.17-written-here-builder-handoff.zip`.

### The human road

Write normally. With default encrypted browser saving, the existing local checkpoint still restores unsent writing after the same identity is unlocked here. This revision closes a gap in that indication: a tab previously kept saying its draft was saved even after another tab had changed, sent, or cleared the shared checkpoint. A conflict was discovered only after another attempted write.

Returning to the tab now checks the saved writing. A changed or missing checkpoint replaces the stale saved indication with **Saved writing needs review**. The words, selection, current conversation, and message history in the open tab remain untouched. **Review saved writing** shows this tab's writing beside the currently authenticated saved copy. **Leave both unchanged** remains the initial choice. **Keep this tab's writing** or **Use saved writing** remains explicit; neither action sends a message.

This also notices a first saved draft created in another tab. It offers a review rather than inserting that text into an empty composer. Unreadable new slots cannot supply a trusted room mapping. Same-revision damaged ciphertext removes the old saved claim because comparisons include the complete envelope, not only its revision. A disappeared checkpoint is not silently recreated: retaining this tab's text requires the existing explicit review/commit.

Observation failure is separate from a save failure. The words remain in this tab and **Check saved writing again** retries the local check without rewriting or sending. Changed or unchecked in-tab writing participates in the existing **Before you lock** review. An unchanged committed draft still permits ordinary one-click Lock. A read can only establish what the store returned at that moment; this is not a cross-tab lock, independent durability proof, latest-state oracle, or live multi-device synchronization.

### Local hints, not a new transport or authority

After authenticated default-saving startup, the client optionally opens `BroadcastChannel("Vibechat-writing-changed-v1")`. A successfully completed draft write can publish the single constant string `changed`. No text, chat name, room ID, identity, slot, revision, password, key, capability, or ciphertext is included in the hint. It communicates only that local draft storage might have changed. It is not authenticated evidence and cannot supply replacement writing or authorize any action.

A recognized hint schedules a local read; unrecognized values do nothing. Bursts coalesce into one pending check with a bounded 100–1,000 ms scheduling delay and a one-second cooldown after completion. A further hint while checking requests at most one subsequent check. Hidden tabs defer scheduled observation until visible. Focus and visibility checks remain available without BroadcastChannel; its absence or constructor failure is not a chat failure. There is no periodic idle polling, network request, service worker, permission prompt, additional key, new database schema, or mandatory setup step.

Reads use the existing identity index, 33-row overflow check, eight-second transaction bound, and 170,000-byte envelope bound. The read must complete before its result is used. The application queue serializes observation with this tab's draft commits. Already authenticated slot mappings permit complete-envelope comparison. Previously unseen slots must be opened by the unchanged cryptographic provider before they can be associated with a room. Observation never adopts, seals, writes, sends, connects, or changes accepted room policy. An authenticated empty-to-empty tombstone can refresh an idle empty baseline without manufacturing a review ceremony; existing conflicts and unsent writing are not silently cleared.

Lock closes the channel, cancels timers, invalidates observation tickets, and aborts draft transactions through the existing cleanup. Old callbacks, delayed reads, replaced providers, and later unlocked identities cannot inherit pending observations. Temporary sessions do not open the watch or draft database. The underlying revision compare-and-swap remains the hard write-conflict fence; optional hints only improve when the person learns about a change. Different devices, origins, profiles, and storage partitions remain separate. This does not make snapshots synchronize or put drafts into chat backups, profiles, message history, peer transport, or Waystations.

The implementation follows the browser's local-channel and transaction boundaries, not a custom broadcast protocol: [BroadcastChannel API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/BroadcastChannel) and [Indexed Database API 3.0, transaction lifecycle](https://www.w3.org/TR/IndexedDB/#transaction-lifecycle), consulted 2026-10-17. The latter document identifies itself as a Working Draft. Neither specification is a receipt that a browser preserved data on physical hardware.

### Repair the inherited Friends assertion without weakening its journey

The received rev0086 failed its extra Familiar journey at the combined offline-Connect/caption assertion. The test still required the pre-holding words `New messages stay here`, while the ordinary conversation now retained a Homecoming route. Its later steps also assumed the primary Connect button always opened the manual signed invitation flow.

The final test records the actual combined state: Connect visible and enabled, manual fallback visible, and the contextual caption. It requires a truthful disconnected caption for the observed route, then deliberately uses **the manual fallback** for the signed offer/answer round trip that this journey is intended to test. It still checks local room opening, unchanged text/selection, no implicit peer creation, offline message retention, exact-room reuse, once-only catch-up, authenticated conversation in both directions, and Lock/reopen fencing. The separate Reunion lane tests the automatic primary route; its assertions were not replaced by this manual test.

One product wording defect was corrected as well. Absence of a live channel previously said the friend **is away**. It now says **Not connected live to [friend]**. A transport state is not evidence of where the person is or whether they are online elsewhere. No connection, identity, invitation, holding, or repair protocol was changed by this wording repair.

### Source and compatibility boundary

Changed runtime behavior is confined to `client.js`; the carrier frame/CSP is resealed from the checked sources. `draftkeep_checks.py` carries the focused regressions and `familiar_checks.py` the repaired current-route journey. The existing writing lane also retains its native/worker interoperability and encrypted draft custody checks. Driver revision, bounded current status, source-binding lengths/hashes, and prescribed memorandum-body digests are refreshed. Rebinding is not execution of every historical laboratory.

`native.py`, `worker.ts`, `worker.js`, `crypto.ts`, `kdf.ts`, and `vendor.json` are byte-identical to the received product. No compiler run, package download, dependency, provider operation, envelope format, new key, or server change is needed. First-meeting link/QR/code, Homecoming, encrypted holding, negotiated automatic repair, ordinary file backup, Carry Link, resumable transfer, signed Arrival, and manual recovery retain their existing implementations.

## 260. Written Here — keep unfinished writing without making it a message

Date: 2026-10-17. Input: `Vibechat-rev0085-2026.10.17-steady-crossing-builder-handoff.zip`.

### The ordinary human road

With the default encrypted browser saving selected, write in a conversation as usual. Vibechat checkpoints the draft automatically and says **Draft saved encrypted on this device** only after the storage transaction completes. Lock, reopen Vibechat at the same browser origin, and unlock the same identity: the unsent words return to their accepted conversation. Continue writing, or explicitly choose Send. No extra password, preference, invitation, or draft-saving ceremony was added.

A checkpoint is local to this browser/profile/origin. Another browser, another site address, a different identity, cleared browser data, or a different device is not the same draft store. This is local recovery, not synchronization or guaranteed hardware durability. Wait for the saved indication; the newest unfinished edits may not have committed yet. Temporary sessions and the other storage modes retain their tab-only draft behavior. A draft store failure does not prevent ordinary chatting; the interface instead retains the text, offers **Try saving draft again**, and keeps unfinished writing in the existing risk-only Lock review.

First meetings still use one link, QR or compact code, then review the person. Returning friends still use the existing conversation and Connect; compatible live connections retain negotiated automatic repair. Deliberate Disconnect and Lock remain deliberate. Offline encrypted holding, message/file deduplication, Carry Link, same-tab resumable snapshot transfer, signed Arrival results and manual/file recovery remain the existing paths. No network service was added or selected by draft recovery.

### Local encrypted custody, separate from messages and backups

The browser client opens a separate version-1 IndexedDB database, `Vibechat-writing-v1`, only after authenticated default-saving startup. It does not migrate or change the existing profile/event database. Its `drafts` object store uses an opaque `id` key and an `identity` index. It retains at most 32 encrypted slots per identity, including encrypted empty tombstones. Hitting that bound leaves additional writing in the tab with an explicit error; tombstones are not silently pruned in a way that could let an old tab resurrect a cleared draft.

The encrypted payload binds the accepted room and exact policy, text, UTF-16 selection offsets/direction, and an optional exact prospective message event identifier. The client retains that policy when editing; it does not silently redirect a recovered draft to changed participants. A changed accepted policy stages a review of the writing and current participants, rather than adopting a new audience or sending text.

The store contains no readable draft text, room name, room identifier, password, private identity key or transfer capability. It does expose the existing public identity identifier, opaque per-room slot and random revision, plus ciphertext sizes and slot counts locally. This is not a metadata-free store. Drafts do not enter the message log, encrypted profile export, Back up chats, Carryover snapshot, peer transport or Waystation. Exporting a chat backup does not back up unfinished writing.

Checkpoints are debounced by 500 ms and use the existing operation queue. A multi-room flush yields between rooms so draft saving cannot monopolize normal conversation work. Browser database opening and transactions have an eight-second bound. Only transaction completion can advance the saved baseline. Errors, aborts, a blocked open, late crypto replies, lock, provider replacement and stale generations cannot be presented as saved work. The client requests strict write durability where the API supports the transaction option, but does not represent it as proof of physical storage surviving every shutdown.

### Two tabs must not silently replace each other's words

Each draft envelope has a fresh random revision. A write reads and compares the expected revision in the same read/write transaction before replacing the saved ciphertext. Another tab's changed or cleared revision is a conflict, not permission to overwrite it. An encrypted empty tombstone retains that conflict fence after a draft is cleared or sent.

**Review saved writing** shows this tab's text and the currently saved text, with current participants visible. The initial focused action is **Leave both unchanged**. **Keep this tab's writing** and **Use saved writing** are explicit choices; neither sends anything. The selected saved revision, local draft generation and exact room policy are checked again at adoption/commit. Editing or another tab saving during review requires a new review, not a last-writer-wins overwrite.

Closing or pressing Escape leaves the drafts alone, clears readable review copies and fences delayed review callbacks. Cancelling an in-progress review transaction aborts the replacement. Old close events and late reads cannot reopen a dismissed review, clear a newer review, or carry approval into another unlocked session.

The selection is restored from the last checkpoint. Moving only the caret does not continuously rewrite storage, so the recovered selection is not a promise to reproduce the very last cursor movement.

### An interrupted Send is not an instruction to send again

Before the normal message can be admitted or shared, the client attempts an encrypted checkpoint of the submitted draft with that message's exact prospective authenticated event identifier. On later loading, a pending-send draft is suppressed only when authenticated local history contains that exact event, from this identity, in the same room, with the same submitted text. An unrelated or similarly worded message cannot stand in for it.

When the exact message cannot be established, Vibechat recovers the writing and asks the person to check the conversation before sending again. It does not automatically send, reseal a message, invent a receipt, or treat a relay's response as delivery. Completing an older Send cannot erase words typed after that Send.

A failed local message save keeps the encrypted pre-send checkpoint rather than overwriting it with blank text. A later successful write in the same draft slot can replace that checkpoint, so this is not a durable multi-message outbox or replacement for the existing unsaved-message warning and backup route. Conversely, when no saved draft checkpoint exists and an unavailable draft database accompanies an otherwise successful send, the resulting empty composer does not manufacture an unsaved-draft Lock warning.

Saved drafts permit ordinary one-click Lock and are hidden along with readable chat state. Unsaved or conflicting writing remains part of **Before you lock**. Lock aborts pending draft transactions and invalidates late providers/controllers; it does not perform an unreliable shutdown autosave or promise recovery of edits that never committed.

### Authenticated provider additions, not a new chat protocol

Both `native.py` and `worker.ts`/the carried `worker.js` add `draft-seal` and `draft-open`. The native and worker implementations cross-open each other's actual encrypted envelopes. These are authenticated local provider operations; no identity export or general-purpose encryption endpoint was added.

The envelope is `vibechat-draft-envelope-v1` with exact fields `format`, `identity`, opaque `id`, random `revision`, `iv`, and `cipher`. Identity/id are 64 lowercase hex characters, revision is 32, and the IV is canonical base64 for 12 random bytes. AES-256-GCM authenticates the canonical header containing format, identity, id and revision. A separate 32-byte content key is derived from the existing profile key with the identity id as salt and the context `Vibechat/local-draft/content/v1`. The opaque room slot derives separately with context `Vibechat/local-draft/slot/v1/` followed by the room id. Content-key and slot derivation are domain-separated from the existing profile and message operations.

Payload validation limits text to 28,000 UTF-16 units and a 120,000-byte canonical payload, validates scalar text and ordered integer selection offsets, restricts direction to forward/backward/none, and accepts only null or an exact 64-hex event id for the send marker. Stored envelope bytes are capped at 170,000. Seal requires the latest exact accepted room policy and membership; open authenticates and validates without adopting any room. The worker clears temporary key/buffer material where practical; JavaScript/Python memory is not claimed securely erased.

The ordinary chat, identity, room, signaling, message and backup formats are unchanged. Core `crypto.ts`, `kdf.ts` and carried C primitive source were not changed. The generated worker and vendor binding were rebuilt and independently reproduced. The historical native core revision marker is not the carrier revision and was not cosmetically rewritten.

An explicitly configured native provider endpoint must include the matching new local-draft operations. Arbitrary older endpoint/new client combinations are not qualified by these tests; an unavailable operation follows the visible unsaved-draft recovery path, not plaintext fallback. This is separate from ordinary peer-version compatibility: no peer draft protocol was introduced.

There are 148 named sources and 66 discoverable test lanes. `draftkeep_checks.py` is carried as `vibe-writing-tests`, and the driver exposes `writing`. The impact map points to this work and section 261. The current status JSON remains 32,508 bytes under the unchanged 32 KiB limit. Current carrier, client, template, driver, manifest and builder metadata identify rev0086 Written Here.

Exact-source inventories and their original nonrecursive body digest rules were refreshed, preserving each inventory's existing include/exclude treatment of `source_bindings`. Rebinding a digest is byte bookkeeping, not fresh execution of every historical laboratory. Historical analysis and evidence remain historical; section 261 is the current execution receipt.

The inherited Holdfast public-invitation fixture assumed the pre-Beacon default button already produced a reusable static public card. It now deliberately enters **Other ways → Send Vibechat.html for later**, exercising that same compatibility path without changing runtime invitation behavior or weakening its assertions. The temporary speculative Familiar-caption test edit was discarded; the carried Familiar helper is byte-identical to the received one.

Continue from the actual received rev0085 implementation. Its recovery of rev0084 did not contain independently mounted rev0082 Durable Arrival or rev0083 Stay Put runtime changes. This revision does not claim those missing durable receipt-watch/browser-persistence features. Arrival watching remains the existing sending-tab feature. Encrypted draft checkpoints are the new persistence scope, not evidence of unrelated missing work.

API design references: W3C Indexed Database API, https://www.w3.org/TR/IndexedDB-3/ ; Web Cryptography API, https://www.w3.org/TR/webcrypto-2/ . These inform API/transaction design, not qualification of actual browser durability or an independent security review.

Highest-value next checks are ordinary browser/database execution and real-device reopening, storage denial/eviction, two genuinely separate tabs, process-kill send windows and changed-origin expectations. Resolve the recorded inherited Familiar assertion by observing the actual combined state, not simply weakening it or substituting a caption. A future portability option for drafts would need separate explicit consent and authenticated room/audience review; do not silently fold drafts into sent history, profile synchronization or chat backups. Empty tombstones deliberately consume bounded slots: any reclamation design must preserve stale-tab conflict fences rather than merely deleting the last revision.

Keep the central goal in view: one string/QR for a first meeting, no repeated handoff for an established friend, one ordinary conversation, and recoverable work. Do not trade trust, exact room policy or honest saved/sent states for a cosmetic success. Preserve the exact historical suffix and return only one next-revision three-file ZIP.

## 258. Steady Crossing — make the delivered transfer protection real

Date: 2026-10-17. Input: `Vibechat-rev0084-2026.10.15-safe-passage-builder-handoff.zip`.

### The ordinary human roads

First meeting remains **Invite a friend → share one link, QR, or compact code → review the person → connect**. Returning friends retain **open the existing conversation → Connect → chat** and the existing negotiated automatic repair after an accidental live-channel interruption. Deliberate Disconnect and Lock remain deliberate.

Moving chats remains **Back up chats → Make transfer link & QR**, then **Restore a backup → open/scan/paste → Get encrypted backup → original login details**. A transfer is a snapshot, not live multi-device synchronization. File backup remains the no-service and oversized-snapshot fallback.

While a transfer is active, **Let screen sleep** and **Pause transfer** now have separate, visible meanings. Letting the screen sleep never cancels the transfer. Pausing aborts only that task's I/O and retains existing confirmed sender progress or authenticated receiver pieces in the same tab. **Continue transfer** or **Try this transfer again** resumes the same prepared transfer; no repeated scan or paste is required. A deliberate pause is not undone by a later online event.

### What was actually received

The input's 146 named source members are byte-for-byte equal to the mounted rev0081 Arrival carrier. Its only runtime-frame addition is an unsealed `VIBECHAT_REV0084_SAFE_PASSAGE` script appended outside the manifest-bound client. The original verifier refuses it with `HTML/shell frame integrity mismatch`; the existing CSP does not authorize that new executable script. Its external test driver also differs from the carried driver by an appended grep-only tail after an `exec` handoff. Those checks do not establish working transfer protection.

This revision removes the unsealed appendix, implements the feature inside `client.js` and the original template, and seals the exact result. It does not loosen CSP, install a global fetch interceptor, identify actions by button-label regular expressions, or raise a verification limit. The title, opening footer, client, manifest, builder and status view now identify rev0085 consistently.

There is no independently mounted rev0082 or rev0083 implementation in this input. **Do not claim Durable Arrival receipt-check persistence or Stay Put browser-storage requests from their earlier chat descriptions.** Arrival in these bytes still watches from the sending tab. The received rev0084 bootstrap is preserved below verbatim as history, not promoted into proof of missing features.

### Implemented task ownership and continuation

The integrated `passage` controller owns only ephemeral task IDs, AbortControllers, consent/mute flags, deadlines, and a wake-lock sentinel. It stores no profile, credential, message draft, backup, transfer code, or receipt capability. The existing Carryover state remains the owner of its existing same-tab encrypted snapshot, retained capability, authenticated pieces and cursor.

Each Carryover upload and retrieval request has a **15-second headers-and-body deadline** and a task-owned abort signal. Real streaming bodies are bounded before whole-response assembly. Redirects are refused. A timeout also wins against a fixture or collaborator that ignores AbortSignal. The receive loop retains its existing overall lookup and page bounds; local cryptographic preparation is not falsely described as a 15-second end-to-end transfer guarantee.

Pausing, Lock, replacement, offline loss and page exit fence pending work. After every relevant cryptographic or HTTP await, the caller rechecks the exact task and transfer generation before advancing a confirmed part, adopting a received part, moving a cursor or staging the backup preview. A late successful POST cannot skip an uncertain part. Retrying can repeat that part safely under the existing authenticated duplicate rules. Receiver replacement and late cleanup cannot erase a newer transfer.

An online event can continue an interrupted sender's same prepared snapshot. A single pending flag coalesces events while the previous attempt settles; there is no timer retry loop. Explicit pause clears that pending intent. A receiver still has its existing same-code retry and online continuation where eligible.

### Screen and leave behavior

An actual trusted transfer action can request the browser's optional screen wake lock. Page opening and synthetic clicks cannot grant that permission. The same active flow may reacquire it when visible again; no request occurs when hidden, offline or idle. A denial does not interrupt the transfer or create a rapid retry loop. A delayed grant for an ended, replaced, hidden or muted task is released rather than adopted.

Wake protection is bounded to five minutes per active attempt, after which the person can explicitly choose **Keep screen awake** again. **Let screen sleep** releases that protection without pausing I/O. Unsupported browsers simply continue. Successful publication or preview staging ends the active task; waiting for an Arrival result does not keep a screen awake.

The existing browser leave guard now also recognizes active transfer tasks, including retrieval on the locked opening screen. It does not add a warning merely because a transfer is ready, a paused task is parked, or an Arrival result is pending. Existing unsaved-chat and draft warnings remain independent. The interface says to keep the tab open because same-tab progress is not crash recovery.

API design reference: W3C Screen Wake Lock specification, https://www.w3.org/TR/screen-wake-lock/ — visibility, optional acquisition and release semantics informed this integration. This is not evidence that any particular phone will grant or retain a wake lock.

### Preserved boundaries

The native implementation, worker implementation and source, cryptographic implementation, KDF source and vendor inventory are unchanged from the actual received named sources. No wire format, key derivation, identity pin, accepted-room rule, backup authentication, signed transfer result, first-meeting parser, Waystation address policy or consent boundary was relaxed. Receiving the completed encrypted snapshot still stages only the original unverified preview. Authentication and restoration still require the original chat name, password and advanced recovery salt when used.

**Drafts are still current-unlocked-tab state.** No plaintext draft store, encrypted draft persistence, shutdown autosave or automatic browser-storage persistence was added. The bootstrap's draft-recovery target was deferred in favor of repairing the nonfunctional delivered transfer guard and indefinite request seam first.

### Source and builder maintenance

There are now 147 named source members. `safe_passage_checks.py` is a carried named source and `bash test.sh ... safepassage` is a discoverable lane. `impact` includes it for relevant client, transfer, status and builder changes. A deployment must still have reachable holding and traversal support; a QR alone cannot keep a closed browser process running. Do not invent support by weakening verification or hiding a failure.

Continue building. Keep receipts honest and keep the ordinary human path small. Return one revision ZIP.
