## 0. Current-first briefing — Sightglass

### 0.1 What changed, and the guarantee deliberately not made

Sightglass adds the bounded latest-observation exchange recommended by Passageglass. The participant no longer promotes preparation to a new local commit using only an arbitrarily old retained authority prefix. It asks a fresh signed challenge of the exact private authority, verifies the complete bounded returned history, and requires a still-live five-second attempt at the local transaction boundary. Offline or stale answers block new settlement. Already committed results remain exactly recoverable offline.

The guarantee is **an authenticated authority snapshot inside the current bounded attempt**, not current authorization at recipient commit. The named authority ordering point is its first committed-events read inside a new `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction, under the existing non-threaded Orderglass writer lock. The observation writes no event, reservation, nonce cache or anchor and takes no lease. The authority read transaction ends before the participant can commit.

Accordingly, a cutover before that authority snapshot blocks settlement; a cutover learned locally before commit also blocks it; **an unseen cutover after the snapshot can still precede a successful local commit**. The corpus deliberately demonstrates all three orders. Do not erase the last outcome with phrases such as “latest authorization at commit,” “instant revocation” or “atomic freshness.” Five seconds is a local laboratory budget, not a proof of distributed atomicity or a recommended production policy.

### 0.2 The three processes and their exact new seam

The laboratory still has three processes: Loopglass owns prekey reservation, the Sightglass extension of Orderglass owns admission/cutover order and answers observations, and the Sightglass participant performs authenticated session settlement. **Both synthetic endpoint roles remain in that participant process.** Authority and endpoint fixtures are private co-located laboratory material, not independently isolated users or hosts.

Two new domain-separated signed records carry the observation exchange: `vibechat-sightglass-query-v1` and `vibechat-sightglass-observation-v1`. Their explicit purpose is `authority-snapshot-not-commit-permission`. The recipient signs a fresh cryptographically random 32-byte challenge, the fixed request interval, and the exact authority scope, lineage and key; recipient user, installation and authorization; grant and requester wrapper; unchanged inner request digest and reservation receipt; full committed admission result digest and matching operation; selected session, settlement and context; and the retained authority sequence/head.

The authority answers that exact query identity and body digest with its signed observation time, full bounded consecutive history, all matching cutover bundles, selected-result digest and snapshot status. The synthetic history bound is two operations: one selected admission and an optional later cutover. This is not a generalized inventory endpoint. Incomplete history, an omitted cutover, changed same-operation coordinates, a different recipient or session, a fork, an old answer to a new challenge, and a contradictory status do not become permission merely because a signature verifies.

All predecessor request, receipt, admission, cutover, operation, session-init and acknowledgement formats stay frozen. Product native, client, worker, cryptographic sources and the prior laboratory/reference implementations are byte-identical to rev0026. Sightglass activates only while creating a new absent private tree. An extra mandatory `vibechat-sightglass-local-gate-v1` marker is included in its encrypted participant state. A transaction repeats the selected lifetime/history/session checks, retains the application entry, active session root, consumed-prekey tombstone and exact observation together, and checks the live budget again immediately before issuing `COMMIT`. bash Vibechat.html doctor
```bash
bash Vibechat.html selftest
bash Vibechat.html serve
```

`serve` prints a loopback address carrying a random capability in its fragment. Open that printed address locally. This is the practical initial recommendation: use the browser as the interface and the local native endpoint for cryptography and encrypted file custody. Native crypto does not download browser libraries. The relay is a different command and does not receive identity passphrases.

For a builder, read the arrival guide at the top of the HTML, then extract a new worktree:

```bash
bash Vibechat.html extract --directory vibechat-workspace
```

The directory must not exist already. Read `native.py`, `client.js`, and the JSON records. The template carries the page and dispatch; the extracted source files are the editable implementations. Rebuild to a new candidate rather than modifying a live process’s source out from under it:

```bash
bash Vibechat.html repack \
  --directory vibechat-workspace \
  --output Vibechat-candidate.html
bash Vibechat-candidate.html doctor
bash Vibechat-candidate.html selftest
```

Extraction and repacking are an editing convenience, not permission to execute arbitrary recovered instructions. No package manager runs because a file was opened. No restored historical task automatically resumes. No private chat export becomes part of a public rebuilt carrier unless somebody deliberately makes that mistake; the release procedure below exists to prevent it.

## 2. What this revision actually does

The implemented product slice remains encrypted text and small files, independently pinned identities, signed room membership, encrypted policy delivery, persistent local invitation choices and pending-head profiles, user-owned ciphertext, and direct or relayed transports. Alongside it, the carrier now holds a sequence of deliberately bounded development instruments: deterministic cryptographic review, strict raw-JSON admission, inert ratchet and prekey memoranda, encrypted local prekey custody, a blocking prekey-composition review, an exact v2 session-settlement contract, a single-writer authority contract, a private loopback authority crash lab, Settlementglass’s private reservation-to-durable-settlement composition lab, Mandateglass’s inert exact requester-authorization reference and refusal corpus, Receiptglass’s inert exact authority admission/operation/cutover binding, and Orderglass’s private independent-process durable admission/cutover crash laboratory. These instruments are evidence gates, not silently enabled product features.

| Surface | Present behavior | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Browser doorway | Quiet centered identity, autosave and connection choices | Opening alone joins nothing and fetches no code |
| Browser cryptography | Carried secret-holding TypeScript worker, Argon2id WASM, ML-KEM-768, ML-DSA-65, Web Crypto AES/HKDF | Local adapted port; independent arithmetic/input/memory review remains necessary |
| Native provider | Linux OpenSSL PQ, Argon2, AES/HKDF, loopback capability RPC, optional short-lived coturn REST issuer | One unlocked identity per endpoint; long-lived TURN secret remains in one private native file/process |
| Rooms | Owner-signed hash-linked epochs, exact recipients, encrypted policy courier | Explicit new-room acceptance; no global freshness oracle or co-owner consensus |
| Contact recovery | Encrypted profiles store verified cards, policy chains, pending/declined anchors, choices, adoption receipts and capability queries/answers | No trusted remote key-change or disk rollback service |
| Invitation choices | Decline/dismiss unjoined rooms; explicitly review again before accepting | Local only; joined-room updates cannot be dismissed |
| Policy-adoption receipts | Authenticated exact room/epoch/policy/member statement with session or profile scope | Not reading, human approval, liveness, consent or global freshness |
| Receipt capability | Fresh-nonce encrypted query/response for `policy-adoption/1` between two pinned identities | Silence is unknown; support is not a promise and never changes membership |
| File exchange | Up to 2 MiB, 16 KiB encrypted chunks | Reassemble and verify before saving; no attachment execution |
| Relay and federation | Token-gated bounded ciphertext, explicit relay peers | Admission token is not room membership or user identity |
| Terminal | TCP/TLS/SOCKS5 text, persistent rooms/profiles, room commands | Whole-file composition/assembly remains primarily a browser function |
| WebRTC | Target-bound ML-DSA signal v2, explicit/manual ICE or native-issued short-lived TURN credential, ordered RTCDataChannel framing | Actual owned-loopback TURN/TCP relay-candidate lane; no public direct-NAT, voice or video claim |
| Managed TURN custody | Short-lived credentials, encrypted restart journal, optional external witnessed head/CAS and revocation observation | Provider-specific, explicit, no global lease or absolute revocation proof |
| Prekey design/custody | Exact inert device/publication formats and encrypted local synthetic custody | Not automatic publication, discovery, remote one-time proof or product session setup |
| Authority design/lab | Exact single-writer contract plus explicit private capability-gated `127.0.0.1` crash laboratory | No public service, multi-host transaction, consensus, trusted clock or product route |
| Settlement composition lab | One exact synthetic publication → reservation → Contextglass session-init → authenticated payload → local durable settlement → acknowledgement → authority observation | Single process, owned loopback, private state, no product integration or FS/PCS claim |
| Requester authorization | Exact user/device/requester/authority/target/context grant and signed-wrapper reference; user-only terminal revocation | Memory-only conformance; not called by product or laboratories; its authority consequence is bound only by the separate inert Receiptglass reference |
| Authority admission binding | Exact grant/wrapper/request-to-reservation admission receipt, consecutive operation record, authority-observed cutover and recipient local-history refusal | Memory-only conformance; no listener, persistence, independent process, product route, global freshness or rollback-proof store |
| Admission/cutover process lab | Separate explicit Loopglass and Orderglass processes, exact replay, one SQLite admission/cutover order, encrypted rows, signed local anchor, nine crash edges | Private synthetic owned-loopback evidence; no product route, public service, distributed transaction, global freshness, independent witness or physical power-loss qualification |
| Workshop | 65 named source members, manifest, source/find/impact/compare, exact protocol summaries, extract/build/repack | Integrity is not independent authorship, provenance, permission or execution authority |
| Development tests | Separate CLI, transport, provider, journal, witness, browser, WebRTC, interop, review, malformed, admission, ratchet, prekey, custody, composition, session, authority, authority-lab, settlement-lab, authorization, binding, orderlab and carrier lanes | Scopes remain distinct; overlapping counts are not an aggregate security score |

Voice, video, screen sharing, reactions, message editing, a forward-secret product ratchet, automated native NAT traversal, automatic prekey publication/discovery, a separate-process Orderglass-to-Settlementglass session composition, streaming attachment encryption, contact-key replacement, room-owner transfer, and PQ-protected live media remain separate work. The courier delivers policies through existing links; it does not silently publish every edit or claim that every peer has adopted one. Ordinary WebRTC media encryption is not substituted for application-layer PQC. No provider or laboratory failure enables plaintext or a classical-only suite.

### 2.1 Offline browser dependency closure

All browser cryptographic program bytes travel in the HTML. `vibe-worker` is the compiled program; `vibe-vendor` carries the WASM modules, hashes, upstream references, compiler identities and notices. Six readable source members reproduce the cryptographic worker and WASM. Worker creation uses a local Blob, not a remote script URL. The boot message supplies carried bytes; hash or module-import failures stop initialization. There is no dynamic import, `importScripts` call, fetch-based dependency resolver, CDN retry, or runtime crypto-module download.

The native provider is independent of that browser implementation. OpenSSL provides its ML-KEM/ML-DSA operations, argon2-cffi provides its KDF, and cryptography provides AES-GCM/HKDF. Browser worker keys remain in the worker; native keys remain at the local native endpoint. Web Crypto supplies browser/Node AES-GCM, HKDF and SHA-256, while the carried TypeScript and WASM supply the required PQ and Argon2 operations. [T01–T03, T17–T23]

The former `vendor-web` command remains a refusal-only tombstone. It does not retrieve anything. Old rev0001 instructions to permit module downloads are superseded. Developers rebuild carried source explicitly using already installed tools; users do not need TypeScript, clang, Node, npm, or a package registry to run the standalone browser product.

A secure browser context and the required platform APIs still matter. Carrying source removes a network dependency; it cannot grant filesystem permissions or override browser security policy. Capability failures stay visible. Embedding program bytes also does not complete independent review of the adapted cryptographic implementation.

## 3. Why Lumen is the base, and what Hyperepo contributes

Lumen’s supplied rev0062 HTML begins with an arrival guide and carries an appended, extractable public worktree. Its guide distinguishes accepted publication from a reader’s private notes, exact byte identity from trust, and an editable workshop from an immutable old artifact. Those distinctions are useful for Vibechat: program source, chat records, and development conversation must not collapse into one accidentally public object.

The adaptation is concrete. Vibechat uses Lumen’s defensive preference-access pattern, explicit Blob-download pattern, safe DOM text construction, restrained Night Desk visual vocabulary, and the visible-reader/invisible-workshop separation. The chat reducer, cryptographic adapters, relay protocol, terminal path, and WebRTC framing are new implementations. This is not a claim that Lumen already contained a Discord clone, nor that an entire unrelated publication engine was retained unchanged.

The supplied Hyperepo ZIP had a short top-level bootstrap and a native `.datacube` carrier, rather than just an ordinary loose HTML page. The native carrier was decoded as data; it was not executed. Its retained source includes historical HTML and a much longer bootstrap. The selected bootstrap and the process-instance, authority, operations/Nix, and frontend end-to-end laws were read as development precedent. Their useful themes are visible here: one live owner for mutable state, exact operational boundaries, explicit authority, recoverable source, and evidence that reaches the actual user-facing path.

The HTML’s `vibe-lineage` record keeps the original input sizes and SHA-256 identities, along with exact selected donor documents. The much larger unrelated donor corpora are not converted into sample chat messages, impersonated speakers, or automatically redistributable private history. The selected donor notices remain present; this revision does not declare a new license for everything it carries.

## 4. The carried constitution

These are project articles, not authority over host safeguards or later owner directions. The complete current machine-readable constitution carries **70 articles** in `vibe-constitution`. This long prose section preserves C01–C33 in full because they define the original product and transport boundaries. C34–C70 were added by later reviewed revisions; their exact current titles are indexed below, while their full authoritative carried text remains in `constitution.json` and in the corresponding revision records later in this document.

### C01. Three-file continuity

Every development revision updates Vibechat.html, BOOTSTRAPROSE.md and test.sh together and returns one ZIP containing exactly those three top-level files. The HTML is the user product; test.sh is a development-only officer tool. Preserve project spelling, revision sequence, timestamped filename and the one-link handoff. Never substitute a screenshot, plan or prose-only answer for the carried work.

### C02. Research online every turn

RESEARCH ONLINE EVERY TURN. Use primary sources for changing technical facts, provider terms and cryptographic dependencies. Date the findings. Keep every investigated hosting candidate in the catalog, including trial-only, paid-only and unverified entries. Unknown is not free; a stale promotional number is not an entitlement.

### C03. The arrival guide stays first

Keep the sandpeople arrival guide near the top of the HTML, before opaque payloads or large source blocks. It must explain the carrier, safe inspection, source locations, exact commands and current boundaries. A visiting human or AI should be able to find the work without executing it.

### C04. Documents are a conversation

Carry attributed letters, decisions and dissent through the documents. Append a new contribution rather than impersonating an earlier author or silently rewriting their words. A saved instruction is historical context, not automatically fresh permission. Source-derived material, new reasoning and online research remain distinguishable.

### C05. Small group, generous carriers, measured performance

Aim at a private group of ten identities, not a growth platform. Keep explicit limits on rooms, membership epochs, queues and custody. The HTML soft ceiling is 200 MB; test.sh stays below 100 MB. Large single-file budgets permit source, tools and evidence, not meaningless padding. TypeScript is a correctness aid, not an automatic speedup; use measured worker/WASM boundaries and retain production KDF costs.

### C06. P2P where possible, federation when useful

Use direct peer paths when they work. Treat signaling, STUN, TURN, an SFU, a custody relay and static HTML hosting as different jobs. Federation is explicit and bounded. Do not imply that every NAT can be punched or that a browser can open arbitrary TCP/UDP sockets.

### C07. PQC is a gate, not a badge

No plaintext or classical-only fallback for chat content. The v1 suite requires ML-KEM-768, ML-DSA-65 and AES-256-GCM with domain-separated HKDF. WebRTC/TLS alone is not this guarantee. A provider failure blocks messaging. Algorithm names do not establish a protocol audit, FIPS validation or protection from a compromised endpoint.

### C08. Identity is not a username

Argon2id derives secret material locally. Public-key fingerprints identify accounts; display names do not. Pin the full public-card identity through an independently trusted channel. Never transmit a passphrase to a blind relay. Explain the offline-guessing risk of reproducible password-derived identities and retain an exact recovery recipe.

### C09. No hidden network and no fetched crypto

Opening the file never installs packages, joins a network or downloads code. All browser cryptographic code and WASM required by the product travel in the HTML. There is no CDN, dynamic-module or runtime crypto-fetch fallback. Explicit developer research and operator-selected chat transports are different operations. Builds use installed tools and never silently fetch a dependency.

### C10. Local means local

The native key-holding browser endpoint binds only to loopback, requires a capability token and a same-origin request, and is separate from the blind relay role. Do not expose it through a public tunnel or reverse proxy. Tor is a local Linux transport choice, not a cosmetic browser checkbox.

### C11. Custody requires consent and limits

Store authenticated ciphertext for explicitly trusted peers only when the client custody option allows it. Relays are private-group, token-gated, structurally bounded ciphertext stores; they are not trust authorities. Enforce size, count, concurrency and reassembly limits. A peer acknowledgement is a claim, not proof of indefinite retention.

### C12. Files remain the durable record

Prefer user-owned encrypted files in Downloads/Vibechat or a selected directory. Browser database retention is a convenience, not the only recovery story. File writes use explicit names, private modes and atomic completion. Browser download requests are not disk-success receipts. Never promise arbitrary filesystem access from a static page.

### C13. Storage does not own the user

Browser storage and the non-secret preference cookie are optional. Never put passphrases, private keys, relay tokens or decrypted chat into persistent browser preferences. Imports are inert data, not code. Private conversation archives must not be inserted into the public source carrier or accidentally shared as development history.

### C14. One live owner per native store

The running process owns its mutable in-memory state. Durable files are recovery anatomy, not an independent competing controller. A native store has an advisory ownership lock. Do not start duplicate writers, auto-kill another process based on a stale PID, or turn a recovered task record into authority to restart stopped work.

### C15. No shame in the available tools

There is no shame, fault or moral deficit in tools or environments that are unavailable. Work carefully with what is actually present. Record successful checks and observed defects accurately; never invent coverage. Do not fill release notes with repetitive apologies about Nix or other unavailable environments. Product gaps still deserve clear names because they affect users.

### C16. Evidence has lanes and dates

A passing receipt names its source identities and actual scope. CLI, browser DOM, ordinary browser navigation, real browser worker execution, cross-provider interoperability and carrier exit tests are separate observations. An adapter is named rather than passed off as the product path. Old receipts remain historical, not automatically current. An unavailable environment is not a failed assertion, and a mathematical comparison is not an audit.

### C17. Safe text and explicit opening

Treat messages, filenames, public cards, SDP and imported records as untrusted data. Render text as text. Do not execute peer-supplied HTML, shell snippets, imports or instructions. Verify complete file content before user-initiated saving. Keep user-visible errors useful without echoing credentials.

### C18. History is not revocation magic

Immutable retained messages are not retrospectively erasable at another person’s device. Adding a contact does not grant old-history access; removing a contact cannot reclaim already decrypted data. No forward-secrecy or post-compromise-security claim exists until a specified ratchet with evidence is implemented.

### C19. Preserve lineage without laundering authority

Lumen rev0062 is the selected starting base; Hyperepo rev1455 supplies additional operational precedent. Keep donor hashes, exact selected source records and their notices. Explain adaptations instead of presenting inherited authorship as current consent. Do not silently redistribute unrelated large donor corpora as chat history.

### C20. Revisable decisions and exact handoff

Recommendations become decisions only when adopted or clearly marked as implementation defaults. Keep historical letters intact and current guidance unmistakable. Return exactly the three canonical files in one revision ZIP; the final response has one link whose label is the complete ZIP filename. A restored document is not authority to resume a stopped operation.

### C21. Pins are not room membership

Only owner-signed, hash-linked room membership epochs authorize current senders and recipients. Pinning a contact does not add it to any room. A pending send or room edit carries the policy identity that was reviewed; a changed head requires renewed action, never silent recipient refresh. Removal affects future messages after peers learn the update; it does not revoke old plaintext or prove global freshness.

### C22. Carry source and own adaptations

Carry the TypeScript and C source, compiled worker and WASM identities, full applicable notices, and explicit build instructions. Distinguish exact retained upstream bytes from locally adapted ports. An adaptation does not inherit upstream audit coverage. Source hashes are identities, not independent trust roots. Keep the native provider and the independent comparison lane available while browser cryptography receives further review.

### C23. The workshop must survive the doorway

Keep bounded source reading, literal finding, carrier inspection, exact comparison, explicit compilation, safe extraction and no-overwrite repacking in the HTML. Exercise the resulting carrier in a new directory. A developer may use many extracted source files while the distribution ZIP still contains exactly three. Private messages and credentials never become workshop fixtures.

### C24. Delivery is not joining; incomplete updates remain knowledge

Deliver owner-signed policy changes inside the required encrypted envelope. A new-room invitation requires explicit acceptance of its exact complete head; receipt, a relay acknowledgement and contact pinning are not that acceptance. Complete authorized updates to joined rooms may apply automatically. Retain authenticated newer heads and earlier anchors through profile recovery, fence outgoing stale operations while an update is incomplete, and never silently erase pending knowledge to make a send succeed. A learned head is not a global freshness oracle. Publication, delivery, local adoption and another person’s participation are separate claims.

### C25. A local stop survives replay and recovery

Decline only a room that has not been joined, using its exact observed policy and prior local choice token. Preserve the signed knowledge and the local decision prefix; a later owner epoch, ciphertext replay or older profile must not silently reopen it. Reconsideration is explicit and does not join. Keep joined-room update fences outside dismissal controls. Bound retained decisions without silent expiry, eviction or invented completion of missing policy parts.

### C26. A changed screen is not a saved choice

Distinguish memory changes, requested downloads, completed storage operations and remote acknowledgements. Preserve known policy protections when a save fails, and make the retry boundary explicit before accepting the corresponding ciphertext as already seen. Profile persistence is not a transaction across every record store or a guarantee against complete rollback. Checkpoint completed test output during development, but never promote an interrupted or partial receipt into a completed passing lane.

### C27. A receipt names one exact claim

A policy-adoption receipt means only that the named member identity’s client adopted one exact owner-signed room policy at one epoch in the declared scope. Bind room, owner, member, epoch, policy identity and scope inside the authenticated encrypted envelope. Do not translate that statement into human reading, approval, consent, current presence, application processing, durable custody, global freshness or acceptance of later epochs. The absence of a receipt is not evidence of refusal or non-adoption unless a separate reviewed protocol establishes that expectation.

### C28. Persist the claimed state before sealing the claim

Issue a profile-scoped adoption claim only after the selected encrypted profile operation has committed the exact policy state; otherwise label the claim session-only. On the owner side, commit the compact room/member index before marking the receipt ciphertext accepted. Same-head replay and fresh re-encryption must be idempotent; a session claim may upgrade to profile scope, but an older epoch or weaker scope must not replace stronger current knowledge. A removed previous member may attest the exact removal head without regaining membership. Receipt acknowledgements must never request receipts for themselves.

### C29. Capability discovery answers one exact question

Ask only a pinned identity, bind the request and response to one fresh exact nonce, and retain the current query before its ciphertext is offered. Silence remains unknown: it can mean delay, offline state, refusal, loss, incompatibility or no answer. An authenticated omission means only that the feature was not advertised in that exact response. An authenticated positive answer means only that the named client advertised that versioned feature for that query; it is not a promise to issue a receipt, remain online, preserve future support, read a message or approve a policy.

### C30. Negotiation neither joins a room nor acknowledges itself

Capability query and response records use the ordinary required PQ envelope for exactly two pinned identities, but they do not add, remove or authorize room members. A response must not request another response or a policy-adoption receipt. Commit the exact query and authenticated answer in the selected encrypted profile before accepting their ciphertexts as already seen; older profiles may not silently erase or replace them. Keep capability support, exact policy adoption, relay custody and human participation as separate observations.

### C31. Signaling is an authenticated control surface

Manual WebRTC signaling targets one exact pinned identity. Sign the canonical role, session nonce, sender, target, complete SDP description and answer-to-offer packet identity with ML-DSA-65 under a protocol-specific domain. Refuse unsigned legacy packets, altered SDP, wrong targets, unpinned senders, role confusion, session substitution and answers that do not name the exact offer. Signaling remains visible metadata and may reveal network addresses; authentication does not make it secret.

### C32. Transport protection does not replace the PQ content envelope

DTLS, SCTP, ICE and TURN protect and carry a transport path according to their own standards; they are not Vibechat’s post-quantum content guarantee. Every text, file and control event remains independently ML-KEM-768 encrypted, ML-DSA-65 signed and room-policy bound before it reaches an RTCDataChannel. Never add a plaintext RTC fast path, never describe DTLS as post-quantum, and keep candidate metadata, transport confidentiality, application confidentiality and endpoint compromise as separate questions.

### C33. A relay exercise names the relay and the path

A local WebRTC result must name whether the selected candidate was host, server-reflexive or relay, whether TURN used UDP, TCP or TLS, and which stats and bytes were observed. An owned-loopback TURN-over-TCP fixture proves only that actual browser peers opened an RTCDataChannel through that fixture. It does not prove direct NAT traversal, a public provider, production credential handling, voice/video, global reachability or automatic hole punching. Never weaken a managed browser security policy merely to turn unavailable direct-candidate evidence into a pass.
