| Native room/profile | 34 | Signed membership, exact recipients, removal, stale sends/edits, rollback, forks, encrypted profiles and disk restart |
| Native transport | 20 | Owned-loopback HTTP capability/Origin guards, WebSocket/TCP, bounded federation and persistence |
| Terminal PTY | 1 | Actual password prompt, caller stdin, PQ text over TCP, durable ciphertext and clean exit |
| Chromium browser | 25 | Product DOM workflows with a named adapter, actual carried primitive worker, desktop/mobile checks |
| Worker/native interoperability | 99 | SHA3/SHAKE vectors, KEM/DSA cross-provider operations, Argon2 comparison, identity, room events and profiles |
| Carrier exit | 10 | New-directory extraction, unchanged repack, verification, no overwrite, changed-byte rejection, source tools and size budgets |

The browser receipt must be read literally. Ordinary local navigation was unavailable under the host's browser policy; no policy was changed. The DOM workflows used an explicitly named native RPC/digest fixture. Separately, a real Chromium Blob worker executed the carried TypeScript/WASM primitives, and its signature verified in native OpenSSL. The complete secret-holding worker protocol used real Node WebCrypto and was compared with the native provider. These are useful separate observations, not a manufactured ordinary-browser end-to-end success.

The browser lane attempts ordinary navigation first on future hosts. Officers can require that exact route with `--require-navigation`; absence then returns the distinct unavailable exit code 77 instead of being called a failed assertion or silently counted as navigation. The default aggregate receipt uses `passed-scoped` when its stated assertions pass, preserving the browser scope inside its detailed JSON.

```bash
# The three-file release is sufficient to extract every test's source.
bash test.sh --html Vibechat.html --output cli-receipt cli
bash test.sh --html Vibechat.html --output browser-receipt browser
bash test.sh --html Vibechat.html --require-navigation browser
bash test.sh --html Vibechat.html --output interop-receipt interop
bash test.sh --html Vibechat.html --output exit-receipt carrier
bash test.sh --html Vibechat.html --output all-receipts all
```

The native lane requires the normal application dependencies. Interop additionally needs Node. The browser lane additionally needs Python Playwright and an installed Chromium executable; `VIBECHAT_CHROMIUM` selects it explicitly. The driver never downloads browsers or packages. A missing required executable is not repaired by reaching out to a registry. Generated report directories are private development outputs and do not increase the ZIP member count.

Some retained transport fixtures use fixed owned-loopback ports in the 18851–18859 range. Run the current driver sequentially in a workspace rather than launching competing copies against those ports. It creates and terminates only its own processes and uses disposable synthetic credentials. It does not scan for external systems or enroll a hosted service. The genuine PTY test is retained precisely because DOM automation cannot prove that shell stdin and process ownership work correctly.

The full rebuild exit was also executed: the six extracted cryptographic source files were compiled with the recorded TypeScript/clang versions, their worker and WASM identities matched, and repacking was byte-identical. That is additional reproducibility evidence, not another vaguely inflated test total. `vibe-evidence` keeps exact component hashes and the detailed test names so a later officer can tell whether a source change invalidates a receipt.

## 25. A second reading of the donor machinery

Lumen's source/workshop distinction remains the base, not merely a visual inspiration. Its arrival guide makes an exact carrier identity different from trust, and its operating interface makes editable authored material different from the executable toolset. Its cloudtainer notes and public/private publication boundary reinforce that an exported working object must not quietly absorb a reader's private notes. The rev0002 `source`, `inspect`, `compare`, manifest and fresh-directory exit checks are new Vibechat implementations of those operating patterns. The exact selected donor texts travel in `vibe-lineage`; they are not paraphrases relabeled as original source.

Hyperepo supplied a different lesson in its authoring and retained-source machinery. Headless authoring and browser behavior have separate paths. A retained source identity is not replaced by a nearby title or current projection merely because an exact read is inconvenient. A prepared operation with stale source observations requires renewed review. Recovery does not equate an uncertain receipt with a completed write. Those distinctions informed the fixed source catalog, no-clobber output settlement, split test lanes, and policy-head fences for sends and edits.

The reread covered the supplied Hyperepo workbench HTML and its related authoring, retained-source-catalog and recovery documents. Its native datacube was decoded as data; no uploaded ELF was executed. The HTML was not assumed to be the whole repository or the only relevant evidence. Similarly, Lumen's appended ZIP worktree was inspected for actual operating documents, rather than treating the visible homepage's prose as a build specification.

There are limits to this inheritance. Vibechat has not imported Hyperepo's complete transaction system, a general checkpoint service, or Lumen's full publication engine. `compare` reports exact changed members, not a semantic change-radius atlas. The manifest is not a personal signature. Room policies are new application work, not functionality donated by either unrelated project. The review ledger lists source-derived patterns and new adaptations separately so future officers do not accidentally turn inspiration into a false implementation claim.

Thirteen exact selected documentary records are retained in the current lineage member, including the previous constitutions and bootstrap material. Original input sizes and hashes remain unchanged. Larger unrelated corpora are not included as chat data or unnecessary distribution ballast. This is how we preserve the sandpeople's source doorway and conversations without making the user traverse a donor's entire historical publication to send one message.

## 29. Relayglass: the encrypted policy courier

**Historical design baseline (rev0003), retained for the courier rationale.** Section 34 supersedes the lack of invitation decline and the profile v2-only description; the existing owner-authentication, transfer and send-fence rules remain current.

### 29.1 Four operations, not one reassuring word

A room owner can sign a policy without delivering it. A relay can receive ciphertext without its intended member decrypting it. A recipient can decrypt an invitation without deciding to join. A joined client can adopt a newer owner policy without proving that every other client has done the same. Relayglass gives these four operations separate paths and keeps them separate in the status text.

The practical change from Hearthforge is that a user no longer has to move a plaintext signed policy file between every pair of clients merely to distribute ordinary membership updates. The existing PQ envelope and ciphertext transport now carry policy fragments. This is application work over the previous envelope, not a different cipher suite, a new account server, or a third-party signaling SDK. The browser's required crypto still travels with the file.

The owner first changes the room's membership as before. The **Send encrypted policy** button is a separate deliberate action. In the terminal, the corresponding command is `/policy-send`. The publisher snapshots the selected room and exact head, verifies that it still owns that head, and creates records for each other member in the current or immediately preceding epoch. Each target receives a separately encrypted transfer. A changed head invalidates the publication plan rather than quietly substituting recipients midway through the operation.

A removed member needs the removal notice, so the immediately previous member set matters. This is not a permanent right to future room metadata. Someone removed several epochs earlier cannot demand a current courier through `policy-seal`; retained older removal records can still be delivered by ordinary custody synchronization. A newly added member receives the bounded full policy chain and therefore learns its historical membership metadata. They do not receive the content keys of old chat messages. That distinction is intentional and should remain visible when the interface later grows invitation previews.

Publication retains local encrypted records and offers them to ready links. With no link connected, the records remain local until a chosen link or an explicit ciphertext export carries them elsewhere. A successful publication status is not a claim of remote adoption. There is no delivery daemon secretly contacting a provider, no automatic publication after every edit, and no new membership receipt protocol in this revision.

### 29.2 The control record and its limits

Courier v1 reserves the outer channel marker `_room_policy`. That exact name is refused for user room policies in both providers, including imported signed chains. This prevents a user channel name from being mistaken for a control dispatch. Existing unusual rev0002 rooms with that reserved name need a deliberate transition to a differently named policy or new room; do not silently reinterpret their old messages as control instructions. Other room names remain ordinary labels, not authority.

The decrypted body is an exact object with these fields:

```text
{
  type: "room-policy",
  v: 1,
  target: <full recipient fingerprint>,
  tip: <complete owner-signed destination policy>,
  record: <one complete owner-signed policy from that chain>
}
```

`tip` and `record` have the existing policy-record format: `body`, `signature`, and content-derived `id`. The record's epoch supplies its index; the tip's epoch supplies the total number of positions. There is no unsigned name lookup, guessed predecessor, or separately trusted fragment count. The outer signature and exact recipient set must identify the immutable room owner and this one target. The target is not the owner; the owner retains its own envelope access as with other sent records.

Each fragment repeats the destination tip. Repetition costs bytes, but lets an early authenticated fragment establish which newer head the transfer is trying to reach. At the project's ten-person scale, this simple bounded rule is preferable to inventing a compact unsigned index whose meaning would need another protocol to authenticate. It is not a claim that repeating large PQ signatures is optimal for a large service. Complete chains are capped at 64 epochs, and each transfer uses at most 64 envelopes per target. The existing event, clear-payload and store bounds still apply.

The visible header discloses sender and target fingerprints, timestamps, approximate sizes and the control-channel marker. It does not conceal the existence of policy traffic. The encrypted body protects the room name, exact room ID, chain and member lists from a nonrecipient, but a group participant already entitled to receive the chain can read and copy that metadata. The product does not claim traffic-analysis resistance or a secret room directory merely because the policy body is encrypted.

A recipient verifies the already pinned sender, both owner signatures, content IDs, field types, room/owner consistency and exact recipients before admitting a fragment. An owner signature is necessary but not sufficient to make a complete chain: continuity must still be checked. A custodian outside the recipient pair may retain authenticated blind ciphertext when its custody choice permits it, but that retention does not create an invitation or a membership entry.

### 29.3 The inbox is a state machine with a visible boundary

A newly encountered room remains outside the accepted room book. Its authenticated fragments enter a bounded policy inbox. The interface shows the name, owner fingerprint, exact destination policy, epoch, part count and whether the current tip includes this identity. Once the full chain has arrived, **Accept this invitation** enables an exact-head acceptance. The terminal requires `/policy-join FULL_ROOM_ID FULL_POLICY_ID`, rather than accepting a short name or an invitation that changed after it was inspected.

Joining does not pin every person named in the chain. The room owner must already be pinned, and a sender still needs each current recipient's card independently confirmed. This preserves the distinction the owner accepted in rev0002: relationship trust and room membership are separate decisions. A relay token cannot make either decision on behalf of the user.

For a room already accepted, a complete later authorized chain is an update rather than a new invitation. It is applied automatically. This includes removal: a client that was legitimately in an earlier accepted epoch can adopt a later removal and disable its composer. Requiring the removed client to remain in the new policy would prevent it from learning its removal. It must still verify the exact original owner and every linked epoch.

When a newer signed tip arrives before missing intermediate epochs, the accepted head is not prematurely advanced. The inbox records the incomplete update, and outgoing room messages, pending file chunks, membership edits and lower-head manual imports are fenced. The user sees an update-pending state instead of a composer that can silently continue from obsolete local knowledge. The incomplete chain is not a current accepted epoch, and older incoming messages still follow the explicitly selected live/history verification mode against the accepted room book.

A later tip may supersede an incomplete earlier transfer, but it must not erase what was already authenticated. Earlier signed parts and the earlier tip are retained as anchors at their exact epoch positions. Completing the transfer must demonstrate a single chain through those anchors. An authenticated same-epoch conflict is refused; it is not resolved by arrival time, a larger timestamp, or whichever relay delivered it first.

New invitations can be withdrawn before acceptance. A later owner tip excluding the target replaces the earlier invitation as pending knowledge, and the older join operation becomes stale. A complete withdrawn invitation is visibly marked as withdrawn and cannot be accepted. Its continued presence preserves the newer observation; deleting it without a retained rejection/withdrawal marker would let a replay of the old invitation look new again.

This conservative choice has a usability cost. There is not yet a reviewed decline/dismissal protocol with durable tombstones. Ready invitations and withdrawals occupy the same maximum of eight pending room slots as incomplete transfers. The ninth transfer is refused without evicting earlier entries. An operator must not “fix” that bound by deleting a joined room's pending update and thereby erasing its send fence. The next decline design needs explicit semantics for replay, withdrawal and recovery, not just a close icon.

### 29.4 Recovery preserves incomplete knowledge

The encrypted profile now writes inner format `vibechat-local-profile-v2`, adding `policy_inbox` to the identity, trusted-card and accepted-chain fields. The outer envelope stays `vibechat-profile-envelope-v1`; its identity-bound AEAD and separately derived profile key are unchanged. Readers accept the older inner v1 format where it does not discard already known room or inbox state. No private identity seed is added to the profile.

Profile import validates the candidate cards, accepted chains, pending tips, parts, sizes and anchors before replacing current state. It refuses a profile that loses an accepted room, lowers a known head, drops a pending newer tip, or omits an earlier authenticated intermediate anchor. A complete chain offered through manual import or a different profile is checked against the same pending anchors. A matching final tip alone is not permission to forget a conflicting signed intermediate record retained earlier.

The last point matters across interfaces. A restriction in `policy-open` would be insufficient if a caller could bypass it by importing the equivalent room file. The native and TypeScript implementations now check these anchors before the manual-import state mutation. Native changes also retain their rollback snapshot around profile writes. The worker stages candidate profile state before the final map replacement. The courier, manual room import and profile restore therefore converge on the same local knowledge constraint.

Native receipt commits membership knowledge before publishing event custody in the duplicate index. Otherwise a failed profile write could leave an event marked as already seen while its pending-head fence had been rolled back. That ordering is exercised with a profile-only write failure: no event is published as retained, and retrying the same fragment can commit the pending knowledge and then retain the ciphertext.

The reverse failure has a different outcome. When profile commitment succeeds but writing the ciphertext event fails, the authenticated membership knowledge remains committed. The operation reports the custody failure; retrying the same semantic update can fill in the missing ciphertext record without rolling the head back. These are two files with explicit ordering, not an advertised atomic multi-file transaction. A successful in-memory or profile update must not be relabeled as successful event custody.

Browser modes preserve the previous consent boundary. Memory-only mode does not write a profile. Native mode lets the local endpoint commit its profile. Chosen-directory and IndexedDB modes attempt their encrypted profile saves; a failure remains visible. Download mode requests a profile download rather than certifying disk success. A device restored wholesale to a past snapshot can still lose all knowledge of a later update; a local encrypted profile is not an external monotonic anchor.

### 29.5 Reordering chat around its policy

The browser and terminal can receive a valid authenticated room message before accepting the policy it names. The provider reports the typed error prefix `POLICY_PENDING:` for missing accepted room/epoch coordinates after envelope authentication and bounded content validation. The client holds at most 64 such envelopes in a deferred in-memory map. It neither renders them as chat nor acknowledges them as accepted application records at that stage.

After explicit invitation acceptance, automatic complete update adoption, or manual room import, the client retries deferred envelopes. The retry uses the original live/history mode and verifies the exact signed room, sender and recipient binding again. It does not advance the room merely to make the message decrypt. A message inconsistent with the completed policy is rejected. A still-incomplete one remains bounded and pending.

This is deliberately not durable deferred custody. Closing a memory session can lose its deferred map. Existing connected custodians or an explicit reimport can redeliver the encrypted records, but there is no claim that every pending envelope has already been saved locally. The native terminal also skips ordinary duplicate inventory IDs; restoring only an old profile beside a pre-existing event tree is not automatically a complete application-state replay. Use a fresh chosen recovery store plus profile and explicit ciphertext import when rebuilding from separate artifacts. A future durable deferred queue must preserve why an event was pending and must not grant unverified data the status of accepted history.

### 29.6 A small operational drill

For two browser users, first exchange public cards and verify the full fingerprints through an independently trusted channel. Connect the selected private relay or peer path using the existing connection controls. Alice creates a room containing Alice and Bob, then uses **Send encrypted policy**. Bob opens **Rooms**, inspects the invitation and selects **Accept this invitation**. Neither a copied username nor an ICE credential replaces the public-card check.

Alice can now remove Bob, sign the next epoch, and publish its encrypted policy. Bob's already joined client adopts the complete update and disables outgoing sends for that room. A peer offline during this operation remains unaware until it receives the retained control records. There is no instantaneous global revocation, and old readable messages remain old readable messages.

The terminal equivalent, after starting the ordinary client and selecting a room, uses these commands:

```text
/room-add FULL_BOB_FINGERPRINT
/policy-send
```

Bob inspects and accepts with:

```text
/policy-inbox
/policy-join FULL_ROOM_ID FULL_POLICY_ID
```

Future complete updates to that joined room apply automatically; a new `/policy-join` is not required for every epoch. `/sync` requests the ordinary inventory exchange, not a special unauthenticated policy fetch. Manual signed policy export/import remains useful for deliberate offline handling. Encrypted **Export records** can also move courier records without exposing the decoded membership chain to a third-party transfer channel.

## 30. Historical rev0003 evidence and its change radius

The current test results belong to Relayglass source identities, not to the old Hearthforge counts. The exact component digests and test names are carried in `vibe-evidence`. Some scenarios deliberately run in more than one provider; overlapping scopes should not be added into an impressive but misleading security score.

| Executed scope | Passing checks | What the observation reaches |
|---|---:|---|
| Native core | 19 | Existing identity, PQ envelope and storage contract |
| Native rooms/profiles | 34 | Existing room binding, membership and profile checks |
| Native courier | 64 | New invitation/update state, anchors, bounds, restart and commit ordering |
| Owned-loopback courier transport | 12 | Real WebSocket publisher, TCP recipient, blind relay, offline catch-up and removal |
| Existing native transports | 20 | HTTP endpoint, WebSocket/TCP, explicit federation and storage |
| Interactive terminal | 1 | Actual PTY input, PQ send, retained ciphertext and clean exit |
| Chromium browser lane | 30 | DOM controls with named native adapter, plus actual carried primitive worker |
| Existing worker/native interoperability | 99 | Carried TS/WASM and Node WebCrypto compared with native providers |
| Carried-worker courier | 64 | Actual Node worker RPC, cross-provider controls/profiles and negative cases |
| Carrier exit | 12 | Extract/repack, byte identity, no overwrite, manifest, driver equality and source-impact tooling |

The browser lane separately records its DOM adapter and its actual Chromium primitive-worker execution. It does not claim that a named native adapter is the standalone browser product path. Full secret-holding worker protocol checks use real Node WebCrypto and the compiled carried worker in the interoperability lanes. Ordinary browser navigation, direct WebRTC delivery and the synthetic relay test remain distinct scopes. The available navigation mode is retained in the JSON receipt rather than used as a recurring release-note apology.

The 12 new transport assertions use freshly allocated owned-loopback ports. They exercise a WebSocket sender and a native TCP recipient through a blind relay, an explicit new invitation, chat after acceptance, delivery of retained missed epochs after the recipient disconnects, a pending-head fence, removal and native restart. They do not establish a real browser-to-browser WebRTC path or a commercial TURN service's behavior. Existing transport fixtures retain their own fixed-port sequential-use notes.

The courier provider checks exercise both directions of the worker/native relationship. They include unknown owners, exact-tip joins, nonowner publication, unrelated targets, malformed signatures, reserved control names, wrong channels, duplicate/superseded fragments, inconsistent chains, eight-slot inbox limits, withdrawals before join, persistent pending knowledge, and same-identity profile transfer. Tests of the accepted-chain shortcut cover both manual import and profile import. Native profile-only and event-only write failures distinguish state adoption from custody completion.

Two review findings changed the implementation rather than merely enlarging the report. First, pending intermediate anchors must constrain complete manual/profile imports, not only courier fragments. Second, native policy knowledge must be committed before the received event enters the custody duplicate index. The write-failure tests preserve the intended retry outcome in both ordering directions. The browser harness also received narrower corrections: a counter inside a closed dialog must be tested for attached state, not visibility, and the lock assertion must await the asynchronous return to the identity door rather than inspect it immediately after a click. These are recorded engineering findings, not claims of an independent audit.

The new `impact ID` command helps a future officer choose a relevant lane without pretending to compute all dependencies. It returns the source's current hash, suggested tests, whether a compiler step is required, and whether that hash matches the evidence entry. A match identifies unchanged bytes within the recorded scope; it does not refresh the date or increase the independence of an old receipt. A mismatch is useful information, not permission to overwrite the expected hash and call the change tested.

```bash
bash Vibechat.html impact vibe-native
bash Vibechat.html impact vibe-worker-source
bash Vibechat.html source vibe-courier-tests --start 1 --lines 100
bash Vibechat.html compare PREVIOUS-VIBECHAT.html  # replace with the actual path
bash test.sh --html Vibechat.html --output current-cli cli
bash test.sh --html Vibechat.html --output current-browser browser
bash test.sh --html Vibechat.html --output current-interop interop
bash test.sh --html Vibechat.html --output current-carrier carrier
```

Use a real single path for `compare`; it accepts the known rev0002 and rev0003 manifest inventories and never executes the compared carrier. It reports added, removed and changed members separately. rev0001 and arbitrary donor HTML remain outside that schema. The test driver preserves partial output in a timeout receipt instead of discarding the last useful observation. It does not install a browser, invoke a registry or change host security policy to make a lane look successful.

The release also exercises an unchanged extract/repack and an explicit fresh TypeScript/WASM build in new directories. The reproducibility result is recorded separately from assertion counts. Only `worker.ts` changed among the six compiler inputs; `crypto.ts`, `kdf.ts`, Argon2 C, BLAKE2b C and the WASM header retain the prior edition's bytes. The compiled worker changes with its application state machine; primitive arithmetic is not quietly rewritten under the phrase “policy delivery.”

## 31. Historical rev0003 online research and resulting decisions

Primary-source research during rev0003 revisited authentication, delivery and delayed group-state processing rather than searching for a new library to fetch at runtime. RFC 9750 distinguishes authentication from delivery and places application access-control choices above the generic group protocol. RFC 9420 addresses processing of delayed and reordered traffic. Those distinctions informed the review questions: which key authorizes an update, what state is known before all parts arrive, and what should remain pending? [T26, T27]

The resulting courier and its exact field layout are new Vibechat design choices. They are not an implementation of MLS. The application does not gain MLS forward secrecy, post-compromise security, tree-based group-key agreement or protocol audit coverage from having read its architecture. The chosen model remains a small owner-controlled signed chain over the existing static-identity PQ envelope. A future ratchet needs a separate versioned design and evidence.

Only two hosting entries were freshly rechecked in this turn: Cloudflare Realtime TURN/SFU and Metered Open Relay. The official Cloudflare pricing page still describes a shared first 1,000 GB monthly egress allowance across TURN/SFU, with listed overage of $0.05/GB and other product charges separate. Metered's Open Relay page still advertises 20 GB of free monthly TURN traffic. These are dated provider observations, not a prepaid entitlement promised by this artifact. [R01, R02]

All 37 investigated infrastructure candidates remain in the catalog. The other 35 are retained with their actual earlier review revision, not relabeled as freshly checked. Signaling limits remain different from TURN bandwidth, self-hosted code remains different from a free public service, and a proprietary SDK entry remains an option rather than an installed adapter. No service account was created, no payment accepted, no live ICE credential embedded, and no new hosted dependency selected automatically.

The carried research ledger now has 22 technical references (with preserved historical ID gaps through T27) and a third-edition research note. Research is an officer activity in the current development turn. It is not a recurring task hidden in the end-user HTML, an analytics feed, or a license for chat clients to replace their carried cryptography with remote code. Review the changing provider terms again when a deployment decision actually depends on them.

## 32. Historical rev0003 return point: carry knowledge, not just confidence

Begin with `brief`, `verify`, this current-first account and the exact source you plan to change. The owner's recurring `/run` sentence is sufficient to select a bounded useful continuation; it does not require a new checklist approval for every local test. It also does not authorize a service signup, publication to an external account, or revival of a stopped process just because an old letter mentions it.

The new working baseline is encrypted policy delivery, not manual files alone. Keep the owner signature, explicit new-room acceptance, automatic complete updates to joined rooms, exact recipient rule, pending-head fences, and encrypted profile closure together. A UI-only membership change or a new channel permission label without provider enforcement would be a regression. A “dismiss pending update” button that erases a newer signed tip would be a regression disguised as convenience.

The first recommendation remains independent review of the adapted browser crypto. Comparison vectors and interoperation expose real mistakes but do not replace arithmetic, side-channel, memory-lifetime and protocol analysis. Retain the source and notices, the native alternative and the strict build relationship while that review proceeds. Do not trade the user's no-fetch boundary for an easier import statement.

The next application improvement should make rejection and delivery outcomes usable. An explicit invitation decline needs a bounded durable marker so replay does not reopen it. Withdrawal should be dismissible without erasing what makes the old invitation obsolete. Joined-room pending fences need a recovery path that preserves contradictory signed evidence rather than silently choosing a fork. Plan those cases together before adding a cosmetic inbox close button.

Authenticated adoption and custody receipts are also valuable, but they must say which event, which policy, which identity and what retention scope they attest to. A room owner should be able to distinguish “I offered the update,” “a relay has the ciphertext,” and “Bob's client adopted this exact head.” None of these facts proves that Bob personally read it or that a custodian will retain it forever. Start with a small bounded receipt rather than a global presence service.

Deferred ciphertext currently survives only as long as its in-memory queue or another retained copy. A future durable queue should preserve its pending reason and original live/history mode, reject malformed sources before custody where possible, and retry without inventing new room authority. Recovery from a profile and an event directory needs an explicit application replay account. Restoring a duplicate index is not the same operation as restoring all policy state.

Direct WebRTC evidence, automatic native traversal, high-throughput native provider bindings, streamed attachment work, owner transfer and PQ-protected media remain important but separate directions. Choose one bounded improvement that can be carried and understood. Do not dilute the next turn across a dozen attractive half-features simply because the single-file size budget is generous.

Preserve the letters, constitutions and source arrival guide. Lumen's base and Hyperepo's operational influence remain attributable rather than impersonated. The new impact map is a declared local tool; it is not Lumen's entire dependency atlas. The courier is our application code; it is not a donor feature magically uncovered in an unrelated workbench. That honesty makes inherited machinery more useful, not less.

Update `Vibechat.html`, `BOOTSTRAPROSE.md` and `test.sh` together. Keep the final ZIP to those three regular members, with the next consecutive revision and an actual release minute. A user should receive a working room; another sandperson should receive enough source, reasons and evidence to continue it without the original cloudtainer.

## 34. Quietkeep: a declined invitation stays declined

### 34.1 The chosen task and its exact boundary

The previous handoff recommended a durable invitation-decline mechanism. That is the application work selected under this turn's standing `/run` request. A cosmetic close button would have been insufficient: the courier is explicitly replayable, another peer can retain its ciphertext, and an owner can publish additional epochs. Clearing only a rendered invitation would let the same invitation return. Clearing its pending head would also destroy the knowledge that makes an older invitation obsolete. The implementation therefore changes both providers and encrypted recovery, not just the screen.

The new action is **local decline of an unjoined room**. Its effects are intentionally smaller than revoking membership. It removes that room's transfer from the active invitation/update inbox, records the exact observed owner policy, and retains the signed head and received anchors in a closed collection. The local client will not join this room from a courier replay, a newer owner epoch, or a manual room-file import. An already joined room is outside this operation, including a joined room whose newer policy is incomplete. No close control is offered for those pending updates, and calling the provider operation directly is also refused.

A withdrawal is an owner policy that no longer includes the target. It can arrive before the target ever accepts the original invitation. That state deserves a way out of the active inbox too. The browser labels the corresponding local action **Dismiss withdrawn invitation**. It has the same replay-preserving semantics as decline, rather than deleting the withdrawal and exposing the older invitation again. The client does not tell the owner whether the user dismissed it. This revision sends no new remote rejection message and makes no inference about another human's attention.

There is no expiry timer. A later owner policy remains closed, even if it re-adds the target. There is no automatic decision-history eviction. These defaults are deliberate: an elapsed timer or a memory-budget decision must not silently turn a previous refusal into permission. A user who changes their mind chooses **Review again** from the declined section. That moves the same retained transfer back to the active inbox. It does not complete missing epochs, trust other members, or accept the room. A complete current invitation still requires a separate **Accept this invitation** action.

### 34.2 How the browser presents the choice

Open **Rooms** after receiving an encrypted policy. An unjoined invitation includes the authenticated owner's identity, full room and policy identifiers, observed epoch and transfer progress. A partial invitation can be declined before every intermediate part arrives. The precise wording and progress remain important: the client has an authenticated tip, not necessarily a complete chain. Declining must not make “two of three parts” turn into “three of three” merely because the final tip also exists elsewhere in the transfer record.

The **Declined locally** disclosure is separate from the active inbox. Closed entries remain inspectable; the disclosure is not a deletion confirmation. It shows the newest authenticated head known locally and whether its retained chain is complete. This lets a user see that the owner changed a policy while preserving the original refusal. Replays do not generate an ordinary chat message or reopen the invitation. Other ciphertext custody behavior remains governed by the existing storage consent and quotas.

Every button captures the exact policy and prior local choice token that it displayed. If an owner update arrives before the queued action executes, the provider refuses the stale click. If the user made another local choice first, the old click is refused even if the owner policy did not change. The user reviews the newly displayed state instead of the code silently substituting a newer policy. This keeps the same expected-state discipline already used for room edits and queued sends.

The completion message names storage scope. In memory-only mode it tells the user to export the encrypted profile before locking. Download mode says a download was requested and asks the user to confirm saving. A chosen-directory write and a completed profile database transaction have different messages. Native endpoint saving has its own message because that provider performs its profile write before returning the successful mutation. These messages report completed application steps, not absolute proof against disk failure or user deletion.

### 34.3 The terminal and provider interface

The terminal's `/policy-inbox` output now distinguishes active transfers from declined ones and includes each current choice token. The first decision has no preceding token; the terminal represents that with a dash. Use the full identifiers printed by the current state, not abbreviated fingerprints or a name that may collide.

```text
/policy-inbox
/policy-decline FULL_ROOM_ID FULL_CURRENT_POLICY_ID -
/policy-inbox
/policy-reconsider FULL_ROOM_ID FULL_CURRENT_POLICY_ID FULL_PRIOR_CHOICE_TOKEN
/policy-inbox
/policy-join FULL_ROOM_ID FULL_CURRENT_POLICY_ID
```

The last line is appropriate only after explicit review, complete chain receipt and a current policy that includes this identity. Reconsidering a withdrawal does not convert it into an invitation. An updated policy may require a new exact head before either action. The command descriptions and provider errors preserve this distinction rather than manufacturing a successful join from a convenient terminal shortcut.

The native endpoint and the carried worker accept `policy-decline` and `policy-reconsider`. The request has exactly three fields: `room`, `policy` and `choice`. For the first decline, `choice` is JSON null. For later actions it is the nonce of the most recent local decision for this room. Additional, missing, malformed or stale fields are refused. The result identifies the new local state and token and explicitly reports `local_only: true`. It is not an event suitable for relay distribution.

Both providers implement the authorization checks. The page does not protect a weak provider merely by hiding a button. Direct calls cannot decline a joined room, bypass closed state with a manual policy file, or use an obsolete join click to undo a decline. The new terminal commands use that same provider path. The terminal's actual-PTY regression remains a separate test from the provider-operation tests; command presence alone is not a claim that every new command was exercised through an interactive terminal.

### 34.4 Local decision history and encrypted profile v3

A local decision record belongs to one room and its authenticated, pinned owner. Its ordered steps alternate between `decline` and `review`, starting with decline. A step stores the action, the epoch and full policy ID observed when making it, and a fresh 16-byte random nonce encoded as 32 hexadecimal characters. The nonce is an expected-state token, not a password, signing key, remote capability or proof that a person clicked. It distinguishes different local operations against the same owner policy.

The history remains after reconsideration and after a later explicit join. Otherwise a profile exported during decline could be imported after reconsideration and silently reinstate an old refusal, while an even older profile could erase refusal altogether. The current client accepts a candidate decision history only when the already-known history is an exact prefix. A longer, structurally valid continuation can be restored. A shorter history, missing room, changed earlier nonce or different choice at the same position is refused. The current client does not guess which concurrent branch is more recent from wall-clock time.

The clear document inside the existing authenticated encrypted envelope is now `vibechat-local-profile-v3`. Its fields are exactly:

```text
format
identity
trusted
chains
policy_inbox
policy_declined
policy_choices
```

The outer format remains `vibechat-profile-envelope-v1`, with the existing identity-bound additional data and separately derived profile key. This revision changes application state, not the encryption suite. The `policy_inbox` contains active transfers. `policy_declined` contains closed transfers in the same signed-tip/sparse-parts representation. `policy_choices` contains the local room/owner/steps records. These collections are encrypted together with trusted cards and accepted chains; they are not written into a cookie or a plaintext dismissal database.

Restore verifies the whole candidate before replacing live state. It checks trusted cards, accepted room chains, active transfers, closed transfers, step alternation, nonce structure, epoch bounds, owner consistency and exact policy anchors. A closed transfer requires a matching final decline. A reviewed record requires a retained active transfer or accepted chain. A room cannot be both declined and joined, or both declined and active. A choice cannot float free of the signed policy knowledge it claims to reference. A profile cannot erase a currently known pending tip or intermediate anchor simply because it includes a compatible-looking later head.

Older inner v1 and v2 profiles remain readable on an identity with no conflicting newer knowledge. Compatibility is not authority to downgrade current state. Once this client knows a choice prefix, importing an older profile that lacks it is refused. A fresh client given only an old profile does not magically know that another device later declined an invitation. There is no hardware monotonic counter, external trusted checkpoint or global rollback oracle. The durable record must actually be preserved and brought to the next place where that knowledge matters.

Two independently active devices can extend the same local choice history differently. This revision refuses conflicting branches rather than selecting one by timestamp, last import or lexical order. That is a usability limit with an explicit safety purpose. A future reconciliation tool must show both choices, retained signed anchors and the scope of any deliberate override. Removing this check to make profile import convenient would erase the very boundary this revision implements.

### 34.5 Replays, later policies and sparse knowledge

Declined state still processes authenticated courier records for that room. A repeated event ID may be suppressed by existing ciphertext handling, but that is not the important new guarantee. The owner can encrypt the same policy again, generating a new event ID. The provider recognizes the room's closed disposition and keeps it closed. Newer signed heads update the retained closed transfer without moving it back into the active inbox. Missing parts can arrive out of order and complete that closed transfer, still without joining.

An older valid delivery can be superseded, but authenticated contradictions cannot be discarded merely because their epoch is lower. Known tips and intermediate parts remain exact anchors. A conflicting signed record at an already-known position is refused. This does not solve owner equivocation globally; it preserves the contradiction boundary observed here. The current API refuses rather than offering a fork-resolution interface, and it does not claim to retain every rejected contradictory packet as a new forensic archive.

Reconsideration moves the existing transfer representation, including null missing parts. A local UI action must not fill a missing final part from the separately stored tip and pretend the transfer is complete. That distinction was caught in this turn's review and added to the tests. Ordinary authenticated delivery may contribute records; a choice operation may change disposition only. Exact profile export/import preserves that sparse shape as well as the latest known head.

Room ciphertext for a declined room is refused with the distinct `POLICY_DECLINED:` condition. It does not become a pending-invitation message waiting to appear automatically after reconsideration. The browser removes corresponding entries from its deferred queue when applying the decline. This removes deferred ciphertext references; it is not secure erasure of plaintext from an adversarial endpoint. After review and actual joining, explicitly synchronize or import the retained ciphertext again to request its processing. Copies held by peers or files are not erased by a local decision.

### 34.6 Capacity is part of the contract

The active policy inbox remains capped at eight transfers. A successful decline releases one active slot. Closed rooms and decision histories have a separate cap: at most 32 room decision records, and at most 32 alternating local decisions per room. Complete accepted rooms remain subject to their existing separate room bound. Every signed chain still has its own finite epoch limit. The entire decrypted profile must fit the existing 2 MiB budget.

These are independent constraints, not interchangeable free space. A small closed transfer can still be refused if the decision-room count is full. Reconsideration is refused when all eight active transfer slots are occupied. An attempted thirty-third local decision for one room is refused even if the serialized profile has plenty of bytes left. Nothing is silently evicted to make room. This edition has no reviewed compaction or archive-and-prune command for local choice history, so reaching a bound is a real product limit, not an invitation to edit authenticated state behind the provider's back.

Limits apply in memory-only mode too. Otherwise the worker could accept state that cannot be exported later, or the native endpoint could accept a transition that fails as soon as persistence is enabled. Candidate mutation is checked against the clear profile budget, and validation or budget failure restores the prior maps. The new tests exercise both the per-room history boundary and the separately bounded set of declined rooms. They also verify that a refusal leaves the original state unchanged rather than partially moving a transfer between collections.

### 34.7 Persistence failures: what changes, what remains and what retries

Native mutations stage the trusted cards, accepted chains, active transfers, declined transfers and choice histories. They validate the new state and write the encrypted profile before returning success. A failed profile write rolls those application maps back to their prior values. The snapshot uses an actual deep copy, preserving insertion order as well as nested content. An earlier canonical-JSON snapshot changed contact ordering after a rejected operation; an exact-state test exposed the mismatch, and the snapshot method was corrected.

The worker runs application mutations transactionally with respect to validation and its serialized-profile quota. Its secret-holding process does not itself own the browser's disk API. After the worker returns a successful choice, the browser requests persistence using the selected mode. If that storage operation fails, the worker retains the newly known decision in memory, and the browser reports the failed save instead of claiming durable completion. Export the current encrypted profile or retry the selected store before locking. Rolling back an already learned policy merely to hide a storage error would be a different and potentially dangerous operation.

The browser's courier acceptance path now saves changed policy state before entering the corresponding event into the accepted-event map and custody path. If the profile save fails, the policy remains known in the provider, but the ciphertext is not marked already accepted by the browser. Retrying the same ciphertext can therefore try the profile write again, including when the provider now returns the unchanged closed state. Only successful acceptance enables the normal duplicate shortcut. This is ordering across application steps, not an atomic transaction joining the provider, IndexedDB, downloads, a directory and every remote relay.

For profile database writes the code requests the `strict` durability hint and waits for transaction completion, not just the request's success callback. Abort after request success rejects the promise. The chosen-directory branch waits for the writer to close. Download mode cannot establish that the user accepted or retained the downloaded file, and memory mode deliberately does no persistent write. The specification-informed choice of a stricter hint is documented in [T29]; the seven new browser function units use synthetic collaborators and do not pretend to reproduce physical disk failure.

## 36. Historical rev0004 online research, kept separate from application invention

This turn reviewed the primary Matrix client-server specification's distinction between invitations, joined membership and rejecting an invitation. Matrix represents rejection through its membership-event model. Vibechat's new operation deliberately does something smaller: it is local encrypted profile state and does not send a server membership event. The source sharpened the question “what does rejection mean here?”; it did not supply a compatible protocol or authorize calling Vibechat a Matrix client. [T28]

The other directly applied primary reference was the W3C IndexedDB 3.0 transaction lifecycle and durability guidance, retrieved as the Working Draft dated 13 August 2025. Request success and transaction completion are different steps. The strict hint prioritizes persistence confidence over the cheaper relaxed path, with performance and power costs. This revision uses the stricter request for profiles, whose choice and membership knowledge should not be treated like a disposable cache. Actual application outcome messages still distinguish browser transaction completion from downloaded files and native endpoint writes. [T29]

Those references are not experimental results for this application. The choice-prefix format, alternating local history, exact prior-token operation, sparse closed transfers and profile rollback rules are new Vibechat design decisions. Their support comes from the implemented checks and stated assumptions, not from treating a standards citation as an audit. The browser ordering units test the code with fake storage collaborators; the specification explains the API contract they are modeling.

R01 and R02 were freshly rechecked against their official pages. Cloudflare's Realtime pricing page lists the first 1,000 GB of monthly egress free, shared by SFU and TURN, then $0.05 per GB; associated Workers and other products have separate pricing. Metered Open Relay advertises 20 GB of TURN usage free each month and requires account-issued configuration. These observations are dated provider terms, not a guarantee of free permanent hosting. The current HTML adds no account setup, API key, SDK adapter or automatic TURN selection. [R01, R02]

All 37 investigated infrastructure options remain carried. The other 35 retain their actual previous review revision. Metered's signaling option remains separate from its TURN option, and a public STUN service, SDK, free trial and self-hosted server are still different categories. Do not refresh a whole catalog's timestamp because two shortlist entries were read again. The technical ledger now has 24 retained references with its historical ID gaps preserved through T29.

Online research is an officer task during each authorized development turn. It is not end-user telemetry, a dependency loader, a hidden recurring automation or permission to replace embedded crypto after a remote update. A future officer should reopen the relevant primary sources before making a temporally sensitive dependency, provider or protocol decision, and preserve the previous observation as history where it matters. External account creation, spending and publication still require their own user authorization.

## 37. Return point for the next officer: make the outcome answerable

Start from the current three files and their actual source identities. Read the arrival guide, current briefing, C25/C26 and the Quietkeep design chapter. Use `brief`, `verify`, `impact` and the bounded source tools before choosing work. The owner's repeated `/run` phrase is enough to select a useful bounded local continuation; it is not authority to provision a provider account, disregard a refusal, publish to an external repository or restart a historical stopped operation.

The application's new baseline includes durable local invitation choices when profile saving completes. Do not reintroduce a cosmetic dismissal path outside the provider. Do not auto-expire a declined room when a new epoch arrives. Do not drop a local decision prefix on reconsideration or joining. Do not fill null policy parts during a UI action. A current joined-room pending update remains knowledge, not an invitation that can be declined. Keep those invariants together when changing storage or the room editor.

The recommended next application slice is a narrow **authenticated policy-adoption receipt**. It should identify the exact policy, responding identity and outcome that the client is entitled to attest to. Bind it to the appropriate room and recipient; validate it before changing an owner's delivery display. Decide whether it says “this client has adopted this exact head” or “this identity explicitly accepted a new invitation,” and do not mix those meanings. It should not assert that a human read a message, that another peer is continuously online, or that ciphertext will be retained forever.

Receipt emission needs a persistence boundary. Sending an adoption receipt before the corresponding profile commit could let a receiver believe an update survives restart when it does not. Memory-only operation needs a distinct scope or a refusal to claim durable adoption. A replayed receipt should not inflate counters; an old receipt should not certify a newer policy. A recipient removed by a later known policy is still a historical actor, but its old acknowledgement cannot settle the new membership. Design those cases before adding an “everyone synced” badge.

Independent review of the locally adapted browser crypto remains important. Keep exact sources, notices, the native alternative and interoperability vectors available. This turn intentionally did not modify primitive arithmetic or claim a new audit. A proper next review can be a bounded source comparison with testable findings, but it must be attributed to the actual reviewer and scope. A self-review in a new assistant turn is useful work; it is not an independent external cryptographic assessment by renaming it.

Durable deferred-ciphertext recovery is another separate candidate. The current queue is bounded and in memory; decline removes matching entries so reconsideration cannot silently resurrect their display. A future persistent queue needs explicit pending reasons, original history/live processing intent, identity binding, quota behavior and retry ordering. Keep accepted ciphertext custody separate from the authority needed to display or send in a room. A recovered duplicate index is not a recovered membership decision.

The bounded local choice history also needs an eventual usability path when full. Any compaction or reconciliation proposal must retain enough evidence to prevent old profiles and replay from reversing a stop. A reviewed explicit reset with a clearly stated rollback boundary would be different from silent eviction. Concurrent device choices currently fork and are refused; an operator-facing explanation or export of competing branches may be useful before a merge algorithm. Do not let a timestamp become a substitute for authority.

Performance work should begin with measured paths. The worker keeps key derivation off the main UI thread, existing per-message work remains bounded, and this revision avoids unnecessary native profile writes for unchanged controls. It does not replace native OpenSSL subprocesses with a high-throughput binding, stream multi-megabyte files or establish a new real-network throughput result. The generous carrier budget permits retained sources and diagnostics, not careless hot-path work or fabricated speed comparisons.

Keep the two doors distinct. A person opening the page should find their room and clear choices. A sandperson opening source should find the constitution, source map, tests, research and prior conversation without depending on this cloudtainer. The 13 exact donor records and seven earlier letters are still preserved. The additional letter owns this turn's implementation choices and mistakes. Historical absence of a feature is not a current defect merely because its original sentence remains in an attributed letter.

Update all three canonical files, research online, execute the relevant lanes and return one named ZIP containing exactly those three regular members. Preserve intermediate completed test output when a run is interrupted, but only a completed final receipt supports a completed-lane claim. The final handoff should name the implemented change, the important product boundary and the next useful decision. It need not apologize for tools that are not present, and it must not imply work was done outside the observed scope.

## 39. rev0005 design: an adoption receipt names one exact policy, and nothing larger

The next bounded product question from rev0004 was whether a room owner could learn that another named client had actually adopted one exact signed membership state. The result is intentionally narrower than the familiar colored checkmark in a consumer messenger. Vibechat’s new receipt means:

> The client authenticated as member **M** says it has adopted owner **O**’s exact signed policy **P**, at epoch **E**, for room **R**, in the stated local scope.

Every noun in that sentence is part of the claim. A receipt without the room is too broad. A receipt without the policy identity could float forward over later membership changes. A receipt without the epoch is difficult to compare with pending or removed-member state. A receipt without the member identity could be confused with transport custody by a relay. A receipt without scope could make session memory look like a successfully written encrypted profile. The protocol therefore carries all of them.

The reserved application channel is `_room_receipt`. Its body is a versioned object with the following fields:

```json
{
  "type": "policy-adoption",
  "v": 1,
  "room": "32 hexadecimal characters",
  "owner": "64 hexadecimal characters",
  "member": "64 hexadecimal characters",
  "epoch": 3,
  "policy": "64 hexadecimal characters",
  "scope": "session or profile"
}
```

The body is not transported as an exposed JSON control frame. It is sealed inside the same post-quantum envelope used for room records, on the reserved receipt channel, with exactly the owner and member as recipients. The sender’s ML-DSA identity authenticates the envelope; ML-KEM wraps the message secret independently for the two recipients. A blind relay can retain the resulting ciphertext without becoming the authority that issued or adopted the policy.

The receipt parser refuses a payload whose `member` differs from the authenticated outer sender. It refuses an owner mismatch, an unknown room, an unknown policy, an invented future epoch, a wrong channel, an outsider who is only pinned, or a receipt whose policy is not in the accepted signed chain. A room named `_room_receipt` is also refused so ordinary application data cannot acquire control semantics through a name collision. These checks do not prove the client software is benevolent or uncompromised. They do prevent several much cheaper ambiguities inside the implemented protocol.

### 39.1 “Adopted” is not “read”

The word **adopted** is about the client’s active room-policy state. It does not say that a human opened the Rooms panel, read every member fingerprint, understood a policy, agreed with an owner, approved any message, or consented to any future policy. It does not say that the identity is online now. It does not say that the device will remain available. It does not say that a relay delivered every chat record. It does not say that the member has read a room message.

This separation is not etiquette around an otherwise broad technical claim; it is part of the wire contract. The UI labels the record as a **client adoption claim**. The workshop command prints the nonclaims. The constitution now carries the same boundary. Future officers should resist compressing it into “Bob read the update” or “everyone is synced.” Those phrases silently add human, liveness and global-freshness semantics that the event does not establish.

The primary-source comparison this turn reinforced that choice. XMPP XEP-0184 explicitly says a delivery receipt reports delivery to a client, not that a human read or understood the message, and warns that absence of a receipt is ambiguous. Matrix read receipts have intentionally different semantics: clients send them with some confidence that an event was displayed, and the receipt stream is ephemeral state outside Matrix’s event graph. MLS calls each committed group state an epoch, but Vibechat does not implement MLS and inherits none of its ratchet guarantees. We borrow one discipline from the comparison: an acknowledgement of group state should identify one exact state, not a floating room label.

### 39.2 Compact state, not an applause counter

For an owner, the stored view is keyed by `(room, member)`. A newer valid adoption replaces the earlier current one for that pair. Replaying the exact event does nothing. Encrypting the same semantic claim again with fresh randomness also does not increase a counter. A `session` claim may be upgraded by a later exact-head `profile` claim. A `profile` claim cannot be downgraded by a later session claim. An older epoch cannot replace a newer one.

This is why the interface shows exact epoch and policy identity rather than “three receipts.” A count can be useful as a summary, but it should not reward duplicate delivery or turn retransmission into evidence of more people. The compact index is also bounded. It does not retain every historical receipt ciphertext as active UI state, although a user-owned ciphertext store may still contain those events. The distinction is the same custody/state distinction used elsewhere: encrypted records can be retained without every record becoming the current application claim.

The following paths are now available:

```text
Browser Rooms panel: Send current adoption claim
Terminal: /policy-adopt [FULL_ROOM_ID]
Terminal: /policy-receipts
Workshop: bash Vibechat.html receipts
```

The workshop command is deliberately usable while locked. It prints the payload, scope, replay rule, command surface and nonclaims without asking an officer to reverse-engineer minified browser behavior. It is a protocol description, not a live network test or independent audit.

### 39.3 Removal is still a policy a previous member can authenticate

A removal update creates an important edge case. Once Bob is removed, Bob is no longer a current recipient for ordinary room traffic. But Bob may still receive and authenticate the owner-signed removal policy through the courier path designed for former members. Bob’s client may then attest that it adopted that exact removal head. The owner can index the receipt with `member_current: false`.

That event does not restore Bob. It does not grant Bob permission to send. It does not allow Bob to decrypt later room messages. It records the exact boundary Bob’s client says it learned. The transport suite exercises invitation, adoption, room chat, removal and removed-member adoption across an owned loopback WebSocket/TCP relay. After restart, the owner recovers the compact exact-head claim from its encrypted profile and the removed member remains fenced from sending.

An old receipt cannot certify a later re-addition. If the owner later creates a new epoch that includes Bob again, Bob must adopt and attest to that new exact policy. This keeps historical participation and current membership from collapsing into one boolean.

### 39.4 Publication, custody, adoption and reading remain different states

The project now has several words that look similar in a status panel but carry different evidence:

| State | What is established | What is not established |
|---|---|---|
| Offered | The owner prepared encrypted policy events for a selected pinned link | Relay custody, recipient processing, joining |
| Retained | A relay or local ciphertext store accepted the exact encrypted record | Decryption, policy validation, adoption |
| Ready invitation | A pinned recipient authenticated enough signed chain material to review a new-room invitation | Membership or acceptance |
| Joined/adopted locally | The recipient accepted or automatically advanced a complete valid chain into active room state | Profile durability unless the selected mode committed it |
| Adoption receipt sent | The member client sealed an exact-head statement in session or profile scope | Owner receipt, reading, liveness |
| Adoption receipt indexed | The owner authenticated and compactly stored that member’s exact-head statement | Human approval or global convergence |
| Message displayed/read | Not represented by this protocol | Everything a consumer read receipt might suggest |

That table belongs in the current operating account because product language is part of protocol safety. A future interface may choose better labels, but it should not merge rows merely to look familiar.

## 40. Encrypted profile v4 and the ordering of a durable claim

Profile v4 extends the existing encrypted recovery object. It still carries verified contact cards, signed room chains, pending policy heads, declined invitation records and local decision prefixes. It now also carries the compact policy-receipt summaries. The profile remains encrypted to keys derived from the local identity passphrase and recovery salt. Plaintext contact names and room policy bodies are not written into the wrapper.

The important change is not the version number. It is the rule for the `profile` scope: the client must not seal a profile-scoped adoption claim until the selected profile persistence operation has succeeded. Otherwise a peer could receive a statement that claims durable local adoption while the sender has only changed volatile memory.

In the native provider, the application operation takes a snapshot of receipt and policy state, validates the event, updates the compact index, writes the profile where appropriate, and restores the previous application state if that profile write fails. Ciphertext custody is still a separate write. If profile state commits and the later ciphertext-file write fails, the application retains the learned policy knowledge and may retry the missing event custody; it does not erase the accepted membership change merely to pretend the two stores were one transaction.

In the browser route, `persistProfile()` completes before a received policy or receipt event is added to the accepted-ciphertext duplicate index. A failed profile save leaves the event retryable. Replaying an unchanged policy or exact-head receipt attempts the save again. Only after the state commit succeeds does duplicate suppression turn the repeated event into a no-op. The IndexedDB helper requests strict durability and waits for transaction completion, not just request success. Those are useful ordering properties, not proof against browser eviction, device loss, disk-controller failure, user deletion or an attacker rolling back the entire storage origin.

The browser test lane now includes exact-function units for this ordering. They use the carried `accept` and `idbProfile` functions in Chromium with deliberately synthetic provider, persistence and IDB collaborators. They exercise failure before ciphertext acceptance, retry after unchanged semantic state, successful commit, duplicate shortcut activation, transaction completion and abort after request success. The test labels call them synthetic; they are not disguised physical-disk fault injection.

### 40.1 Session scope is honest rather than second-class

Memory-only and download-oriented modes cannot truthfully claim that a profile was durably updated merely because an event exists in memory. Their automatic receipt scope is therefore `session`. The member may still send a valid exact-head statement, and the owner may still display it, but the scope remains visible.

Directory, native endpoint and IndexedDB modes can use `profile` only after the profile operation succeeds. A user can later upgrade the same exact head from session to profile. The owner’s compact index accepts that one-way strengthening. A later session statement cannot erase it.

This is not a universal hierarchy in which profile always means “safer.” A profile can be copied, deleted or rolled back outside the application. The scope names the local commit the implementation observed. It is not a warranty about future survival.

### 40.2 Rollback and omission checks now include receipt state

An older encrypted profile cannot silently discard a newer known adoption receipt. A profile cannot omit a known receipt while retaining the rest of the room. It cannot replace profile scope with session scope for the same head. It cannot contain duplicate `(room, member)` entries, and each receipt summary must retain a real policy anchor in the imported signed chain.

These checks deliberately make some multi-device merges refuse rather than guess. If two devices have incomparable current statements, a timestamp is not accepted as authority to erase one. The project still lacks a trusted monotonic storage service or a complete multi-device merge protocol. Refusal preserves the disagreement for an explicit future design instead of using wall-clock recency as a quiet policy decision.

The same principle applies to earlier invitation choices. Profile v4 is backward-readable where the existing migration rules allow it, but importing an old profile into a client that already knows a later decline, reconsideration, pending head or receipt cannot make the client forget the stronger local knowledge. Recovery is an attempt to restore evidence, not permission to resurrect an old state over a newer stop.

## 41. Online research and donor machinery reviewed in this turn

The constitution requires online research every turn. This turn did not use web research as decorative confirmation after implementation. It used primary protocol and current provider sources to define the receipt boundary and to recheck one concrete WebRTC infrastructure option.

### 41.1 Protocol sources

**RFC 9420 — The Messaging Layer Security Protocol.** The group evolves through committed state transitions called epochs. Vibechat does not implement MLS, TreeKEM, its proposal/commit processing or its post-compromise guarantees. The useful comparison is structural: one state acknowledgement should identify one exact epoch and group state. URL retained in the research catalog: `https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9420.html`.

**XEP-0184 — Message Delivery Receipts.** The stable XMPP extension distinguishes client delivery from human reading or understanding, warns that missing receipts have many possible causes, prohibits receipt-request loops, and requires exact message IDs. Vibechat’s event is not XMPP-compatible and has narrower semantics: exact policy adoption rather than generic message delivery. The cautions about nonreading, ambiguous absence and loop prevention are directly useful. URL: `https://xmpp.org/extensions/xep-0184.html`.

**Matrix Client-Server API v1.13 — `m.receipt`.** Matrix read receipts are ephemeral deltas keyed by event and user. The client behavior deliberately asks for some certainty of display. The security considerations state that receipt contents are outside the event graph and do not receive its integrity checks. Vibechat does not reuse `m.read`; its policy statement is part of the authenticated PQ envelope and anchored to its own signed policy chain. URL: `https://spec.matrix.org/v1.13/client-server-api/`.

These comparisons also explain a deliberate omission. The current protocol does not infer a negative result from silence. No receipt might mean unsupported software, offline transport, refused receipt, lost event, failed profile commit or a client that has not adopted the head. The owner may show “no claim received,” but should not translate that into “member rejected” or “member is stale” without a different protocol.

### 41.2 Managed TURN/SFU recheck

Cloudflare Realtime was rechecked against its current primary documentation. The pricing page says the SFU and TURN services share the first 1,000 GB of monthly egress free, with listed egress after that at $0.05 per GB. This is one shared allowance, not two. The TURN documentation exposes standard STUN/TURN URLs and alternate ports. Credential documentation says the long-term TURN key belongs on a backend and clients should receive expiring credentials. The FAQ documents a maximum credential expiry of 48 hours.

That makes Cloudflare a plausible managed option for a group this small, but not a secret that can be embedded in `Vibechat.html`. A future integration needs a local or federated credential issuer, explicit account configuration and a clear cost boundary. This revision creates no Cloudflare account, sends no API request, stores no provider key and adds no runtime dependency. The research catalog retains all 37 investigated infrastructure options rather than promoting the rechecked one into an unearned default.

Current pages retained in the research record:

The Lumen carrier’s arrival guide remains a model for the first duty of a visiting sandperson: inspect before executing, name editable source separately from generated projection, use no-clobber extraction, and treat hashes as byte identity rather than external signature or authority. Its Source Glass and Carrier Clinic make exact source and verification boundaries findable without putting the workshop across the reader’s doorway. Its Change Radius and impact-oriented tools make a useful precedent for naming affected evidence lanes rather than claiming dependency completeness.

Hyperepo reinforces a related operating discipline. Current canonical source should be distinguished from retained ancestry. A stale plan or old receipt is not fresh authority. Private roots should be explicit. Nonces and output destinations should be named. Absent output is safer than silent overwrite. A successful operation should leave enough machine-readable evidence to be checked from a fresh directory.

The implementation taken from those ideas in rev0005 is concrete:
