## 168. Steadypost — one explicit authority send, exact resume, local finish

### 168.1. Chosen slice and frozen boundaries

The previous handoff delivered existing-account continuity and an explicit local outbox/inbox projection. The remaining manual sequence exported an intent, separately invoked authority decision, moved its exact result, imported it at the recipient and then committed locally. Steadypost places a bounded controller around the **authority request/result portion** of that sequence. It starts with a Pinpost recipient that already authenticated the actual Plainpost text and completed `account-bind` against the exact creation-only authority origin.

`native_dispatch.py` is the implementation, `native_dispatch_checks.py` is the owned-loopback corpus, and `native_dispatch_memorandum.json` describes the selection, journal, commands, boundaries and source bindings. They are carried as `vibe-native-dispatch`, `vibe-native-dispatch-tests` and `vibe-native-dispatch-memorandum`. `dispatches` is the bounded workshop summary/full-memorandum entry point; `dispatch` is a separate development lane. Extraction, comparison, impact mapping, manifest sealing and carrier checks recognize all three.

The implementation imports the existing account bridge, original text recipient and frozen authority verifier. It neither copies their code into a new implementation nor changes their signed formats. This is still one pairwise text per creation-only role selection, not a reusable installation registry or general chat queue. Existing `account-*`, `message-*`, `isle-lab-*` and `decision-lab-*` routes remain inspectable recovery tools. Deliberately running an older route is not prohibited by the new local marker, and holding existing role keys is not transformed into an account-password-protected keystore.

All new CLI entry points use the same original public account card, encrypted profile, full pinned contact and hidden/pipe unlock as Pinpost. A full selected account/contact guard runs under the role lock before opening the original recipient. The caller retains the cooperative role lock and original recipient advisory lock for the controller lifetime. No remote signing service, profile modification, account-key directory export or hostile-process confinement is implied.

### 168.2. Exact command meanings

| Command | Local/network effect | What it does not mean |
|---|---|---|
| `dispatch-status` | Authenticates selected account and retained local state; reports preparation, pending intent, permission, commit and acknowledgement separately. | No socket, new intent or claim that no other path sent anything. Reopening can reconcile an inherited local anchor. |
| `dispatch-send` | Creates/retains the existing immutable intent if absent, pins one selected endpoint in an encrypted journal, persists possible-send evidence, performs one POST, retains the verified exact reply and imports permission. | No sender-to-recipient delivery, local application commit, automatic retry, new listener or acknowledgement. |
| `dispatch-resume` | Imports retained verified response offline, returns existing local permission, or repeats the exact pending request with explicit URL/capability. | No new write identity, renewed intent window, replacement port or switch from a pending read to a write. |
| `dispatch-recover` | After a retained attempt, explicitly signs a bounded read proof for the original intent and asks for its exact terminal result. | Missing results cannot create work. The changing read proof does not change the original write intent. |
| `dispatch-finish` | Imports an available retained result, invokes the original local transaction, retains postcommit acknowledgement and exports its exact bytes. | No authority contact, extra inbox transaction, plaintext export, delivery to sender or human-reading claim. |

`--experimental` remains explicit. A success view records `network_attempts_this_call`, `application_admissions`, the original and pending request digests, the retained local phase and acknowledgement presence. Transport state and local application state are independent fields; retained authority permission can coexist with zero local application admissions. Exports require an absent destination. Repeating finish with another absent output exports the same retained acknowledgement, without another application admission.

The controller journal bounds attempts at sixteen. The budget covers retained attempts, including a process exit after retention but before its first socket. An exhausted budget stops rather than deleting history or constructing a different operation. A verified result may still be imported through the frozen explicit recovery tools and completed locally. Do not clear the journal to make an uncertain operation look new.

### 168.3. Network selection, response verification and uncertainty

The selected URL has exactly one accepted shape: `http://127.0.0.1:PORT/v1/order`, with a canonical decimal port from 1 through 65535. Schemes, hostnames, user information, alternate paths, query strings, fragments and noncanonical ports are refused before a new selection is created. A later call cannot silently change the selected URL, including when the result is already cached. Restart the authority on the selected port or use an explicitly verified file-mediated recovery route; automatic relocation is not implemented.

The caller supplies a private regular capability file for each actual network call. Its bounded ASCII token is sent only in the existing authorization header, not a URL, journal, ordinary status or result file. The code uses a direct `http.client.HTTPConnection` for one request and closes it afterward. There is no redirect handler, environment proxy discovery, connection-pool retry policy or scheduler. The response must be status 200 with one exact JSON content type, a single positive bounded Content-Length, and no content or transfer coding. The full bounded body must arrive; the original signed Decisionglass response verifier, not HTTP status, decides whether those exact bytes match the selected intent.

Before the first socket, the encrypted journal has already retained the pending request and a consecutive attempt digest. A connection error does not erase that evidence. After a socket attempt, unsigned errors, malformed JSON, an invalid signature, a truncated result, a redirect, ambiguous framing, or inability to retain/apply an observed result all remain uncertainty. No untrusted HTTP detail or capability is echoed in the diagnostic. The CLI returns exit 75 for a sent-uncertain or mutated-review state, and never reports successful cancellation. A missing response is not evidence that the authority did not commit.

An authenticated response is saved as its original canonical bytes before being passed to the original recipient. Thus interruption can leave a real authority decision without a local response, a retained local response without imported permission, or imported permission without local commitment. Each case has a different explicit recovery. Once permission or a verified response genuinely exists locally, resume needs neither the authority nor its capability. Missing a terminal response to a read remains uncertainty: the controller does not transform that failed read into a commit request.

Fifteen seconds is the timeout supplied to blocking socket operations, not a hard end-to-end elapsed deadline. Message size, request size, response size, operation identity and retained attempt count are bounded, but this version is not a hard-total-deadline transport. Holding a local operation lock while a selected peer responds slowly is a usability/availability boundary, not a claim of hardened public-service behavior.

### 168.4. The transport journal is evidence, not another application store

`native-dispatch.selected.json` identifies the selected local binding; `native-dispatch.sealed.json` holds the encrypted transport state. Binding covers original account/contact, role, recipient database identity, exact preparation, complete bundle and authority origin. The journal key is HMAC-SHA256-derived from the existing recipient storage key with a distinct domain and exact binding; AES-256-GCM uses that binding as associated data and a fresh random nonce on each publication. This adds no new user/authority-signed wire record.

The state contains the immutable original commit request, pending exact request, endpoint, at most sixteen request-digest/kind entries and an optional exact verified response. It does not copy the application entry, active root, message text or HTTP capability into a second inbox. The original recipient SQLite database remains the sole application settlement owner. No transaction across that database, authority database and sidecar is claimed.

Existing private atomic replacement writes and synchronizes the candidate file and parent directory before the controller adopts candidate state in memory. A mutation failure invalidates the controller, requiring close/reopen. Review extended that rule to **selection-marker publication**, so a trusted direct caller cannot keep using a partially initialized handle merely because the CLI context manager would normally close it. The exact recipient intent may already have been retained before a marker error; it is not silently discarded or renewed.

A marker without a journal, or a journal without its marker, refuses explicit review. Invalid authenticated content, changed selection, changed original intent, inconsistent attempt sequence and an altered final attempt digest also refuse. These checks are not independent freshness. Restoring a complete earlier authenticated journal may remove evidence of a later attempt. The corpus intentionally demonstrates that valid restoration and then replays the same immutable intent, obtaining the same authority decision rather than another event. Status retains `external_sends: unknown`; even an absent controller journal does not establish that an original file-mediated command never sent anything.

The original recipient's signed local anchor continues to provide its own scoped rollback contradiction when later observations survive. It does not make this sidecar a new independent witness. Joint rollback, secure erasure, independent administrative isolation and physical-power-loss qualification are not established. A private key file under the same user remains accessible to that user, and account unlock requirements on the new route do not retrofit an anti-downgrade policy onto predecessor tools.

### 168.5. Consent, cutover, abandonment and recovery

The existing policy remains `authority-decision-first/exact-settlement/v1`. An exact commit decision ordered first permits only that authenticated retained preparation to finish later, including after original request windows or a later requester cutover. An abort or requester cutover ordered first prevents an undecided commit. Local abandonment can decline completion after permission, but it cannot cancel the remote decision, recycle a reserved prekey or erase older encrypted preparations.

The controller does not manufacture new cancellation semantics from unsigned error responses. A valid signed abort recovered with the recipient's original abort witness is a terminal refusal, not commitment. A remote cutover that causes an unsigned HTTP refusal is not presented as a new authenticated cutover observation; use the existing signed-history mechanisms to establish that knowledge. Original recipient history/fork/abandonment gates remain authoritative at local finish.

The recovery command signs only a bounded proof asking to read the exact original terminal result. It can operate after the original intent deadline while the recipient device authorization still permits the read. Resume after an unsuccessful read repeats that pending read byte-for-byte; it cannot quietly return to a commit. Preparation, retained permission, local commitment and acknowledgement remain separate durable facts, and none alone proves sender delivery or human reading.

### 168.6. Practical shell workflow

Use section **166.7** to prepare the original account cards/profiles, select the already-pinned peers and perform separate-role setup **through `account-bind`**. Do not run the older manual `message-request → isle-lab-decide → message-accept` sequence as well merely to make the controller's status change. Initial setup remains explicit and the signed session has its original short window; an expired undecided preparation is a refusal, not permission to renew an uncertain request.

Reuse that section's public shell variables `H`, `A`, `R`, `PUB` and `RBASE`. The recipient array contains `--experimental`, its exact role directory, original card/profile and full sender fingerprint, never a passphrase. Commands prompt with echo disabled, or a trusted supervisor supplies an inherited private pipe. Include the original recovery-salt prompt option when needed.

In an authority terminal, deliberately start the **existing** listener:

```bash
bash "$H" decision-lab-serve --directory "$A" --port 0 \
  --ready-file "$PUB/authority-ready.json"
```

The ready record publishes a loopback URL and capability **file location**, not the capability. Have the authority operator explicitly delegate the private token to the recipient through a suitable local private file. `CAP` below names that delegated file; it is not an invitation to pass the authority's private directory or keys to the recipient. In the synthetic same-host exercise, the test supervisor deliberately performs that one token copy. No new automated capability distribution is claimed.

In the recipient terminal, set public `URL` to the exact ready URL and `CAP` to the explicitly delegated private file path:

```bash
bash "$H" dispatch-status "${RBASE[@]}"
bash "$H" dispatch-send "${RBASE[@]}" --url "$URL" --capability-file "$CAP"
bash "$H" dispatch-status "${RBASE[@]}"
```

Successful sending here means exact authority permission was retained and imported; it must still report zero application admissions. A timeout, interrupted process or exit 75 is not successful cancellation. For an uncertain operation, explicitly choose one of these alternatives, not both as an automatic fallback chain:

```bash
# Same pending request and same original intent; one explicit attempt.
bash "$H" dispatch-resume "${RBASE[@]}" --url "$URL" --capability-file "$CAP"

# A separately signed read proof for the same original terminal result only.
bash "$H" dispatch-recover "${RBASE[@]}" --url "$URL" --capability-file "$CAP"
```

Once the verified result or local decision is retained, the following resume is offline and needs neither flag. Finish is a separate consent to local persistence, and acknowledgement export is not its transmission to the sender:

```bash
bash "$H" dispatch-resume "${RBASE[@]}"
bash "$H" dispatch-finish "${RBASE[@]}" --output "$PUB/ack.json"
bash "$H" dispatch-finish "${RBASE[@]}" --output "$PUB/ack-again.json"
cmp "$PUB/ack.json" "$PUB/ack-again.json"
bash "$H" dispatch-status "${RBASE[@]}"
bash "$H" account-mailbox "${RBASE[@]}"

# Explicit plaintext disclosure from the already committed application entry.
bash "$H" message-read --experimental --directory "$R"
```

Every output path must be absent; choose another absent path to re-export exact bytes. The authority's port must remain the one selected for a further network attempt. The actual-shell execution in section 169 uses real wall time, stops the authority, removes sender/authority directories and the delegated capability **before local recipient commit**, then proves offline resume and identical acknowledgement recovery. It does not depend on fixture clock injection or a shared all-key setup process for role-key generation.

### 168.7. Research reviewed this turn

Four primary-source records, T175–T178, were added without removing or relabeling previous research or any of the 37 infrastructure options. They are interpretation inputs, not external endorsements of Vibechat.

**T175 — RFC 9110, HTTP Semantics, §9.2.2.** https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html . The specification distinguishes idempotent-method semantics and circumstances under which retry is justified. Application here: explicit recovery must preserve the frozen operation's exact semantics; an unsigned error or missing response is not proof that a non-idempotent action never happened. The controller deliberately offers no blind automatic retry. The RFC does not validate our signatures, persistence or selected-operation implementation.

**T176 — Python 3.13 `http.client`.** https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/http.client.html . The documented connection/request/response interface supports a direct selected HTTP exchange and explicit close. Application here: one exact bounded POST, explicit response framing checks and no proxy/redirect layer. The configured timeout is not represented as a hard total elapsed bound. The live documentation may carry a later patch-level heading than the observed interpreter; no runtime upgrade is inferred from reading it.

**T177 — Python 3.13 `os.fsync`.** https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/os.html#os.fsync . The documentation explains synchronization of an open file descriptor and the need to flush buffered file objects. Application here: reuse the existing private file publication and directory synchronization machinery, then adopt memory. This is not an independent rollback witness, hardware qualification or proof that every filesystem honors identical persistence guarantees.

**T178 — SQLite 3.51.3 release record, March 13, 2026.** https://www.sqlite.org/releaselog/3_51_3.html . The official release records the WAL-reset fix. This turn does not patch or replace the observed SQLite 3.46.1 runtime or claim a supported pinned closure. A fixed supported build/backport remains a deployment prerequisite. No reproduction of an engine vulnerability is part of these tests.

### 168.8. Review findings and rejected/incomplete exercises

The development source probe first passed a real account-bound send, retained permission with zero local admissions, offline resume and explicit local finish. It was a development probe, not final-carrier evidence.

An initial source-corpus invocation was interrupted by the tool-call execution bound after partial checks. A second invocation found a test-instrumentation bug: its network guard read `sys.argv` after the tested CLI had replaced that list, accidentally disallowing the selected owned loopback port. The guard now captures the allowed port before invoking the CLI. A subsequent source run passed the crash paths but attempted an immediate same-port restart of the intentionally non-reusing authority listener. The test now changes its owned reply fault in the same server process rather than weakening production socket reuse policy.

The next accumulated source run failed its expected post-commit assertion after the original two-minute text fixture window had elapsed; inspection showed that the corpus was still requesting fresh intents from that expired preparation. Repeated adversarial scenarios now retain an explicit authorized test-time snapshot, including paired authority/recipient clocks; the expired-intent read-recovery case explicitly advances it. Setup and the actual Bash happy path use real time. No production deadline, signed record or verification rule was widened to make a long corpus pass. Development invocations spanning source edits are exploratory only and are not relabeled fixed-carrier results.

Direct-call review found that an exception publishing the initial selection marker should invalidate the controller just as a later journal-write failure does. Initialization now fences its handle on such failure, and the new corpus injects that specific error. A separate budget test proves refusal before capability read or socket when all sixteen retained attempts are used.

The first assembly attempt inserted new script placeholders at a matching string inside the launcher's routing regular expression instead of at the anchored source block. Repacking refused the resulting duplicate/missing inventory before emitting a carrier. The assembler was corrected to use the actual line-anchored block. The inventory and closing-script safeguards were not relaxed. The first emitted carrier's dispatch lane was interrupted when the expired-fixture issue was identified; its completed carrier-only lane is historical candidate evidence, not the final release result. The revised fixed carrier receives independent current execution in section 169.

A preservation-inspection helper also initially assumed that `letters.json` was an object rather than its actual list. That inspection stopped; no carried history was modified. The corrected preservation check handles the original representation and verifies every earlier letter as an exact prefix. These incidents remain documented instead of being erased by the passing final run.

### 168.9. Constitution, attributed handoff and the next practical gap

Two articles were appended, preserving all earlier text: **C96** requires possible-send evidence before a controller socket, exact pending bytes after uncertainty and a clear read-proof/write-intent distinction; **C97** prohibits treating a transport journal as application authority or independent freshness. The new attributed `letter-0038-officer` records the implementation decision, limitations, research and recommendation. Earlier letters, all 13 exact donor records and the complete received bootstrap remain preserved.

This increment removes manual request/result shuffling from one existing-account message's permission exchange. It does not remove initial setup ceremony or establish sender-side delivery. Next work should make a selected operation easier to inspect and act on, replace fixture pre-signed-cutover convenience with deliberate on-demand account revocation, and pin a supported fixed native environment. Independent cryptographic review and a considered recoverable-preparation retention policy remain necessary before broader account/room use. Preserve the file-mediated path as an explicit recovery option; do not manufacture another protocol family or a falsely reassuring “sent” badge.

### 169.3. The new controller corpus

The final fixed-carrier result records **85 passing checks**, **125 controller child invocations** (including **four actual HTML/Bash controller calls**), **42 setup/runtime-helper role invocations** and **27 authority processes**. These are cooperating synthetic account/role processes with actual profile authentication, signatures, KEM and AEAD, not independently administered machines or a proof of hostile-process confinement.

There are **22 actual abrupt-exit cases at nine distinct boundaries**: six new controller boundaries and three inherited recipient commit/acknowledgement boundaries. Source and carried repetitions, and four additional source controls at already-named boundaries, are explicitly listed. They do not create 22 distinct persistence guarantees. The tests inject process exits, not physical power loss.

Six owned authority response faults occur after a real remote commit: an unsigned HTTP error, altered signature, malformed JSON, redirect, truncated body and duplicate response-length header. Each remains uncertain locally; a subsequent explicitly requested healthy exact retry recovers the original result without appending another authority event. Explicit read recovery advances beyond the original intent deadline while preserving its original write identity. A missing terminal read remains read-only on resume. Abort-first, cutover-first, local abandonment, journal tampering/missing halves, direct-call storage failure invalidation, selected-operation conflict and the sixteen-attempt preflight bound are exercised.

The corpus also demonstrates that restoring an older authenticated controller journal can hide local attempts. That is not reported as global nonexecution or healed freshness. The original retained immutable intent and frozen authority idempotency remain the means of exact recovery. Repeated non-shell scenarios use an explicit authorized fixture clock for both authority and recipient; setup and actual-shell happy paths use real time. The explicit expired-intent case advances its test clock. Production windows and record verification were not widened.

### 169.4. Separate real-time manual shell exercise

A separately executed workflow used **24 actual HTML/Bash commands**, including the deliberately started original authority server, after four instrumented child invocations created synthetic existing account cards and encrypted profiles. The workflow recorded **97.910 seconds**, used real wall time without clock injection or response faults, and preserved both original account identities and both input profiles byte-for-byte.

One `dispatch-send` retained authority permission while reporting zero application admissions. The authority process was stopped and the sender directory, authority directory and explicitly delegated capability file were removed **before local recipient commit**. Offline `dispatch-resume`, explicit `dispatch-finish`, a second finish to a different absent output, `message-read`, `account-mailbox` and final status completed. Exactly one local application admission existed and the two acknowledgement exports matched byte-for-byte, SHA-256 `9ee91acc8a6c38850e7f41ccc968bb1609cdc5b08c357c4cf557e0152a45fc32`. The exact read text's UTF-8 SHA-256 was `2e99c67b7dfdcff3f7425abc6c111c9735b32a35c435bf3770b6a763d65d3470`.

The receipt records public paths and fingerprints and the descriptor number used for private unlock, not password or capability values. The cooperating supervisor intentionally knows synthetic setup passwords in memory; these tests are not a general secrecy proof. Initial ciphertext and setup exchange are still file-mediated. A retained or exported acknowledgement is not its delivery to the sender, let alone proof of human reading.

Distribution remains **one HTML file**. Extracted source development remains supported through the HTML's own no-overwrite workshop.

Publication is gated on the actual final ZIP passing CRC validation, exact root-name comparison, independent extraction, byte-for-byte comparison of all three extracted members with the fixed release inputs, carried manifest verification, all 189 source-binding checks and all 23 established body-digest checks, external-versus-carried driver equality, and preservation of the exact received bootstrap. The fixed HTML also matches the independently rebuilt HTML. The release closure record is kept outside the bytes it measures; no outer ZIP hash or final bootstrap self-hash is embedded recursively in these three members. The delivered filename uses rev0034 and the actual America/New_York packaging time.

The next implementation step should reduce selected-operation and initial-setup ceremony, with explicit on-demand revocation and a supported pinned runtime, rather than widen the trust claim or invent a new protocol family. The present controller already removes request/result-file coordination from one recipient's exact authority exchange, while keeping uncertain transmission, retained permission, local persistence and acknowledgement visibly different.

## 170. Stagepost — one selected operation, visible stage, deliberate action

### 170.1. What this increment changes

Steadypost made one account-bound recipient-to-authority exchange explicit and recoverable, but an operator still had to remember which commands made sense at each point. Stagepost adds a presentation and choice boundary over that existing controller. It neither moves the authority's ordering point nor introduces another recipient persistence transaction.

The work is bounded to one already-created **recipient** operation after `account-bind`, with its original account card, authenticated recovery profile and exact pinned sender. Sender outbox creation, initial public-file exchange, group rooms, attachments and ordinary terminal/browser chat remain separate. The one-file distribution carries the new Python source, executable test corpus and memorandum. No new dependency is needed to display the operation: the implementation uses the existing Python runtime and standard library rather than curses, a web framework or a terminal daemon.

Two commands are added. `operation-view` computes a current local projection and displays it once. `operation-act` executes one explicitly named choice only when the supplied expected-view token still matches that projection. Neither command chooses the next action for the user, evaluates a generated shell command or installs an automatic retry loop.

This is a practical reduction in state-tracking work, not a claim that a complete everyday chat send is now one command. The authority exchange begins only after authenticated preparation; ciphertext delivery before that and acknowledgement delivery afterward are still explicit external steps.

### 170.2. What the view knows and does not know

The view reports the original account and selected contact fingerprints, role identifier, local stage, authenticated recipient generation/head, intent and decision identities, application-admission count, acknowledgement retention, controller transport state, pending request kind and retained attempt budget. It carries neither payload text nor active key material. The default terminal presentation does not preview the message. An explicit `read` action is required even after commitment.

“Locally available” means the retained local state admits selecting that operation. It does not promise that a remote authority will accept the request, that the network will deliver it, that a later storage/output operation will succeed, or that the account's saved contact profile is globally current. The exact underlying engines continue to validate signatures, selected identities, history, deadlines, storage and outputs. An unseen remote cutover can make a displayed send fail at the authority; that is not a stale-local-token bug or permission to guess a different request.

The view deliberately avoids `Recipient.request`, because that method can retain an intent or other signed request. It also does not call the controller's result-import method. Repeated viewing must not sign, create a controller selection/journal, append an attempt, make a connection, adopt an authority reply, commit a message or produce an acknowledgement. The existing recipient constructor authenticates persisted state and can reconcile a lagging signed anchor. Thus “no protocol action” is the claim; “no possible filesystem write” is not.

No recipient listener is added. Merely viewing a possible network action does not read the delegated capability file or open a socket. The selected URL is local retained metadata when a controller already exists, not a capability or proof that the selected server is online.

### 170.3. Locally admissible choices

The following table is a guide, not a replacement for actual authenticated state. The view can withhold a choice because of a clock floor, expired creation window, attempt budget, known cutover, terminal abort, history conflict or missing prerequisite.

| Retained condition | Typical displayed choices | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Authenticated preparation, no controller selection, live creation window | `send`, `abandon` | Send may create/reuse the exact intent and make one selected authority request; abandonment declines local completion. |
| A selected request may have been sent, no verified reply | `resume`, `recover`, `abandon` | Resume preserves the pending bytes; recover explicitly creates a bounded read proof for the same intent. Neither means cancellation or successful remote execution. |
| A verified exact reply is retained but not yet imported | Offline `resume`, possibly `abandon` | Import the cached authority reply without opening a connection; do not commit the message. |
| Exact commit decision imported, local tuple not committed | `finish`, `abandon` | Finish is the separate choice to perform the original local transaction and retain its acknowledgement. |
| Local tuple committed, acknowledgement not yet retained | `read`, `finish` | Read the committed entry or recover the postcommit acknowledgement. Finish does not recommit the message. |
| Local tuple and acknowledgement retained | `read`, `export-ack` | Read the exact committed entry or export the exact existing acknowledgement to an absent path. |
| Abort or cutover known before commitment | No new send or finish; local abandonment where applicable | A terminal refusal is not presented as authority permission. Recovery choices remain governed by the underlying controller. |
| Locally abandoned | No finish or read of a nonexistent committed entry | A prior uncertain attempt can still make a separately authorized result read relevant, but abandonment does not reopen completion. |

A resume of a pending recovery request preserves its read bytes. The frozen controller also applies its original local commit-gate check to resume; the view does not promise a broader resume right after abandonment/cutover. A separately selected fresh `recover` can remain possible where the original read-proof rules permit it. This revision does not silently alter those predecessor semantics to make the menu more permissive.

Acknowledgement export is not acknowledgement delivery. Neither acknowledgement nor explicit terminal reading proves that a human read the message. The recipient necessarily authenticated plaintext during preparation; committed-only presentation is not a claim that plaintext was cryptographically inaccessible to that recipient operator before commitment.

### 170.4. Expected-view guard and locking

`operation-act` requires `--action ACTION` and `--expect-view FULL_TOKEN`. Tokens are exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Their full value is compared with `hmac.compare_digest` only after shape validation. Account unlock/selection and authenticated storage opening happen first; under the original cooperative role and recipient locks, the command recomputes the view and refuses a mismatch before action-specific intent creation, capability access, network I/O or local commitment.

The checkpoint includes the existing controller's bound role/database/preparation/origin coordinates, the selected account record, recipient generation and signed head, a digest of the exact controller state, current admissible actions, blockers and a clock-readiness bucket. The wall clock is not embedded as a continuously changing timestamp. A repeat view with unchanged relevant state therefore has the same token; crossing a relevant time/eligibility boundary can invalidate it. The underlying engine rechecks its live rules during the action as well.

The token is HMAC-SHA256 under a **purpose-specific MAC subkey derived from the existing controller key**, using separate key-derivation and token-message domains. The journal's encryption key is not used directly as the token MAC key. No new key file, signed wire family or durable view-token registry is created. This is local implementation domain separation, not an independent cryptographic audit or a replacement for the existing ML-DSA signatures.

The guard addresses a stale local choice; it does not grant authority. A token is not a password, remote credential, lease, freshness witness or proof that an action never occurred. It cannot detect a joint rollback that restores all of its relevant local inputs, and the corpus deliberately demonstrates restoration of an earlier token after restoring the complete recipient observation set. It does not constrain older `dispatch-*` or `message-*` commands, which remain available with their original rules. Cooperative locks are not an operating-system sandbox against hostile same-user processes.

A caller using the direct Python functions must retain both original locks across view comparison and action. The CLI does that. The returned view describes the state at that computation; the locks are released before printing, so another cooperating operation may subsequently make the displayed token stale. The correct response is to inspect again, not to weaken comparison or automatically authorize the newer state.

### 170.5. Action inputs, output and failure meaning

Network choices require the explicit exact loopback authority URL and a separately delegated private capability-file path. The existing controller enforces the same selected destination, bounded request/reply framing, no redirect/proxy layer, no automatic retry and sixteen-attempt bound. For local choices, URL and capability options are refused rather than ignored. `finish` and `export-ack` require an absent acknowledgement-output path; other choices reject that option. Every action still requires the same original account/profile/contact selection and private unlock.

A stale token or locally unavailable choice exits with refusal before the selected action. A failure after mutating retained state, or an uncertain authority response, retains the existing exit-75 review/recovery meaning. A failed output after local commit cannot undo that commit. The operator must reopen and inspect before choosing recovery. The view token is not evidence that the last command's output reached the terminal, and this work does not claim exactly-once terminal display.

`send`, `resume` and `recover` delegate to the unchanged Steadypost controller. `finish` delegates to its original local finish, which uses the unchanged recipient transaction. `read` reads the already-committed application entry. `export-ack` publishes the existing exact acknowledgement without importing transport state or constructing a new signature. `abandon` delegates to the original recipient abandonment method. None of these creates a parallel inbox, mirrors a second local commit or exports the account's private identity into the operation directory.

No successful cancellation is inferred from missing or unsigned replies. Exact authority permission is not persistence at the recipient. An action can be uncertain while the authority has genuinely committed, and an acknowledgement can be locally retained while the sender still knows nothing about it. The new view carries these distinctions rather than replacing them with one “sent” flag.

### 170.6. Terminal presentation and plaintext

The default output is deliberately one-shot plain terminal text, with account/contact/stage/transport and free text rendered through JSON string escaping. Dynamic control characters, bidi controls and embedded newlines are not emitted as terminal instructions. The program does not evaluate shell fragments from any displayed string. Explicit `read` shows the exact text as an escaped JSON string; `--json` supplies its structured value. The application payload remains the existing exact 1–4,096 UTF-8-byte text, without normalization.

The ASCII display is bounded to 16,384 bytes. The corpus checks hostile-looking free text at the renderer boundary and the largest legitimate two-byte Unicode payload, which is a worst expansion case for six-character JSON escapes under the 4,096-byte message limit. These are presentation checks, not a claim that all such input is admitted by the underlying text protocol. Redirecting an explicit read's output creates a plaintext record outside the encrypted store; the adapter does not claim to erase that export, terminal scrollback, the original draft or older encrypted preparation snapshots.

### 170.7. Practical shell workflow

Prepare the existing cards/profiles, pinned peers and separate roles using section **166.7**, stopping immediately after **`account-bind`**. Do not also run that older section's `message-request`, `isle-lab-decide`, `message-accept` and `message-commit` sequence just to change the view. Reuse its public path variables `H`, `A`, `R`, `PUB` and account-selection array `RBASE`. No passphrase belongs in those variables. Commands use the original hidden prompt or an inherited private pipe from a trusted supervisor; a nonempty original recovery salt still needs the original prompt option.

In the recipient terminal, inspect first:

```bash
bash "$H" operation-view "${RBASE[@]}"
```

For machine-readable inspection, use `--json`:

```bash
bash "$H" operation-view "${RBASE[@]}" --json
```

Copy the **full** `View token` / `view_token` from the current display into the public `TOKEN` variable only after inspecting the shown account, contact, stage and available actions. This variable is a local precondition value, not an unlock secret. There is no command substitution that automatically chooses an action, and the program emits no shell script for evaluation.

In the authority terminal, deliberately start the unchanged listener:

```bash
bash "$H" decision-lab-serve --directory "$A" --port 0 \
  --ready-file "$PUB/authority-ready.json"
```

The ready record identifies a loopback URL and capability **file location**, not the capability value. The authority operator deliberately delegates the capability into a suitable private file under the recipient operator's control; do not share the authority's private directory or key files. In the synthetic same-host exercise the test supervisor explicitly copies only that selected token. `URL` below is the exact selected ready URL, and `CAP` names that delegated private file.

When `send` is shown and the operator chooses it:

```bash
TOKEN='PASTE_THE_FULL_CURRENT_VIEW_TOKEN'
bash "$H" operation-act "${RBASE[@]}" --action send --expect-view "$TOKEN" \
  --url "$URL" --capability-file "$CAP"
```

A successful authority exchange still reports **zero local application admissions**. The resulting display provides a new token for its actual retained state. An exit 75, disconnect or missing output is not cancellation. Inspect again before choosing a recovery action. When the view shows network resume or read recovery, choose one explicitly, not both in an automatic fallback chain:

```bash
# Same pending request bytes and same selected authority.
bash "$H" operation-act "${RBASE[@]}" --action resume --expect-view "$TOKEN" \
  --url "$URL" --capability-file "$CAP"

# A separately authorized bounded READ for the original terminal decision.
# This is an alternative explicit choice, never a fallback that creates work.
bash "$H" operation-act "${RBASE[@]}" --action recover --expect-view "$TOKEN" \
  --url "$URL" --capability-file "$CAP"
```

Use the token from the immediately relevant view, not an old token copied before an intervening successful or uncertain command. A fresh view is also required after local state or eligibility changes. A cached verified reply can make `resume` a **local-only** choice; when the view says local-only, omit both network arguments. The adapter refuses irrelevant arguments rather than silently taking a different path.

Once the imported commit decision makes `finish` locally available, choose whether to complete this exact preparation. Finish does not need a running authority, sender directory or delegated capability:

```bash
bash "$H" operation-act "${RBASE[@]}" --action finish --expect-view "$TOKEN" \
  --output "$PUB/ack.json"
```

After successful finish, inspect/use the resulting token. The committed entry can be read explicitly, and the original acknowledgement can be exported again to another absent path:

```bash
bash "$H" operation-view "${RBASE[@]}"
# Set TOKEN from the current complete-stage display.
bash "$H" operation-act "${RBASE[@]}" --action read --expect-view "$TOKEN"
bash "$H" operation-act "${RBASE[@]}" --action export-ack --expect-view "$TOKEN" \
  --output "$PUB/ack-again.json"
cmp "$PUB/ack.json" "$PUB/ack-again.json"
```

Repeated read or exact acknowledgement export does not add another application admission. These actions leave the token unchanged when relevant state is unchanged; the final software checks still apply. An output path must be absent. Never overwrite an input, account profile, key or previous exported result merely to make the specimen rerunnable.

Before local commitment, an operator who deliberately declines local completion can instead choose `abandon` when displayed:

```bash
bash "$H" operation-act "${RBASE[@]}" --action abandon --expect-view "$TOKEN"
```

That is terminal for local completion, not cancellation of a possible remote decision, requester-grant revocation, prekey recycling or secure erasure. No network flag is accepted for abandonment. Do not present it as a way to take a message back from another participant.

The separate actual-shell exercise in section 171 uses real wall time throughout, removes the selected sender and authority directories and delegated capability **before** local finish, confirms a stale pre-send token is refused, reads the exact Unicode text and exports the same acknowledgement twice. It is not the entire test matrix, a hostile-process sandbox or a demonstration of cross-store atomicity.

### 170.8. Scope decision: requester revocation remains different

The previous next-step recommendation named both a selected-operation view and on-demand requester revocation. This turn implements the former and records the latter as unfinished rather than conflating the two. The existing `account-authorize --allow-presigned-cutover` still separately approves constructing an exact user-signed terminal grant revocation for the authority fixture. No new command automatically signs or sends it here.

A proper replacement must be a sender-side account operation: select the exact retained grant and authority, construct only that terminal revocation on explicit request, retain its exact bytes before uncertain delivery, recover the authority's actual cutover result without issuing a replacement grant, and distinguish “signed locally,” “may have been submitted” and “authority ordered cutover.” It must preserve commit-first rights for the already-selected exact preparation under the frozen policy, refuse a false claim of instantaneous recipient cancellation, and never require a lost device's cooperation for user-signed terminal revocation. Those are recommendations, not implemented behavior in rev0035.

Similarly, token comparison does not establish current contact revocation, device expiry at physical persistence, a global order across stores, secure erasure, forward secrecy, post-compromise security or independent cryptographic review. The existing preparation-retention policy remains a choice between recoverability and confidentiality of old retained material, not something an interface label can settle.

### 170.9. Research reviewed this turn

Four official/primary-source records **T179–T182** were added on October 8, 2026. All previous technical records, their authored dates, the 37 infrastructure options and their review histories remain unchanged. Record identifiers are not a count: the current research array contains 177 technical records. This turn did not recheck every provider price or silently treat old infrastructure notes as current offers.

**T179 — RFC 9110, HTTP Semantics, June 2022, sections 13.1.1, 13.2 and 9.2.2.** https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html . The standard discusses evaluating preconditions before performing a method and distinguishes idempotent semantics from blind repetition of non-idempotent requests. The design analogy here is an expected local state checked before effect under existing locks. Stagepost does **not** implement HTTP `If-Match`, convert POST into an inherently idempotent method, prove remote freshness or obtain correctness from the RFC alone.

**T180 — Python `hmac` documentation.** https://docs.python.org/3/library/hmac.html . The library provides keyed digests and recommends `compare_digest` rather than ordinary equality for externally supplied digest verification. Stagepost fixes token shape before comparison and uses distinct local derivation/message domains. The documentation is not a review of this key hierarchy, account bridge or implementation. Its current page heading does not upgrade the observed interpreter.

**T181 — Python `json` documentation.** https://docs.python.org/3/library/json.html . The encoder's `ensure_ascii` behavior escapes non-ASCII data and required control characters. Stagepost uses that encoding to present dynamic terminal fields and explicit read text without interpreting them as commands. JSON encoding is not itself shell permission, application validation or a complete strict-JSON admission policy; the frozen application parser and exact canonicalization rules remain separate.

**T182 — SQLite 3.51.3 release record, March 13, 2026.** https://www.sqlite.org/releaselog/3_51_3.html . The official release records the WAL-reset fix. The observed experiment still uses SQLite **3.46.1**; this revision neither patches the engine nor claims a supported pinned runtime. A supported fixed build/backport remains a deployment prerequisite. This is a release-record check, not a vulnerability reproduction or a claim that 3.51.3 is the newest SQLite release.

### 170.10. Review findings and rejected/incomplete development work

The first source-corpus call was interrupted by the tool execution bound after partial assertions. That is incomplete development output, not a completed pass. A later source run reached the intended postcommit crash edge but its new assertion expected exit 97; the inherited recipient deliberately exits **94**. The assertion was corrected to the actual documented boundary. No storage implementation or crash behavior changed for that repair. The subsequent complete source-only corpus passed 36 checks, but did not establish carried-code or shell completion.

The first sealed candidate passed its carrier checks, then the carried operation corpus stopped after an actual successful offline finish. Its test had mixed a real-time Bash happy path with a later instrumented reread forced back to the older fixture timestamp. The retained clock floor had correctly advanced, making the earlier token stale under that artificial rewind. The test now keeps **the complete actual-Bash happy path and its adjacent comparisons/rereads on real time**, while repeated adversarial source/carried scenarios retain their explicitly named synthetic clock. The standalone real-time workflow independently passed. No production clock floor, deadline, token comparison or state transition was weakened. An early conversational pass update was premature: the source portion had passed, not the entire carried lane; this final record preserves the actual failing receipt rather than that mistaken shorthand.

Before that candidate result completed, a second candidate had already introduced a purpose-specific token MAC subkey and an explicit completed-command line in the one-shot display. Its newly started broader matrix still included the same test clock mismatch and was deliberately interrupted; it is not counted as final execution. Its separate actual-shell workflow did complete, but remains historical candidate evidence. The third sealed carrier includes the corrected test clock handling and receives the final-byte replay in section 171.

The local-view review also checked the frozen controller's resume gates rather than broadening them invisibly. A pending read is still subject to that controller's original resume path; fresh authorized read recovery remains a separate choice. A view is not permission to bypass a predecessor's refusal merely because the new menu could display another button.

### 170.11. Workshop, preservation and the next officer

The bounded current-status index's `next_gate` names the remaining work. Its inherited `next_work` array retains the earlier combined “compact selected-operation command view and deliberate on-demand revocation” wording: the **view half is implemented here**, while on-demand sender revocation remains open. Read that older combined wording with this explicit partial-completion distinction, not as evidence that Stagepost has no view or has implemented revocation. The fixed carrier is not resealed merely to erase that inherited wording after its execution started.

`operations` reports current source bindings; `operations --full` emits the complete memorandum. `impact` maps the three new members to the `operation` lane and carries the transitive account/dispatch dependencies. The extraction catalog, Bash routing, comparison support, carrier checks, `status` and `brief` were extended together. External `test.sh` must remain byte-identical to `vibe-test-driver`. Development and public distribution still use the same named single HTML; extraction creates the editable files instead of inserting a second nested carrier.

Two constitutional articles were appended: **C98** separates displaying an operation from performing it; **C99** separates a local choice guard from remote authority, freshness and rollback evidence. The attributed **letter-0039-officer** records this bounded decision and the deferred revocation work. Earlier articles, letters, exact donor records and received bootstrap are preserved. The earlier evidence block is not relabeled current, and old memorandum bodies retain their original contents while current dependency bindings are refreshed using each record's existing body-digest convention.

Next work should remove fixture pre-signing through a deliberate sender-side revocation workflow and provide a supported pinned native environment. Subsequent reduction of setup/public-file ceremony should compose existing typed operations without sharing role/account secrets. Keep the file-mediated path as an explicit recovery route. Do not broaden browser/interactive-room defaults or add an abstract protocol family just to make the growing project look more integrated than it is.

## 171. Stagepost fixed-carrier execution, preservation and archive closure

### 171.1. Fixed bytes and accounting rule

The final carrier is the third sealed candidate. Every completed lane below names its exact SHA-256, **`662e49acb4ecd0fbbbb3f6a68a432387c29eb1eaa2fc617457be2931a33ed3c5`**. Its length is **8,128,473 bytes**. The release renames those bytes to `Vibechat.html`; it does not rebuild or alter them after the replay. The external/carried development driver is **29185 bytes**, SHA-256 `982d9fd6e333bcb6015029a8f1ef29fcc5a2c274235a98730d2a969f46e29053`.

**All 33 selected lanes completed and passed within their recorded scopes.** They were separate driver invocations, scheduled by a three-worker test supervisor, not a single completed `all` invocation. The supervisor recorded **1482.017 seconds** of wall time. Individual driver/command durations remain below; they overlap and are not an application-performance benchmark. Neither distinct processes nor check counts add up to a security score. Older crash laboratories are not relabeled new Stagepost storage implementations.

The final operation lane passed **67 checks**, recorded **93 operation child invocations including six actual HTML/Bash invocations**, **43 setup/runtime-helper role invocations**, and **nine owned authority processes**. It exercised **nine real abrupt process-exit cases at three distinct boundaries**, including source/carried repetitions and a separate pending-read case. Those numbers do not mean nine independent persistence guarantees.

The source/carried repeated fault scenarios retain a named fixture clock; the actual Bash happy path and its adjacent comparisons use real time consistently. The separate manual exercise uses real time throughout, with no fault server or clock injection. Deadline checks and refusal semantics were not widened for the tests.

An additional **five-check direct-API probe**, run against freshly extracted final source on the already-completed manual recipient, observed the actual HMAC calls. It confirmed that the view derives the purpose subkey, uses that subkey rather than the journal encryption key for the checkpoint MAC, returns that observed MAC as its token, rejects an unavailable send in the completed state, and leaves exact retained state unchanged. The probe recorded only booleans/digests, never keys or plaintext. This is a separate trusted in-process observation under the original locks, not another account-unlock/CLI test or an independent cryptographic audit. Its replay source and receipt are preserved here rather than added as a fourth release file.

#### Guard probe replay source

This reproducer names the local manual directory and extracted workshop used in this run; supply equivalent paths only to an intentionally created synthetic completed recipient. It does not create or recover an absent store. Source SHA-256: `a0895e6449de51c750451ae64b07fcb1dc58ac89c568caa46a367d1c5b336807`.

```python
"""Additional direct-API observation of the sealed source's MAC derivation.
Use an already-completed synthetic recipient from the separate manual exercise.
No account unlock, network, signing, storage mutation or plaintext output.
"""
import hashlib,json,pathlib,sys,time
R=pathlib.Path('/mnt/data/rev0035-work');sys.path.insert(0,str(R/'fresh-rebuild'))
import native_operation as V
root=R/'manual-candidate3/roles/recipient';checks={};start=time.monotonic()
with V.X.role_lock(root) as (root,marker):
 mode=V.M.read_mode(root,marker)
 with V.M.TextRecipient(root,marker,mode) as r:
  with V.E.Controller(root,marker,r) as c:
   state=V.canonical(r.state);heads=list(r.heads);transport=V.canonical(c.state)
   original=V.hmac.digest;key=bytes(c.key);subkey=original(key,V.TOKEN_KEY_DOMAIN,'sha256');seen=[]
   def observe(k,m,algorithm):
    raw=original(k,m,algorithm)
    if m==V.TOKEN_KEY_DOMAIN or m.startswith(V.TOKEN_DOMAIN):
     seen.append({'derivation':m==V.TOKEN_KEY_DOMAIN,'checkpoint':m.startswith(V.TOKEN_DOMAIN),'key_is_journal':k==key,'key_is_subkey':k==subkey,'digest_hex':raw.hex()})
    return raw
   V.hmac.digest=observe
   try:view=V.view(c)
   finally:V.hmac.digest=original
   checks['actual_view_derives_the_purpose_subkey']=len(seen)==2 and seen[0]['derivation'] and seen[0]['key_is_journal']
   checks['actual_checkpoint_mac_uses_subkey_not_journal_key']=seen[1]['checkpoint'] and seen[1]['key_is_subkey'] and not seen[1]['key_is_journal']
   checks['returned_token_is_the_observed_checkpoint_mac']=view['view_token']==seen[1]['digest_hex']
   try:V.act(c,'send',view['view_token'],url='http://127.0.0.1:1/v1/order',capability_file=root/'nonexistent-capability')
   except V.Refusal as e:checks['completed_state_refuses_send_before_effects']=e.code=='operation-action-not-locally-available' and c.network_calls==0
   checks['probe_and_refusal_leave_exact_retained_state_unchanged']=V.canonical(r.state)==state and r.heads==heads and V.canonical(c.state)==transport and not c.mutation
assert all(checks.values()),checks
result={'status':'passed-scoped','checks':checks,'passed':len(checks),'carrier_sha256':hashlib.sha256((R/'candidate-3.html').read_bytes()).hexdigest(),'source_sha256':hashlib.sha256((R/'fresh-rebuild/native_operation.py').read_bytes()).hexdigest(),'seconds':round(time.monotonic()-start,3),'scope':'Direct trusted API under original locks on an already-completed synthetic recipient; observes actual HMAC use without outputting keys or plaintext. Not another CLI/account-authentication test or independent cryptographic audit.'}
(R/'guard-probe-receipt.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2));print(json.dumps(result,indent=2))
```

### 171.4. Separate actual-shell workflow

A separate real-time workflow completed **26 actual HTML/Bash commands**, including the explicitly started original authority server, after four instrumented child invocations created synthetic preexisting account cards and encrypted profiles. It recorded **114.542 seconds**. It used the third sealed carrier, not an editable worktree implementation or the prior candidate's manual result.

One send retained exact authority permission while leaving zero local application admissions. A stale pre-send token refused before a second authority exchange. The supervisor then stopped the authority and removed the selected sender directory, authority directory and delegated capability **before** local recipient finish. Offline finish committed one application entry, explicit read returned the exact Unicode text, escaped terminal reading remained ASCII, and two acknowledgement exports were byte-identical. The original account identities and both input encrypted profiles remained byte-unchanged.

The final acknowledgement SHA-256 is `d99a924785767e425524589d00cfcbaf966e215849eda6805b243aca233b7843`; the exact text's UTF-8 SHA-256 is `5f4cf0162a7e1d160bb02d46e12cb6b71291be1c5ee1565db1b9e145fe8ce652`. These are synthetic exercise values, not new deterministic protocol vectors. The supervisor intentionally knows its synthetic passwords in memory and both profiles remain available to the supervisor; removing selected role directories is not proof that every way to rederive a foreign test account disappeared. The child access controls and physical missing-directory checks have the previously described scopes, not hostile same-UID/native-child isolation.

The receipt contains public arguments, descriptor numbers, selected public identifiers and explicit test-message output, not password or capability values. An exported acknowledgement still is not delivery back to the sender or evidence of human reading.

### 171.7. Rejected and incomplete candidates

These are development history, not final passes. The first short source invocation was interrupted before completion; the second failed the new test's wrong expected crash exit, which was corrected from 97 to the actual inherited exit 94. The completed third source-only run passed 36 checks and has no carried-code completion claim.

The first sealed carrier, SHA-256 `55280228bcbe86adc8e75dffe54e9efae5c8936eb10a6901d7c0fae630283291`, passed its carrier lane but failed its operation lane after successful carried offline finish because a test reread rewound the clock. The actual refusal and traceback are retained below. The second candidate, SHA-256 `f034cdd77ce5c9e2658ae8d5d43ca4ee850d700f88f7f49a261da97601e4a0c3`, added purpose-specific token key derivation and an explicit completed-command display; its broader matrix was deliberately interrupted when the inherited test mismatch was identified. Its separate real-time manual workflow did pass 26 shell commands, but is not substituted for the final candidate's execution.

The final test correction keeps the actual Bash scenario and adjacent rereads on real time. The production view-token floor/eligibility checks remain intact. The earlier conversational shorthand that the first sealed lane had passed was premature; this record and the retained failure supersede it.
