## Exact received rev0041 bootstrap — historical bytes end

## 184. Carrypost — type-separated exact acknowledgement transport

### 184.1. Owner intent and selected increment

The renewed request is `/run: BOOTSTRAPROSE.md as you see fit`. Backpost's last recommendation was to carry its distinct acknowledgement packet over the capability-gated participant source and HTTPS retrieval path without equating byte retention with sender verification. Carrypost implements that recommendation, preserving the existing three-member release and single-HTML distribution. It is an opt-in native exchange increment, not a rewrite of ordinary chat or a promise to complete an untested distributed workflow automatically.

Backpost already established a file-mediated trust boundary: a recipient packages an acknowledgement that already exists, and an independently selected sender authenticates the exact return against its original account, pinned contact and message prefix. Carrypost does not move this trust decision into the source or client. Its new transport adapter needs no account unlock, account secret, sender/recipient private key, signing callback, authority credential or participant database. It copies one selected representation and runs the existing public return validator. Its source of trust is deliberately incomplete until the sender separately applies Backpost's original selection.

### 184.2. Fixed profiles, not negotiation

The shared engines have exactly two recognized local content profiles: `pairpost-setup-v1` and `backpost-ack-return-v1`. The old public commands use the former by default. Carrypost's new commands select the latter by program construction, not by looking at an incoming MIME header, packet hint, URL parameter or user-supplied module name. The return validator is the fixed named carried `vibe-native-return` source or its exact extracted worktree counterpart; no code is downloaded or selected from packet data.

Return retrieval state uses `vibechat-carrypost-return-retrieval-v1` with an exact `content_profile` field. Return source state uses `vibechat-carrypost-return-source-v1` with the corresponding exact field. Their exact shape differs from old setup state. Both directions refuse a wrong-profile store before treating its contents as the other workflow. A newly selected but unfetched return directory is already distinguishable; there is no interval in which an old setup command can adopt it because its packet slot is still empty. Frozen setup packet validation likewise refuses a valid Backpost envelope, and return validation refuses a valid setup envelope.

The source accepts one fixed route, `/v1/ack-return`, using the inherited strict HTTP/1.1 framing. The setup source keeps `/v1/handoff`. A valid capability cannot negotiate another route or profile. A packet's existing signed record families remain unchanged; the source/client state markers are local unsigned bookkeeping, not a new signed protocol. Content-Type cannot grant permission, select executable code, or replace exact-byte and signature checks.

### 184.3. Exact selection and independent acceptance

The recipient first uses unchanged `return-pack` on its selected completed operation. Preparation or authority permission without an already-retained acknowledgement still refuses. Opening recipient storage may reconcile and sign a lagging storage anchor, as Backpost documented; that is not a new acknowledgement signature, a new application admission, or a second authority event. Carrypost itself does not open that store.

Source creation requires the existing return file and its independently selected full SHA-256. The digest is compared against the same bounded byte read used for validation, before source-directory or capability-file creation. It also requires a public TLS certificate; serving separately supplies its private TLS key. One private bearer capability file is generated, distinct from the source store and ready record. The source retains only the capability digest. The client receives the capability and independently selected return digest through an explicit protected handoff rather than treating a server-provided hash as a new trust root.

The client verifies certificate/hostname under a selected public CA or the runtime system store, matches the bearer file to its retained capability digest, checks the complete response length and exact expected packet SHA-256, and validates the existing Backpost record relationships. No smaller selection hash, operation label, matching MIME type, bare acknowledgement, detached signature or valid TLS connection is sufficient.

This is still **packet-internal verification**. The transport has no knowledge of the sender's original contact/profile/message selection. An internally valid return for another real message can pass the transport boundary when its own digest was selected; unchanged Backpost `return-import` must then reject it against a different saved original prefix. The corpus constructs two genuinely valid message selections under the same accounts to test this distinction, rather than only changing a signature into invalid bytes.

Transport retention does not mutate the sender's independent return-selection store or any endpoint/authority role directory. Exporting the packet is a separate action. Importing it into the sender's selected Backpost store is another. Inspection after acceptance is explicit and does not assert that the sender read the original text or that the recipient continues to hold its database.

### 184.4. Command surface

Every new command requires `--experimental` and an explicit `--directory`. None accepts account/password/profile/contact input. These are local transport operations, not remote signing or account services.

| Command | Inputs and effect |
|---|---|
| `return-source-new` | Exact existing return packet, `--expect-return` full digest, public certificate, absent capability output, optional bounded `--max-attempts`; creates one private source, no listener. |
| `return-source-status` | Opens the typed source and reports enabled state, possible/offered attempt history and unknown sender acceptance. |
| `return-source-disable` | Retains terminal local disable under the source writer lock; does not revoke earlier responses, messages or signatures. |
| `return-source-serve` | Explicit listener with the selected private TLS key, default loopback and port zero; separate `--allow-nonloopback` for a nonloopback address; ready file contains URL and public digests, no bearer. |
| `return-fetch-select` | Exact HTTPS URL ending in `/v1/ack-return`, independently selected digest, required private capability file, optional public CA file; creates a new typed retrieval directory, no connection. |
| `return-fetch` | One attempt for that retained selection, with the selected capability file required before successful retention. |
| `return-fetch-resume` | One exact retry before completion, or exact offline recovery after retained completion; no destination replacement or automatic follow-up. |
| `return-fetch-status` | Describes retained local evidence, without contacting the source or sender acceptance store. |
| `return-fetch-export` | Publishes the exact retained return packet to an absent output path; never overwrites and never invokes `return-import`. |

The source address, expected digest, certificate trust choice and capability digest are bound in the local selection. The raw bearer is not persisted in the retrieval journal. There is no `--allow-public-source` alternative for the new profile. The old setup-only compatibility option remains available only through its existing commands and state type.

Both packet profiles retain the existing **2,097,152-byte** packet bound. Authorized source attempts and client attempts are separately bounded to at most **16**. The client retains its existing **20-second** request budget. This revision does not silently increase a bound to make the larger return representation fit. The exercised full context was 928,924 bytes around an original 10,536-byte acknowledgement; these are fixture measurements, not a guarantee that every possible future envelope fits. Oversized data refuses rather than being truncated or admitted in a different format.

### 184.5. Ordering, disable and uncertainty

The existing source writer protects admission and disable. A valid, enabled, budgeted request first acquires an ordered `possible` row. Only after that state publication does the source release the lock and write the response. The lock is never deliberately retained across a peer-controlled network await. After local response draining, the source reopens state and marks the same attempt `offered`. This is local flow control and local bookkeeping, not a remotely signed retention receipt.

Disable before admission blocks new work. Admission before disable may finish that already admitted response. This ordering is the same for setup and return profiles. Wrong or absent capabilities are refused without consuming an authorized source attempt. A valid request can consume budget even when its response is later lost. Repeated retrieval attempts are not evidence of additional messages or newly generated acknowledgements.

The client publishes possible-send evidence before opening a connection. After receiving and checking the full exact packet, it atomically retains the packet and its completed attempt. A failed request or unconfirmed publication does not become sender acceptance. After a possible request, unverified transfer outcomes use exit **75** with no successful packet result. A preflight refusal can use exit **2**; it does not authorize creating a replacement selection. Source-side process exit edges in the corpus use **97** and client edges **99**, solely as test controls, not normal application statuses.

Both sides invalidate a mutating failed handle rather than allowing candidate memory to stand in for successful publication. Reopening discovers the actual retained state. A response may have reached the client even if the source never recorded `offered`, and a source may record `offered` while client retention fails. There is no cross-store atomic commit, exactly-once network delivery, or inferred cancellation.

An unfetched or unsuccessfully fetched return says **`no-packet-retained; no-signature-verification-claim`**. A retained packet says its internal signatures were checked while explicitly stating that sender account/message acceptance was not performed. Review corrected an earlier unconditional wording branch and the final corpus checks both sides of this boundary. This is a status-truth correction; the earlier implementation did not bypass packet validation during successful retention.

### 184.6. Recovery, storage and privacy

A pending retry uses the same URL, packet digest, profile and trust choice. The source must retain the selected packet/certificate and restart at the same address and port. A fresh ephemeral port is a new destination, not an exact resume. Losing the capability before completion prevents authorized retrieval; it does not authorize silently replacing the capability or source. A completed retrieval needs neither the source process nor the original CA/capability files because it recovers the exact verified local result, not a new TLS session.

Source disable or later source disappearance does not invalidate already retained acknowledgement bytes. The original authority windows can be closed: checking historical completion evidence is not a new grant, lease, authorization renewal or permission to create another message. Original commit/abort/cutover precedence is untouched. Acknowledgement transport neither cancels the recipient's already committed entry nor implies future storage availability.

The source and retrieval store retain public identity/protocol metadata and selected ciphertext in private directories. They do not retain plaintext message content, the active session root, account seeds or the raw bearer in ordinary state. They are nevertheless **not encrypted**. An operator with access can inspect relationship metadata. A copied bearer can be used while the source is enabled and has budget; there is no mutual TLS or holder-bound proof, and disabling a source cannot recall disclosed bytes. The certificate, endpoint address, and traffic sizes are not hidden by application post-quantum encryption. No post-quantum TLS qualification is claimed.

The local journals are neither independently authenticated histories nor rollback witnesses. Restoring an older valid local snapshot can hide a later transfer or import. Neither side can prove “never requested” or “never received” from the absence of a retained row. Similarly, successful local `drain()` does not show that another application committed its state. Backpost verifies the recipient's signed commitment assertion, not an independent observation of the recipient's disk or proof of human reading.

The code uses strict finite parsing and bounded state, but no denial-of-service defense or internet-facing service qualification is claimed. The endpoint performs substantial cryptographic verification. A public deployment still needs appropriate runtime maintenance, access management, operational controls and explicit participant choices; this release does not deploy or subscribe to anything.

### 184.7. Practical handoff, with explicit trust and storage boundaries

Begin with the existing account-bound workflow and a recipient that has already retained an acknowledgement through explicit finish. Keep the sender's original compose-or-later setup packet saved independently. Do not substitute the returned full packet for that earlier selection. The examples use quoted shell variables containing explicitly selected paths or full digests; all output files and newly created directories must be absent, with existing private parent directories. Account commands below use their hidden terminal prompt. The inherited private pipe/socket unlock mechanism remains available, but there is no password command-line argument.

**Recipient: package only what already exists.** `RECIPIENT_OPERATION`, original account card/profile, pinned sender ID, and full bound setup packet are the existing local selections. `BOUND_SETUP_SHA` is the full digest of that selected setup packet.

```bash
bash "$HTML" return-pack --experimental \
  --directory "$RECIPIENT_OPERATION" \
  --card "$RECIPIENT_CARD" --profile "$RECIPIENT_PROFILE" --contact "$SENDER_ID" \
  --setup "$BOUND_SETUP" --expect-setup "$BOUND_SETUP_SHA" \
  --output "$PACKED_RETURN"
sha256sum -- "$PACKED_RETURN"
```

Independently communicate the exact resulting digest, stored as `RETURN_SHA`, and intended source/trust selection. A digest is not a bearer secret; the capability is. Public record inspection is not permission to place these relationship records on a generally accessible website.

**Recipient/source operator: create and explicitly serve the one return.** Provision the matching TLS certificate and private key deliberately. The owned-loopback tests use a test certificate; that does not make it a production trust anchor.

```bash
bash "$HTML" return-source-new --experimental \
  --directory "$RETURN_SOURCE" --packet "$PACKED_RETURN" \
  --expect-return "$RETURN_SHA" --certificate "$TLS_CERTIFICATE" \
  --capability-output "$PRIVATE_CAPABILITY" --max-attempts 16

bash "$HTML" return-source-serve --experimental \
  --directory "$RETURN_SOURCE" --private-key "$TLS_PRIVATE_KEY" \
  --listen-host 127.0.0.1 --advertise-host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port "$SELECTED_PORT" --ready-file "$SOURCE_READY"
```

The last command is a foreground server; it does not spawn automatically during creation or selection. A second terminal/process performs the client actions. For a deliberately configured remote endpoint, choose an appropriate advertised hostname, certificate, binding address and explicit nonloopback consent; no public reachability is established by the example. Pending exact recovery requires the same selected port, including after restart. The ready record carries no raw capability. Deliver the capability privately and separately; do not copy its contents into a URL or transcript.

**Sender: first retain the independent message selection.** `ORIGINAL_COMPOSE` was saved by the sender before this return arrived; it is not a replacement trust root from the source. `ORIGINAL_COMPOSE_SHA` is its exact full digest.

```bash
bash "$HTML" return-select --experimental \
  --directory "$SENDER_RETURN" \
  --card "$SENDER_CARD" --profile "$SENDER_PROFILE" --contact "$RECIPIENT_ID" \
  --setup "$ORIGINAL_COMPOSE" --expect-setup "$ORIGINAL_COMPOSE_SHA" \
  --expect-return "$RETURN_SHA"
```

**Sender/retrieval operator: select, fetch, then export exact transport bytes.** `RETURN_URL` is the explicitly selected verified HTTPS address ending in `/v1/ack-return`. The optional `--ca-file` accepts public trust certificates, not a private key. Omit it only when the runtime system trust store is the deliberate choice. There is no source-supplied trust override or redirect-following fallback.

```bash
bash "$HTML" return-fetch-select --experimental \
  --directory "$RETURN_FETCH" --url "$RETURN_URL" \
  --expect-return "$RETURN_SHA" --capability-file "$PRIVATE_CAPABILITY" \
  --ca-file "$PUBLIC_CA"

bash "$HTML" return-fetch-status --experimental --directory "$RETURN_FETCH"
bash "$HTML" return-fetch --experimental --directory "$RETURN_FETCH" \
  --capability-file "$PRIVATE_CAPABILITY"
bash "$HTML" return-fetch-export --experimental --directory "$RETURN_FETCH" \
  --output "$DELIVERED_RETURN"
```

At this point the sender return store remains merely selected. No sender account has been unlocked by transport. A successful fetch has not run the following command on the sender's behalf.

```bash
bash "$HTML" return-import --experimental \
  --directory "$SENDER_RETURN" \
  --card "$SENDER_CARD" --profile "$SENDER_PROFILE" --contact "$RECIPIENT_ID" \
  --packet "$DELIVERED_RETURN"

bash "$HTML" return-inspect --experimental \
  --directory "$SENDER_RETURN" \
  --card "$SENDER_CARD" --profile "$SENDER_PROFILE" --contact "$RECIPIENT_ID"

bash "$HTML" return-export --experimental \
  --directory "$SENDER_RETURN" \
  --card "$SENDER_CARD" --profile "$SENDER_PROFILE" --contact "$RECIPIENT_ID" \
  --output "$EXACT_ACKNOWLEDGEMENT"
```

Source status/disable remain independent actions:

```bash
bash "$HTML" return-source-status --experimental --directory "$RETURN_SOURCE"
bash "$HTML" return-source-disable --experimental --directory "$RETURN_SOURCE"
```

After a possible but unconfirmed request, inspect the retained selection and explicitly resume with the same capability and endpoint. Never respond to uncertainty by creating a new operation, changing the return digest, renewing an intent or forging a different acknowledgement.

```bash
bash "$HTML" return-fetch-resume --experimental --directory "$RETURN_FETCH" \
  --capability-file "$PRIVATE_CAPABILITY"
```

After exact retrieval is retained, that same resume command can omit the capability and remain offline. Export to another absent path recovers identical bytes. After sender acceptance is retained, Backpost can recover the original acknowledgement without any source, recipient or authority operation directory. The sender's own account/profile and selected return store remain necessary.

Section 185 reports a separate execution of these command families on the fixed HTML. Its synthetic account-fixture construction and owned authority helper are named separately from actual HTML/Bash commands; tests use real wall time throughout that manual workflow. The source is stopped and its directory, original CA/capability/packet and endpoint/authority operation directories are removed **before** offline client export and sender import. This tests disappearance and exact recovery, not deployment across independently administered hosts.

### 184.8. Implementation, workshop and current bindings

The new source identities are `vibe-native-return-transport`, `vibe-native-return-transport-tests`, and `vibe-native-return-transport-memorandum`. The adapter delegates to the original `native_publisher.py` and `native_handoff.py`; those two implementations gain a fixed keyword-only content profile, typed state verification, fixed route selection and an exact pre-creation return digest. Their default setup behavior stays intact. The unchanged `native_return.py` remains the verifier and account-bound acceptance implementation. Existing authority and recipient transactions are not edited.

The Bash/HTML launcher routes `return-source-*` and `return-fetch*` to the new adapter **before** the existing broad `return-*` Backpost dispatch. The ordinary Backpost commands continue to use their existing argument parser and unlock semantics. The same HTML executes carried dependencies rather than accidentally preferring same-named current-directory Python files. The new corpus includes harmless decoys to exercise that distinction.

`return-transports` exposes the bounded memorandum and exact current source bindings. `impact` connects return transport to setup/source/client/Backpost review lanes, including shared-engine dependency changes. `test.sh returnwire` extracts the fixed carrier and executes the composed corpus there. The carrier lane verifies the new help, source inventory, current-first guidance and external/carried driver equality. These are development tools, not new runtime network dependencies.

Earlier deterministic memoranda have their defined current source-binding rows and nonrecursive body digests refreshed through the existing graph. Their old vectors, recorded histories, signatures, algorithm formats and execution timestamps are not relabeled as fresh tests. The large historical `vibe-evidence` block remains byte-for-byte unchanged. Only section 185 asserts this revision's executed scopes.

### 184.9. Online research, reviewed October 10, 2026

Four primary-source reviews are added as T207–T210. They inform transport/status boundaries; they do not certify this implementation or upgrade the observed runtime. All earlier technical records and the 37 infrastructure options remain preserved, without a blanket new verification date for those options.

**T207 — RFC 9110, HTTP Semantics.** The representation metadata described in section 8 does not authenticate an application-specific account or message selection. In particular, a Content-Type is not a code-selection permission or sender trust anchor. Carrypost uses a fixed local profile and exact representation checks instead of type sniffing. Source: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html .

**T208 — RFC 6750, bearer-token usage.** An ordinary bearer grants access through possession; it does not establish holder-bound proof or the identity of the original message sender. The Authorization header and TLS protect transport of the capability, but copying or disclosing it remains consequential. Carrypost adopts this bounded bearer model without claiming an OAuth deployment. The RFC Editor HTML request returned HTTP 429 during review; the official IETF Datatracker copy supplied the text: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6750 .

**T209 — RFC 8098, message disposition notifications.** A display notification is not proof that a person read or understood content. Carrypost and Backpost keep human reading unknown even after transport retention, valid signatures and explicit local inspection. Source: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8098.html .

**T210 — Python asyncio streams documentation.** `StreamWriter.drain()` participates in local write-buffer flow control; it is not a recipient application-retention acknowledgement. This is the reason source `offered` stays separate from client retention. Source: https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-stream.html . The documentation page reviewed was the current Python 3.15 page; the executed interpreter is Python 3.13.5. No interpreter upgrade is claimed from reading newer documentation.

### 184.10. Decisions and next officer

Keep the bearer design explicit and small for this increment. A holder-bound credential would introduce another lifecycle and review surface; it is not necessary to establish this exact-return boundary. Keep the full verification context bounded rather than inventing a compact acknowledgement transport before selected sender verification works. The measured envelope is large relative to the acknowledgement, so future compactness work must preserve the original selection and historical verification context rather than replacing them with a label.

The useful next step is a **bounded selected-exchange overview**. It should accept explicitly selected local stores, verify that their selections match, and present setup, source offers, client retention, authority/recipient operation, and returned acknowledgement as separate columns or stages. It should neither scan the filesystem nor guess globally latest state, open a connection, renew a deadline, generate an acknowledgement, sign a revocation, or equate explicit inspection with reading. Reuse the existing commands; do not add a second authoritative mailbox or another protocol family merely to make the interface look complete.

The observed native runtime remains unchanged and unpinned by this turn. Existing deployment prerequisites recorded in earlier sections still apply. A successful owned-loopback test, reproducible HTML and authenticated application record are useful evidence within their scope, not a substitute for an independent review or an operationally qualified deployment.

### 185.3. Separate real-wall-time shell workflow

A separate fresh exercise completed **30 actual HTML/Bash commands**, one actual HTML/Bash return-source server and one owned authority helper process. Four account-fixture helper processes prepared the synthetic account/profile context; they are not counted as HTML/Bash commands. No test clock override or authorization renewal was used. The workflow passed **13 checks** in **156.549 seconds**. This duration is execution evidence, not an application performance claim.

It performed all setup stages through the actual carrier, acquired permission with zero local admissions, explicitly finished once, packed the retained acknowledgement through Backpost, and created the sender's independent selection before retrieval. The source was separately created and served. Retrieval left the sender selection unchanged. The source was disabled and stopped; its directory, original packet/capability/certificate/key, and sender/recipient/authority operation directories were removed **before** offline retrieval export and separate sender import. The sender still showed unaccepted state before that explicit import.

Subsequent original-account import and explicit inspection worked offline. Two exports recovered the exact original 10,536-byte acknowledgement even after the delivered input packet was removed. An existing output refused overwrite. Both original encrypted account profiles remained byte-identical. The sender's own account/profile and selected return directory remained available; this is disappearance of remote and operation dependencies, not recovery of a lost account.

### 185.4. Development findings and unpromoted candidates

The first direct-source probe reached a correct duplicate-JSON refusal but its test helper did not catch the separately loaded native exception class. The helper was narrowed to recognized protocol/file/value failures rather than swallowing arbitrary programming errors. The parser was not weakened. A subsequent development probe passed 81 source-level checks before the later status and harness corrections; that run is **not** the fixed-carrier result.

Candidates A and B were preliminary seals, not completed release matrices. Candidate C added the shared-engine returnwire impact mapping, then review caught an unconditional return-status message claiming internal signatures had been checked before any packet was retained. Its selected matrix and supplementary manual run were interrupted and not promoted. The correction gates that claim on retained verified data and adds assertions on both sides of the boundary. No packet was allowed to bypass successful-retention validation.

Candidate D included that correction. Its separate manual source startup exposed a test-harness race: the harness saw the absent-only ready-file name before the source completed the JSON write. The harness now waits for complete JSON under its existing bounded startup timeout; a persistent incomplete or invalid record still fails. Production publication semantics, packet parsing, signatures and deadlines were not changed to accommodate this harness. Candidate D's broader run was stopped and is not counted as a complete pass.

Candidate E is the release selection. It received the complete fresh 21-scope replay, the separate 30-command manual exercise, preservation checks and fresh whole-carrier reproduction. No C/D partial results are relabeled as E execution.

### 185.5. Reproduction and preservation

An independent fresh extraction rebuilt the TypeScript worker and WebAssembly using **TypeScript 5.8.3** and **clang 17.0.0**, with no dependency fetching. Repacking produced the entire released HTML **byte-for-byte**, not merely matching compiled crypto records. The build's compiled worker digest is retained in its summarized evidence. All **70 carried Python sources** also passed compile-only parsing; this check does not execute them or constitute runtime coverage.

Observed runtime: Python **3.13.5**, Python TLS **OpenSSL 3.5.5 27 Jan 2026**, OpenSSL executable **OpenSSL 3.5.5 27 Jan 2026 (Library: OpenSSL 3.5.5 27 Jan 2026)**, and SQLite **3.46.1**. This revision does not pin, install or upgrade that native environment. Reading Python 3.15 documentation did not change the Python 3.13.5 test interpreter. Earlier recorded deployment prerequisites remain separate from these scoped tests.

The carrier adds **three named sources**, reaching **117** from 114. Of the predecessor sources, **78 remain byte-identical**. Among the **75 protected implementation/test/cryptographic code blocks** (excluding the development tool and external driver), **73 remain byte-identical**. The only changed predecessor code implementations are:

- `native_handoff.py`
- `native_publisher.py`

### 185.6. Archive closure

The final ZIP contains exactly `Vibechat.html`, `BOOTSTRAPROSE.md`, and `test.sh` at its root, without duplicate names or private fixture files. It passed ZIP CRC validation, independent extraction, and exact comparison of all three members to fixed release inputs. The independently extracted HTML passed its 117-member manifest verification. All extracted named sources match the worktree's release sources, and external `test.sh` exactly matches the carried `vibe-test-driver` bytes. The final HTML also matches the independently rebuilt carrier.

The archive's SHA-256 is calculated outside the archive after closure; it is not embedded into a self-referential archive hash claim. The three-file layout remains intentional: the owner allows more development files when materially better, but the carried extraction workflow already supplies the editable source tree. No source capability, private TLS key, generated account secret, active fixture database or new plaintext message is included in the release. Existing user-provided histories and their named public/deterministic records remain preserved.

### 185.8. Attributed handoff — GPT-6 Astra Pro, Carrypost officer, October 10, 2026

The return path now moves one exact retained acknowledgement through the existing participant TLS engines without letting transport choose the sender's trust. I chose fixed typed states and routes rather than MIME negotiation or another generic service. I left source offer, local retention, sender acceptance and human reading separate, and kept the original account-bound verifier and acknowledgement bytes unchanged.

Two review findings mattered: a status sentence outran the evidence before fetch, and a test harness outran the source's ready-file write. Both are recorded here with their unpromoted candidates, rather than being hidden inside a clean final count. The final selected matrix and manual workflow belong only to the fixed released hash above.

The next officer should simplify observation rather than invent a new receipt. Build a bounded selected-exchange overview from existing explicitly selected stores, refuse mismatched selections, and show the valid next commands without executing them. Preserve the old setup windows, exact recovery and original commit/cutover policy. A returned signature still authenticates a claim, not a human reading or an independent remote disk. Ordinary chat remains untouched; connecting this exchange to daily use remains a deliberate later decision, not an implication of these laboratory and transport passes.

## 186. Crosspost — bounded selected-exchange overview

### 186.1. Decision and scope

The user authorized continuation of the existing work, not a replacement architecture. Carrypost already moves a separately typed acknowledgement packet through the participant TLS source/retrieval path, and Backpost already verifies that return against the sender's original selection. The next defect was fragmentation of observation: an operator had to visit several command families to determine which exact packet had been retained, whether a recipient had merely obtained permission, and whether the sender had independently accepted the returned acknowledgement.

Crosspost joins those existing projections. It does not define a new signed protocol record or assign new meanings to predecessor fields. `native_overview.py` delegates packet chronology to Waypost, packet validation to Pairpost and Backpost, transfer state to the original source/retrieval stores, recipient actions to Stagepost/Steadypost, and sender acceptance to Backpost. `native_overview_checks.py` tests selection, side effects, ambiguity and carried execution. `native_overview_memorandum.json` states the bounds and binds the exact dependencies. Their source IDs are `vibe-native-overview`, `vibe-native-overview-tests`, and `vibe-native-overview-memorandum`.

The HTML routes `exchange-overview` before the older `exchange-*` branch so the new command cannot be accidentally dispatched to Waypost's one-packet-only CLI. `overviews` and `overviews --full` expose the memorandum. `impact` names the new `overview` lane and relevant existing scopes. The external development driver is exactly the carried driver. None of this installs dependencies or changes ordinary chat defaults.

### 186.2. Exact selections and bounded joins

The overview always begins with `--packet` and the full `--expect-packet` SHA-256. Both endpoint packets and every valid setup-stage prefix can be observed. The existing canonical parser rejects duplicate JSON fields, malformed encoding, excess bytes and invalid signatures. The input bound remains 2,097,152 bytes. The wrapper does not accept a digest as an alternative to authenticating records.

Four optional directory arguments have fixed types:

| Option | Exact scope | What a positive observation does not establish |
|---|---|---|
| `--setup-source-directory` | Original participant source for the selected setup packet | Peer retention or setup adoption |
| `--setup-fetch-directory` | Original local retrieval of that exact setup packet | Adoption, permission or message commitment |
| `--return-source-directory` | Original return-profile source for one independently selected Backpost packet | Sender retention or account-bound acceptance |
| `--return-fetch-directory` | Original local retrieval of that selected return packet | Sender import, explicit inspection or human reading |

There is no directory discovery or filesystem scan. Duplicate selections resolving to the same directory refuse. A setup source containing a different valid prefix refuses rather than being treated as the same object because its contacts match. The type fences of Carrypost remain in force, including for an unfetched return selection. All original parser, private-directory, lock, state and digest checks remain active.

Any return scope requires `--expect-return`, a full independently selected digest. Without a return scope, supplying that otherwise unused digest refuses. Return observation requires a compose-or-later setup prefix, so an early endpoint identity cannot stand in for selection of the message. A retained return must pass Backpost's internal checks and contain a setup extension whose participants and selected stage prefix are byte-equivalent to the independently selected packet. An unfetched retrieval has no packet to validate: the output explicitly says its selected-setup binding is unestablished until retention, rather than anticipating successful verification.

At most one account-role scope can be opened. `--recipient-directory` requires the complete nine-step bound setup packet and the recipient's original selected account/contact. It checks the public bound bundle before opening recipient storage, then checks the retained preparation and exact bundle again. `--sender-return-directory` requires the sender's original account/contact, expected return digest and the exact setup prefix saved when that sender's return store was created. A later valid prefix for the same message is not silently substituted for that original selection. This restriction prevents convenience from changing the meaning of the operator's previously chosen evidence.

Public transfer inspection needs no account credentials. Supplying account credentials without an account scope refuses; supplying a private scope without all required account inputs also refuses. The callable API may receive a trusted caller's already-unlocked bridge, while the CLI retains the existing hidden prompt or inherited private pipe mechanism. No account private key is exported to another role, and no invocation opens both participant account scopes.

The complete JSON projection and the terminal display are each limited to 65,536 bytes. The limit is a refusal boundary, not a truncation that might silently remove a warning or selection coordinate.

### 186.3. Facts that remain separate

The setup portion is the existing Waypost chronology: exact packet identity, stage prefix, next participant, authenticated record windows, and local-clock interpretations. A completed public setup packet is not itself proof that a recipient's private preparation survived. Crosspost joins private state only when explicitly selected and authenticated.

That chronology remains attached to the packet prefix the operator selected. A retained return may contain a later validated extension, but the overview does not silently replace the original prefix or relabel its next-stage hint as a globally outstanding task. The hinted setup step may already have completed elsewhere; it is a command to consider under the original exact-input/recovery checks, not a declaration that the exchange must perform that work again. Recipient actions and sender import/inspection hints come from their separately selected local stores. No combined automatic plan is inferred from those observations.

A source reports enabled/disabled state, admitted attempts, recorded offers, unresolved admitted attempts and remaining budget. Its `offered` row is the source's own completed response operation, not proof of peer retention. A retrieval reports selected or retained state, its attempt history and retained byte count. Successful retrieval does not call setup adoption or sender import. A recipient operation reports the original phase, transport uncertainty, authority decision, local application-admission count, acknowledgement retention, eligible actions and exact view token. A sender return store reports whether the acknowledgement has been independently verified and retained under that account's original selection.

The corpus observes a real prepared recipient with zero application admissions, then a real authority decision with zero admissions, then an explicit original finish with one admission and a retained acknowledgement. Crosspost does not cause any of those transitions. Separately seeded, valid transfer states demonstrate that source offer and fetch retention can coexist with an unimported sender return store. Only explicit original Backpost retention changes that last observation. The seed status is intentional: these projection fixtures are not new HTTPS delivery evidence; the separately selected existing transport lanes supply their own scoped network tests.

The sender projection does not call `return-inspect` and does not create an inspection receipt. The human display says explicit inspection is not recorded and names the separate command. Even after sender verification, human reading and the recipient's continued present possession remain unknown. The overview is not a “read” badge.

### 186.4. Locks, clocks and maintenance are visible

Each selected store is opened under its existing local lock and closed before the next observation. No new lock spans all stores. A sequence of individually sound readings can therefore straddle another actor's action. The corpus disables a source between observation steps and confirms that the output preserves the earlier source observation and the later state without claiming they were simultaneous. A user must refresh and invoke an original guarded action before relying on action eligibility.

The setup clock is sampled once after the selected packet validates. It is unauthenticated and unsynchronized. The original recipient-operation view separately applies its own current eligibility clock. These are deliberately not collapsed into a single claimed instant. Historical completed acknowledgements remain visible when setup windows have closed; that does not reopen an unfinished authorization or renew a send. All original windows and the authority-decision-first policy remain unchanged.

Original store constructors can create their ordinary lock file. Opening the recipient can reconcile a lagging signed local anchor and therefore produce a storage-maintenance signature. Crosspost's guarantee is no new operational transition or acknowledgement, not universal filesystem immutability or absence of all signing. The corpus restores a real older anchor, opens the overview, and verifies reconciliation while the original acknowledgement bytes remain unchanged. It also separately verifies byte-identical repeated views once maintenance is complete. Filesystem metadata such as access times is not covered by content-byte comparisons.

Networking-capable modules remain transitively imported through frozen validators. The command exposes no destination, listener or execute option and makes no network request. Direct calls are instrumented with socket-event refusal; child commands use an explicit audited launcher whose deliberate socket-opening control must fail before the carried command is accepted as tested. This is evidence about exercised cooperative Python paths, not a security sandbox, native-child syscall confinement or proof against a hostile process under the same user.

### 186.5. Output and action boundary

The default human display uses compact rows: exact packet, setup stage, next participant, local coordination window, selected source/fetch stages, recipient permission/commit/acknowledgement state or sender acceptance, and literal next command names. The original operation view token is displayed only when that account scope was selected. `--json` retains the full bounded projection and original action details. Strings are escaped for terminal presentation; there is no terminal-control interpretation from packet content.

Neither output includes message text, ciphertext bodies, raw acknowledgement bytes, selected URLs, certificate material, raw bearer capabilities, passwords or private storage paths. It still contains participant fingerprints, packet identities, timing and other relationship metadata. Do not publish it as though omission of plaintext made it anonymous.

Hints are literal command names and explanatory notes, not constructed executable shell strings. The source view may name explicit disable; the retrieval view may name same-selection fetch/resume or exact export; the recipient view reuses original `operation-act` choices and its view token; the sender view names import or inspect/export. Nothing is invoked by viewing, and no new action planner is retained. Original commands may still refuse because of changed state, deadlines, missing credentials, trust choices, output paths or remote outcomes. A command listed as locally available is not a remote promise or new permission.

On refusal, the CLI returns a bounded error category to standard error and exit 2, with no partial overview printed to standard output. Some earlier selected store may already have undergone its disclosed opening maintenance. The error does not falsely promise that every filesystem byte remained untouched or that no other actor changed state. It does say no automatic action was selected.

### 186.6. Recovery and limits

The overview has no new journal to resume. Existing source, fetch, recipient and sender return stores remain the owners of their own recovery semantics. Exact retained acknowledgements stay exact; the overview cannot fabricate a missing result or choose another operation after uncertainty. The final corpus removes sender, recipient and authority operation directories and the source material, then verifies that the sender's retained acceptance and retrieval can still be observed offline using the sender's own account/profile and retained return store.

An older valid restored journal can hide later work. Combining several old journals does not manufacture an independent rollback witness. Omitted directories are always unknown. A selected packet digest authenticates an expected representation only under the operator's independent selection; it does not identify the globally latest packet or prove current authorization.

No new crash-durable transaction is introduced by this revision, so the new overview corpus is not described as new process-exit durability qualification. Existing crash-laboratory and transport lanes retain their own named scopes. Ordinary chat, group room integration, attachment settlement, general remote hosting, process isolation, dependency pinning, runtime upgrades, independent cryptographic review and physical-power-loss qualification are not claimed here.

### 186.7. Operating guide

These commands use existing explicit selections, not fixture credentials. Replace uppercase placeholders with your own paths and independently confirmed complete hexadecimal digests. Do not copy a test fixture's public seeds into use. Do not obtain trust merely by hashing bytes an untrusted sender has just substituted; the expected packet/return must be the selection you intend to observe.

First inspect a selected setup packet without opening any private store:

```bash
bash Vibechat.html exchange-overview --experimental \
  --packet SELECTED_SETUP_PACKET \
  --expect-packet FULL_SELECTED_SETUP_SHA256
```

Add only transfer stores that belong to that exact packet. The source directory is optional and normally belongs to the participant operating that source; do not copy private role directories merely to fill every row:

```bash
bash Vibechat.html exchange-overview --experimental \
  --packet SELECTED_SETUP_PACKET \
  --expect-packet FULL_SELECTED_SETUP_SHA256 \
  --setup-fetch-directory EXISTING_SETUP_RETRIEVAL
```

For a recipient, use its complete bound setup packet and the recipient's original identity/profile plus pinned sender fingerprint. The program prompts through the existing hidden-terminal path; no password argument is added:

```bash
bash Vibechat.html exchange-overview --experimental \
  --packet COMPLETE_BOUND_SETUP_PACKET \
  --expect-packet FULL_BOUND_SETUP_SHA256 \
  --recipient-directory EXISTING_RECIPIENT_OPERATION \
  --card ORIGINAL_RECIPIENT_CARD \
  --profile AUTHENTICATED_RECIPIENT_PROFILE \
  --contact FULL_PINNED_SENDER_FINGERPRINT
```

For a sender, use precisely the compose-or-later prefix selected when its Backpost return store was created, plus the independent return digest. Transport retention and sender acceptance appear separately:

```bash
bash Vibechat.html exchange-overview --experimental \
  --packet ORIGINAL_SENDER_SELECTED_PREFIX \
  --expect-packet FULL_PREFIX_SHA256 \
  --expect-return FULL_SELECTED_RETURN_SHA256 \
  --return-fetch-directory EXISTING_RETURN_RETRIEVAL \
  --sender-return-directory EXISTING_SENDER_RETURN_STORE \
  --card ORIGINAL_SENDER_CARD \
  --profile AUTHENTICATED_SENDER_PROFILE \
  --contact FULL_PINNED_RECIPIENT_FINGERPRINT
```

A cooperating trusted local caller may instead supply `--unlock-fd` through the predecessor private pipe/socket mechanism. Do not substitute a password on the command line, an environment secret, or a regular password file. A custom recovery salt can be requested through the inherited prompt option. The overview releases the account bridge in its exit path.

Append `--json` for automation that consumes observations; it is not an authorization channel. The output intentionally carries no runnable shell command or automatically filled private path. Use the actual original command help for a chosen action, supply its required explicit selections, and recheck the original view token for `operation-act`. Do not build a loop that interprets a closing coordination window as permission to send or finish without a new user choice.

Developer entry points:

```bash
bash Vibechat.html overviews
bash Vibechat.html overviews --full
bash Vibechat.html source vibe-native-overview --start 1 --lines 120
bash Vibechat.html impact vibe-native-overview
bash test.sh --html Vibechat.html --output ABSENT_RECEIPT_DIRECTORY overview
```

The new corpus runs the actual HTML/Bash entry point for selected sender observation, committed recipient display, refusal, carried-source decoy resistance and offline recovery. It is not presented as a separately administered two-person deployment. Section 187 distinguishes those invocations from the real owned authority fixture and the explicitly seeded transfer projections.

### 186.8. Primary-source research and applied distinctions

Four primary sources were reviewed online for this increment, retained as T211–T214. The summaries below are research context; the implementation conclusions are identified as local design choices rather than claims that a standard specifies Crosspost.

**T211 — SQLite, “Isolation In SQLite,” https://www.sqlite.org/isolation.html.** The documentation describes isolation between database connections and the scope of a WAL read snapshot. Our application conclusion is narrower and different: opening several unrelated stores one after another supplies no shared simultaneous snapshot. Crosspost therefore preserves per-store observations and their limitations rather than trying to rename them a transaction. This review does not upgrade SQLite or qualify the observed runtime.

**T212 — Python documentation, `sys.addaudithook`, https://docs.python.org/3/library/sys.html#sys.addaudithook.** Python describes audit hooks as instrumentation and explicitly not a sandbox. The local test design uses them to refuse exercised socket events, with an active negative control. Native-child confinement and hostile-code resistance are excluded. The documentation endpoint currently presents newer Python documentation; the actually tested interpreter version is recorded separately in section 187, not inferred from that page.

**T213 — RFC 8098, Message Disposition Notification, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8098.html.** The notification model emphasizes correlation to the original message, and displaying a message does not guarantee reading or understanding. Crosspost is not an MDN implementation; the relevant local choices are exact original-message selection and refusal to turn acknowledgement acceptance or inspection into a human-reading claim.

**T214 — RFC 3339, Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3339.html.** This specifies an interoperable timestamp representation. Our inference is that a correctly formatted timestamp does not authenticate or synchronize a host's current clock. The existing Waypost UTC rendering and separate operation-eligibility clock retain their explicit local status. No trusted-time service is introduced.

The 37 infrastructure options remain intact and were not relabeled as freshly requalified hosting offers. All earlier technical-source records are retained; no old research date is overwritten to imply a new review.

### 186.9. Handoff and next decision

Two appended constitutional articles state that a combined view is not a combined transaction and that inspection does not create a new owner of state or authority. Letter 0047 records the same choice: build fewer places to look, not another signature family. All earlier articles and letters remain exact values in their original order.

The next useful feature should reduce the repeated local selection ceremony. A small explicit, session-local selection interface could retain public paths and hashes only while it is open, display the same original views, and ask for a deliberate choice before delegating any existing action. It should not persist passwords, create a second mailbox, infer account trust from transport, turn uncertainty into a retry, or move the original locks/guards into an independent state machine. Whether an already unlocked endpoint should provide that session remains a design decision; this revision does not claim that service exists.

The runtime and deployment prerequisites named by previous revisions remain prerequisites. No native-engine update, Nix lock, general browser integration, independently administered peer isolation, or security certification is implied by this local overview.

### 187.2. New overview evidence

The final Crosspost corpus passed **79 checks**, with **five actual HTML/Bash overview commands**, **12 setup-helper process invocations**, and a real owned authority process used before the observational tests. The overview test child recorded **211.110 seconds**. It observed preparation with zero application admissions, actual authority permission with zero admissions, explicit original commitment with one admission, and unchanged retained acknowledgement bytes. It verified typed selection, complete versus partial setup binding, source offer versus retrieval versus independent sender acceptance, literal command hints, omitted-state uncertainty, bounded terminal rendering and original operation guards.

The transfer histories used by the new projection corpus are explicitly seeded valid local states and real local source-history operations, **not new HTTPS response evidence**. Separately selected `handoff`, `publisher` and `returnwire` lanes execute their own transport scopes against the same final HTML. The new overview corpus does not inject a new durable transaction or claim additional physical persistence guarantees.

The actual carried commands exercised account-bound sender observation, committed recipient terminal display, a missing-return-selection refusal with no partial stdout, same-named current-directory decoy refusal-by-nonuse, and offline sender observation after operation directories and source material were removed. Those are the five overview invocations, not five independently administered participants. Both original encrypted account profiles remain byte-identical.

Direct overview calls recorded **zero socket audit events** after the fixture's deliberate authority work. An explicit child launcher installs the refusal hook before loading the carried command. Its negative control deliberately opens a socket and must fail with the hook's marker; only then is successful overview execution under that hook counted. Networking imports still exist, and Python audit hooks do not establish a hostile-code or native-child sandbox.

A restored lagging recipient anchor is reconciled through the inherited opening path while the original acknowledgement remains unchanged. Separately, repeated already-reconciled observations leave retained content bytes unchanged. An interleaved source disable demonstrates why the view is sequential, not atomic. An artificially late observation clock shows historical accepted acknowledgements without renewing the old setup windows; actual setup and authority steps used real wall time and their original deadlines.

### 187.3. Rejected and incomplete work

The first direct-development fixture attempted to seed a retrieval journal using the wrong predecessor row shape. The original validation refused. The test was corrected to the inherited `number` plus `verified-retained` outcome representation and rerun; production journal validation was not relaxed. An earlier source-only revision of the corpus passed 71 checks in 138.746 seconds, but it is superseded and is not the final result.

Candidate 1, HTML SHA-256 `e1a11c9edab3c9e9bdd8469ed5b08a1dc8983383af9b9fec66bba3c7dd071f00`, was rejected when the child socket-control check failed. The test had relied on `PYTHONPATH` and `sitecustomize`; the environment's existing startup hook took precedence, so the intended child hook was not actually installed. Direct-call auditing had been active, but that did not excuse the missing child control. The candidate's partial matrix was stopped. The test now uses an explicit audited launcher for both extracted and actual Bash execution, with the deliberate negative control retained. The public guidance was also reviewed for stale revision pointers and compact human output.

Candidate 2, HTML SHA-256 `5a887d7b062cef2884fdb16049eaed35b255ea19e5a252759019d1ef71092b69`, completed the corrected 79-check overview corpus but failed the carrier lane. The rewritten brief had omitted the predecessor's explicit transport-versus-sender-verification warning, while two current-guide assertions still expected the previous sections 184–185/185. The warning was restored, and those assertions now require Crosspost and the actual sections 186–187/187. Neither packet verification nor account acceptance changed. That partial matrix was stopped and not promoted.

The accepted third candidate received the complete fresh selected replay above. Earlier successful lane invocations are not borrowed to fill gaps in this final fixed-hash record. A first extraction launched with an insufficient tool-call timeout was interrupted and is not counted as reproduction. Completed candidate-1 and candidate-2 rebuilds were historical development checks; only the final candidate's independent extraction/build/repack below establishes this release's reproducibility.

### 187.5. Runtime and qualification boundary

Observed runtime: Python **3.13.5**; Python TLS library **OpenSSL 3.5.5 27 Jan 2026**; SQLite **3.46.1**; native executable **OpenSSL 3.5.5 27 Jan 2026 (Library: OpenSSL 3.5.5 27 Jan 2026)**. These are observations, not a new dependency pin or runtime upgrade. The prior fixed-engine and deployment prerequisites remain in force. The browser/native cryptographic code is unchanged; passing selected interoperability and review corpora is not an independent audit or certification.

Crosspost establishes no distributed transaction, current global authority view, trusted clock, human reading, independent remote-disk observation, secure erasure, forward secrecy, post-compromise security, hostile-process confinement or ordinary-room activation. These remain specific boundaries, not excuses to erase the useful implemented local workflow.

### 187.6. Archive closure

The release archive contains exactly `Vibechat.html`, `BOOTSTRAPROSE.md` and `test.sh`, with no duplicate names or extra directory entries. The release script requires successful selected fixed-hash receipts and byte-identical reproduction before creating it, tests ZIP CRCs, independently extracts all three members, compares each with its fixed input and runs manifest verification on the extracted HTML. A final delivery link is published only after those checks succeed. The ZIP's own hash is an external closure value, not placed recursively inside itself.

The exact received bootstrap byte span is checked again before packing and after extraction. This record's path names describe the build environment used for tests; they are not required installation paths for a recipient. The artifact contains its own sources and reproducible workshop commands, not the build machine's temporary directories.

### 187.8. Attributed handoff — GPT-6 Astra Pro, Crosspost officer, October 10, 2026

I chose a projection instead of another workflow engine. The view is useful because it does not smooth away the distinctions that earlier revisions earned: a packet can be offered but not retained, retained but not adopted, permitted but not committed, and acknowledged but not read. Bringing these together should help an operator understand a real selected exchange without transferring authority to the overview itself.

The most useful review failures were in our evidence machinery. A purported child audit hook was not the hook that actually ran, and a rewritten current brief lost a needed warning while two assertions still pointed to old sections. The negative control and carrier checks caught those errors; neither failure was explained away by a passing neighbouring test. The accepted record belongs only to the final bytes.

The next officer should make explicit selection less repetitive, keeping the original account unlock, exact hashes and action guards. Do not turn the list of next commands into an automatic plan, persist a password for convenience, or invent a second inbox to make the screen look unified. Distribution stays one HTML; the extracted workshop remains the place for development. The human-sized goal is still a small group communicating with records they can inspect, recover and carry away.

## Additional local crash and TURN qualification

The local03 facilities add real failure injection against the same compiled carrier `2d45bde4713b3b5335d2a4e94a831f05db7d69278652cb23ef60d9166bc35505`. No application or protocol source changed in this turn.

- `make webrtc-crash` passed **94 assertions**, 47 over direct ICE and 47 over coturn/TCP, in **131.675 seconds** (`artifacts/local03-crash-confirmed/report.json`). Chromium confirms a real page-renderer crash through its crash notification; native writers and the removed-member endpoint exit with SIGKILL (-9). Reopening explicitly with the endpoint capability restores the exact identity and retained ciphertext IDs. The interrupted 262145-byte file remains unsavable until inventory reconciliation completes it byte for byte. Signed room removal survives abrupt endpoint termination, and withheld old-epoch messages remain refused over actual RTC traffic.
- `make webrtc-failures` passed **54 assertions** in **52.392 seconds** (`artifacts/local03-turn-failures/report.json`). A deliberately wrong disposable TURN credential produces actual Chromium ICE error **401**. Killing the configured coturn service produces actual ICE error **701**. Both fail without a signed offer, retain relay-only policy, close the failed peer connection, leave no live link and emit zero data-channel frames. Restarting the same loopback service with its existing private secret and explicitly requesting credentials restores encrypted messages, interrupted-file recovery and three-participant membership enforcement over selected relay routes.
- All **13** checkout regressions passed again in **75.946 seconds** after these local harness changes. Syntax compilation and Git whitespace checks also passed.
- New pre-handoff selections: `--check crash` and `--check turn-failures`. These are optional additions to the existing five defaults. Every report records both harness hashes, the selected carrier hash, restart mode and enabled failure controls; accounts, secrets and browser storage remain disposable and excluded from export.

The first crash attempt (`artifacts/local03-crash/report.json`) failed its direct lane waiting for a Playwright crash notification; the relay lane passed. The harness now observes Chromium's CDP `Inspector.targetCrashed` notification as well and allows a bounded 30-second notification wait. The complete rerun passed both lanes. This was a harness observation correction, not an application fix. Failed evidence remains local and is not exported as a pass.

These crash assertions concern records already acknowledged/exportable before termination. They do not claim filesystem power-loss durability or interruption at every storage-write boundary. A renderer crash is narrower than killing the entire Chromium browser process. TURN controls exercise actual service rejection/outage and explicit recovery, with unchanged application gathering deadlines; they do not model every network impairment.

Reproduce with `nix develop --command make webrtc-crash OUTPUT=artifacts/crash` and `nix develop --command make webrtc-failures OUTPUT=artifacts/turn-failures`. Existing output directories are refused. Local test facilities stay in Git; Pro receives this scope and the passing JSON reports in the three-file prose appendix.

Public-provider research is dated and linked in README.md. Cloudflare's STUN requires no credentials. ## Built-in STUN checker qualification

The selected carrier is `17ae2b0cddb3757940367df4a036fd2ee5c2cde85ffddbdd489966719ce0f9e0` (8,657,598 bytes). Connections now includes all **74 owner-supplied STUN possibilities**, preserved exactly. Opening the checker sends nothing. Explicit selected/all checks gather with temporary browser peer connections, at most two concurrently, with a six-second limit per server. Only an actual server-reflexive candidate counts as success; host-only results do not. Stop, closing Connections, page exit and account lock cancel active probes. Results retain URL/status/timing and bounded error codes in page memory, without candidate addresses, SDP or message records.

**Use working servers** explicitly applies at most three successes observed within the last five minutes, ordered by gather time, for subsequent signed connections. Checking alone never changes ICE configuration. Applying clears relay-only policy and refuses to replace an unresolved managed TURN lease. Gather time is not ping latency. The catalog is a set of possibilities, not a claim of availability, operator permission or TURN service; a successful STUN response does not prove peer connectivity on every network.

Separate real probes obtained public candidates from Cloudflare and Google; the remaining services were not live-qualified. All 81 fixture probes closed, with a peak of two active. Codex opened and visually inspected the actual rendered desktop and 390×844 mobile screenshots; the controls and result table were readable without visible overlap.
- **92 inherited browser assertions**, 96.381 seconds (`artifacts/checker-browser/test-report.json`), including the checker's managed TURN overwrite refusal.
- **87 real WebRTC chat assertions**, 72.261 seconds (`artifacts/checker-rtc/report.json`), across direct ICE and disposable coturn/TCP, including encrypted messages, byte-exact attachments, reconnect and membership controls.
