## Local reproduction guide

# Vibechat

A local development repo for the self-contained Vibechat HTML/Bash application, imported from ChatGPT Pro's rev0043 release. The original release is preserved at the Git tag `received/rev0043`. The editable sources live in `workshop/`; the built application is `build/Vibechat.html`.

## Run locally

On Linux with Nix:

```sh
nix develop
make setup
make build
make doctor
make serve
```

Open the capability URL printed by the server. The default development server uses memory only and listens on `127.0.0.1:8765`. To choose persistent storage or another port, pass `SERVE_ARGS`, for example `make serve SERVE_ARGS='--data-dir /your/private/records --port 8775'`. Each identity needs its own endpoint process, port and records directory.

`flake.lock` pins the Linux toolchain, Chromium, coturn and OpenSSL. `requirements.lock` pins Python dependencies, including Playwright; `package-lock.json` pins TypeScript 5.8.3. Installation happens only in `make setup`. Builds and tests use installed tools. A short project-local `.tmp` directory keeps Chromium Unix socket paths within their length limit. The Nix shell supplies the C++ runtime needed by Python wheels and uses its Node executable for Playwright's driver.

Without Nix, install Python 3.12, Node, Chromium, coturn, Clang with `wasm-ld`, Make and OpenSSL with ML-KEM-768/ML-DSA-65 support, then run `make setup`. Set `VIBECHAT_CHROMIUM` or `VIBECHAT_TURNSERVER` to select installed executables. `make doctor` checks native dependencies and algorithms. The inherited driver supports a system Chromium; no browser download is hidden in a test.

## Free connection defaults

New browser pages start with Cloudflare’s free STUN service, `stun:stun.cloudflare.com:3478`. No account, username, API key, credit card or personal TURN credential is needed. The service is contacted only when you explicitly create/apply a WebRTC signal. The Connections preset can switch to Local only or custom ICE configuration; locking clears ICE configuration and credentials. Profiles do not retain them. STUN helps discover a public address for direct peer connections; it cannot relay traffic when NAT/firewall policy prevents those connections. [Cloudflare’s service documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/realtime/turn/faq/).

Connections also carries all 74 owner-supplied STUN candidates under **Find working STUN servers**. **Check selected** probes one; **Check all** automatically works through the list with at most two temporary peer connections at once and a six-second limit per server. **Stop checking**, closing Connections, or locking cancels pending checks. A response is successful only when Chromium returns a server-reflexive candidate; host candidates alone are insufficient. The UI retains only URL, result, gathering duration, checked time and bounded ICE error codes in page memory, never candidate addresses or chat records. Loading/unlocking the app does not run these probes.

**Use working servers** selects up to three successful results checked within five minutes and applies them to the next signed connection. It requires an explicit click, leaves existing links unchanged and refuses to replace an unresolved managed TURN lease. The supplied candidates are possibilities, not promises of free/public access or current uptime. A six-second miss describes this browser's observation, not a global outage; gather time is not RTT. STUN success does not prove peer connectivity or TURN availability.

`make stun-checker OUTPUT=artifacts/checker` tests checker behavior with local browser fixtures. `make stun-checker-public OUTPUT=artifacts/checker-public` additionally performs explicit real Cloudflare/Google checks and captures desktop/mobile screenshots. The optional pre-handoff check `--check stun-checker` uses only fixtures.

Provider research and live checks on 2026-10-11:

| Service | Account-free option | Suitability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Cloudflare](https://developers.cloudflare.com/realtime/turn/faq/) | Free, unlimited STUN | Default; actual Chromium obtained a server-reflexive candidate. TURN’s 1,000 GB/month allowance requires an account key and can bill beyond it. |
| [rstream](https://rstream.io/tools/turn-server) | Free one-hour TURN evaluation credentials, no account | Manual short-lived test option linked from Connections; the provider restricts this generator to evaluation, not recurring automated app use. |
| [Metered Open Relay](https://www.metered.ca/tools/openrelay/) | Public static-auth secret is documented; standard free plan requires signup | Public TCP relay endpoints produced no candidates in our bounded probe and their TCP connections timed out here. Not selected as a working default. |
| [freeSTUN](https://freestun.net/) | Advertises shared `free/free` TURN access | No relay candidates within our bounded probe; website returned HTTP 403 here. Not selected as a working default. |
| [PeerJS](https://github.com/orgs/peers/discussions/1172) | Free signaling | Its free TURN service was discontinued; signaling does not replace TURN. |

Public-provider availability and terms can change. The shared TURN probe failures describe this host’s observations, not a global outage claim. No account-free recurring TURN relay was verified here. Account-free STUN is the selected usable default; unrestricted-network connectivity is not promised. Existing native-managed TURN and pasted standard ICE configurations remain available.

`make webrtc-public-stun OUTPUT=artifacts/public-stun` explicitly exercises the public default; `tools/pre_handoff.py --check public-stun` selects the same opt-in check. The regular local direct/relay tests select Local only or ephemeral coturn before gathering, so routine test runs do not contact public ICE providers.

## Development and tests

Edit the named files in `workshop/`. Edit the shell, layout and CSS in `workshop/Vibechat.template.html`. The build copies just those declared inputs to temporary staging, compiles TypeScript and WASM with the original build routine, regenerates the deterministic review packet through its original generator, refreshes source bindings in dependency order, then repacks and verifies the HTML. Binding refresh validates each existing authored body digest and retains its digest convention and exact JSON style; it changes binding metadata and derived body hashes while preserving authored content and signed vectors. It leaves the received root-level carrier and editable generated snapshots intact. `make repack` packages source changes that do not need a crypto rebuild; stale generated source hashes are refused.

```sh
make test-local                          # Carrier and revision-handoff regressions
make test-packets                        # Compare binding snapshots with original corpus generators
make webrtc                             # Actual direct ICE and coturn/TCP paths
make webrtc-lifecycle                   # Durable restart, interrupted files and membership removal
make webrtc-crash                       # Actual Chromium renderer crash and native SIGKILL recovery
make webrtc-failures                    # Rejected TURN credentials, killed coturn and explicit recovery
make test LANE=browser                   # Inherited real-navigation browser workflows
make test LANE=interop                   # Native ↔ TypeScript/WASM comparisons
make test LANE=carrier                   # Carrier integrity and exact repacking
make test                               # All 41 inherited default lanes; several minutes per long lab
make test-lab LANE=sightlab TIMEOUT=1200  # Same carried corpus, explicit overall budget for a busy host
```

The inherited driver has 41 ordinary lanes; `bench` is an additional alias for its interoperability benchmark and is not in `all`. `make test` requires ordinary localhost browser navigation. Each run writes to a new private directory in `artifacts/`, with the exact carrier hash, statuses and outputs. You can set `OUTPUT=artifacts/a-specific-run`; an existing receipt directory is refused. An unavailable tool is reported separately from a failed assertion.

The inherited driver caps most long native labs at 480 seconds and its native workflows at 900 seconds. On a heavily loaded machine, `make test-lab` runs the exact carried script with an explicitly selected overall process budget and a separate hash-bound report. It supports `settlementlab`, `orderlab`, `passagelab`, `sightlab`, `decisionlab`, `landinglab`, `islelab`, and the native workflow lanes from `message` through `overview`. This changes the test process budget; all application expiry, clock and five-second freshness assertions still run. Passageglass now creates fresh signed fixtures for independent scenarios so a long corpus cannot age every later request past its five-minute lifetime. The native message positive flow also creates a fresh fixture after its negative controls and dispatches the signed 30-second request before read/replay inspection. Crash/replay within a scenario still uses its exact original request. The dispatch fault-server fixture uses a separate 60-second readiness budget. Known failures and incomplete runs remain recorded in the handoff notes.

Our WebRTC harness starts independent native CLI processes and navigates the built HTML. It checks account unlock, explicit identity pinning and signed room selection; altered-SDP refusal; encrypted messages and fragmented files; candidate-pair traffic and route type; explicit disconnect/reconnect; and lock teardown. The direct path uses no ICE server. The relay path starts real coturn on loopback with an ephemeral REST secret and tests native-issued temporary credentials over TURN/TCP. Route checks follow each transport's current [`selectedCandidatePairId`](https://www.w3.org/TR/webrtc-stats/#dom-rtctransportstats-selectedcandidatepairid), then require nominated, succeeded pairs and bidirectional traffic. Screenshots and a JSON report are retained. The crash variant deliberately terminates a page renderer through Chromium CDP and kills native endpoints with SIGKILL, then verifies retained identity, ciphertext IDs, byte-exact file recovery and durable membership removal. This covers acknowledged records, rather than a power interruption during a filesystem write. The TURN failure variant uses a real rejected credential and a killed local coturn process: relay-only gathering must fail visibly, emit no signed offer, close the failed peer connection and send no data-channel frames. Restarting the same service and explicitly requesting credentials must restore the ordinary encrypted three-peer workflow. These tests use the application’s actual ICE deadlines.

See [LOCAL_HANDOFF.md](LOCAL_HANDOFF.md) for the current executed results, changes and next steps. [BOOTSTRAPROSE.md](BOOTSTRAPROSE.md) remains the exact received project history; its execution claims retain their original dates and scopes.

## Continue with ChatGPT Pro

Commit the source changes and update `LOCAL_HANDOFF.md`, then export:

```sh
make build
make export OUTPUT=artifacts/vibechat-handoff
```

The default ZIP contains exactly three files: the selected built `Vibechat.html`, `BOOTSTRAPROSE.md`, and matching `test.sh`. The prose file preserves the received history and appends our local handoff notes, reproduction guide and selected receipts. Editable application sources remain embedded in the carrier; local infrastructure stays in this Git repository. A checksum and commit/file-hash receipt are written beside the ZIP. Export uses `git archive` and refuses uncommitted or untracked source changes. It includes no ignored browser profiles, caches or account directories. Add selected JSON execution receipts with `tools/handoff.py export --evidence PATH`; receipts for another carrier hash are refused. `--layout repository` explicitly selects the larger developer archive.

Upload that ZIP to Pro and ask it to read the final “Local repository continuation” appendix in `BOOTSTRAPROSE.md` first. Let it continue work and return its updated carrier, bootstrap and driver. Preserve our local infrastructure when importing the returned trio.

`make pre-handoff OUTPUT=artifacts/next-release` builds into a private output, runs checkout regressions, packet generators, carrier verification and both WebRTC harnesses, collects exact-carrier receipts, and exports `release.zip` only after those selected checks pass. To choose checks or include native corpora, invoke `tools/pre_handoff.py --check carrier --check lifecycle --native-lane islelab ...`. The optional `--check crash` and `--check turn-failures` add the destructive process tests with disposable storage. `--fresh-rebuild` stages a temporary three-file export into a fresh source tree, installs locked Python/npm dependencies in new directories, compiles canonically, requires the exact selected carrier hash and runs real-navigation browser smoke. Nix and package download caches may be reused. `--evidence PATH` includes additional completed passing reports for this exact carrier.

Stage the returned ZIP without overwriting our repo:

```sh
make stage ZIP=/path/to/returned.zip OUTPUT=incoming/rev0044
git diff --no-index -- workshop incoming/rev0044/workshop
```

Staging checks archive paths, duplicates, member types and byte limits, verifies the carrier with our current verifier, and extracts named sources without executing incoming code. `review.json` lists source changes and HTML/shell/CSS frame changes. Review and merge those changes on a branch, preserve the local facilities, build again and run the affected tests. The prose appendix gives Pro's starting commit; the local ZIP receipt retains all three file hashes. The original carrier's `compare` and `impact` commands remain available for protocol-level review.

## 188. Frontporch — an ordinary invitation path

### 188.1. Owner direction and bounded choice

The owner asked whether an average human would tolerate the friction, understand the terminology, and be able to open one HTML file, discover or invite friends, and begin chatting. The received Crosspost recommendation favored fewer places to look. The local continuation supplied extensive native/browser infrastructure but not that repository itself. This session chose the ordinary browser interface as the useful integration point. It did not create a new authority, acknowledgement family, account service, daemon or operational journal.

The implementation reduces separate card, fingerprint, room, offer and answer operations to one guided exchange. It does not claim that three manual file handoffs are the eventual consumer answer. No independent user usability study was performed. An invitation service and a relay policy remain architectural decisions requiring an explicit service/trust/privacy review, not defaults that can honestly be inferred from a self-contained HTML artifact.

### 188.2. The first road a person sees

Open Vibechat.html in a supported browser. Enter a name and password, or generate a strong password with the helper. Save both in a password manager: the identity is derived from the supplied credentials, and no password-reset service is introduced. The helper uses 24 random bytes; password visibility is a deliberate toggle. Ordinary device saving is checked, while technical provider/storage/connection controls are inside a closed Advanced disclosure. A temporary session is an explicit one-checkbox choice. Passwords are cleared from the entry field after unlock.

In the browser provider, the saving default selects encrypted IndexedDB storage. In an explicitly selected native bridge it selects the native endpoint’s durable encrypted store. This difference is deliberate; choosing a native bridge is not an implicit browser install. Browser storage can be cleared or evicted, and the interface says to export records for backup. This revision does not store a password or export a private key to make login convenient.

The empty workspace offers Invite a friend and Open an invitation rather than a cryptographic setup checklist. The ordinary two-person chat title shows the friend’s name. On narrow screens the technical sidebar is hidden; More retains Connections, Rooms/profile, Export records, Research, Custody, Workshop and Lock. Existing room and people tools are not removed. Some inherited technical status badges remain; this revision is not a claim that every advanced screen has been redesigned.

### 188.3. The invitation, from both sides

1. Alice chooses **Invite a friend → Make an invitation**. Vibechat prepares a small public invitation file. This step does not start a peer connection or contact an application service. Alice sends the file through a messenger or another channel she already uses. Bob also needs Vibechat.html; the file is not an installer or a self-opening chat application.
2. Bob chooses **Open an invitation**. Reading the file previews Alice and the complete identity code without trusting the contact or starting a connection. They compare the full grouped 64-hex code independently, such as over a known call or in person. Bob explicitly confirms that comparison and chooses **Verify & make reply**. Vibechat pins the verified contact through the existing mechanism and prepares the existing signed, recipient-bound offer inside a reply file. Bob sends that reply to Alice and keeps his tab open.
3. Alice opens Bob’s reply, compares Bob’s full code and explicitly chooses **Verify & start chat**. The signed offer is authenticated before room or ICE creation. Vibechat creates the existing owner-signed two-person room, or reuses an eligible existing one, and prepares the signed answer and room in a final connection file. Alice sends that file back. Bob opens it and explicitly chooses **Join chat**. The guide applies the original answer and room checks, then shows the conversation when the connection is ready.

The independent comparison is not silently replaced with first-use trust. An exactly matching contact already pinned in the unlocked profile does not need repeated manual comparison. The guide handles the plumbing, not the decision about who the friend is.

Each outgoing step offers native file sharing only when supported, plus Save file and Copy instead. A selectable text fallback remains when clipboard access is unavailable. A successful share API call or file save does not prove the other person received it. Invitations normally occupy roughly 4.5 KB, replies 10 KB and final files 15 KB; these are format-scale observations, not a fixed-size guarantee. Both tabs must remain open for setup. Files carry a ten-minute expiry; the live flow also tracks a monotonic session deadline. Clock checks do not create trusted time.

### 188.4. Wrapper admission and unchanged authority

The new envelope is `format: "vibechat-friend-invite-v1", v: 1`, with `invite`, `reply` and `ready` kinds. It has a random 32-hex invitation identifier, bounded expiry, exact kind-specific field sets and a maximum admitted size of 262,144 bytes. Existing strict JSON admission rejects duplicate keys and ambiguous representations. Replies bind the exact locally prepared invitation through `replyTo`; final files bind the exact reply and pending session. Own invitations, another invitation’s replies, unexpected fields, expired inputs and wrong-session answers are refused.

**The outer invitation wrapper is not a new signed protocol.** Public cards, existing signed signal-v2 offers/answers and existing signed room policy retain their original authenticity contracts. The wrapper correlates these objects with a tab-local flow. A rehashed forged signal still fails the existing ML-DSA verification. The final room must have exactly the two selected identities and the original one-tip room chain; a hidden third member or corrupted room signature cannot enter via the guide. The offer and answer target identities and roles remain exact. No cryptographic primitive, signed signaling format, room format, native account implementation, worker payload or vendor cryptographic source was changed.

Reading an invitation alone does not pin a contact, create a room or start ICE. Explicit continuation may perform those actions through the original controls. Repeated accepted files are idempotent in the same live flow. No invitation code implies a discoverable global handle, no address book is uploaded, and no new HTTP/WebSocket rendezvous is configured. The received STUN preset remains available; TURN remains a separately configured relay facility rather than free capacity invented by this revision.

### 188.5. Cancellation, locks, reconnect and durability

Pending setup belongs to the live tab. Lock, reload or an expired setup requires a fresh exchange; saved chats do not reconstruct an old live offer. Lock clears pending invitation bytes and identity previews. Confirmed contact pins, accepted rooms and previously persisted messages remain under their original storage rules. A cancellation does not claim to recall a file already shared or erase an accepted room.

These steps are **not one atomic transaction**. A contact may have been explicitly pinned or a room accepted before a later network operation fails. The interface and current status preserve this distinction. Same-owner reconnection reuses an eligible existing epoch-one two-member `chat-*` room; a reverse-owner invitation can still create another room. Reconnection still requires fresh handoffs, not an automatic rendezvous or background reconnection service.

Journey testing exposed a real lifecycle edge in the previous client: a closing data channel removed its link but did not necessarily close its parent peer connection. The client now closes the parent idempotently and clears the associated handlers/partial buffers. Answerer connections are tracked before `ondatachannel` attaches a link. Provider/identity generation and pending-flow guards prevent late callbacks from resurrecting a workspace or publishing fresh connection output after Lock. The final journey test covers established connections, not-yet-bound answerers and an intentionally delayed offer callback.

### 188.6. Workshop and preservation

The carrier has 121 named sources: 80 byte-identical predecessor sources, 40 changed named sources and one addition, `first_run_checks.py`. No named source was removed. The frame changes separately. The changed named set contains ten directly maintained sources plus 30 dependency-binding metadata documents; those metadata refreshes do not amount to executing the corresponding laboratory suites. The new first-run harness is exposed as the `justworks` lane, giving 42 selectable lanes excluding the `bench` alias. It uses the original browser/WebRTC support rather than a replacement cryptographic mock.

Direct work includes `client.js`, the HTML/CSS frame, `dev.py`, `test.sh`, the browser and WebRTC UI harness adapters, and current status/research/lineage/constitution/letter guidance. Prior advanced regression tests now explicitly open their technical controls and select their intended temporary-storage fixture; their security assertions were not removed. Existing historical evidence remains byte-identical. Constitutional article C118 and letter 0048 record the humane-first-road constraint. The 37 infrastructure option records and earlier technical-source entries remain preserved as values with their original dates; they were not relabeled as freshly qualified services.

All changes were made in the canonical extracted workshop and repacked. The external test.sh matches its carried source. The owner’s full received bootstrap, including local Git/Nix/browser/native facilities and previous qualification receipts, is retained exactly between the markers above. The actual local repository and its private build/test stores were not supplied or modified. Merge reviewed source/frame changes into that repository while retaining its pinned tools, tests and execution records; do not substitute this three-file distribution for the repository. No account/profile/password/private-key test stores belong in the ZIP.

### 188.7. Primary-source review on October 11, 2026

Research ledger entries T215–T218 record these primary documentation checks and their bounded uses:

- W3C, WebRTC: Real-Time Communication in Browsers — https://www.w3.org/TR/webrtc/ — peer-connection APIs are not an application friend directory; existing signed signaling still needs a handoff or a deliberately selected service.
- Cloudflare, Realtime TURN FAQ — https://developers.cloudflare.com/realtime/turn/faq/ — distinguish the retained account-free STUN setting from authenticated TURN relay capacity and universal reachability.
- MDN, Navigator.share — https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/share — detect sharing support and retain file/copy fallbacks; context, activation and permission requirements remain relevant.
- MDN, Storage quotas and eviction criteria — https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Storage_API/Storage_quotas_and_eviction_criteria — disclose clearing/eviction and keep export/backup separate from local saving.

No public STUN sweep, provider account, installation, pricing refresh, service provisioning or public relay deployment was performed. Research is design input, not live operational qualification.

### 188.8. Next acceptance gate

Run the first-road harness with ordinary navigation required on the owner’s local browser facilities, without a native-RPC projection. Exercise the default embedded worker and actual browser IndexedDB persistence, reload/recovery, clipboard/file saving, and native Web Share on supported desktop/mobile browsers. Test the exact Bash/HTML parser and effective CSP before making a runtime policy-enforcement claim. Then exercise two independently administered devices and restrictive networks using an explicitly reviewed relay. None of these is established by the local fixture here.

After those checks, reduce the remaining three handoffs with a concrete, opt-in rendezvous design: define who operates it, what metadata it sees, how an invitation expires, where relay credentials come from, how outages appear, and how it preserves the existing independent identity check. Do not choose an unaudited public signaling endpoint or publish a contact directory merely to make a demo look automatic. The product goal remains an understandable invitation and a dependable conversation; another protocol family is not the default next step.

### 189.3. First-road findings and their limits

The final journey generated and opened all three UI handoffs in independent Chromium contexts, enforced full identity comparison, refused altered/expired/misbound files, established actual RTCDataChannels, sent encrypted text in both directions and transferred a byte-exact **65,537-byte file**. Captured frames were scanned for the test plaintext and carried the existing PQ envelopes. File SHA-256: `237356e18b503616912abb8ffaed3a72591e397d4ac294c4637917d48a3f529d`. Same-owner reconnect reused the existing room; locking closed established and unbound connections; native durable storage restored contact, room and message state; delayed callbacks did not resurrect setup. Desktop/mobile-width layouts were rendered and checked for overflow. Native OS share sheets were not exercised.

The local TURN/TCP collaborator is a real socket-level test relay used with real browser RTC APIs, not a substituted message transport. Its credential and route assertions are local. This host exposed no useful direct ICE candidates under its managed WebRTC policy. No public TURN, arbitrary Internet NAT traversal, production provider account, independent remote administrator or availability service was exercised. Opening the page and reading the initial invite caused no application-service contact in the observed HTTP/WebSocket scope; that observation is not a general claim that later explicit ICE negotiation is network-free.

Both ordinary `file://` and localhost navigation returned administrator-policy blocks. The test did not disable or alter policy, HTTPS checking, browser security or host networking to get a pass. The allowed fallback renders the full carrier in a labeled about:blank Chromium fixture with an explicit native-RPC/digest adapter and native encrypted storage. The delivered default worker was tested separately against native cryptography under Node, not as a navigated browser-worker/login/storage chain. Synthetic IDB transaction unit checks in the older browser suite do not establish actual IndexedDB durability. The strict navigation-required run declines the fallback and exits 77.

**Inherited CSP parser observation:** the full-DOM parser reports that the existing Bash/HTML prefix leaves the meta CSP outside the parsed head, where it is ignored. This revision did not fix that carrier-prefix/parser issue. Static sealing correctly verifies the expected client/style hashes and policy text, but must not be described as proof that the browser enforced the policy. Ordinary-navigation policy behavior was unavailable here. Treat real parser/CSP qualification as an explicit next gate, not as a passed assertion borrowed from integrity checks.

No production readiness, security certification, secure erasure, arbitrary remote storage durability, physical-power-loss survival, forward secrecy, post-compromise security, universal reachability or human-reading proof is claimed. The new wrapper is unsigned coordination around the original authenticated objects. The profile, room and pending-network mutations remain non-atomic. The legacy `product_chat_integrated: false` status flag continues to refer to the separate experimental account/session laboratories; the current status now explicitly distinguishes that from the implemented ordinary-browser invitation guide.

### 189.8. Attributed handoff — GPT-6 Astra Pro, October 11, 2026

I chose to make the ordinary doorway legible. The old powers remain, but a new person should not have to understand a public-card transport, room policy and signed SDP before seeing a conversation. This revision puts that work behind one invitation guide and makes encrypted saving the visible default. The first-road test found a cleanup edge that the separate technical controls had not made obvious; that is a useful reason to keep testing the journey, not only the primitives.

The remaining friction is real. Three files and an independent identity comparison are still a lot to ask of a casual friend. I did not hide that with a fake discovery list, automatic trust or a public service chosen without review. The next revision should qualify the real browser/storage/share doorway and then remove handoffs through one concrete, accountable rendezvous/relay design. Retain the full history, but measure progress by people successfully talking to each other.

## 190. rev0045 / Doorstep — the arriving friend gets a first road

### 190.1. Intent and product boundary

The owner's continuing focus is “just werx.” I chose the arriving friend and the browser startup gate rather than another native protocol family. Frontporch already gathered public-card, room and signaling steps into one invitation guide. Doorstep removes the preceding instruction “open your own space, find the right panel, then import my file,” and repairs the parser boundary that could undermine the page's existing security policy.

The actual ordinary path is: open Vibechat.html; choose **Open invitation file** (or paste/drop); see **Invitation from …**, explicitly not verified; enter a name and password; choose **Open this invitation**; continue in the existing independent-identity review. With no file, the same name/password doorway leads to the empty workspace's Invite a friend and Open an invitation actions. Advanced provider/storage/connection controls remain available, not prerequisites. Outgoing invitation help now names the first-screen file action.

This does not eliminate the three files, ask a messenger to upload anything automatically, configure a provider, or add a contacts address book. Both people still need the HTML and a live tab. Reply and final connection files depend on their original tab's exact connection state; the locked first screen refuses them with an explanation to return to that tab or begin a fresh invitation. It does not pretend a file can recreate a lost private peer-connection state.

### 190.2. The repaired Bash/HTML boundary

The received first line was `: '<!--'`. Actual Chromium parsing of the full received bytes rendered the shell fragment, produced `BackCompat`, and put the CSP meta element in BODY, where the browser reported it ignored. A valid static policy hash did not cure that placement.

The new first line is:

```text
</./dev/null : #><!--
```

Bash reads a colon no-op with its input redirected from `/./dev/null`; the following `#` starts a shell comment. There is no output, missing-file probe, or consumption of the caller's input pipe. The redirect is limited to that no-op, not the later native/password input. The dot component is essential: do not normalize the prefix into a different HTML token.

For the HTML tokenizer, `</.` is an invalid end-tag start and follows the standard's **bogus comment** recovery path to the next `>`. The following real comment encloses the shell bootstrap. The subsequent real doctype therefore remains effective, and the real head contains the policy before the executable client. This deliberately uses specified parse-error recovery; it is not a claim of fully conforming HTML source syntax or universal-browser qualification.

The policy's restrictions were not relaxed. Repacking refreshes the authorized client/style hashes as before. Doorstep's first parser pass uses the complete unmodified HTML, with no provider adapter, digest adapter, client rewrite, `bypass_csp`, or browser-policy change. It observes `CSS1Compat`, one policy in HEAD before the client, no rendered shell fragment, and execution of the hash-authorized client. It then inserts an unauthorized inline script, an unauthorized stylesheet, and a base element: their effects are absent and actual policy-violation events are observed. Inspector-driven test evaluation is not being mistaken for a normal script permission.

The enforced policy exposed old Playwright waits that evaluated strings inside the page. The four relevant test sources now use bounded inspector polling without in-page `eval`, rather than adding `unsafe-eval` or disabling CSP. The local TURN fixture also handles an expected peer disconnect during explicit lock/cleanup without an unhandled callback traceback; unrelated failures are not swallowed.

### 190.3. A bounded, untrusted invitation preview

The shared `friendDecode` path reuses the existing strict duplicate-key/field/version admission and public-card validation. The wrapper remains `vibechat-friend-invite-v1`; ordinary initial/reply/final signed inner records are unchanged. Files are bounded to 262,144 bytes, must decode as UTF-8, and retain the original ten-minute lifetime and bounded local-clock tolerance. The wrapper itself is still unsigned. Hash-consistent public keys are not an independently verified person.

Before unlock, successful admission stores only canonical public wrapper bytes and a bounded local deadline in the current tab. It starts no identity worker, signing provider, peer connection, network request, contact pin, room creation or database operation. The sender name is rendered as text and labeled unverified; the name/password inputs are not populated from it. The selected file and pasted text are cleared, and a removal action is visible. A serial invalidates late asynchronous results after cancellation/replacement. A timer discards expired previews; unlock rechecks both wall-clock expiry and its local monotonic deadline. Neither clock supplies trusted remote time or signed expiry.

Unlock carries the pending bytes directly into the original review. It does not check the “verified” box or bypass full independent fingerprint comparison. A failed or expired review leaves the successfully opened space usable and says what went wrong. Lock discards staging. Duplicate, oversized, malformed, expired, unknown-field and invalid-card inputs clear any previous enabled preview. Files dropped on the page cannot navigate away from an existing conversation; the invite surfaces accept a single file, while multi-file drops explain the limit instead of choosing a file silently.

The previously established session/generation guards, exact reply bindings, signed offer/answer checks, two-person room checks, and explicit trust decision remain. This is not a transaction across trust persistence, room creation and ICE. An explicitly accepted pin or room can remain after a later failure, as already disclosed by Frontporch.

### 190.4. Storage recovery is a choice, not a silent downgrade

The default is still encrypted device storage. Its database is opened before provider construction/key derivation. Synchronous denial, asynchronous open error, blocked open and an eight-second timeout share an actionable typed failure, while retaining the selected saving mode and entered password. A blocked tab is named as something to close. Failures release partial local state and keep the workspace locked.

The recovery surface states that temporary use will not load saved chats, will not delete stored chats, and will not automatically save new chats. Only the explicit **Continue without saving** action switches the save checkbox and underlying mode to memory and requests a new submit. Existing advanced temporary selection remains available. No private identity or password is cached to make this look instant.

A settled failed open cannot later resolve successfully: late success closes its handle, and a late upgrade aborts. A successful connection yields on `versionchange` by closing. These are open-lifecycle safeguards, not a claim that every browser storage operation has an eight-second deadline. They do not eliminate quota failures, browser clearing, transaction failure, or the need for backups. Actual IndexedDB durability was not qualified here; the test receipt labels synthetic callbacks and the UI submit-intent boundary explicitly.

### 190.5. Carried development, research, and preservation

There is one new named source, `doorstep_checks.py`, and one new selectable lane, `doorstep`. Current source mapping, no-clobber extraction/repack, impact routing, compare compatibility, brief/status, visible revision/title and the external/carried test driver are aligned to rev0045. The first-run lane now passes the initial file through the locked doorway and automatic review before completing the original actual RTC exchange. It deliberately reselects the owned local test relay after lock, because lock correctly erased the prior page-memory credentials.

The predecessor implementation code changes are limited to `client.js`, `dev.py`, `test.sh`, `first_run_checks.py`, `browser_checks.py`, and `webrtc_checks.py`. Original native implementations, compiled worker, TypeScript crypto/worker/KDF sources, WASM source/vendor material and the 4,281,710-byte inherited evidence payload remain exact. Thirty existing JSON documents have only declared source-binding records and their derived body hashes refreshed; their contract/vector/review contents and historical execution meanings are unchanged. A source digest is not a new execution receipt. Of the predecessor's 122 source/manifest blocks, 80 remain byte-identical. The added source brings the release to 122 named sources plus its separate manifest.

Constitution article C119 and attributed letter `letter-0049-doorstep` are appended. Every earlier article, letter, research source/turn note, all 37 infrastructure-option objects and previous lineage content remain. The complete received bootstrap is retained literally, not reconstructed from parsed text. No local Git repository was available, so no commit, branch, merge or Nix-build claim is made; the owner's existing repository continuation remains in the historical bytes.

Online review added four primary documentation entries, T219–T222, dated October 11, 2026:

- **T219 — WHATWG HTML parsing:** end-tag-open tokenization and initial insertion mode informed the explicit bogus-comment prologue and actual standards-mode check.
- **T220 — W3C CSP Level 3, meta delivery:** placement and order informed the runtime policy probes; hash presence alone is insufficient.
- **T221 — MDN IDBOpenDBRequest blocked event:** explicit blocked-open feedback and bounded late-callback cleanup.
- **T222 — MDN IDBDatabase versionchange event:** closing a held connection on a requested version change.

Their exact source URLs and use statements are in `research.json`. The WHATWG page fetched during this turn was dated October 9, 2026. These are design reviews, not an independent audit, provider account, pricing refresh or external reachability test. Older infrastructure options retain their own dates and were not blanket-revalidated. The previous default STUN endpoint remains unchanged; no public STUN/TURN probe or new service was used in these tests.

### 190.6. Next officer: remove real friction, not useful boundaries

First qualify the actual unmodified file/localhost browser startup, embedded worker, encrypted IndexedDB reload behavior and native sharing on an unrestricted desktop and real mobile browser. Keep the strict navigation-required lane strict; this host's administrator refusal is not a product pass, and a DOM/native fixture is not a replacement for that gate.

Then choose a concrete reviewed rendezvous/relay model with honest defaults, availability, metadata disclosure and operating limits. The ordinary friend should not need to understand three transported files or choose ICE servers. Do not solve that by publishing a people list, trusting an arbitrary matching name, silently pinning a supplied key, or inventing guaranteed free capacity. The job remains two people beginning a conversation, not increasing the number of protocols or test receipts.

Both ordinary `file:` navigation and owned localhost navigation returned `ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ADMINISTRATOR`. The strict run returned 77 and the driver labeled the lane unavailable. Only the synthetic eight-second timeout is accelerated for that model. The actual product deadline is unchanged. This is not a physical storage, eviction, origin-sharing, browser-restart or disk-survival qualification.

The complete first-friend UI journey uses a clearly named native-RPC/digest fixture, actual local TURN/TCP and actual RTCDataChannels. Post-quantum envelopes carry text in both directions and a byte-verified file; independent code comparison and signed inner-record/room checks remain active. The original rev0044 full-document probe reproduced `BackCompat`, a BODY policy, visible shell text and the ignored-policy console warning. Prefix prototypes established the silent Bash no-op and preserved caller input; the delivered Doorstep lane rechecks those properties against the final bytes.

The fixture now handles that expected peer-disconnect exception; the final sealed carrier was then rerun through all nine selected lanes. These earlier results are development history, not substituted for the final-hash receipts below.

### 191.6. Attributed continuation — GPT-6 Astra Pro, October 11, 2026

I made arrival a first-screen action and repaired the document boundary underneath it. An arriving friend should not have to navigate a workspace to discover where to put the invitation they already have. A browser refusing saving should not strand them after a costly password calculation or silently choose a less durable mode. These are ordinary product obligations, not optional protocol features.

The parser result also matters: a correctly printed security policy is not useful when the browser ignores it. I kept the restrictions and made the test observe actual blocked effects. The host still prevents the ordinary file/browser qualification, so I have recorded that as a concrete open gate rather than pretending a fixture proves it.

The received history and repository continuation remain intact. Carry this work into the owner's existing worktree, preserve its facilities, and keep the next revision focused on a real two-person opening experience. Three handoffs are still too many for the eventual default. Remove that friction through a reviewed concrete transport decision, not a fake directory, hidden upload or silent trust.


## Exact received rev0045 bootstrap — historical bytes end

## 192. rev0046 Reunion — ordinary returning-friend work

### 192.1. Owner direction and selected scope

The owner renewed `/run` against BOOTSTRAPROSE.md. The standing instruction remains “just werx”: would an ordinary person understand the next action and tolerate the friction? After checking the ordinary-navigation gate again and recording its continued administrator refusal, this revision improves returning to a person already known to the application. It does not add another experimental account/session protocol family or pretend to provision a remote service.

The new ordinary route is **Friends → Connect → Make connection invite → send it → open the reply → chat**. A live, eligible existing conversation uses **Open chat** instead, with no provider or connection operation merely to select it. An offline conversation provides the same Connect action alongside an honest local-message status. Friends are sorted by name and identity, with a short distinguishing key suffix; full codes remain available in the closed identity-tools disclosure. The list labels an actual ready peer as connected *in this tab*. It never infers that someone is offline, online elsewhere, available or reading.

The locked doorway from Doorstep remains intact. An initial `connect` file may be chosen, pasted or dropped before unlock, without deriving identity, pinning, persisting a room or starting a peer. The preview is explicitly untrusted. After unlocking, the guide checks the exact target identity; an equal display name is insufficient. Use the original name/password rather than creating a new identity when returning to a pinned friend.

### 192.2. Two files reuse the original authenticated objects

`vibechat-friend-connect-v1` is a bounded **unsigned coordination wrapper**, not a new signature, cipher or transport family. The original `vibechat-friend-invite-v1` three-file route remains for new people and legacy compatibility. Rev0045 does not interpret the new wrapper as a legacy invitation; both participants need the new release for the shortcut.

The `connect` wrapper has the exact fields `format`, `v`, `kind`, `invitation`, `expires`, `card`, `recipientName`, `signal` and `room`. It carries an unchanged signed v2 offer targeted to the selected exact pinned key and the unchanged signed two-person room chain. The `accept` reply has the exact fields `format`, `v`, `kind`, `invitation`, `expires`, `card`, `recipientName`, `replyTo` and `signal`. It carries the original signed answer. Its `replyTo` binds the full canonical initial wrapper, while the signed answer independently binds the original signed offer and session. There is no third file.

The initiating person must already have the selected exact verified contact. A recipient who has not pinned the sender still sees and must complete the full independent safety-code review; the shortcut does not silently accept that identity. Reading a wrapper is separate from signature verification and approval. The providers still verify the original signals and room signatures before applying them. Wrong recipient keys, wrong sessions, mismatched wrapper bindings and corrupt signatures do not consume the intended pending invitation.

Same-conversation reuse is intentionally narrow: an accepted, unchanged epoch-1 `chat-xxxxxxxx` room with exactly the two sorted member identities, owned by either participant, and without pending or declined room history. The current eligible room is preferred; otherwise selection is deterministic. This removes the earlier owner-only asymmetry. Changed, rotated, group or otherwise advanced histories are not flattened into a fresh epoch-1 policy. Those workflows remain advanced work, not a silently weakened shortcut.

Wrapper size stays bounded to 262,144 bytes. Existing strict JSON admission, canonical names, ten-minute wall-clock/monotonic local expiry, explicit action and tab-local lifetime rules remain. Wrapper metadata and expiry are not newly authenticated, local time is not trusted remote time, and a file share is not evidence of delivery or reading. Public wrapper metadata includes public identities, signed connection details and the selected public room policy; it is not a private address-book service.

### 192.3. A useful Cancel must work during preparation

The UI previously ignored Cancel while a friend task was busy. Testing also exposed a stale local connection label when data-channel opening and peer connection-state updates arrived in a different order. Both are repaired rather than hidden behind a longer spinner.

The ordinary guide now passes its owning flow into offer and answer preparation. Each newly constructed peer is registered with that flow before the first asynchronous offer/answer wait, including an answerer peer that has not yet received a data channel. Continuations recheck flow ownership, provider and generation. Cancel closes pending peers; late offer/answer results cannot restore output or a cancelled guide. A peer’s connected state alone is not enough to preserve it: it must have an associated usable ready channel. Lock still closes all pending and established peers and clears the visible Friends and invitation state.

Connection-state changes now refresh local Friends and conversation status; opening Friends also refreshes the list. User-facing interruption copy explains reconnecting without claiming that temporary-session data was saved to disk.

Accepted trust and rooms are **not transactionally undone** by Cancel. Provider verification, pin persistence, room import/creation and ICE are separate operations; an approved pin or accepted conversation can remain after later preparation fails. Cancellation does not erase previously shared files, revoke someone else’s permission, securely erase backups or prove that a remote participant has stopped. No automatic retry or persistent setup-resume journal was added.

### 192.4. Carried sources, research and continuity

`reunion_checks.py` is the single new named source. The existing first-run harness invokes it after establishing the original ordinary friendship, then returns to the original restoration/reconnection/lock tests. The test driver adds the `reunion` lane, explicit scope language and carrier assertions; discovery/impact, comparison through rev0046, extraction guidance, current status, constitution C120, letter-0050 and lineage are updated together. The browser/DOM/WebRTC advanced-identity tests now explicitly open the identity-tools disclosure rather than requiring the ordinary Friends screen to expose it.

The owned TURN fixture treats expected socket closure during deliberate disconnect as cleanup, while still allowing unrelated errors to surface. Its relay is an explicitly owned loopback collaborator, not a deployment recommendation or a public TURN claim. No installed dependencies, runtime policies or long-lived provider secrets were changed.

Research records **T223–T226**, checked October 11, 2026, cite primary documents: W3C WebRTC, the WebRTC project’s peer-connection guide, W3C WAI’s modal-dialog pattern and W3C Web Share. Their URLs and scoped uses are carried in `research.json`. The design separates signaling from peer data, local connection state from human presence, modal focus from broad accessibility qualification, and share-target handoff from recipient delivery. All 37 infrastructure option objects retain their original contents and dates; this is not a pricing or service-entitlement refresh.

Thirty inherited JSON memoranda/corpora receive only dependency byte/hash and their own defined digest refreshes. Their substantive bodies, vector/contract content, dependency path order and historical revision labels remain unchanged. Landingglass intentionally hashes its memorandum body separately from source bindings; that existing convention is preserved, not normalized into a different format. A source-binding refresh is not fresh execution of those historical laboratories. Original native, crypto, worker, vendor and historical evidence bytes remain unchanged, and no owner repository was mounted or rewritten.

### 192.5. What this release still does not solve

A first meeting still needs three file handoffs and independent full-code comparison. Returning friends still need two files, live tabs and a usable network path; both need the HTML. The new local Friends list does not find strangers or contacts on another device, and a lost name/password does not have an account-recovery service. Encrypted device saving is not a backup. Actual normal-browser persistence, embedded startup, mobile share and public-network reliability remain deployment gates.

The next ordinary-product task is not more knobs: qualify the real device path and make one reviewed rendezvous/relay choice that removes manual exchange while preserving explicit identity checks and clear service contact. Avoid silently expanding the narrow same-room shortcut into group membership, epoch rotation or globally current presence. The native account/session laboratories retain their inherited boundaries and are not integrated into ordinary browser chat by this revision.

### 193.6. Attributed continuation — GPT-6 Astra Pro, October 11, 2026

I made coming back to a known person an ordinary action. A person should not have to remember room ownership, public-card import, target selection and a third file merely to return to the same friend. The UI now reuses what they already verified and accepted, without calling a name trustworthy or a local connection human presence.

The most important correction was not a label: Cancel now owns the preparation it promises to stop, including the period before a peer has a data channel. That ownership is explicit and tested. Accepted trust and conversations are not falsely described as rolled back, and a temporary session is not described as saved storage.

This is a meaningful reduction, not the final arrival experience. Keep the original history and repository continuation intact. Qualify unrestricted real devices, then remove handoffs through an explicit reviewed service decision rather than a fake directory, hidden upload or silent trust. The next measure is still whether two ordinary people can begin and return to a real conversation.


## Exact received rev0046 bootstrap — historical bytes end

---

## 194. rev0047 Steady — ordinary composing and reading

### 194.1 The product job and reproduced defect

The owner continued “just werx” and clarified that there is only one product, Vibechat.html. Unrestricted startup was checked first and remained administratively unavailable. Rather than weakening the browser or adding another protocol laboratory, this continuation addressed ordinary conversation behavior. The received sendText awaited encryption/acceptance and then unconditionally cleared and focused the current input. A delayed-send regression showed that newly written text disappeared. sendFile also selected the room after awaiting File.arrayBuffer, allowing a conversation switch to change the destination.

The fix captures room, exact policy, members, channel, provider and session generation before asynchronous preparation. Pending text and file work are tracked separately per room. Repeated text submits while one is preparing do not create another operation. A late success may clear only the same submitted draft revision and exact raw value; editing away and back to identical words still creates a newer revision. Focus is set only at the explicit initial send action, never by its eventual completion. Active composition starts an edit revision even before its first text-change event. Enter confirmation during composition is not Send; Shift+Enter remains a newline.

### 194.2 Draft lifetime and failures are visible

Each accepted room has an in-tab draft with raw text, selection endpoints/direction and textarea scroll. Room navigation shows a small draft/preparing indicator without putting private draft text in labels. Switching conversations restores the matching draft and caret without forcing focus. Drafts are bounded by the existing room and composer limits, and no new draft persistence or transport interface is introduced. The leave handler requests a browser warning for drafts or pending work even when encrypted message saving is selected. Actual browser leave-dialog presentation remains a user-agent decision.

Pre-admission refusal retains the complete untrimmed draft for explicit retry. A real room-policy update during a gated send is rejected by the original provider; the UI does not silently replace its target policy. Once an event has been locally accepted, a later failure is not permission to make a duplicate retry message. Accepted ciphertext whose save failed is tracked as unsaved, remains exportable, and keeps its warning instead of being overwritten by a generic success note. File failure reports the number of accepted parts; already accepted/shared parts are not rolled back, and a new selection is a new transfer. No automatic retry, successful delivery or human-reading inference is added.

Lock increments the session generation and clears draft/reading state and the visible input before waiting for existing work. Guards before local admission prevent a late seal or file read from recreating locked work. Already accepted operations are not transactionally undone. Clearing a JavaScript reference is not a physical memory-erasure claim; pending runtime/provider work may retain values until it settles.

### 194.3 Reading stays where the person put it

The message list reconciles rows by authenticated event identity, and files by sender/file identity. Unchanged message nodes are not detached or rewritten, preserving existing selection. Files occupy their chronological first-chunk position instead of always being appended after all text. Empty invitation/member hints are rebuilt on room or trust updates so that they cannot preserve stale participant descriptions.

Each conversation records a visible message anchor and pixel offset. Incoming changes restore that anchor when the person is reading history. A view already near the end follows new messages; otherwise a visible Jump to latest/New messages control offers an explicit move. Activating it leaves keyboard focus in the named chat log. The log uses a polite sequential-update role and the composer exposes status without async focus changes. This is an implementation informed by primary accessibility guidance, not a WCAG or screen-reader certification. Desktop and 320-/390-pixel layout tests are observations, not native mobile qualification.

### 194.4 What did not change

The original native.py, worker.js, worker.ts, crypto.ts, kdf.ts, Argon2/BLAKE2b sources/header, vendor record and historical evidence payload are byte-exact. Room signing, membership checks, envelope validation, live/history admission, trusted pins, record formats, provider semantics and TURN custody remain their original contracts. No speculative forward secrecy, post-compromise security or public deployment assertion is made. Initial three-file and returning two-file guides, independent identity comparison and exact verified-pin reuse remain intact. The experimental native account/session/authority laboratories remain separate from ordinary browser chat.

The new named source is steady_checks.py. client.js and the HTML/CSS shell implement the product changes. first_run_checks.py provides the inherited complete journey with an optional Steady extension; browser_checks.py’s three isolated accept() state fixtures were updated to include the new unsaved set. dev.py and test.sh expose the new selectable lane and current inventory/receipt locations. Current status, constitution C121, letter 0051, lineage and research append the continuation. Thirty inherited corpus/memorandum documents receive dependency-hash/body-digest refreshes only; their authored content is unchanged. Source bindings are not new execution evidence.

### 194.5 Research and reproducibility

Four primary-source records were appended as T227–T230: W3C ARIA23 (sequential chat logs), W3C WCAG 2.2 Understanding Status Messages, WHATWG HTML text-control selection APIs, and W3C Input Events Level 2. Their exact source URLs and scoped uses are in the carried research.json. Every previous technical entry and all 37 infrastructure option objects retain their own original review dates; no provider pricing or allowance was blanket-revalidated. No package or browser installer ran, and no new runtime dependency or service was introduced.

Builder replay, not user onboarding:

```sh
bash Vibechat.html verify
bash Vibechat.html extract --directory /absolute/ABSENT_WORKSHOP
bash test.sh --html Vibechat.html --output /absolute/ABSENT_STEADY_RECEIPT steady
bash test.sh --html Vibechat.html --output /absolute/ABSENT_REUNION_RECEIPT reunion
bash test.sh --html Vibechat.html --require-navigation --output /absolute/ABSENT_STRICT_RECEIPT doorstep
```

Use fresh absent directories and outputs. Run heavyweight browser lanes sequentially on this memory-bounded host: an over-parallel development attempt produced cgroup OOM kills and failed browser runs, recorded below. The final selected lanes were re-executed sequentially without relaxing timeouts, assertions or browser policy. A failed early synthetic IME test and missing isolated unit-fixture state were repaired in their harnesses. Lock’s deliberate credential erasure required the journey fixture to explicitly reselect its owned local relay before reconnecting, not to silently restore it in the product.

### 194.6 Next gate

Continue with the HTML alone as the human experience. Qualify actual file/localhost startup, embedded worker startup, real IndexedDB durability, ordinary mobile sharing and real keyboard/screen-reader behavior in unrestricted environments. Keep the strict unavailable distinction. Then choose and implement a reviewed rendezvous path that removes manual handoffs without calling a source offer delivery, silently trusting a name, uploading an address book or importing account secrets into the browser. Preserve the owner’s local repository facilities and all exact historical handoffs when merging this work.

## 196. rev0048 Keepsake — one backup for people and chats

### 196.1 The product decision

Vibechat.html remains the only product. A backup is the person's data, not another application or a builder prerequisite. Keeping an identity/profile export and a separate record export, remembering their relationship, and finding the right advanced import order was unnecessary ordinary-user work. Keepsake provides **Back up chats** in the workspace and More menu, and **Restore a backup** as a quiet disclosure on the opening screen. The original separate exports/imports remain available in advanced tools. No builder command, hosted account, upload, public directory, new transport or service is required by this new path.

The backup dialog has one primary action: **Save backup file**. It counts verified friends, conversations, messages and files loaded in this tab, with correct singular/plural labels, and warns when drafts or unfinished sends are excluded. Instructions inside the HTML explain reopening Vibechat.html on this device or another and supplying the original name/password. A closed technical disclosure explains public metadata, incomplete attachments, custody exclusions, and the limits of the snapshot. The page says a download was **requested**, not that a durable saved copy has been confirmed.

Restoration starts on the opening screen, before deriving an identity. The selected file has a visibly unauthenticated name/date preview; the name is only a hint and may fill an empty name field. The password generator is hidden while a backup is selected because a newly generated password cannot restore the old identity. The single submit action changes to **Restore this backup**. The existing encrypted-device-saving default and explicit temporary-session fallback are retained.

Conversation editing stays unavailable while the selected backup profile is being authenticated and its records restored. Successful saved recovery presents **Your chats are back**, with optional Recovery details and a Done button that returns the full reading area. A partial or unsaved recovery opens its details and keeps a visible warning with a Back up chats action. Temporary/download-only modes state their different lifetime instead of pretending to have saved device storage. Recovery does not initiate a peer connection, send history, or mean that a friend received anything.

### 196.2 Format and trust boundaries

The new outer data format is `vibechat-backup-v1`. Its exact fields are `format`, `revision`, `created`, `user`, `profile`, `events` and `digest`. The profile is the original `vibechat-profile-envelope-v1` encrypted envelope. Events are the original accepted and currently decrypted text/file conversation envelopes; their original signatures, encryption and room membership rules remain in force. No new cryptographic primitive, key derivation, signature family, room protocol or secret exporter was introduced.

The wrapper SHA-256 covers its canonical body and detects accidental modification. It is **not** authorship authentication, a completeness proof, global freshness, or an independent rollback witness. The file's name and outer user/date are untrusted metadata. An attacker able to edit the wrapper can recompute this unkeyed checksum. Exact derived identity checking and the original authenticated profile/record providers remain the security boundary. The tests explicitly recompute the checksum around a corrupted encrypted profile and separately around a bad record signature; those changes do not become trusted chat.

Pre-unlock selection checks strict UTF-8 and duplicate-key JSON, exact wrapper/profile fields, original envelope shape/hash, unique event IDs, channel fences and bounded counts/sizes. The outer bound is the existing 128 MiB event budget plus the existing 4 MiB profile budget and 64 KiB wrapper allowance. There are at most 4,096 events, and summed canonical event bytes cannot exceed the original 128 MiB limit. Oversized declared files are refused before reading bytes. File reading has a selection serial; removal, replacement or an invitation superseding the selection prevents late completion from reviving it. A backup and an invitation cannot both be the pending entry action.

Only visible text/file conversation events are exported. Room-policy, receipt and capability control envelopes are excluded and refused in this restore format, because replaying the original control-admission path could create side effects even with ordinary history forwarding disabled. Unreadable relay custody and obsolete controls remain outside this human backup; the advanced exports are still available. Partial file transfers may be included, but are not presented as proof that an attachment is complete. The restored attachment still requires its original whole-file verification before saving.

Chat content and the friends/profile data remain encrypted. The chat name, backup date and existing public envelope metadata are visible. Passwords, private identity keys, drafts, relay credentials, recovery salt and unfinished connection setup are not added to this file. The original login details, including an advanced salt when one was used, must be retained separately. This is not password reset or account recovery without the original secret.

### 196.3 The roomless-friend retention defect

Both original providers already rejected profile import that discarded known rooms or rolled back existing room/policy/choice state. They did not reject an authenticated older profile that omitted a verified friend who had no room yet. A legitimate backup restore could therefore silently forget that exact pin.

The native `apply_profile` path now requires every existing trusted card to appear unchanged in the imported profile. The worker `profileImport` path checks membership before comparing the canonical card. Both checks occur before replacing provider state and use the original transactional/checkpoint wrappers. The failure explains that the profile would discard a verified friend and directs the person to their current saved space. Names are not compared as identity. No pin is silently reverified, removed or merged.

An actual original-native/original-carried-worker regression was executed against the received rev0047 HTML: export the owner-only authenticated profile, add a verified friend without a room, then import the earlier profile. All four retention assertions fail on that original build, as expected. The corresponding native and carried-worker checks pass on this revision and retain the exact pin with no room. The worker test imports the same real native encrypted envelope and runs its carried code under Node WebCrypto, not a mock cipher.

Only one native source line and one worker TypeScript source line implement this stricter provider policy. The worker was explicitly rebuilt using the installed TypeScript and clang toolchains; no installer or dependency fetch ran. Worker bundle and vendor worker/source bindings consequently changed. Original `crypto.ts`, `kdf.ts`, Argon2/BLAKE2b C sources, header and the WASM payload records remain byte-exact. Native and worker files must **not** be described as unchanged in this release.

### 196.4 Export, restore, cancellation and failures

Export goes behind already admitted application work, takes the accepted conversation-event snapshot, then exports the matching provider profile. Later profile additions may be included, but cannot remove the earlier records' anchors. The assembled JSON is bounded and checksummed. A provider/identity/session-generation fence is checked across awaits and before requesting a download; locking while preparation is pending suppresses the late download. Drafts, still-reading attachments and pending messages are not waited on or silently counted as completed work. Make another backup after they finish.

Restore requires the exact derived identity before importing the selected profile. A wrong name/password/salt leaves the page locked and does not enter the selected profile-import path. After existing device state is opened, the original profile guards run before the selected profile can replace it. Older/conflicting state may be refused rather than merged. Removing the selected backup and opening normally retains the current saved space.

Profile import, profile persistence, and each event admission/persistence are separate operations. This revision does **not** claim a transaction across all of them. Records use original verified history admission with no forwarding. Duplicate accepted IDs are counted but not appended again. A bad or unreadable record is skipped and counted; valid records may still be recovered. The result explicitly says some messages or file parts are missing and keeps the original backup as the recovery source. A failed device save leaves accepted ciphertext in the tab's unsaved set, visible in the warning and included in the next backup. Successfully imported state is not falsely described as rolled back after a later failure.

A declared test seam delays File.arrayBuffer to exercise cancellation; another delays the original provider operation to prove that restore does not expose editable conversation state while authentication is pending. A selected native retain failure proves that accepted-but-unsaved ciphertext remains exportable. These are scoped fault injections over real providers, not actual browser storage failures or physical power-loss tests.

### 196.5 Carried builder changes and history

The new named source is `keepsake_checks.py`; `first_run_checks.py` invokes it as an optional extension to the original complete friend journey. The extension uses independent empty restore stores/browser contexts, original providers and original messages/file bytes, and leaves the inherited A/B journey intact. The existing driver exposes `keepsake` separately. There are now **125 named sources and 46 regular lanes, plus optional bench**. This is inventory, not a claim that all lanes ran.

Current status, the short brief, source impact/compare maps and driver assertions point to sections 196–197. A failed candidate exposed the 20,000-character current-status ceiling; duplicate directions and the new backup index were shortened rather than raising that limit. The inherited lane-count assertion was updated from 45 to 46. All selected suites were then re-executed on the corrected final bytes. Constitution C122, letter 0052 and the rev0048 lineage entry append this continuation. Thirty-two inherited corpus/memorandum JSON documents receive only derived source-binding/body-digest changes; their authored fields are identical. Every earlier article, letter, lineage entry, research record and all 37 infrastructure option objects remain exact as structured values. Their original review dates were not blanket-refreshed. The 4,281,710-byte historical evidence payload remains byte-for-byte unchanged at SHA-256 `87e0d07d8d68fcb77c512356046f6caca763a877cfde58346ac2ca938703b97f`.

Three primary-source research notes, T231–T233, were appended for the W3C File API, WHATWG HTML downloading rules, and W3C IndexedDB transaction scope. Their exact URLs and limited uses are carried in research.json. These informed bounded explicit selection, download-request wording and the refusal to claim a multi-operation restore transaction. No hosting/provider allowance or pricing was newly qualified.

The entire received rev0047 bootstrap is nested above as exact bytes, including all previous continuations and the owner's local-repository handoff. The starting repository commit remains `af98b724e9616be52a32566033fc8b9cb679bd25`. **Merge into that repository and retain its Git/Nix/build/test facilities; do not replace it with the handoff trio.** It was not supplied here; no repository commit or repository build is claimed.

### 196.6 Replay and next gates

These commands are for builders, never ordinary-user onboarding:

```sh
bash Vibechat.html verify
bash Vibechat.html extract --directory /absolute/ABSENT_WORKSHOP
bash test.sh --html Vibechat.html --output /absolute/ABSENT_KEEPSAKE_RECEIPT keepsake
bash test.sh --html Vibechat.html --output /absolute/ABSENT_INTEROP_RECEIPT interop
bash test.sh --html Vibechat.html --require-navigation --output /absolute/ABSENT_STRICT_RECEIPT doorstep
```

Use absent output directories. Run heavyweight browser suites sequentially on this memory-bounded host. Keep actual native, carried-worker primitive, browser-DOM, synthetic fault, owned local transport and ordinary-navigation evidence separate.

The product gate is still normal unrestricted device qualification: opening the actual HTML, embedded worker startup, real encrypted IndexedDB persistence and recovery, native OS downloads/mobile sharing, real input methods and screen-reader behavior. Do not weaken administrator policy or relabel a fixture as that qualification. Then make one concrete reviewed rendezvous/relay decision that removes first-time three-file and returning-friend two-file handoffs without hidden service contact, public address-book upload or name-based trust. No handoff count was reduced by this backup revision. The experimental native account/session/authority laboratories remain separate from ordinary browser chat.
