## 198. rev0049 / Lantern — find local conversations and notice new arrivals

**The product remains Vibechat.html alone.** This continuation executes the owner's ordinary-human focus, not a new product made from the builder trio. Chats now gives the person already inside a space a single place to find a person/conversation and return to new arrivals. The application contacts no directory, requests no notification permission, and sends no human-reading receipt for this feature.

### The selected product seam

I inspected the initial invitation exchange before choosing this scope. The first wrapper carries the inviter's public card, not an already target-bound two-way session for an unknown recipient. Removing another handoff is not a harmless copy change; the existing independently verified and signed pairing must still bind the right participants. No unreviewed protocol shortcut, silent trust, rendezvous provider, account or publicly reachable service was introduced. First meetings remain three file handoffs and exactly verified returning friends remain two.

An initial strict navigation check again found that this host administratively blocks file and localhost Chromium navigation. No host policy was changed. That leaves normal-device qualification open, rather than turning the native/DOM fixture into a claimed ordinary first-run pass. Within the available scope, the daily gap was clear: an ordinary mobile user had a technical room selector, no straightforward local conversation finder, and no cross-conversation new-item indication.

### The ordinary road

Choose **Chats**, type a friend's name or a conversation name, and open the matching conversation. The list searches only accepted rooms in the current unlocked space and their locally known participants. It is not address-book discovery, message-content search, a remote directory, or a presence display. The input has a visible label, an empty result explains the next action, and an optional checkbox narrows the list to conversations with new items.

Search normalizes compatibility characters, case and surrounding spaces, and matches all entered terms. Display strings are inserted as text, never as HTML. Selecting a result binds the exact full room identifier; when visible names collide, a short room suffix helps distinguish entries. The existing room ID still owns the conversation and its draft. Search is cleared on close and lock rather than silently retained in browser storage.

At narrow widths, Chats replaces the cramped technical room selector and Rooms button in the ordinary header. More still reaches the original room/profile controls. Friends, Invite / join, backup and the advanced facilities remain available. On desktop the existing room tools remain alongside Chats.

### What a new marker means

A marker represents a newly accepted live peer text or the first admitted part of a shared file in this unlocked tab. It is an attention aid, not proof of delivery to an absent device, complete file recovery, human reading or continued presence. The tab title contains only the generic count, not a person's name or a message preview. The header, existing room list/selector and a textual live region expose the new count without relying only on color.

The hook is after original envelope, provider and payload validation. Rejected authentication cannot create a marker. Own sends, explicit record imports/restored history and duplicate accepted events cannot create one either. A room/sender/file identifier groups authenticated parts of one transfer; subsequent parts do not inflate the count or recreate a marker after the first part was viewed. The original whole-file hash and byte assembly remain responsible for file-download verification. Neither an alert nor a first file part promises a complete usable attachment.

Marker and known-content sets remain in tab memory, bounded by the original accepted-record/room limits, with no added localStorage, cookie, profile, database or remote write. Lock clears them and restores the base tab title. Restoring saved ciphertext after unlock does not resurrect old new-item counts. Closing the tab discards this attention state. Existing open-tab transport behavior is unchanged; no closed-tab receiving service was added.

### Do not take away the person's place

A local marker clears only for the selected conversation when the workspace is visible, the document is visible and focused, no modal dialog covers it, and its stream is at the existing latest-message threshold. That predicate is a navigation heuristic, **not evidence that a human read anything**. Hidden or unfocused documents and covered conversations retain their markers. Opening a conversation at an earlier retained scroll position does not clear its count; Jump to latest is explicit. Existing Steady draft ownership, selection and history-node preservation are retained.

The finder initially prioritizes conversations with new items, but an arriving message does not rerank an already-open list under the pointing hand. Existing result buttons are updated in place so keyboard focus stays with the same exact room. Explicit typing/filter changes can reorder results. Entry focuses the labelled search field; selection focuses the message history without triggering a mobile composing keyboard. Closing restores the opener when it is still appropriate.

Development testing found a native search-input detail: Escape with a nonempty search first cleared the input rather than closing the dialog. A composition-aware handler now closes Chats on one Escape, while leaving composing/key-code-229 events alone. Synthetic composition coverage is not a real operating-system input-method qualification.

### Source and builder changes

The ordinary changes are in the client and HTML/CSS. New `lantern_checks.py` extends the original first-friend journey; `first_run_checks.py` routes and records it. The existing Steady and browser harnesses now use the mobile Chats/More routes instead of a newly hidden technical selector. The test driver, source map, brief, manifest revision, impact map and bounded current index discover Lantern. There are **126 named sources and 47 regular test lanes, plus the optional benchmark**. Inventory is not execution.

Native code, the compiled worker, worker TypeScript, cryptographic/KDF/C sources, WASM/vendor payload and immutable earlier evidence remain byte-identical to the received rev0048 release. No compile, dependency installation or dependency fetch was required. Thirty source-bound corpus/memorandum documents have only dependency byte counts/hashes and their corresponding body hashes refreshed. Their original non-binding bodies compare equal; this is metadata rebinding, not fresh execution of every historical laboratory or a renewed independent review. All earlier research options, technical sources, letters, constitution articles and exact lineage records retain their prior values; current entries are additive. The full received bootstrap is retained as an exact byte sequence.

The broad browser suite also caught a test-harness dependency gap: its extracted control-only `accept` unit did not include the newly called `recordNotice` function. The harness now extracts that actual carried declaration too; the original ordering assertions remain intact and no application hook is stubbed away. A temporary source-generation newline error was caught by Python compilation and repaired before final qualification. All selected scopes were rerun against the final sealed HTML rather than pooling earlier passes across different carrier hashes.

The raw-JSON admission lane then caught a source-serialization error: dependency rebinding had written compact JSON while the retained generator requires the original pretty-printed bytes. Original formatting was restored for all thirty rebound corpus/memorandum documents, and exact admission regeneration was checked before resealing. The complete selected set then ran again on that final HTML. No corpus assertion was weakened.

The first sealing script stopped before inserting the new source block because it assumed the wrong existing script-tag attribute order/type. The source edit was resumed at that boundary, not rerun over already modified files. No affected candidate was presented as a release. Later, a manual bounded-status check caught an overlong current index before completion of a carrier run. The index was shortened; the limit was not raised. Development interruptions and failed assertions remain distinct from the final fixed-carrier execution below.

### Current primary-source consultation

The session consulted WHATWG HTML's `Document.hasFocus` semantics, MDN's `Document.visibilityState` documentation, and W3C's ARIA APG modal-dialog pattern. These inform API use and keyboard/focus behavior, not a claim that document state proves human attention or that a screen reader was qualified. The exact dated entries are T234–T236 in the carried research record. All 37 infrastructure options retain their original dates and evidence; none was blanket-revalidated or silently activated.

### Next gates and owner continuity

The next important product gate remains an unrestricted real-browser/device exercise: ordinary file startup, carried worker startup, real IndexedDB persistence, native save/share behavior, mobile keyboards and screen readers, then independent networks. A DOM/native fixture cannot close those gates. The other large remaining friction is the initial/reconnection exchange: select and review one rendezvous/relay model with an explicit metadata, availability and trust boundary before promising one-link chat. No directory or relay account was created here.

The owner's local repository was not supplied. Its starting commit remains `af98b724e9616be52a32566033fc8b9cb679bd25`. Merge the handoff into that repository and preserve its Git/Nix/build/test facilities; do not replace the repository with the product/handoff trio. No owner-repository commit or build is claimed. Older account/session laboratories remain separate from ordinary browser chat, and all of their previously stated negative boundaries remain in force.


## 199. rev0049 / Lantern — fixed-carrier execution and release receipt

All passing release claims below bind to the single final HTML hash. Earlier prototypes and interrupted/failed runs are recorded separately, never pooled with these passes. The fourteen regular lanes are `cli`, `transport`, `lantern`, `keepsake`, `steady`, `reunion`, `doorstep`, `justworks`, `browser`, `webrtc`, `interop`, `review`, `admission` and `carrier`. The additional strict `doorstep --require-navigation` result is unavailable/77, not a fifteenth passing lane.

The Lantern journey includes real authenticated peer messages, an actual three-part 40,001-byte shared file verified byte-for-byte, native-provider restore/lock behavior, inert local search, keyboard/modal/reading behavior and explicit synthetic negative attention/timing seams. The broad browser lane separately executes carried worker cryptographic primitives and the original storage-ordering units. A test harness's historical revision labels, where retained, are not a substitute for the driver/carrier hash bindings below.

Replay from an absent output directory, for example:

```sh
bash test.sh --html Vibechat.html --output /chosen/absent/lantern-receipt lantern
bash test.sh --html Vibechat.html --output /chosen/absent/browser-receipt browser
bash test.sh --html Vibechat.html --require-navigation --output /chosen/absent/strict-receipt doorstep
```

The first two permit only the explicitly labelled fixtures when ordinary navigation is unavailable. The third refuses that substitution. Commands do not install dependencies or grant permission to weaken host policy. Each selected lane is repeatable through the carried/external matching test driver. Source seals and unchanged repacks identify bytes, not independent authorship, authority or audit coverage.

The screenshot of the notes view in the Lantern fixture is captured after a deliberately invalid signed peer record is rejected. Its retained error status is expected negative-test evidence, not a cosmetic failure hidden by altering the DOM. Finder screenshots otherwise show the actual tested mobile/desktop layout.

## 200. rev0050 — Plainview / ordinary sending and recovery

### The product road

Type and send as before. A single small status below an own message answers what the current tab knows: local saving in progress, a save failure, waiting for a connection, an unconfirmed offer, an interrupted sharing attempt, or a particular recipient tab's report. Incoming messages gain no sender-reading UI. No dialog opens itself on arrival and no notification permission is requested.

Opening the status gives two sections, **On this device** and **At the other end**. A failed local save takes precedence over a successful peer acknowledgement. After a successful saving retry, the repaired item’s cached composer warning is cleared. A tagged global save warning clears only when no unsaved records remain; a newer unrelated status is not overwritten. The ordinary actions lead to local saving retry, the existing single encrypted backup, or the existing exact verified friend connection guide. They do not require export-format knowledge, an identity directory, connection logs or builder instructions. Self-notes have no remote recipients to invent. Memory-only and download modes explicitly retain their weaker local-saving meaning.

An offline new message stays accepted locally and shows Waiting for connection. Connect opens the existing friend review without starting ICE. The original two-file reconnect then reconciles that same event once. History restored after lock is **Earlier message · status unknown**, because this tab did not observe its original journey; it may already have arrived. Reconnection may legitimately obtain a fresh report for an old event.

### What the report actually means

The existing wire acknowledgement is unchanged: `type`, `id`, and `scope`, with the established `peer-memory` and `peer-save-attempt` scopes. New code accepts attribution only from a current registered ready RTC link whose exact peer identity is trusted and is an original encrypted-envelope recipient. Unknown scopes, extra keys, unknown events, a same-name wrong identity, stale or unready links, and generic relay acknowledgements do not upgrade a friend's status. Multiple links to the same identity do not count as multiple recipients. Groups retain a per-original-recipient result.

The signed signaling binds the RTC peer selection. The small acknowledgement itself is **not a new ML-DSA-signed receipt**. Its scope is an application claim over that connection, not an independent observation of remote disk, future availability, whole-file verification, or human reading. A peer can misreport. No stronger durability claim is inferred from `peer-save-attempt`, including when the original peer's save attempt failed. Ordinary send completion only records a local offer; missing acknowledgement remains unconfirmed. No existing envelope, signaling, key, wire signature or cryptographic provider format changed.

### Retry without duplication or changed recipients

`offerEvent` wraps original event offers from initial forwarding, inventory reconciliation, explicit wants and the new user retry. It passes the same retained event object/bytes to the original connection sender. It neither seals a second event nor reads the composer. The local and remote event-ID duplicate paths remain the originals.

`retrySharing` coalesces work per stable message/file-group key. It rechecks session/provider ownership and, for remote sharing, current room membership, exact epoch and pending-policy absence. It does not update recipient lists or bypass a changed conversation. Acknowledged parts are skipped for the corresponding exact peer. Closing or switching the dialog cannot redirect a late result into another selection; lock fences late state and feedback. Saving retry uses the original queued profile/record persistence functions and does not transmit the message. Backup uses the ordinary Keepsake path, not a new recovery format.

For a file, `shareView` requires the expected distinct index count and consistent file metadata before complete status. A first-part acknowledgement is not an all-parts acknowledgement. The status selection expands as retained parts arrive, even while the details dialog is open. Preparation is distinguished from an incomplete stopped transfer. Missing parts cannot be synthesized by retry; choosing the original file again starts a new transfer and cannot recall previously shared parts. The original Verify & save file action still validates the assembled file independently.

### Reading, focus and lifetime

Status refreshes update retained row controls, not the message body. Existing reading anchors and selected text remain in place. The native labelled dialog restores the opener on close/Escape. When an asynchronous receipt hides a currently focused retry action, focus moves to the dialog's close control rather than outside the modal. Reports, pending jobs, selected message IDs, stored opener and detail/feedback text clear on lock. They are not added to a profile, record export, backup, cookie or persistent outbox. Original Steady drafts and Lantern attention remain tab-local with their existing semantics.

### Sources, history and builder surface

Product changes are confined to `client.js` and the HTML/CSS frame. `plainview_checks.py` is the one additional named carried source. `first_run_checks.py` dispatches the new journey; `browser_checks.py` includes the actual new admission helper in its pre-existing control-only synthetic units rather than stubbing it away. Steady's obsolete literal `Export` prompt expectation now requires **Back up chats** plus the own message's **Not saved** status; its substantive refusal, retention, encrypted-export, draft and reading assertions remain.

`dev.py`, the exact carried/external `test.sh`, the bounded current index and new current-first shell guide expose rev0050, 127 sources, 48 regular lanes, Plainview's impact map and section 201. The compare reader supports the received rev0049 inventory without executing that target. All historical shell guides remain. Research appends T237–T238 for the W3C WebRTC send semantics and W3C ARIA modal-dialog guidance; no infrastructure offer was silently re-dated or service selected. One article, one builder letter and one distinct lineage adaptation are additive. Thirty predecessor documents receive only exact source-binding and dependent body-hash updates; their original cases, conclusions and dates remain unchanged. Immutable `evidence.json` and original native/worker/crypto/vendor payloads remain exact.

### Development observations, not hidden passes

Provisional browser and Plainview journeys passed before integration. A progressive-file check exposed the need to follow newly retained parts in an already open details view; the stable group key and selection refresh now cover it. Broad regression testing caught the old Steady `Export` copy expectation and a current-index presentation exceeding the original 20,000-character bound. The expectation was strengthened to the ordinary backup/status route; current summary prose was shortened without raising the bound. A provisional Keepsake renderer crashed during overlapping browser qualification, and several direct tool calls were externally timed out; none counts as a pass. The provisional fixed-byte batch was stopped when its already extracted Steady test became obsolete. The first complete fifteen-suite batch passed, but screenshot review then revealed stale composer/global save-failure text after successful retry. Save warnings now carry an explicit origin, and only the repaired item’s warning or the resolved all-records save warning is cleared. A new browser assertion covers the recovery. The final qualification serializes browser-heavy lanes, retains the original tests/time limits and reruns all fifteen selected suites on one final carrier. The renderer crash cause was not independently established; a nonconcurrent passing run is scoped evidence, not a general crash-freedom claim.

The final Plainview journey includes deliberately withheld acknowledgements on actual owned RTC channels, a rejected unsupported ack scope, a single injected RTC send exception, a local retain failure after real encryption, repeated retry, exact canonical-event comparison, partial/all-part reports, an open progressive-file view, backup routing, local saving retry, offline waiting, actual two-file reconnection, lock cleanup and restored unknown status. The distinct Node projection corpus uses synthetic event/link/store collaborators and does not perform cryptographic verification; it covers attribution, grouping and guard logic. Neither fixture is an independent security audit or normal browser-storage qualification.

### Next work

Keep the HTML as the sole human-facing product. The larger unresolved friction is still the first three-file and returning two-file exchange. On unrestricted devices, first qualify the unchanged ordinary file entry, carried worker, actual IndexedDB persistence and mobile save/share lifecycle. Then choose a reviewed rendezvous/relay design with explicit privacy, credential, reliability and identity-verification boundaries; do not activate a service or upload an address book as an unannounced default. Preserve the existing no-network-until-explicit-connection boundary, backups and failure recovery. In the owner repository, merge these sources into its existing Git/Nix/build/test workflow rather than replacing it. No owner repository was available here.

## 202. rev0051 — Homeward / return to your saved chats

### The product road

**Vibechat.html is the only product.** No builder document, local server, shell command, extra application or workshop knowledge is an ordinary-user prerequisite. This revision repairs a first-screen mistake with unusually confusing consequences: in a deterministic-identity system, a mistyped chat name, password or advanced salt can derive a perfectly valid but different identity. The received default browser flow would open that empty identity while the old encrypted chats remained in its database. To a returning person, that looked like lost conversations or a successful login to an empty account.

The default saved-browser path now distinguishes that situation from first use. After the person explicitly unlocks, it reads the exact encrypted-profile key and whether any saved profiles exist. A matching profile goes through the original authenticated import without another question. A missing match in a nonempty profile store opens **Let's find your saved chats**. **Check my details** is the primary focused action; **Restore a backup** goes to the existing Keepsake chooser. A closed **Starting a separate space?** disclosure retains deliberate **Open a separate space**, explaining that this creates a different safety code and does not recover the old conversations. Escape chooses rechecking, not creation. The permission is a single decision, not a remembered bypass.

There is no plaintext account-name list, password lookup table, eager profile scan at document opening, new storage schema, remote directory or network request. The dialog does not name another user's saved space, infer which credential was wrong, or promise a password reset. It says the saved data has not changed. A staged initial invitation stays inert across retry, then continues to original independent friend verification after correct unlocking. There is no second import and no silent trust.

A first default-browser opening now adds the original provider's encrypted empty profile, before the first friend or room is created. This lets a later typo be recognized even when the person has not yet invited anybody. First use in an empty profile store gains no new decision screen. The encrypted envelope remains the original `format`, public `identity`, `iv` and `cipher` object; names and credentials are not copied into a new unencrypted index. This is not retroactive recovery of a previously unsaved profile.

### Keep failure distinct from a fresh start

`homewardStorage` is a small scoped transaction helper. The lookup reads the exact profile and profile count in one readonly transaction. It resolves only at transaction completion, not at a successful request callback. An aborted, failed or timed-out read is an unavailable store, never evidence that it is empty. Initial profile creation uses `add`, not replacement: a concurrent same-key creation causes an explicit retry so the saved copy can be loaded. The helper waits for transaction completion and requests strict durability for that insertion. That request is not independent evidence of physical disk retention.

The new read/initial-insert operations have an eight-second bound. Timeout aborts where possible; late callbacks cannot turn failure into success. A late write can remain uncertain, so the UI does not promise that no write happened after an unavailable result. Ownership checks also refuse a completion for a database handle no longer owned by this opening. Existing general profile updates and historical storage paths are not redesigned into a global multi-tab transaction or rollback witness.

A matching but damaged profile is passed to the original cryptographic authentication and refused on failure. It is not treated as an empty profile and overwritten. Refusing a save does not quietly switch storage modes. The existing **Continue without saving** choice remains explicit. Because a later storage failure can occur after the password field has been cleared, that route now says when the password must be entered again rather than silently submitting an invalid empty form.

While opening is in progress, identity, password, salt, storage, generator and connection choices are disabled and the login form is marked busy. The mismatch dialog clears the entered password before appearing. Retry/restore/cancel release the derived provider state; generation and provider-ownership checks prevent the pending decision from reviving a cancelled opening. The conversation workspace stays hidden while original saved records are being authenticated and loaded. A progress note updates during that work; editing is not offered against a misleading temporarily empty conversation. Unopenable retained records are counted honestly and their encrypted copies are kept, rather than automatically called missing friend pins.

### Scope, not a new account system

The new recognition guard covers the ordinary default **IndexedDB browser-saving mode**. It does not infer identities from directory exports, native-endpoint stores, temporary sessions or download-only modes. A deliberately selected backup already names its exact intended identity, so it continues through the original exact-identity backup guard instead of a warning about unrelated local spaces. It does not bypass encrypted-profile authentication or record validation.

No local recognition is possible when its saved profiles are absent, cleared, unavailable under another origin/file location, or never saved. The guard does not recover a password, restore missing browser data, guarantee durability, announce human presence, create read receipts or remove the manual connection exchange. The existing Argon2/PQ providers, key derivation, wire formats, signed room policy and exact verified friend identities are unchanged. The helper's bounded operations do not claim to bound every existing history/provider operation or implement a general cancellation system for all legacy paths.

**New friends still exchange three files; exactly verified returning friends exchange two.** No hosted rendezvous or relay provider was selected. That is still the larger ordinary onboarding problem. New UI conveniences are not a substitute for a reviewed way to remove those exchanges or actual real-device qualification.

### Tests, and what the development run taught us

`homeward_checks.py` is a new independently selectable lane. Its 45 checks use Chromium UI and the exact carried native cryptographic provider, with an explicitly synthetic in-memory IndexedDB transaction collaborator. The seeded profile, room, message and damaged ciphertext are real provider objects. The storage adapter deliberately separates request success from completion and supplies abort, read-error and same-key collision cases. Seven of the 45 are separately identified Node callback/timer units, exercising the exact production helper with synthetic timing and database collaborators. These are not 45 real-storage, standalone-worker, accessibility or public-network checks.

The journey checks wrong password/name/salt, primary focus and Escape, no pre-unlock store probe, no premature state publication or profile write, correct original-identity recovery and pin retention, deliberate separate-space creation, exact original encrypted bytes retained, no persistent bypass, backup selection and wrong-backup refusal, slow history loading, empty-first-use recognition, inert invitation retention and later verification, corrupted-profile refusal, request/transaction failures, temporary password re-entry, insertion collision, lock cleanup and no peer/external contact. The original received rev0050 fails the first wrong-identity assertion when run with this new harness in regression-only mode; that is an expected counterexample, not an old-build qualification failure disguised as a pass.

Development runs exposed two additional issues. The first correct-retry test initially sampled the workspace before its old message had loaded; that revealed the inherited prematurely editable workspace and led to the delayed-history gate and test. The initial-profile save failure also exposed a temporary-entry no-op after password clearing; the explicit re-entry step fixes that. Another assertion initially rejected all database puts, even the inherited unchanged history-record writeback; it was narrowed to its actual purpose, no unnecessary **profile** rewrite, while exact saved profile/event snapshots remain checked.

The first integrated Doorstep replay stopped on a stale builder-summary assertion requiring the literal old title `Reunion`. Its shell-startup assertion now requires the exact current revision extracted from the carried client instead; exit-zero, empty stderr, preserved stdin and subsequent DOM/CSP tests remain required. It is not a relaxation of the product's security policy. Several tool-level execution deadlines interrupted development drivers, including one whose Homeward child had already written a 45-check result; partial drivers are not counted as release passes. The deterministic review and raw-JSON corpus replays also caught an overly compact serialization in a development rebinding script. The original exact pretty serialization was restored, including two now entirely unchanged documents; their byte-for-byte regeneration assertions were not weakened. A later carrier replay also found an old chapter pointer and missing legacy transport-caution clauses in the new brief. The current pointer and explicit cautions were restored without dropping the checks. The final selected replay has separate complete receipts.

### Research and the builder handoff

Primary sources T239–T240 were checked on 2026-10-11:

T239: W3C **Indexed Database API 3.0**, Working Draft dated 13 August 2025, <https://www.w3.org/TR/IndexedDB/>. Applied to transaction-completion versus request-success handling and initial insert collision refusal. The durability hint is not treated as proof of physical storage. This remains a draft reference, not a newly claimed Recommendation or browser qualification.

T240: W3C **ARIA APG — Dialog (Modal) Pattern**, <https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/>. Applied to modal focus, explicit recovery actions and cancellation returning to credentials. A DOM keyboard test and visual inspection do not establish screen-reader or real-device accessibility.

All 37 infrastructure options, earlier research entries and their original checked dates remain unchanged. No provider was silently refreshed, selected or activated. C125 and letter-0055-homeward record the saved-identity principle and the remaining gates. Existing lineage values, prior constitutional articles and letters remain intact.

The current-first shell guide, `brief`, bounded `status`, source mapping, impact routes and carried/external test driver now name Homeward and sections 202–203. The read-only compare reader accepts known manifest editions through rev0051, including the received parent, without executing the compared carrier. There are **128 named sources and 49 regular lanes plus optional benchmark**; that inventory is not an execution claim. `homeward --require-navigation` explicitly refuses its fixture-only scope with unavailable/77; the separate required-navigation first-run test actually attempts ordinary navigation.

Thirty older dependency documents changed only derived source bindings/body hashes; their substantive bodies and original JSON serialization are preserved. Rebinding is not fresh execution of those historical laboratories. Original native, worker, cryptographic/KDF/C, vendor/WASM and immutable evidence bytes remain exact from rev0050. The legacy evidence hash is still `87e0d07d8d68fcb77c512356046f6caca763a877cfde58346ac2ca938703b97f` (4,281,710 bytes).

The entire received bootstrap remains byte-for-byte in this continuation. The owner's repository starting commit remains `af98b724e9616be52a32566033fc8b9cb679bd25`. Merge into that repository and preserve its Git/Nix/build/test facilities; do not replace it with the three-file builder handoff. The repository itself was not supplied, and no repository commit, Nix build or external deployment is claimed.

### Next gates

Qualify the actual standalone HTML, carried worker, real IndexedDB restart/durability, mobile saving/sharing, operating-system input and screen-reader interaction on unrestricted real devices. Keep those tests separate from synthetic callbacks, native-provider browser fixtures and owned loopback WebRTC. Test the new default saved-space flow there, including failed/blocked storage and multiple browser tabs.

Then prioritize a reviewed rendezvous/relay path that removes the manual first-friend and reconnect exchanges without hidden service contact, address-book upload, weaker independent identity binding or builder setup becoming onboarding. Retain the deliberate offline/manual fallback and honest service limits. More protocol-laboratory panels are not the ordinary user's road.

## 204. rev0052 / Postcard — let an introduction wait

### 204.1 Selection and ordinary journey

Author: GPT-6 Astra Pro. The owner again authorized `/run` and kept the HTML-only “just werx” product standard. The selected friction was the old initial file's ten-minute expiry and original-tab dependency even though that file contained no live connection description. Invitations should tolerate people having ordinary lives before both choose to connect. The revision does not select an external service or pretend that a static file can resume a closed live peer connection.

The first **Invite a friend** action now prepares the reusable file immediately. Share, save and copy stay in the same guide; the redundant Make step and introductory block disappear once the file is ready. First-screen open/paste/drop carries it through unlock into the existing independent full-code review. Both the connection action and **Save friend for later** are disabled for an unknown identity until that review is explicitly acknowledged. Saving is an original provider pin plus the original selected encrypted profile persistence, not a separate contact database, directory upload or new account format. The Friends dialog then focuses the exact named Connect button.

The ordinary direct road remains available: verify the new friend and prepare the connection reply without first taking Save for later. If the identity is already pinned, no fresh trust ceremony is invented. If the exact pair already has a ready connection and reusable unchanged room, the existing conversation opens rather than creating another room or peer. Reopening the card after restart reuses the unchanged signed pair room under the original Reunion rules.

### 204.2 Narrow format and trust boundary

The new unsigned UI wrapper has exactly `format = vibechat-friend-card-v1`, numeric `v = 1`, `kind = card`, and `card =` the existing complete public identity card. It has no nonce, expiry, session description, room, private data or grant. The existing bounded strict JSON reader refuses duplicate keys, extra fields, wrong types/version/kind and malformed public keys. The original full public identity hash is recomputed. Hash consistency alone does not identify the human; independent full-code comparison is still mandatory before pinning an unknown identity.

The public-card flow is explicitly marked internally and has no repeating timer. That local flag is created only for the exact public format; received data cannot set it on a live connection. Old expiring invitation, connection and final-reply parsing is not treated as a public-card fallback. A synthetic clock advance exercises non-expiry; it is not a claim that a month elapsed in the laboratory. Closing or clearing the UI cannot revoke copies of a public identity; the interface says so. No contact/network operation occurs merely because the public file is created or previewed.

Once the recipient chooses to connect, `friendConnect` uses the original signed v2 offer and exact signed two-person room inside the existing `vibechat-friend-connect-v1` wrapper. No new signature family, encryption primitive, KDF, room authority or provider API was added. The original sender can reopen with exactly the same identity and receive this normal targeted offer; nothing depends on their earlier public-card dialog still existing. An unknown replying identity still requires independent comparison. The final accept binds the exact offer and complete wrapper and needs the actual pending offer tab. Wrong exact target, hidden third room member, wrong session and forged rehashed signature are refused. Local wrapper expiry remains separate from cryptographic authenticity and globally trusted time.

Public-card repetition cannot replace an active prepared connection, and another public identity cannot silently redirect it. Preparing a connection remains deliberate and uses the previously selected ICE settings. The new UI-only `fromCard` annotation changes explanatory copy, not the transmitted signed objects. The original recipient-side pending peer is owned by the existing cancellation flow before asynchronous setup finishes. Cancellation closes it but does not pretend to undo an already accepted pin or signed room. Trust, persistence, room creation and ICE are not one atomic transaction.

### 204.3 Compatibility and late callbacks

A closed compatibility disclosure retains **Make a temporary invitation** for older versions, with its existing expiry and original-tab constraints. The carried first-run baseline now explicitly opens that disclosure and invokes the real compatibility action at each of its three initial creation points; its original 54 assertions remain. This is a declared test-route change, not a hidden override of the production default. Postcard separately exercises the actual new default from the first Invite action through chat.

Share and copy operations retain the exact flow/generation before awaiting browser callbacks. A late failed share or clipboard callback after clearing or locking cannot revive the old output, error status or copy fallback. This cannot recall a file already handed to the operating system. The tests' mocked promise completions are explicitly synthetic and do not establish real OS sharing behavior.

An early development run exposed the reusable flow's Clear button remaining hidden after creation because no interval would repaint the guide. Reusable creation now paints immediately without starting a timer. The final suite explicitly creates, clears and recreates the same byte-identical public file. Earlier test-harness errors from referring to IIFE-private state and reading a hidden code with `inner_text` were corrected to ordinary DOM counts and the element's exact text content; no production state escape was added.

### 204.4 Carried work and evidence discipline

New source: `postcard_checks.py`, exposed as `vibe-postcard-tests` and test lane `postcard`. The source inventory is 129, the regular lane inventory is 50, and benchmark remains optional. `dev.py` discovers the new source, keeps older comparison schemas, points current brief/impact at sections 204–205, and preserves no-clobber extraction/repack. `test.sh` carries the lane and explicit scope text. The existing below-20,000-character status-output guard was kept: two preliminary editorial versions measured 20,172 and 20,094 characters; the final current status was shortened without removing the distinction between ordinary product, unsigned public identity, live signed connection, historical labs and unqualified environments. The final projection is 19,833 characters. Full selected qualification was restarted on the final bytes; preliminary passes are not substituted.

The current-first shell/HTML arrival comments prepend the prior guides. C126 and letter-0056-postcard append attributed product and continuation guidance. T241–T242 append primary-source review of W3C WebRTC (Recommendation 13 March 2025) and the W3C ARIA APG modal-dialog pattern. Guidance informed separating public data from live sessions and focusing the useful next action; it does not qualify a real browser/device. All 37 infrastructure options retain their original dated evidence. No pricing or provider deployment was revalidated, selected or silently contacted.

Exactly 30 historical dependency documents change only declared source lengths/hashes and their derived canonical body hashes. Their original pretty serialization and substantive historical fields remain exact. All original constitutional articles, letters, research entries and lineage donor/input values remain. `vibe-evidence` remains the exact 4,281,710-byte historical record, SHA-256 `87e0d07d8d68fcb77c512356046f6caca763a877cfde58346ac2ca938703b97f`; it was not refreshed or relabeled current execution.

### 204.5 Next builder

Keep the reusable introduction and the two live handoffs distinct. Do not remove independent identity checks to make the remaining ceremony look shorter. The exact normal-file browser/worker/storage/mobile gate still needs an unrestricted environment; respect the existing host policy rather than working around it. A reviewed rendezvous plus relay-access model remains the substantial coordination/reachability decision. It must fit the single HTML product without exposing service secrets, uploading contacts, inventing account recovery, claiming presence from silence or outsourcing the user's first run to builder instructions.

Preserve the owner repository handoff and the complete received history. This turn received only the archive, not that repository, so no Git commit or Nix build was possible to execute from supplied materials; none is claimed. The builder ZIP is not the product.

## 206. rev0053 / Holdfast — execution selection and implementation

### 206.1 The everyday gap

The preceding HTML immediately ran destructive lock cleanup when Lock was clicked, even with unfinished writing, pending file reads or accepted-but-unsaved changes. That contradicts the ordinary expectation that leaving a conversation should not accidentally discard work. This revision adds a targeted recovery decision, not a routine confirmation on every clean lock and not new hidden persistence.

Only `Vibechat.html` is the application. `client.js` and the template are builder editing surfaces whose final bytes are sealed back into it. The existing native and worker providers, cryptographic code, event/profile/backup wire formats and experimental laboratory controllers were not changed.

### 206.2 Risk, recovery and deliberate exit

`holdfastRisk` combines existing per-room draft/preparation state with live setup, unsaved records, temporary/manual-download custody and a new session-local failed-profile-save flag. Empty temporary spaces, clean saved chats and inert reusable public invitations do not cause a confirmation. The flag distinguishes a failed friends/room profile from a failed message; a friend without a conversation must not disappear without warning.

The native modal has a safe primary focus, Escape/X exit, keyed named draft rows and direct review without copying draft text into the sheet. A bounded timer runs only while the sheet is open and updates status without replacing focused buttons. `Back up chats` opens the existing backup dialog without stacking dialogs and returns to a fresh risk view, without claiming that a browser download was retained. Backup still excludes drafts and live setup.

`holdfastSave` queues one explicitly requested recovery batch, reexports the original encrypted profile and retries retained ciphertext through original persistence. Repeated clicks coalesce. No message is resealed, retransmitted or replaced by a new draft. Failed records remain at risk after partial recovery. Profile/provider/generation fencing prevents a dismissed or locked session from reviving recovery UI or claiming late success. Already-started storage commits and already-admitted/shared message parts are not rolled back.

`requestLock` separates ordinary intent from `lock`, whose cleanup remains directly available through **Lock anyway**. Lock immediately invalidates the session, clears draft/review and readable workspace content, closes dialogs and pending links, then waits for queued work/provider release. The entry action is disabled until release completes, including a competing programmatic submit. Provider release can still be delayed or fail; no instantaneous secure-erasure or remote revocation guarantee is introduced.

The existing beforeunload listener now uses the same risk projection rather than treating every unlocked identity as equally risky. It only requests the platform's generic warning. There is no new unload save, send, backup, permission or service. W3C modal guidance and WHATWG unload-event rules informed the boundary; actual browser/OS and assistive-technology qualification remains open.

### 206.3 Carried tests and preservation

`holdfast_checks.py` is a separately scoped 54-check suite with original native cryptography, the carried Homeward synthetic IndexedDB collaborator, synthetic provider/file gates and cancellable leave events. It tests clean and risky exits; inert inspection; named draft/selection return; pre-input composition; pending send/file/live setup; exact ciphertext recovery; profile-only and friend-only save failures; partial repair; ordinary backup contents/checksum; delayed recovery, immediate UI hiding, key-release entry fencing and explicit temporary/manual-download limits. No external request was observed in this lane.

Eight inherited UI harnesses now use a small explicit-confirmation helper when they deliberately test lock cleanup. Where relevant they wait for the entry action to be enabled, rather than confusing an immediately hidden workspace with completed key release. The helper does not itself wait for release: some original fixtures must first release their synthetic callback. Original cleanup assertions remain. The helper preserves the legacy DOM harness no-argument path default. Shared helper imports do not make fixture evidence standalone qualification.

The workshop mapping, script inventory, compare schema, impact map, driver, bounded status and current brief now identify rev0053, sections 206–207, 130 sources and 51 regular lanes. The readable status stays below its inherited 20,000-character guard. Prior metadata is preserved by exact-prefix/value checks; historical dependency documents retain substantive fields and their original serialization while derived lengths/hashes are refreshed. The unchanged immutable rev0030 evidence remains historical, never relabeled as current execution.

### 206.4 The next gate is still ordinary use

Replay current Holdfast behavior with `bash test.sh --html Vibechat.html --output ABSENT_DIRECTORY holdfast`. Run `justworks --require-navigation` on an unrestricted device for the real startup gate; do not disable administrator policy to turn this host's unavailable result into a pass. The actual default initial invitation is exercised by `postcard`; `justworks` deliberately retains the older temporary compatibility route.

Qualify opening the HTML, the carried worker, actual browser storage, physical mobile save/share/leave behavior, real input methods and screen readers. Then pursue a reviewed rendezvous/relay path that removes manual handoffs without making users deploy builder tools or silently exposing an address book. Do not switch cryptographic protocol, weaken exact peer verification, activate the experimental laboratories, choose an unseen service or invent closed-tab reception just to make a screenshot look simpler.

---

## 208. rev0054 / Parcel — send the only product with the invitation

### 208.1 Ordinary path and product boundary

**Vibechat.html is the only product.** The new first path is **Invite a friend → Share Vibechat / Save Vibechat.html → send that HTML → friend opens it**. The public invitation is already inside the application. A recipient does not first need a separate app file and then an import ceremony. The release itself contains a `null` invitation: no developer or fixture identity is preselected.

The invitation screen leads with “Send Vibechat to your friend,” a short explanation and the prepared HTML action. Unsupported native HTML sharing leaves Save as the primary button. The reusable introduction has no countdown; the sender may close that tab. Smaller JSON, existing clipboard fallback and earlier temporary compatibility remain available without competing with the first path. The first-screen heading acknowledges an invitation that is already present rather than asking whether one exists.

Opening the copy previews the claimed inviter locally. It does not derive keys, save a friend, create a room, start ICE, trust a name, or send anything. Unlock carries that exact introduction to the existing independent full-code check. **Save friend for later** still creates only an explicitly verified contact; **Connect** retains the original signed live setup. A sender who closed the original public-introduction tab can reopen with their original login details to receive the live reply.

**Three handoffs remain for new friends:** the application/public introduction, then two live connection files. Exactly verified returning friends still use two. The live files still need their original pending tab and ten-minute setup window. This is not one-link chat, background receiving, a directory, hosted rendezvous, new relay capacity, password reset, revived WebRTC state or a revocable invitation.

### 208.2 Copy source, never the unlocked page

`parcel_frame.json` is a finite, build-generated descriptor of the static carrier frame. It alternates literal shell/HTML/CSS/tag text with named source slots, including one slot for the descriptor itself. It contains no source bodies and therefore does not recursively encode an entire earlier app. There are 133 named sources and 134 slots including the separate manifest; its 269-part model stays below the explicit 513-part limit.

The client checks the original manifest revision, inventory and frame digest, then verifies each named source's exact bytes and SHA-256 before assembling anything. It copies those original bodies into the finite frame, replacing only `parcel_invitation.json` and its manifest row with the original canonical reusable public card. The manifest is then serialized canonically. The prepared application retains the original shell entry, standards-mode prefix, carried worker/WASM/vendor bodies, stylesheet and executable CSP hashes.

No live `outerHTML`, DOM clone, user-input attribute, current URL, fragment, storage object, profile, message, draft, preference, native bridge token or TURN credential is serialized. No request for the current file or a hosted app is needed. Source mismatch disables the app-copy action and exposes the smaller invitation route; it does not silently export a modified or instrumented source block. Repeated saves are byte-identical. A recipient making their own invitation replaces the earlier public identity, not accumulating inviters, accepted contacts or nested application copies.

The app-file read/output ceiling is 32 MiB, the existing invitation ceiling remains 262,144 bytes, the manifest parser is bounded at 256 KiB and the finite descriptor parser at 512 KiB. Source-row sizes, unique inventory and output size are checked. Per-preparation serial, exact outgoing packet, flow and unlock-generation checks fence asynchronous hashing and sharing. Clear and Lock discard the prepared copy; late completion cannot restore it or start a download.

**These checks establish internal source integrity, not independent code authorship.** Someone controlling a whole HTML application can also replace its code and manifest. The UI says to open app copies only from a source you trust. A public identity embedded in an application is not authority to trust that application or that person.

### 208.3 Existing trusted copy: read the invitation, not the attached program

The ordinary invitation file pickers and file-drop path now also accept HTML. An already trusted Vibechat reads the selected HTML as bounded text and finds exactly one supported `vibe-parcel-invitation` data slot. It never inserts the attached markup, uses a DOM parser to run it, follows its images or runs its scripts. Missing, duplicate, empty, oversized, non-public or altered identities are refused through the existing local error path. The extracted public JSON still passes the original strict invitation and card validation.

This route deliberately does not certify the attached application's other contents. It does not need to: only inert, independently reviewed public data is accepted into the trusted running application. Old small public cards remain readable in rev0052 and newer; extracting the public slot from an HTML copy requires rev0054 or newer. The app copy itself carries its own rev0054 reader.

### 208.4 Explicit sharing and truthful outcomes

The HTML `File` is prepared before a Share click. `navigator.canShare` is checked for the actual file type, and `navigator.share` is invoked during the click's activation, not after a long hashing operation. Browser/OS refusal retains explicit Save and smaller-file options. Cancelling sharing does not silently download a fallback. A successful API result says only that the file was handed to the share app, not that a friend received, saved, verified or opened it. Download text likewise reports a request, not durable retention or sending.

Native sharing and ordinary HTML attachment opening vary by environment. No messenger allowlist, app-install workaround, hidden service or native-OS qualification was added. A user whose messenger refuses HTML can deliberately choose the smaller invitation, which still requires an existing trusted app.

### 208.5 Tests, fixtures and development corrections

`parcel_checks.py` is a new independently scoped 46-check journey. It covers app-copy generation from a space containing random password/attribute/draft/relay canaries; exact source-only differences; repeated bytes; fresh recipient arrival; independent verification; saving a roomless friend; resharing under the recipient's own identity; inert HTML selection; malformed/oversized refusal; the original complete signed live exchange; bidirectional encrypted text; byte-exact multipart file recovery; source mismatch; cancel-during-hashing; click activation; explicit share cancellation; and late-share lock fencing.

The fixture changes **only the executing client source** to select native RPC and updates only its live CSP hash. After execution it restores that script element's original source text before export; changing that text does not rerun the script. All carried bytes used for the copy are then the original release bytes. SHA-256 uses an explicitly declared opaque-origin collaborator, while the original native cryptographic provider and owned local TURN/real RTCDataChannels perform the conversation. Separate unmodified-client DOM pages check default browser saving, standards-mode parsing and CSP blocking without claiming carried-worker startup. Native share outcomes and timing gates are synthetic. No ordinary file/localhost navigation policy was bypassed.

Early development correctly exposed fixture-wide rewriting of carried sources; those instrumented bytes were refused rather than weakening production checks. Later trial corrections were confined to the test helper's already-connected guide transition and a Playwright expression that accidentally returned a digest function. The latter now uses a non-returning block. The final client does not acquire a test-only bypass.

The inherited Postcard test explicitly opens the smaller-file disclosure and checks its original reusable public wrapper. Its wording assertion now includes the outgoing section's timing and version details. The original first-run compatibility baseline deliberately selects the old temporary route. Neither substitutes for the new primary HTML journey, and overlapping inherited first-run checks must not be summed as independent coverage.

The first broad fixed-carrier wave retained four failures. One was the unchanged 20,000-character developer-status ceiling: the newly expanded pretty-printed current index exceeded it. The index wording was compacted while preserving its boundaries; the limit was not raised. Two Chromium pages crashed and another UI target timed out while multiple browser suites ran together. After that wave the 4-GiB host recorded OOM counters, but no earlier per-event timeline was captured. Final qualification therefore repeats every selected lane with one browser/native journey at a time, alongside non-browser carrier checks, keeping all assertions and per-command timeouts. Preliminary receipts remain separate, not relabeled onto the final bytes.

### 208.6 Source history, research and next gates

C128 records the source-only invitation boundary. T246–T247 are this turn's primary-source review of WHATWG script data blocks and the W3C Web Share API. Earlier research options retain their original dates; no infrastructure pricing or provider allowance was revalidated and no hosted provider was adopted. Every prior research entry, constitutional article, letter and original lineage value is retained. `letter-0058-parcel` and `rev0054_adaptation` carry the continuation forward.

Original native, worker, crypto/KDF/C, WASM/vendor, laboratory implementation and immutable evidence bytes remain unchanged. Thirty dependency documents change only derived bindings/body hashes with their original serialization; those updates are not fresh laboratory execution. The mutable current-status index remains bounded, currently close to its 20,000-character output ceiling; compact repeated wording rather than letting it become another unbounded history.

The owner's repository starts from `af98b724e9616be52a32566033fc8b9cb679bd25`. It was not supplied. Merge this work into that repository and retain its Git/Nix/build/test facilities; never replace that repository with the handoff trio. No repository commit, integration or build is claimed here. The entire received rev0053 bootstrap remains an exact contiguous byte sequence before this section.

Next qualification remains ordinary file startup and carried-worker crypto on unrestricted devices, actual IndexedDB durability, native OS sharing/saving/leave prompts, mobile HTML attachment opening, input methods, assistive technologies and public-network connectivity. The larger product gate remains a reviewed connection path that removes manual exchange without hidden service contact, uploaded address books, name-based trust or ordinary-user developer setup. One HTML is still the only product.

None of these results qualifies standalone carried-worker startup, ordinary browser persistence or native OS interaction.

### 209.4 Two successive fresh roundtrips and source preservation

Cycle one extracts the qualified HTML into a fresh directory, repacks it into a new output and verifies it. Cycle two starts from cycle one’s output, extracts into another fresh directory, repacks into another new output and verifies it. Both complete outputs are byte-identical to the fixed release. Source preservation is a separate inspection, not execution or independent authorship. It retains all 130 original source entries, adds three and leaves 91 original bodies exact. Of the 39 changed original bodies, thirty are derived dependency-document updates only. The native, carried-worker, crypto/KDF/C, WASM/vendor and immutable-evidence implementations remain exact. Prior research options, technical-source entries, turn notes, articles, letters and original lineage values retain their exact values.

### 209.5 Old-version feature assertion, preliminary failures and development receipts

Running the new Parcel feature assertion on received rev0053 stops at the expected absence of the app-copy UI. That is a feature-difference check, not evidence of old data loss or a security exploit. The full 46-check journey passes on the final rev0054 above. The preliminary wave below targeted a different fixed HTML SHA and retains its four failures. Its passing rows are not final qualification of the published bytes. No failed receipt is overwritten by a final pass.

Early development logs follow with their original trial names and results. The initial helper timeout and digest-expression failure were repaired in the harness, without bypassing source checks or changing the product to satisfy the fixture. Trial04’s 46 checks preceded the final metadata/index and repeated qualification. The preliminary roundtrip has its own different carrier hash and is not substituted for the final two-cycle receipt. An inefficient local exploratory probe that repeatedly reparsed the full source per slot was stopped; later probes parsed it once. That probe is not a product-startup test or a product-hang finding.

## 210. rev0055 / Clearway — recover a connection without starting over as a person

### 210.1 The one product and the ordinary route

**Vibechat.html is the only product.** The current work is in its conversation/invitation UI and carried connection helper. Bootstrap prose, a test driver and an extracted source tree are builder materials, never a user's connection prerequisites.

A stalled attempt used to leave technical guidance, and an interrupted established conversation could continue showing its obsolete outgoing connection file. The ordinary guide now distinguishes an expired live invitation, a failed preparation, a slow joined attempt, and an interrupted established connection. **Try a new connection** is inside that guide, above the older controls and within the narrow-screen viewport. It deliberately replaces this tab's pending attempt and prepares a new original-format signed invitation for the same exact verified identity.

The guide hides obsolete outgoing sharing controls when an attempt has failed, expired or been interrupted. A slow joined attempt can still retain the current output while its other participant finishes opening the file. **Invite someone else** remains a visible secondary action; recovery must not trap a person in one old friendship. The original file picker, paste route, accepted conversation and advanced connection settings remain accessible. Settings are a deliberate detour; merely opening them performs no provider operation or service switch.

The retained chat must still be an eligible, unchanged, signed two-person conversation. Retry checks the actual original room, not whichever matching conversation the user selected more recently. Missing rooms, changed policy, pending/declined policy review, a removed exact trusted identity, an already recovered live link, and an unrelated pending connection refuse before resetting setup. The original signed signal and room operations run after those local guards. There is no name-based pinning, signature shortcut or room-policy flattening.

**Unfinished writing is not a connection request.** Retry does not send the draft. Draft lifetime remains the unlocked tab, following Steady and Holdfast; no new draft persistence or backup format was added. Accepted pins, rooms and messages are not rolled back by a connection failure. Trust, saving, room acceptance and peer setup remain separate operations rather than an invented cross-provider transaction.

Retry replaces only **this tab's** attempt. It cannot remotely reset the friend's pending tab or recall an old file. The other participant must open the new file; the existing guard can require cancelling an older pending setup first. Closing or locking a live setup still discards its pending browser peer. New friends still exchange three files; already verified returning friends still exchange two. This revision does not deliver automatic rendezvous or eliminate manual exchange.

### 210.2 A timeout need not discard the routes already found

The original `rtcDescription` rejected every incomplete gathering state at its 15,000 ms timer, even when the browser's own current local description already contained candidates. The received rev0054 reproduces that refusal under the new deterministic helper regression. Clearway waits for normal completion or the original timer, then takes the actual browser `localDescription.toJSON()` snapshot. A bounded, permitted candidate snapshot can proceed through the unchanged signing API.

This is **not** a claim that gathering finished, that a candidate is reachable, or that a connection opened. The guide explicitly labels limited gathering, explains that later routes are not appended to an already prepared file, and offers a new attempt when needed. Candidate-free descriptions still refuse. Relay-only configuration still requires a relay candidate; no host-only fallback is introduced. The helper does not manufacture candidates or an end-of-candidates marker, rewrite SDP, change ICE servers or alter the signed signal format.

The rationale follows the W3C WebRTC specification's distinction between a local description, surfaced candidates and completed gathering. Its local-description attributes allow browser-added candidate state; its transport states also distinguish transient disconnection from terminal failure. Primary sources reviewed this turn are T248–T249 in the carried research ledger: `https://www.w3.org/TR/webrtc/#dom-rtcpeerconnection-localdescription`, `https://www.w3.org/TR/webrtc/#dom-rtcicegatheringstate` and `https://www.w3.org/TR/webrtc/#dom-rtcicetransportstate`. These are a design basis, not device/network qualification or a promise about timer scheduling on a suspended browser.

An established connection that temporarily becomes disconnected is not forcibly closed just because its old setup invitation's ten-minute deadline has passed. It can recover on its own, and recovery removes the prompt without an automatic replacement. An actual failed/closed peer is cleaned up under the original transport rules. No background retry loop, hidden relay choice, ICE restart protocol or server was added.

### 210.3 Cancellation and publication boundaries

The gather helper owns its timer and event listeners in a weakly keyed pending-wait registry. Explicit cancellation and lock settle that wait before peer closure, even when the browser does not emit a useful closure event. Completion, deadline, failure and cancellation settle once and release those owned listeners. Original generation/flow guards continue fencing provider completions and late UI callbacks.

Testing exposed a UI reentrancy problem in the new reset ordering: closing a link can synchronously repaint recovery while the old flow is still current. Clearway resets recovery presentation **after** closing the old pending resources and replacing the flow. Cancelling now returns immediately to usable ordinary controls without leaving that old recovery card visible. It does not erase an accepted conversation or revive an old outgoing file after a delayed rejection.

The first broad wave also found that hiding the old primary invitation button made inviting someone else inaccessible after a disconnect. That is a real UI regression, not a timeout to waive. The corrected screen keeps the action secondary and visible. The unchanged Postcard journey was rerun, as were the new recovery assertions. Preliminary failures remain separately recorded in section 211; none are relabeled as fixed-carrier passes.

### 210.4 Implementation, carried material and reproducibility

Production changes are limited to `client.js` and the HTML/shell frame: bounded gathering, owned-wait cancellation, exact-room selection on retry, recovery presentation and secondary navigation. The prior native, worker, cryptographic/KDF/C, vendor/WASM implementations and immutable evidence remain exact. The generic release contains no inviter. Parcel still assembles an app invitation only from the finite checked source frame, never from an unlocked DOM snapshot; this revision adds no saved state or personal data to that export.

A new carried `clearway_checks.py` contains the scoped helper checks and a first-run extension. `first_run_checks.py` adds only the selected extension/report wiring. The development mapping, source impact, status, test driver, arrival guide, research, lineage, constitution and attributed letter advance to rev0055. The resulting inventory is **134 named sources / 53 regular lanes plus optional benchmark**; it is not an all-lanes execution claim. `status` remains below the original 20,000-character rendered-view assertion; the bound was not increased. C129, T248–T249 and letter-0059 are appended, not replacements for previous contributors.

All 37 infrastructure options, the prior 242 technical-source entries and prior turn notes retain their original values and dates. No hosting price, free entitlement or provider was adopted/revalidated. All 128 previous constitutional articles, all 58 previous letters and prior lineage values remain intact. Of 32 historical dependency documents, 30 change only derived source bindings and their canonical body checksums. Original serialization and non-derived content remain unchanged. Such rebinding is not fresh laboratory execution; selected actual executions are identified separately below.

The entire received rev0054 bootstrap is retained as one contiguous exact byte sequence. The owner's starting commit remains `af98b724e9616be52a32566033fc8b9cb679bd25`. This work was performed in the extracted carrier; it does not claim an owner-repository merge or commit. A repository handoff must retain that repository's existing Git/Nix/build/test facilities, not replace the repository with the handoff trio.

### 210.5 What remains unqualified and what to do next

The new helper tests use actual carried code with synthetic clocks, peer state, candidate descriptions and action collaborators. The browser extension uses the declared native-RPC/digest fixture, original native cryptography and real WebRTC channels through an owned loopback TURN relay. Its gathering completion, candidate omission and transient state/clock changes are explicitly synthetic. They test the app's handling of those inputs, not a real outage, real public NAT or suspended-device recovery. Captured peer traffic and independently recovered shared-file bytes are separate from those UI state simulations.

The actual ordinary file/localhost navigation gate is run separately on the final HTML. **Unavailable / exit 77 is not pass.** No host policy is changed. Standalone carried-worker startup, actual IndexedDB durability, native OS sharing/saving/leave prompts, mobile HTML attachment opening, operating-system input methods, assistive technology and public-network connectivity remain unqualified. A DOM fixture cannot remove those gates.

The next builder should qualify the single HTML on unrestricted real devices and pursue a reviewed, explicit rendezvous/relay path that removes manual handoffs without uploading an address book, trusting display names, silently selecting infrastructure, or requiring developer setup. A smaller immediate UX gate is accepting an explicitly reviewed replacement from the same verified friend while another exact attempt is pending; Clearway intentionally retains the original pending-flow refusal rather than quietly taking over a different setup. Preserve the correct human distinction: available connection details are not an open connection, an open connection is not human presence, and a peer report is not human reading or independent disk evidence.
