## 212. rev0056 / Crossing — the other invitation can have a safe first road

### 212.1 Product route and scope

The user again requested `/run` of the received bootstrap. The selected gate was the explicit rev0055 limitation: the counterpart's old pending-flow guard still demanded Cancel before accepting a replacement. The new route is **open the other connection invitation → choose Keep or Use this invitation & reply → send that reply → friend opens it**. It is all in the ordinary HTML. Advanced connection settings and the three/two-file protocol remain separate unchanged facilities.

A pending flow is eligible only for its exact pinned peer and its already accepted unchanged epoch-one pair room. Similar names are not identity. No trust or room is created merely to qualify a switch. First introductions without accepted rooms, legacy/public files, another peer, another room or an unrelated advanced pending peer are not coerced into this path. The current special handling applies to an older pending flow, not a redesign of every connected-chat import route. A working exact peer blocks the replacement guard. No general claim is made that all other existing import paths were redesigned.

The confirmation names the stored verified friend and makes the consequences explicit. Keep receives initial focus; Escape and close are nondestructive. The candidate is tab-local and cleared on Keep, cancellation, lock or a subsequent read. One-second local rechecks disable a no-longer-valid choice. They do not contact a service or choose between two unsigned dates. The file wrapper's different nonce/date is not an authenticated statement of newness.

### 212.2 Before any teardown

`friendRead` retains all original bounded parsing, exact recipient/card/role checks and duplicate handling. An exact duplicate of the still-reviewed offer reopens its original review. The new controller stages a different pending connect offer rather than changing the current flow or closing its peer.

`crossingGuard` binds the candidate to the identity generation, current friend operation serial, exact flow object and candidate serial. It checks the pinned peer, target user and key identity, offer role, new invitation identifier, signed-offer identity, wall and bounded monotonic expiry, exact room, locally eligible room policy and pending-peer ownership. A rewrapped old offer or changed file reusing the active invitation ID cannot silently replace the active attempt. An expired old attempt can be replaced by a still-valid candidate; that does not renew the candidate's lifetime.

`crossingCheck` invokes the unchanged provider's read-only `signal-open` verification and `room-export`. The returned entire signed accepted-room object must canonically equal the proposed room, not merely share an ID. Guards run before and after each await. Preflight does not call trust, room import, ICE, saving, message send or transport selection. The provider implementations were inspected and retained byte-for-byte.

Keep stays available during explicit-use verification. Candidate and flow serial checks reject late completion. Immediately before closing the old owned flow there is a final synchronous guard with no intervening await. `friendReset(true)` performs the original local pending-peer cleanup; the new flow preserves the accepted room and original candidate deadline. `friendReview` reuses the ordinary review renderer, and the unchanged `friendContinue` rechecks the original signed signal/room and prepares a normal `accept` reply. No draft is submitted and no message is resealed as part of switching.

This is not a distributed or cross-provider transaction. After explicit teardown, failure to prepare the new reply leaves a failed replacement with ordinary recovery. It does not resurrect the old peer or claim remote rollback. Browser closure ends the local peer; neither checking nor closing rewrites the friend's tab. Both people must agree which tab/file to use.

### 212.3 First-meeting correction found by the broad run

The first candidate incorrectly treated every different byte string in a `review-connect` flow as a live replacement. The unchanged Postcard test opens an initial offer, deliberately submits a rehashed forged signature, checks refusal before room/ICE, then opens the genuine offer. The new guard blocked this sequence before any room or peer had been accepted.

The fix preserves the original same-invitation reread route only while the review still owns no room, no peer and no advanced pending connection and the exact peer and invitation match. Real pending flows still require the reviewed switch and reject an altered active identifier. The original Postcard signature/refusal and successful genuine reply assertions remain unchanged and pass on the final bytes. No timeout, byte budget or validation was loosened to obtain that result.

### 212.4 Carried build and evidence scope

One new named source, `crossing_checks.py`, extends the inherited first-run harness with 22 cases and separately executes 32 synthetic controller/guard checks against actual carried functions. The helper corpus explicitly labels its state, provider, clock and dialog collaborators. It covers exact peer/target/room/policy/pending ownership, old/candidate expiry distinctions, signature/accepted-room failures, nondestructive focus, Keep during a delayed verification, recovered links and failure after explicit teardown.

The combined 76-check browser/native fixture uses the original provider cryptography and real owned-loopback TURN/WebRTC channels. Two participants first create crossed signed offers for the same accepted chat. Rehashed modified SDP with a stale original signature and altered room bytes are refused before peer teardown. Keep and Escape preserve the earlier shareable output and exact pending peer. Explicit Use closes the old peer, produces one matched normal reply, retains draft/caret and room, then exchanges encrypted messages in both directions. A 70,001-byte file is recovered exactly; the inherited first-run transfer is separately 65,537 bytes. A second case has one participant retry while the other still holds its unused earlier answer; the new invitation can replace it without Cancel/reimport. The stale answer is refused and the matching new answer connects.

The driver adds `crossing` without removing existing lanes. Current inventory is 135 sources and 54 regular lanes plus optional benchmark. Current status remains under its unchanged 20,000-character assertion. The initial stale `sections 210-211` brief expectation was updated to `sections 212-213` with an added Crossing discovery assertion; all transport/independent-sender boundary assertions remain. Original driver timeouts are unchanged.

The legacy developer `compare` helper still has its inherited supported revision range ending at rev0053 even though later source gates exist. This session does not claim that helper compared rev0055; the independent named-source/hash and historical-content preservation checks below did. Updating that builder helper is a small follow-up, not an ordinary-product prerequisite.

### 212.5 Primary-source research and continuity

T250: W3C WebRTC, closing a peer connection, https://www.w3.org/TR/webrtc/#dom-rtcpeerconnection-close (reviewed 2026-10-12). The local close operation terminates its channel/transport machinery; it does not implement undo or reset the other tab. This informed read-only checking before deliberate teardown. The source is operation semantics, not a public reachability test.

T251: W3C WAI-ARIA APG confirmation dialog example, https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alertdialog/examples/alertdialog/ (reviewed 2026-10-12). Nondestructive initial focus, a programmatic name/description and Escape cancellation informed the native dialog. Applied guidance is not screen-reader qualification.

C130 and letter-0060 describe the local-switch boundary for future builders. Every older research option, source and turn note remains in its original prefix; all older articles, letters and lineage values remain intact. Infrastructure pricing was not revalidated; no discovery or relay vendor was chosen. The previous bootstrap remains a literal contiguous byte sequence in this file. Qualify the unmodified HTML through ordinary file/HTTPS opening on unrestricted desktop and mobile devices, using its actual carried worker and actual IndexedDB. Check native HTML attachment opening, sharing, saving, leave prompts, real keyboard composition and assistive technologies separately. Do not count DOM/native-provider fixtures as completion of these gates or work around an administrator navigation block.

The larger ordinary-person problem remains manual signaling and dependable connectivity. Automatic crossed-offer resolution is not implemented here; both parties still choose the matching setup. Preserve the conservative original wire and permission boundaries unless a separately reviewed change supplies stronger evidence.

## 214. rev0057 / Tray — ordinary file selection and explicit sharing

### 214.1 The chosen human problem

The received global drop handler sent every file to the invitation guide. A photo dropped over an existing chat therefore produced an invitation error. Meanwhile the attachment picker immediately invoked `sendFile`, with no destination/selection review. These are ordinary interaction problems inside the sole product; no new protocol, hosted service or advanced settings page was needed.

The implemented route is choose/drop/composer-file-paste, review, then explicit Send. Opening the review does not read the File's bytes or call a cryptographic provider. It displays text-only metadata, the original room label and its participants. There is no thumbnail, PDF/HTML viewer, content-type inference from bytes, compression or upload. The existing one-file, 2 MiB and 16 KiB-chunk bounds remain. Oversize selection cannot Send; an HTML/JSON-looking invitation can still choose the existing separate bounded importer.

Cancel is focused initially. The visible Cancel, Escape and close control release the selection and restore ordinary composer focus without altering its text/selection. Native dialog close events are asynchronous: the first new browser journey exposed a race where the old item remained after close and blocked an immediately following paste. Cleanup is now synchronous on the explicit controls, and a queued close handler checks that the dialog has not reopened before releasing anything. An empty/cancelled picker result is silent.

A final idle-review probe also caught needless replacement of unchanged live-status and connection text. Two unchanged paint calls produced four child-list mutations in the preliminary DOM. The final paint assigns text only when its wording changes; the same isolated probe then produces zero. A carried full-journey MutationObserver check covers idle refresh for 1.1 seconds. This is deliberately scoped to DOM mutation, not inferred screen-reader announcements or assistive-technology qualification. The prior complete 22-lane wave remains separately recorded; all 22 were rerun against the final corrected bytes.

### 214.2 Original destination and original encrypted transport

`attachment.item` holds one File and the `composeContext()` snapshot: exact room/channel, accepted policy, copied member list, provider and generation. `attachmentGuard` checks the unlocked identity/session, retained room/policy/members, local membership, pending policy review, and an already-running file job. Switching the visible chat does not rebase the selection. The review names the frozen destination; a changed/removed accepted room cannot silently become another destination.

`attachmentSend` consumes the item synchronously before awaiting `sendFile(file, context)`, preventing repeated click reuse. `sendFile` rechecks the snapshot before reading and after `arrayBuffer`, including declared/actual byte length and the original maximum. Original provider sealing and admission guards still apply to each part. Native/worker providers, cryptographic formats, signature families, chunk layout and recipient verification were not changed. File completion does not send or clear a separate text draft, change the selected room or steal focus from a later task.

This is not a new transaction or recall mechanism. After Send, some original encrypted parts may already be admitted/shared when later work fails; those parts remain. Existing status, exact-save recovery and backup behavior apply. Selecting the original file again starts a new transfer, not a byte-retry of an earlier file. Changing permissions cannot be silently flattened to make an old selection succeed.

### 214.3 Routing without accidental invitation trust

The unlocked existing-chat drop path offers file review only when another modal task is not open. The locked opening screen and an already-open friend guide preserve their existing invitation drop behavior. Drops over other dialogs do not hijack those dialogs or silently initiate sharing. Multiple files are refused with an ordinary one-file-at-a-time explanation. A transient drag outline is removed on drop, drag departure and window blur.

Only a `paste` event on the message composer with supplied File objects enters review. Normal text/HTML paste is left to the browser. There is no asynchronous `navigator.clipboard.read()` call, polling, address-book access or permission prompt. Synthetic ClipboardEvent coverage checks routing and cancellation, not real OS clipboard insertion or image-format interoperability.

Filename/MIME hints for JSON, HTML and `.vibechat` offer **Open as an invitation instead**. That explicit action releases the file selection and delegates to `invitationFileText` and the original friend guide. Attached HTML is read as bounded text and only its original inert public invitation slot is extracted; it is not placed in an executable DOM. The new asynchronous detour carries generation/guide-serial guards so a cancelled/reset/locked task cannot become a late import. Opening never grants trust; all existing signature, exact-room and independent safety-code steps remain.

### 214.4 Selection lifetime and leaving

Selection is one volatile object in the unlocked tab, not a message, persisted profile, draft backup or pending transfer. Holdfast adds a separate selected-file risk and a **Your file has not been sent / Review file** section. The section deliberately does not call selection "preparing" or imply that backup includes it. Review returns to the same item without reading it. Keep chatting preserves it; Lock clears it synchronously and cannot restore/send it on the next unlock.

The inherited generic `beforeunload` warning is requested while this risk exists, without shutdown save or network work. A synthetic cancellable event proves only the handler's decision. The browser/OS may not show a leave prompt; process termination and power loss remain outside this evidence. Clearing references/UI is not secure erasure. A selection in this tab does not modify the original file on disk.

### 214.5 Carried sources, tests and research

New source: `tray_checks.py`, mapped as `vibe-tray-tests`. The revised client, HTML/CSS frame, developer mapping/brief/impact/status, manifest, parcel frame and driver are rebuilt through the original no-clobber workflow. Current metadata records rev0057/Tray and sections 214–215. The status snapshot is a mutable index: its first candidate printed 20,750 characters and failed the unchanged 20,000-character gate. Shortening repeated descriptions brought final printed output to 19,476; all detailed historical contracts remain in their original documents and complete received bootstrap. The test bound was not changed.

The new `tray` lane extends the same declared first-run browser/native-cryptography/owned-TURN fixture. It covers inert picker review, safe filename display, initial Cancel focus, narrow layout, Escape/Cancel/close, ordinary text-paste pass-through, explicit pasted/dropped files, multi-file/oversize refusal before reads, byte-exact transfer, repeated Send, separate drafts, frozen destination across a synthetic background room change, explicit invitation routing, selected-file leave/lock review, and absent selection after unlock. Its added self-notes room is accounted for only in the Tray branch of inherited room-count cleanup.

Existing file chooser journeys now click the visible **Send file** action. Their substantive original Python `ok`/`check` expressions remain in place; original timeout and size bounds remain. The received handler fails the new explicit-review assertion and the final handler passes. That is a previously absent consent workflow, not an old cryptographic failure. Fifteen helper checks execute the carried selection handler/guard with synthetic DOM/state/provider collaborators; they are not fifteen additional native crypto or OS tests.

A lock/unlock in the new journey clears the explicitly supplied test relay settings just as the product should. An early cleanup timeout came from the harness failing to reselect those ephemeral owned settings. The harness now does so explicitly before inherited reconnection. No production automatic credential restoration was added.

Primary-source readings, accessed 2026-10-12, are appended as T252–T254: the W3C File API (`https://www.w3.org/TR/FileAPI/`), Clipboard API paste event (`https://www.w3.org/TR/clipboard-apis/#clipboard-event-paste`) and WAI-ARIA modal dialog pattern (`https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/`). They inform metadata/read separation, event-local paste and explicit cancel/focus behavior, not real-device or accessibility certification. Current infrastructure pricing was not researched or adopted. Prior option catalogs/dates remain as received, not silently renewed recommendations.

Preservation is checked against freshly extracted received sources. All 135 old named IDs remain, with one new source (136). Eighty-six old named source files are byte-identical. Of the changed JSON documents, thirty retain all values except derived source bindings/body hashes with matching original serialization. Native, worker, cryptographic/KDF/C, vendor and all laboratory implementation bytes plus immutable `evidence.json` are unchanged. Old articles, research options/technical entries/turn notes, letters and lineage values remain prefix/value-identical; C131, T252–T254, letter-0061 and the new adaptation are appended. The complete raw bootstrap is separately retained byte-for-byte, not reconstructed from parsed Markdown.

### 214.6 What to do next, and what not to claim

The next builder should start with ordinary, unrestricted device execution: a real local HTML open, carried worker/KDF startup, actual IndexedDB save/return/backup, native file picker/paste/share/save and mobile HTML opening, keyboard/IME and screen-reader use, then independently owned public-network reachability. A DOM-native fixture, synthetic clipboard event or internally consistent manifest cannot qualify those paths. Do not bypass host policy or relabel unavailable as pass. Existing dedicated provider/journal/witness, interop, laboratory and optional benchmark lanes were not all rerun this turn; unchanged bindings are not fresh results.

The larger "just werx" problem is still live connection handoff. Revisit the preserved infrastructure/transport catalog and owner repository before selecting any service. Reduce handoffs without hidden service contact, contact uploads, name-based trust, stored shared relay secrets, automatic retries or developer setup on the ordinary path. Do not claim a directory, always-on relay, closed-tab receiver or one-link chat exists. The local file review is complete within its tested scope; it does not solve public connectivity.

Retain the owner's starting repository commit `af98b724e9616be52a32566033fc8b9cb679bd25` and its existing Git/Nix/build/test facilities on integration. This ZIP is not a replacement repository. No repository commit, public deployment, dependency installation, independent security audit or native-device certification was performed here. The older `compare` helper's historical revision range was not broadened; independent exact-source/history audits and fresh carrier round trips supply the current preservation evidence below.

The isolated status probe uses actual carried `attachmentPaint` bodies in a small Chromium DOM with synthetic guard/state collaborators. It establishes repeated versus absent same-value text mutations, not an assistive-technology announcement result. The final full Tray journey separately observes idle review in the application fixture.

Non-lane probe reproducer used in this workspace (paths below identify exact local inputs; this is builder material, not a product runtime dependency):

```python
import asyncio,json,pathlib,shutil,hashlib
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright
R=pathlib.Path('/mnt/data/vibechat-run57')
async def main():
 out=[]
 async with async_playwright() as pw:
  browser=await pw.chromium.launch(executable_path=shutil.which('chromium'),args=['--no-sandbox'])
  for label,path in [('preliminary',R/'release-cycle01/client.js'),('current-workshop',R/'workshop/client.js')]:
   source=path.read_text();fn=source[source.index('function attachmentPaint('):source.index('function attachmentReview(')]
   p=await browser.new_page();await p.set_content('<p id="attachment-status"></p><p id="attachment-connection"></p><button id="attachment-send"></button><button id="attachment-invite"></button>')
   observed=await p.evaluate('''async source=>{
    const $=id=>document.getElementById(id),state={identity:{id:'self'},links:new Map()},friend={busy:false};
    const attachment={item:{file:{name:'file.bin',size:20,type:'application/octet-stream'},context:{members:['self','peer']}}};
```

### 215.4 Preliminary, corrected and interrupted work — not final passes

The first streaming-session attempt was unavailable in this host. An initial synchronous tool call was interrupted before a completed lane receipt, and one preliminary multi-command round-trip tool call stopped before the second extraction; neither is a completed test pass. Subsequent detached local coordinators were polled within this session. Two scratch compaction target checks stopped before writing; an unqualified intermediate `release-v2.html` remained byte-identical to the earlier candidate. The original test bound was never raised.

Trial 1 exposed asynchronous close cleanup blocking a following file paste. Trial 2 completed the new file checks but omitted reselecting the ephemeral test relay after Lock, so inherited reconnection timed out. Trial 3 corrected that fixture. The first broad wave was stopped after the current-index size failure, with its active lane allowed to finish separately. A subsequent complete 22-lane wave passed; the later isolated status mutation probe motivated the two changed-wording guards and new carried idle check. All 22 lanes were then rerun for the published bytes. The earlier full wave is preserved as earlier evidence, not reused as the final qualification.

The ordinary user needs none of those commands. Open the HTML, choose the right conversation and use its visible controls. ## 216. Pathway — a connection default that survives a return

### Product scope and the defect

Vibechat.html remains the single product. The bootstrap, test driver, extracted workshop, receipts and ZIP are builder materials. This turn began by repeating the actual ordinary browser-navigation gate rather than pretending that another fixture solved standalone startup. Administrator policy still refuses both file and localhost navigation. No policy was bypassed. The next bounded product defect was in the return path: the received `clearTurnState()` always selected local/no helper and cleared the ICE field; it could also leave relay-only selected without a relay. Thus even the original non-secret default disappeared after Lock or a failed unlock. The negative regression exercises that actual received cleanup function and fails at the default-restoration assertion.

Pathway preserves only the recognized basic choice, in the current tab: the existing Cloudflare STUN default or no helper. The choice is an enum, not a retained copy of the ICE field. Successful unlock restores the basic fields without making a peer, contacting a provider, testing a server or starting setup. Repeated cleanup and a failed login do not replace the remembered basic selection with the cleanup placeholder. Closing the HTML still returns to its original default; this is not encrypted preference persistence.

Custom settings, temporary credentials, managed lease metadata and relay-only configuration are not treated as harmless defaults. Their fields are cleared by the original cleanup path, and the next connection receives a non-secret “fresh choice required” marker. It cannot silently fall back to direct candidates or a different service. A fresh deliberate basic selection or explicitly entered custom configuration releases that marker. A relay-only checkbox on its own does not. Clearing fields/references is not a secure-memory-erasure claim.

### The ordinary guide, with the advanced route retained

The friend guide now has **For your next connection**. A valid default remains a closed optional disclosure rather than a new mandatory setup step. An outgoing reusable public introduction does not display live-connection configuration at all. A missing or invalid configuration opens its recovery choice and puts it in view on narrow screens.

The two basic choices are **Internet helper · Cloudflare** and **No helper service · local network**. They operate the existing advanced preset controls. The copy distinguishes the existing STUN helper from a relay, warns that some networks need a relay, and does not call the local option anonymous. No new provider, public service, credential, relay subscription, account, directory or rendezvous was added. The existing endpoint was not probed in these tests.

**Advanced connection settings** is an explicit detour. Closing it returns to the same named friend guide, not an unrelated screen; generation, friend serial, lock state and other open dialogs fence that return. The selection's lifetime and the fact that only the next connection changes are stated next to the controls. Same-value status text is not repeatedly replaced. Mobile review caught the initial focus target scrolling the warning out of view; recovery now focuses the choice without scrolling and opens at the top. DOM/layout checks are not screen-reader or real-device qualification.

Choosing an option does not create a peer, request a credential, retry a failed connection, mutate an existing peer configuration or rewrite an already-prepared signed invitation. After a valid configuration change, the person still explicitly prepares a new connection file. Previously shared files remain unchanged. Managed leases that still require release or reconciliation cannot be overwritten through the basic selector. Recovered managed custody takes priority over a remembered basic choice, and original expiry/revocation validation remains authoritative.

### Refuse missing configuration before destructive work

`iceConfig()` remains the strict configuration boundary. It adds the forgotten-custom and relay-only-without-TURN refusals, while retaining the original bounded JSON, server validation, expiry cleanup and recovered-lease checks. The actual next configuration is checked before `makeOffer()` closes an earlier pending offer, before Clearway resets its attempt, before Crossing deliberately takes over, and before the friend flow creates a room or starts applicable trust-and-reply setup work. Saving an independently verified friend for later and accepting a final answer do not require an unrelated future-route configuration.

These are configuration guards, not new trust rules. The original exact verified identities, signed signals, whole accepted-room comparison, changed-policy refusals, pending-tab requirements, conversation retention and cancellation fencing remain. No automatic connection takeover or policy downgrade was introduced. The new recovery journey keeps the same conversation and its unfinished text, explicitly enters a fresh owned relay, reconnects with two connection handoffs, exchanges encrypted text both ways and recovers a 49,000-byte multipart file exactly. Changing the next preset after connection leaves the actual live peer configuration unchanged.

### Carried implementation and preservation

The original native, carried worker, crypto/KDF/C sources, WASM/vendor material, laboratory implementations and immutable evidence retain exact bytes. The final named-source audit finds 94 unchanged inherited named sources, 11 current authored/index/test-driver edits, 30 documents with only derived source-binding/body-digest updates, one resealed finite Parcel frame, and one new named test source. The inventory is 137 named sources and 56 regular lanes plus optional benchmark, not a claim that every lane passed or ran.

`client.js` contains the enum/forgotten-route state, guide projection, explicit advanced return, configuration preflight and corrected preset update order. The HTML frame contains the guide controls and existing-theme CSS. `pathway_checks.py` adds 25 separately scoped helper checks and a 22-check extension of the inherited 54-check full first-friend journey. `first_run_checks.py` integrates that extension and its exact source/receipt identities. The existing Clearway and Crossing helper-only units now explicitly provide a synthetic `iceConfig` collaborator because their actual carried functions call that boundary; the full conversation journeys use the real configuration path and original substantive assertions.

The mutable `dev.py`, `test.sh` and current-status index point to this revision and section 217. The printed current-status index remains 19,443 characters, below the original 20,000-character bound. The current brief retains the original distinctions between experimental return transport and independent sender account/contact/message verification; setup commands still refuse return stores. C132, T255–T257, letter-0062 and the appended lineage adaptation record this turn. Prior research options/sources/turn notes, constitutional articles, letters and lineage values are preserved. No owner repository merge or commit is claimed.

### Preliminary failures, and a separate inherited builder defect

The early preset update order briefly painted a relay-only-without-relay warning between two field assignments. The original preset now clears that flag before dispatching its ICE input event, and a hidden guide does not consume or open the recovery disclosure. Later test corrections fixed new-fixture selection and focus assumptions without weakening the production checks. One interrupted trial has no completed receipt and is not a pass.

The first broad run caught a shortened returning-friend explanation: the guide still needs to say that preparation uses the selected **connection service**. That notice was restored; the original Reunion assertion remains. Parcel's original large inert-HTML input check timed out once. Its unchanged test and original limit passed when repeated alone on the final file; no native OS or public-network success is inferred from that repeat.

The first metadata rebind updated dependency byte counts but omitted their derived body checksums. Original malformed-input and raw-JSON corpus regeneration checks refused it. The final full-body checksums were refreshed and those original suites were rerun. The first carrier run also found the current brief's omitted historical transport warning and stale section literal. The warnings were restored and the current section assertion advanced from 214–215 to 216–217; original bounds and substantive protocol checks were not relaxed.

**A separate inherited memorandum digest inconsistency remains open.** The received metadata uses full-body digests for historical memoranda, while some original inert-model verifiers exclude `source_bindings`. Running the unchanged `ratchet_checks.py` against both the received extraction and the final extraction fails the same authored-body-digest assertion. This is recorded separately from the 26 selected passing suites; it is not called a pass, a production ratchet failure, or newly introduced Pathway behavior. Original authored/frozen-input values and verifier implementations are retained. A future builder must reconcile each memorandum's intended digest convention and its frozen dependency references with a preservation audit before claiming all historical lanes. Blindly regenerating all historical prose/evidence is not a repair.

The final orchestration also accidentally submitted Parcel twice to the same receipt directory. The second invocation was refused by the unchanged no-clobber output guard with exit 2 before any suite ran. Its error and the raw orchestration status are preserved. The first completed Parcel receipt remains intact. The final unique-suite index is constructed from the 26 exact-carrier passing receipts, not from relabeling that duplicate invocation as a pass.

### Evidence boundaries and next gates

The full journeys use explicitly labeled browser-DOM/native-RPC/digest fixtures, original native cryptography and real WebRTC data channels through an owned loopback TURN relay. Basic-choice tests assert no provider or peer creation. Separate helper state, DOM, clock, file and event collaborators are synthetic. None of these qualify an unrestricted carried-worker startup, actual IndexedDB durability, native picker/clipboard/sharing/saving/leave behavior, mobile HTML-attachment opening, OS input methods, screen readers, or public-network connectivity. No infrastructure price, public-service uptime or capacity was qualified. Content hashes prove content equality, not independent authorship, security or permission to execute received HTML.

The actual strict final navigation gate is exit 77/unavailable, not pass. Do not loosen the host policy or relabel a DOM fixture as navigation. The next larger product gates remain ordinary worker/storage/device qualification and a reviewed reduction of manual connection handoffs, with explicit service and privacy choices. New friends still exchange three files; exactly verified returning friends exchange two. The new preset does not provide closed-tab receiving, background reconnection, an address book directory, hosted rendezvous, guaranteed relay reachability or a persistent basic preference.

Primary background sources consulted on 2026-10-12: W3C WebRTC configuration and ICE policy documentation (`https://www.w3.org/TR/webrtc/`); Cloudflare's existing STUN/TURN distinction (`https://developers.cloudflare.com/realtime/turn/faq/`); W3C WAI disclosure interaction guidance (`https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/`). These sources inform semantics, not this implementation's execution receipts. No price claim was adopted.

The owner's repository starting commit remains `af98b724e9616be52a32566033fc8b9cb679bd25`. This turn worked from the supplied carrier extraction. Integrate while preserving the owner's Git/Nix/build/test facilities; the handoff trio is not a replacement repository.

### Continuation commands and receipt interpretation

```sh
# The only end-user product is Vibechat.html. The following commands are for builders.
bash Vibechat.html verify
bash Vibechat.html status
bash Vibechat.html extract --directory ABSENT_WORKSHOP
bash test.sh --html Vibechat.html --output ABSENT_PATHWAY_RECEIPTS pathway
bash test.sh --html Vibechat.html --output ABSENT_STRICT_RECEIPTS --require-navigation justworks
# Expected here: the strict ordinary-navigation gate is unavailable / exit 77.
# It must be repeated on an allowed host before claiming standalone startup.
```

Do not overwrite a receipt directory to make a repeat appear to be its first run. Preserve failures and distinguish a wrapper refusal, an unavailable environment and a failing assertion. The complete original protocol/test implementations remain in the carrier. Reconcile inherited memorandum digest conventions and frozen dependency references explicitly before an all-lanes claim; the selected passing receipts do not repair that separate debt. The bootstrap's own final digest lives in the external package receipt to avoid a recursive self-hash.


## Exact received rev0058 bootstrap — historical bytes end

## 218. Recall — find a message without leaving its conversation

### One product, one ordinary control

`Vibechat.html` remains the only product. No separate search service, database, installer, browser permission or builder file is needed to use **Find**. The control sits beside Chats in the conversation header, including on a narrow screen. It opens an inline **Find in this chat** field rather than another modal or a second copy of the message history.

Type a phrase or filename. A deliberate query selects the newest matching item; **Earlier** and **Later** move through the original items without wrapping. Enter in the field goes earlier; Shift+Enter goes later. **Show match** returns to the selected item and puts keyboard focus on its original article. **Done** or Escape inside the search controls closes the strip, clears the query and leaves the conversation in context. Done does not jump to latest or send the composer's draft. Opening Find with no query does not enumerate history or invoke a provider.

The matcher applies NFC normalization and JavaScript lowercasing to literal substrings. Regex punctuation and markup are ordinary characters, not executable patterns or preview HTML. This is not fuzzy search, locale-specific collation, full Unicode case folding or accent-insensitive search. `cafe` does not silently become `café`. The field and programmatic query path are bounded to 160 UTF-16 input code units. It does not search across conversations, friend names, message drafts, unopened encrypted custody records, protocol controls, or the binary contents of an attachment. A filename is searched without reading the file.

### Search the accepted record, not another copy

Recall reads only the existing loaded event/plaintext maps and selected room. It uses the renderer's chronological order and original text-row key or exact sender/file key. Multipart files count once; their earliest retained filename is the same name used by the original renderer. A matched file is not thereby complete, authenticated as a whole, or safe to open: the original verify/save action remains separate.

The active match receives a CSS outline on the existing article. No message HTML, text selection, download control, sharing status or provider content is rebuilt to insert search snippets. Existing Steady reading/draft retention remains in control. Incoming accepted content refreshes the count, but keeps the selected key when it still matches, does not automatically reveal a newly arrived item, and does not steal input focus or the draft's caret/selection. A user can explicitly select a newer match or use Show match. Search openness suppresses the broad local attention-clear-at-bottom shortcut; this is not a remote read receipt or proof of reading. Closing search while actually visible and focused at latest can resume the original local attention behavior.

The scan snapshots and sorts the retained event references, then matches at most 32 records per animation frame, yielding after a threshold of 64 Ki UTF-16 input units. One record remains bounded by original payload admission. This is a cooperative matching quota, **not** a bound on the existing full-history sort, render, initial restore, or total tab memory. No persistent plaintext index, extra history cache, lazy server search or large-history performance qualification is claimed.

Queries debounce briefly. Each scan carries its own serial, identity generation, room and inventory version. A changed query retires old matches immediately. A queued old callback cannot replace newer results or discard the new callback's cancellation handle. Arrival refresh follows completion without granting permission to move the reader. Changing conversations or locking cancels scheduled work and clears the query, result keys, outline, live status and field. These are reference/DOM cleanup guarantees, not forensic memory erasure. Backups do not contain a query or search index; restored authenticated history can be searched afresh.

The existing composer is untouched by query input. Search has its own composition guards: Enter while composing does not navigate or send. The browser journey dispatches explicit synthetic composition events; it is not an actual operating-system IME or screen-reader test. Live-region wording is only replaced when changed, rather than on every idle repaint. The inline strip uses existing product colors and controls and was visually inspected at 390×844 and 1280×900 in the declared browser fixture.

### Implementation and continuation surface

The production change is in `client.js` and the shell/template presentation. `recall_checks.py` is a new carried named source and `recall` a new driver lane. `first_run_checks.py` keeps its inherited substantive checks and adds the opt-in real-record Recall journey, one extra self-only room, query lock cleanup and searchable restored history. Existing branches continue to identify their historical test revision; the wrapper carrier hash identifies the actual tested product.

The carrier inventory is **138 named sources / 57 regular lanes plus optional benchmark**, not all-lanes execution. `dev.py`, the test driver and bounded current status describe the new surface. C133, T258–T262 and letter-0063 record the design and current source references; prior articles, letters, research inventories and all prior lineage values are retained. Native, worker, crypto/KDF/C, WASM/vendor, laboratory implementation and immutable evidence bytes remain exact. Thirty historical dependency documents change only derived source-binding byte counts/hashes and their received full-body digest. Their historical semantic values and original check implementations remain unchanged. The finite source-only Parcel frame is resealed by the normal repacker.

The inherited ratchet design-memorandum verifier still expects a different authored-body digest convention. It fails the same assertion on both the received rev0058 and this release. This is a separately recorded builder-only failure, not a passing lane, fresh cryptographic defect, or excuse to regenerate historical findings. Do not blindly rewrite the original laboratories or edit their assertions to manufacture green receipts.

### Trials, corrections and honest scope

The first two Recall trials failed a test expectation: the inherited first-run fixture and the new message both contained the exact same `<img ...>` text, so that literal query correctly had two matches. The query was narrowed to the new message's unique following words. That correction did not weaken the inert-markup check or change production matching. The third trial completed the journey. A later direct scheduling check prompted a small defensive correction: test that a callback is current before clearing the current frame handle; the new carried unit asserts that stale callbacks cannot break cancellation of the live job.

One preliminary release command mistakenly supplied two lane arguments to the single-lane driver. Argument parsing refused it before execution; it is not test coverage. The selected release run then used the actual single-lane interface. Parallel lanes caused a Page.set_content crash in Clearway and a Parcel file-input timeout while this 4 GiB host recorded OOM kills. The coordinator was stopped without killing active wrappers or overwriting their receipts. The two failures and host counters are retained. The two failing lanes passed when repeated one at a time on that same candidate, without assertion relaxation or timeout changes. The carrier lane then exposed a stale expected lane count (56 instead of 57). Builder comparison version labels/range were also still rev0058. Those builder-only values were corrected, an exact current self-comparison assertion was added, and a new final carrier was frozen. All selected suites were scheduled anew on it, with at most one full browser journey and one auxiliary lane at a time. Section 219 distinguishes final unique completed passes from earlier failed or partial candidates.

The actual strict ordinary file/localhost navigation gate is repeated, not inferred from a screenshot. Under this host's administrator policy it is **unavailable / exit 77**, not pass; no policy was bypassed. Full message journeys use the declared browser-DOM/native-RPC/digest fixture, original native PQ cryptography and actual RTCDataChannels through an owned local TURN relay. Native default carried-worker startup and actual IndexedDB are not thereby qualified. Source-only Parcel output, cancellation timers, file-input automation, synthetic composition, screenshot layout and actual encrypted message/file round trips have distinct scopes.

Standalone startup, actual browser durability, native OS input methods, picker/clipboard/sharing/saving/leave behavior, mobile HTML-attachment opening, screen readers and public-network connectivity remain unqualified. Functional tests and content hashes are not an independent security audit, independent code authorship, remote durable storage or human-reading evidence. No new relay or hosted provider was selected and no pricing/uptime claim was revalidated.

### Next sandpeople: preserve the real job

The larger gates remain real-device qualification and reviewed removal of manual connection handoffs. Search does not solve friend discovery or rendezvous. **New friends still exchange three files; exactly verified returning friends exchange two.** The reusable public introduction can wait; live setup still needs matching open tabs and its original time limits. There is no new directory, automatic retry, background receive, closed-tab receive or silent service selection.

On a permitted real device, prioritize opening the actual HTML and its friend-carrying copy, real encrypted browser persistence, supported mobile HTML attachment handling, keyboard-visible layout, native input/composition and assistive technology. A snapshot without the soft keyboard is not qualification of the keyboard-open viewport. Also measure large retained histories before claiming the matching quota bounds all UI work. The old compact composer hint's adjacent text on narrow screens is inherited presentation debt, not fixed by this revision.

The owner's repository starting commit remains `af98b724e9616be52a32566033fc8b9cb679bd25`. This session worked from the supplied carrier, not that repository. Preserve its Git/Nix/build/test facilities and integrate changes there; do not replace it with the handoff trio or invent a merge/commit receipt. Keep the entire received bootstrap intact.

Useful independent commands (each test invocation takes **one** lane):

```sh
bash Vibechat.html verify
bash Vibechat.html brief
bash Vibechat.html extract --directory workshop-next
bash test.sh --html Vibechat.html --output receipt-recall recall
bash test.sh --html Vibechat.html --output receipt-carrier carrier
bash test.sh --html Vibechat.html --output receipt-navigation --require-navigation justworks
# Repack only to a new path, after deliberate source changes and derived binding review.
bash Vibechat.html repack --directory workshop-next --output Vibechat-next.html
```

## End of exact received rev0059 bootstrap

## 220. Roomy — room to write without losing the conversation

### Start with the words, not another setting

`Vibechat.html` is the only product. The ordinary chat composer now grows when a draft wraps or contains several lines, then gives that space back when the text becomes shorter. There is no resizing handle to discover, preference to configure, separate editor to open, or new permission. A short message starts with a 44 CSS-pixel field; longer writing is bounded to 144 CSS pixels and can scroll internally. Where the reported viewport is short, the cap also reserves room for the conversation when that is physically possible.

On a narrow screen, the composer uses 16 CSS-pixel text, and Send and the attachment control have at least 44 CSS-pixel targets. Draft state, attachment guidance and the draft-lifetime warning now occupy separate lines rather than running together. The invitation control has the shorter visual label **Invite**, while its accessible name continues to say that it can invite a friend or open an invitation. It opens the original guide; this is not a new invitation protocol.

The current Enter/Shift+Enter behavior remains unchanged. In particular, this is **not** a new mobile-specific Send-versus-newline heuristic. Active composition remains protected by the original Steady handlers. A larger writing area does not send the text, turn it into a file caption, alter its contents, or persist an unfinished draft. Drafts still belong to their selected conversation in the current unlocked tab and disappear on Lock or close. Original risk review and explicit backup limits remain.

### Fit the reported space, without taking control

The controller reads the browser's visual viewport height and vertical offset when available, with a finite layout-height fallback. It only follows approximately normal-scale reports. A substantially zoomed or invalid report leaves the last normal layout alone. There is no user-agent sniff, physical-keyboard assertion, pointer-type rule, `user-scalable=no`, native-event cancellation, focus command or scale reset. This is a bounded layout response to geometry, **not reliable keyboard detection or a native-device qualification**.

The unlocked workspace uses the reported normal-scale frame. Short frames receive tighter nonessential spacing. Search/header, connection, composer and footer rows retain their intrinsic height; the history has a minimum slice, and the chat can scroll at extreme sizes instead of clipping important controls. The status footer is explicitly scrollable and keyboard-focusable, with a focus indication, rather than hiding saving errors to make room. Long backup results remain available through scrolling. This does not assert that every possible browser, font size, dialog or device arrangement has been tested.

Composer measurement uses its existing element's `scrollHeight`, briefly measuring at the minimum and applying the bounded result. No hidden measuring copy or extra plaintext draft cache is added. The existing input value, caret, selection direction and active element are not rewritten by layout. Active end-of-draft writing can follow its internal bottom; a selection elsewhere retains the previous input scroll offset.

The controller reuses Steady's current conversation/reading anchor and original message nodes. It restores the prior anchor after geometry changes and suppresses geometry-induced scroll bookkeeping until the following frame. This prevents an automatic growth measurement from taking the reader to latest or being mistaken for a deliberate change in reading position. Switching conversations reuses the original draft/selection state and measures the new draft; an empty chat returns to the small field. Incoming accepted messages retain their original message nodes and do not acquire permission to move keyboard focus.

Window resizing, visual-viewport resizing/scrolling and selected layout observers coalesce into one animation-frame measurement. The observed nodes exclude the textarea itself. An idle-settled assertion checks that no observer loop repeatedly rewrites its style. Reset cancels current layout and release frames, clears temporary geometry and increments a serial. A stale callback must check its serial **before** changing a newer cancellation handle. Lock cannot revive a pending geometry adjustment or its draft. This is reference/DOM cleanup, not forensic memory erasure.

### Tests that shaped the fix

The received rev0059 keeps a four-line draft in the original single-row field. The new browser regression runs the current first-run/Roomy harness over that unchanged carrier, using its original native cryptographic sources, and fails the first new multiline-height assertion after 43 inherited checks. It is an observed layout regression/missing behavior, not a cryptographic flaw or a claim that every past device behaved the same way.

The first Roomy candidate then exposed a second, real layout defect during an ordinary click. With Find open in a short mobile-shaped frame, the grid's `auto` header row could shrink below its wrapped controls. A message article covered **Done**, and Playwright refused to click through it. The production rows now use `max-content` for non-history content, letting the outer chat scroll when necessary. The same unforced Done click succeeds. No forced/evaluated click, overlay removal or relaxed target assertion was used to manufacture that result.

A later broad carrier run refused the newly expanded current status because it exceeded the original 20,000-character printed-output bound. The mutable summary was shortened to 19,799 characters without raising the bound or deleting the historical records. This is builder index maintenance, not a product performance claim. Preliminary setup errors, the failed first candidate and the failed carrier run are separately retained. A successful trial is not substituted for the selected final-carrier execution.

`roomy_checks.py` adds 25 separately scoped helper assertions with synthetic geometry, DOM/state and animation-frame collaborators. The browser journey adds 29 assertions to the inherited 54 for 83 checks in that run. It exercises multiline growth and shrinking, bounded long writing, selection direction, original reading anchors, small targets/text/hint layout, geometry coalescing, no provider calls from resize, zoom/invalid-report refusal, visible saving-warning text, sizes 320×568 / 390×430 / 844×390, inline Find, separate conversation drafts, idle stability and Lock cleanup. It retains the original independent identity checks, native post-quantum records, bidirectional peer messages, byte-exact multipart file, reconnection and restored-history checks.

The shortened-frame test changes getters on the fixture's existing VisualViewport EventTarget and dispatches the corresponding synthetic events. Its 390-wide frame has a reported height of 430 and offset of 72. The image is a **clipped layout screenshot of those simulated metrics**, not a photograph or screenshot of a real on-screen keyboard. Zoom values are also synthetic, not a physical pinch gesture. No production test hook is introduced. Keyboard focus and DOM geometry assertions do not qualify a screen reader, native IME, touch keyboard or accessibility conformance.

Final fixture screenshots were visually inspected at 390×844, the explicitly simulated 390×430 visible frame, a small Find layout and 1280×900. They show test accounts and owned-fixture messages. They are evidence of the rendered layout, not ordinary HTML startup, public connectivity or independent security review.

### Carried implementation and retained lineage

Production changes are limited to `client.js` and the shell/template presentation. The finite source-only Parcel frame is resealed through the normal repacker. `roomy_checks.py` is a new named source/lane; `first_run_checks.py` adds its optional extension and Lock assertion while retaining the substantive inherited branches. `dev.py`, the current index and driver describe **139 named sources / 58 regular lanes plus optional benchmark**. Inventory is not an all-lanes execution claim. The default lane set and per-command limits are not enlarged to waive failures.

C134, T263–T265, letter-0064 and the rev0060 lineage addition record this turn. All 37 original hosting options, prior research entries, 133 prior articles, 63 prior letters and prior lineage values remain. Ninety-nine named sources retain identical bytes, including native, worker, crypto/KDF/C, WASM/vendor, previous test/laboratory implementations and immutable evidence. Thirty dependency documents change only derived source-binding byte counts/hashes and their received full-body digest convention. Their other semantic values and prior execution claims remain untouched. Rebinding is not fresh laboratory execution.

The inherited ratchet memorandum's separate authored-body checksum assertion still fails on both the received carrier and this release. It is documented outside the passing selected suites, not erased, renamed as green, or fixed by regenerating historical claims. The original authored verifier remains byte-for-byte unchanged. A future builder should reconcile the provenance/conventions deliberately before changing that historical boundary.

Primary documentation consulted on 2026-10-12, without adding a dependency or revalidating hosting prices:

* T263 — MDN VisualViewport: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/VisualViewport . Visual and layout viewport concepts, dimensions, offsets, scale and resize/scroll events informed the bounded geometry reader. Reported geometry does not identify every cause of a change.
* T264 — Chrome's viewport-resize explainer: https://developer.chrome.com/blog/viewport-resize-behavior . The documented difference between resizing layout and visual viewports cautions against claiming that a CSS viewport unit alone handles every keyboard. It is historical platform explanation, not a present-day cross-browser compatibility matrix.
* T265 — CSSOM View: https://www.w3.org/TR/cssom-view-1/ . Viewport coordinate/scale definitions informed the separation of height, offset and normal-scale policy. Specification terminology is not evidence of device-specific behavior.

### Next sandpeople: keep the single-file promise honest

An unrestricted real-device run remains the highest qualification gate: open the actual `Vibechat.html` and its friend-carrying copy, use the original carried worker and encrypted IndexedDB, and test actual soft keyboards, composition, zoom, orientation, tiny windows, long errors, dialogs, sharing and assistive technology. The present host blocks ordinary file and localhost navigation by administrator policy. The strict gate must report unavailable, not be bypassed or replaced with a DOM screenshot. Source/CSP integrity is not independent code authorship or complete standalone startup.

The other large user-experience gate remains removal of live manual handoffs through a reviewed, explicit service choice. **New friends still exchange three files; exactly verified returning friends exchange two.** Public introductions can wait; live setup still needs the matching tabs and its original time limits. This revision adds no directory, hosted rendezvous, new relay service, automatic retry, background upload or closed-tab receiving. More comfortable writing does not solve discovery or connectivity by itself.

The owner repository was not supplied. Its starting commit remains `af98b724e9616be52a32566033fc8b9cb679bd25`. Integrate into that repository without replacing its Git/Nix/build/test facilities with this handoff trio. No merge, commit, deployment or public service qualification is claimed. Keep **Vibechat.html** as the user artifact; everything else is for the sandpeople.

## Exact received rev0060 bootstrap — historical bytes end

## 222. Matchpoint — make the original identity check easier to complete

### Product first, unchanged trust boundary

**Vibechat.html is the only product.** The owner should not need the bootstrap, a shell, a test driver, a repository checkout, or network administration to chat. The received current-first material and latest instructions were read, the original carrier was verified and extracted, and the actual required-navigation gate was attempted before choosing work. Administrator policy still blocks ordinary file and localhost navigation. No policy bypass, hosted-service account or deployment was introduced to relabel that limitation.

This turn addresses another first-friend friction point: manually comparing sixteen groups of identity-code characters. The default unknown-friend review is now **Paste their code → confirm the separate trusted source → Save friend for later / make a connection reply**. **Compare together** preserves the original full-code manual route for a call or in-person comparison. Neither route identifies someone by their name, shortened suffix, familiar avatar, invitation, or clipboard success.

The user must obtain their friend's own safety code through a separate channel they already trust. Copying the code out of the invitation being reviewed would only compare that invitation with itself. The UI says this explicitly. A full match merely enables the existing independent-source confirmation checkbox. It does not check that box, call the original trust API, add a contact, import a room, or start a connection. Those effects remain behind the original explicit Save/Connect actions and original provider checks. Already verified exact identities continue through the inherited known-friend route without a repeated ceremony.

### Exact comparison, not approximate recognition

The new `matchpointCode` helper checks all 64 hexadecimal characters. It normalizes only ASCII hexadecimal case and ASCII spaces, tabs, carriage returns and line feeds. Empty, partial, mismatching, own-code, structured/JSON, oversized and non-code inputs remain distinct or refused. Hidden and non-ASCII formatting characters are not discarded. It neither truncates a fingerprint nor accepts a matching prefix. There is no new hash algorithm, pairwise safety-number format or Signal-compatible wire protocol.

The controller binds review to the exact incoming packet object, current setup object and unlocked generation. Editing the input clears source consent. Switching comparison methods clears the old value and consent. Re-reading an invitation resets the comparison, even when the file is the same. Failed reading cannot leave the previous enabled acceptance route. Changing setup or identity invalidates the old approval. The final trust action rechecks eligibility rather than relying only on the disabled state of a button. Busy verification cannot switch the input or method through the ordinary controls.

The UI retains original admission, public-card identity, signed connection, exact two-person room, room-policy, expiry, cancellation and known-friend checks. No new identity key, crypto implementation, room wire format, service or auto-verification mechanism was added. A code match is not an independent identity proof, security audit, read receipt or remote-storage witness.

### Copy the local code, not the invitation's code

The guide's **Your safety code** disclosure now offers **Copy my code**. The copied value comes from the unlocked local identity, not the incoming invitation or the friend's display name. Clipboard writing is attempted only from the explicit click. The new path never calls a clipboard-reading API, polls the clipboard, requests access to an address book, or contacts a verification service.

If the write API is missing or refuses, a readonly selectable complete local code appears with a manual-copy/aloud alternative. Clipboard permissions and implementations vary; a fallback is part of the feature, not proof that native clipboard access works on a particular device. A success message describes copying only, not sending an invitation or the friend receiving a code. The selected public code can remain in the operating-system clipboard after copying; Lock does not recall it.

Each pending clipboard operation captures its local identity, generation and serial. Close, cancel, reopen, reset and Lock invalidate the old serial. A late success or refusal cannot revive fallback, reenable the wrong operation, reopen a dialog, or steal focus elsewhere. Fallback focus/selection is taken only while the initiating copy button still holds focus. Comparison Enter is not a form submission; composition events are not treated as verification consent. Live-region status changes only when its words change.

Responsive DOM checks cover 320-, 390- and 1280-pixel widths. Screenshots show the scrolled comparison panel, not an ordinary navigated product or a real phone/keyboard. The complete manual safety code remains available in its original presentation. No screen-reader, operating-system input method, native clipboard or actual mobile attachment opening was qualified.

### Test extension and original routes

`matchpoint_checks.py` is the new named source and `matchpoint` the new regular lane. Its separately scoped Node helper tests execute the carried comparison/guard functions against synthetic DOM and lifecycle state. Its browser extension uses the default `parcel` application-invitation journey: source-only HTML distribution, automatic unverified arrival, save without a room, fresh-tab inviter, original live signed exchange, encrypted messages both ways and byte-exact multipart-file recovery. The expected comparison values are selected independently from the original native endpoints, not copied from the imported invitation. Clipboard callbacks and deliberately delayed results are synthetic.

Inherited `first_run_checks.py`, `postcard_checks.py`, `holdfast_checks.py` and the nonextended `parcel` lane now deliberately choose **Compare together** before their original checkbox. Their substantive assertions and original protocol refusal checks remain. The new `matchpoint` lane exercises the actual default paste route, including independent-source consent at the replying-friend review. Existing temporary-compatibility `justworks` is still not the primary product route.

The old build's feature-absence probe refuses because it has no Matchpoint functions. That is not a rediscovered preexisting product defect. Early trials exposed harness mistakes: an assignment expression returning a rejected-Promise callback was invoked by Playwright; an expected identity was read after its original endpoint had locked; a hidden-panel expected-value read was replaced with an independent native identity captured before Lock. Those failures and an interrupted driver run are retained separately. The corrected journey checks the displayed own code against that independent value before testing copying. No product-journey assertion was waived.

A preliminary carrier check also caught the mutable status index's pretty-printed output exceeding its existing 20,000-character bound. The index was shortened to 19,871 characters / 19,877 UTF-8 bytes in the final status output, with the original limit unchanged. A preliminary wider selection was stopped rather than presented as a release pass; final selected tests execute afresh on the new fixed bytes. Development script errors, including an unanchored source-slot insertion refused by the repacker and a temporary inventory helper that included the generated manifest as a named source, were corrected before qualification.

### Research, provenance and next gates

Primary references were reviewed online on 2026-10-12 and appended as T266–T268. Signal's 2016 safety-number UX discussion informs the comparison burden only; this product does not adopt Signal's algorithm or automatic verification. The W3C Clipboard API and events document is the **24 June 2026 Working Draft**, not a finalized Recommendation; its permission and synthetic-event boundaries inform explicit writing/fallback and honest test scope. WAI's modal-dialog pattern informs labelled controls, closing and focus behavior. No source is treated as proof of this implementation's correctness.

- T266: https://signal.org/blog/safety-number-updates/
- T267: https://www.w3.org/TR/clipboard-apis/
- T268: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/

Prior research options, price dates, technical sources, turn notes, constitution articles, letters and lineage values are retained. C135 and letter-0065 record this turn. Thirty source-bound documents change only derived bindings and the inherited full-body digest convention, not historical authored content. The inherited ratchet test uses a different authored-body convention and still fails its separate check; this was not silently relabelled or included in the passing selected count. Native, worker, cryptographic/KDF/C, vendor/WASM, laboratory implementations and immutable evidence keep their received bytes.

**New friends still exchange three files; exactly verified returning friends exchange two.** Independent code comparison is still a human trust step. No directory, rendezvous, relay service, automatic retry, permission-discovery service, background upload, closed-tab receiving or password reset was added. Qualifying real standalone startup/worker/IndexedDB/mobile behavior and removing live handoffs through a reviewed explicit rendezvous/relay choice remain larger adoption gates.

Preserve the owner's repository starting at `af98b724e9616be52a32566033fc8b9cb679bd25`, including Git/Nix/build/test facilities. The repository was not supplied here; no merge, commit, deployment or repository integration is claimed. The handoff trio is builder transport, not a replacement worktree. The next builder should read the current-first prefix and sections 222–223 before the retained older directions.
