## Exact received rev0061 bootstrap — historical bytes end

## 224. Threshold — one doorway and non-destructive file selection

### 224.1 Product decision

The first screen should not require people to distinguish a public introduction, an invitation-carrying application, and a complete encrypted backup before choosing a control. The ordinary action is now **Open a file**. Content decides which original preview is shown. A backup selects the existing original-password restore path; an invitation selects the existing independent full-code review after unlock. No format is inferred to be trustworthy from its filename or MIME label.

The earlier dedicated **Restore a backup** disclosure is retained as an alternate entry, not a prerequisite. Its file action is styled like the ordinary file action, and success returns the preview to the primary doorway. Locked-page and dedicated-backup drops use the same classifier. **Paste an invitation instead** remains invitation-only; large backup text is not accepted through that field. An ordinary unlocked conversation continues to review dropped files through Tray, and the existing guide retains its own invitation route. This is not an unrestricted document viewer or an unlocked universal importer.

### 224.2 The actual loss defect and replacement ownership

The received entry and backup readers cleared the currently staged preview before the next read or validation succeeded. An accidental wrong or malformed file could therefore remove a usable selection and its next action. No saved profile had been deleted, but the person had to locate and import the earlier file again.

Threshold keeps a candidate separate from the existing `entry.packet` or `backup.pending`. `thresholdLoad` captures the current read serial, unlocked-generation boundary and focus. Only a still-current successfully validated candidate commits a replacement; unsuccessful or cancelled work leaves the earlier usable preview intact. A newer selected file invalidates older completions. The login action stays unavailable while a file is being checked. **Cancel file check** is available independently of the old selection's Remove action. Removing the earlier selection also invalidates its pending replacement, rather than letting that replacement silently appear later.

Cancellation fences adoption and subsequent work; it does not claim to terminate a pending `File.arrayBuffer` operation, erase memory, provide a browser-wide cancellation facility or survive page closure. The original storage, lock and login guards still prevent accepting a preview during unlock or after state changes. The preview remains tab-local data, not a contact, live setup, persistent selection or backup restore.

An existing temporary invitation can expire while another file is being read. Its own expiry timer now removes only the expired preview; it does not invalidate the new read. A live reply or final connection file still requires the original unlocked tab. Such a file cannot resume a closed connection by passing through the first screen, and refusal does not erase an otherwise usable preview.

### 224.3 Keep the user's place

Entered name, password and recovery salt are not cleared by a failed replacement. A selected backup may fill an empty name with its unverified public hint, but does not overwrite an already entered name. Successful reading does not steal focus or selection from login details edited while the read was pending. Existing first-arrival focus assistance remains only when appropriate; a replacement does not automatically jump the caret.

The two original status outlets share one visible explanation. A new status hides the other outlet rather than announcing stale and current explanations together; unchanged text is not needlessly replaced. Errors say when the earlier invitation remains unverified or the earlier backup remains selected but unrestored. The preview and Remove action stay visible. This is observed DOM behavior, not a claim of assistive-technology conformance.

### 224.4 Classification is not trust, and bounds remain real

`backupValidate` factors the original complete backup validation out of the file-reading wrapper; the wrapper remains available. The classifier does not parse a large backup twice to choose a UI route. Original strict UTF-8, protocol-JSON admission, duplicate-key refusal, exact fields, wrapper digest, profile structure, envelope bounds and per-record validation remain. Profile decryption and identity authentication still happen only through the original provider after explicit unlock. Wrapper checksums do not authenticate a person or the encrypted profile.

The existing bounds remain: 262,144 bytes for the standalone invitation, 33,554,432 bytes for an HTML application copy, and 138,477,568 bytes for the complete backup wrapper. The ordinary shared-file maximum remains 2 MiB; this revision does not enlarge it. Before a file above the HTML bound is read as a whole, bounded 65,536-byte leading slices identify its first non-whitespace content. Anything other than a potential JSON object is refused as oversized for these smaller formats. The whole JSON object still has to pass the original backup validator. Thus a backup named .html is not automatically refused at the HTML limit, while a large HTML file named .json cannot evade the HTML bound. File sizes and leading-whitespace cases in these checks are explicitly synthetic; they are not stress tests of maximum-sized real device files.

This is not a streaming JSON parser, bounded-peak-memory proof or guarantee that Cancel can interrupt synchronous parsing. Smaller format bounds are rechecked after content classification. A large malformed JSON object can reach the existing overall backup read/parse bound before refusal. Do not describe that as early invitation-size rejection or as better worst-case memory use.

HTML selection uses the original bounded inert extraction of exactly one supported public-invitation source slot. It does not insert or execute attached HTML, preview a live DOM, add a web request or authenticate application authorship. The generic released application contains no included user's invitation. Parcel still creates a source-only copy with the sender's explicitly chosen public introduction. Independent code comparison, exact verified pins, signed connection/room checks, original password recovery, contact/room retention and per-record restore reporting are unchanged.

### 224.5 Evidence and corrected trials

`threshold_checks.py` is the new carried lane. Its preview checks use an unmodified Chromium document and a SHA-256-only adapter on the opaque fixture origin. Fixture backup profile bytes are deliberately synthetic and unauthenticated; the preview lane is not evidence that those bytes can restore an account. Worker construction, IndexedDB access, fetch and peer construction are instrumented to refuse or count unexpected preview effects. Delayed File operations, declared sizes and clocks are explicit collaborators. The lane's strict-navigation option refuses fixture-only qualification; use the separate actual `justworks --require-navigation` gate to attempt ordinary startup.

The separately extended original Keepsake journey uses the primary Open a file control for a real exported encrypted backup, restores into an independent store, authenticates the original native identity and recovers a multipart shared file byte-for-byte. Wrong credentials, altered encrypted profiles, duplicate or partial restores, pin/room retention, saving failure, temporary lifetime, lock cleanup and no restore-time forwarding retain their original checks. This path adds two primary-doorway assertions, not a substitute recovery implementation.

Doorstep and Keepsake refusal assertions were changed to require preservation of the earlier preview. Their malformed-input and cryptographic refusal conditions were not removed. Parcel's large-file fixture now contains an actual HTML prefix and instruments whole-file reads: a bounded prefix inspection is permitted, but the full oversized file must not be read. Both Parcel and the default Matchpoint extension run with that strengthened observation. Other inherited production and laboratory implementations retain their received bytes.

The first regression probe fails on the received HTML. A preliminary preview run caught late focus movement. A direct preliminary full journey was killed by the enclosing command timeout and produced a consequent EPIPE; the fresh detached run completed, but that preliminary run is not the release receipt. A wider candidate run caught an early HTML-bound regression in the first generic router. The bounded leading-read gate repaired it without making the filename choose the operation. A builder carrier check also caught stale expected section numbers and the old test-lane count; those references were updated to the new actual sections and inventory, retaining the checks. Two preliminary wider runs were deliberately stopped; their completed, failed and partial receipts are retained separately. A preservation helper initially classified a memorandum source ID as laboratory executable code; classification was corrected to the actual Python implementation paths without altering the carrier. The final selected run and final same-harness before/after regression are fresh evidence. The publication assembler initially assumed every historical research entry had the newer reviewed_revision key. That assumption was corrected before any archive or product publication was made; the tested carrier was not changed.

### 224.6 Builder custody and next gates

Current-first dev/arrival/status guidance now points to sections 224–225. `vibe-threshold-tests` adds one named source and one lane; legacy revision comparison filters that member from pre-rev0062 inventories. The current status stays below its original 20,000-character bound, rather than raising the bound. `test.sh` remains a builder convenience whose external and carried bytes are identical. The finite Parcel frame, manifest and CSP hashes are derived from the final sources; CSP is not relaxed. Thirty dependency documents receive derived binding/body-hash updates only. Those updates are not laboratory reruns, authored endorsements or a repair of the inherited ratchet authored-body checksum mismatch.

C136 records non-destructive staged replacement. Letter-0066 and research entries T269–T271 retain the distinction between API guidance, test collaborators and device evidence. W3C File API was reviewed as a working draft, not a newly guaranteed browser feature. WAI status/error guidance informed clear feedback and focus retention, not a claim of WCAG certification. Historical research options and pricing dates are left unchanged. No dependency, hosted service, directory or deployment was introduced.

The first next gate remains an authorized environment in which the actual HTML, browser worker, persistence and native mobile interactions can be exercised without bypassing policy. The other large product gate remains reviewed removal of manual live handoffs using explicitly chosen and supportable rendezvous/relay infrastructure. Do not invent automatic discovery, remote presence, public reachability or a service guarantee. Large backup responsiveness remains a separately scoped improvement, not something these selection checks prove. Preserve the owner repository at its received handoff; the ZIP is not a worktree replacement or a claim of Git integration.

### Archive boundary

Only the tested HTML, this bootstrap and the matching builder driver are staged. Runtime stores, relay credentials, browser profiles, screenshots and receipt directories are not archive members. Public deterministic test vectors remain explicitly nonoperational carried source. Reopen and CRC-check the archive, extract to an absent directory, compare all three members to staged bytes, then verify the independently extracted HTML. The external publication receipt binds the ZIP and bootstrap without attempting a self-referential checksum inside this document.

## Exact received rev0062 bootstrap — historical bytes end

## 226. rev0063 — Familiar: open the chat before reconnecting

### Product route and decision

Vibechat.html is the only product. Friends should take a returning person to their conversation, not make opening retained history contingent on another signaling exchange. This turn changes the ordinary Friends route to **Friends → Open chat** for an already accepted eligible two-person conversation, even when the peer is disconnected. The row's Open chat action is visually primary; Invite someone new is secondary once friends exist. The empty list keeps invitation creation primary. The conversation itself retains the existing explicit Connect action and truthful local-message guidance.

Opening selects retained history locally. It does not create a room, import a pin, start ICE, call a provider, send a draft, or contact a new service. A saved exact friend with no eligible ordinary conversation retains the original explicit Connect guide. This change does not try to map every arbitrary group, renamed room or changed policy into one friend row. Chats and the existing policy tools remain available for those cases. The ordinary shared-room predicate is unchanged: an accepted epoch-1 two-member room with the original chat name pattern, one participant as owner, exact members, and no pending or declined policy update.

Once an existing chat is open, reading and writing remain available before reconnecting. A deliberately submitted offline message follows the existing local saving rules. A separate, explicit connection exchange can catch it up; opening Friends itself is not permission to transmit. An unfinished draft stays unfinished through this navigation and connection preparation. This is not new background or closed-tab receiving.

### Actual defect and lifecycle repair

The received `paintFriends()` replaced the entire list on every refresh. The new before/after regression reproduces loss of the currently focused friend action on that received implementation. Familiar keeps keyed DOM rows and changes only status/content that actually differs. Connection arrival or loss does not replace the focused button or selected name node, nor reorder rows by connection state. A removed focused friend returns focus to Invite instead of silently targeting another identity.

An explicitly opened Friends view keeps its displayed exact peer, room and policy while background link updates arrive. Before acting, the handler rechecks the unlocked identity/generation, open dialog, current mounted row, retained exact pin and original room/policy predicate. Removed pins, pending/declined or changed conversations are refused in a local status outlet. An unrelated room cannot be silently substituted for the displayed choice. An explicit reopening can select the currently preferred eligible room. If an older Connect action acquires a room before activation, the UI exposes Open chat and requires the new visible choice instead of invoking a changed action invisibly.

Lock clears row/cache and status ownership. A saved pre-lock callback cannot act in the new unlocked Friends view, even for the same login and restored room. Clearing references and UI is not a secure-erasure claim. No native, worker, cryptographic, vendor or laboratory implementation changed.

### Carried changes and scope

`client.js` adds the small Familiar row/cache/controller next to the existing shared-room helpers, wires the ordinary Friends button to explicit selection, and clears the cache during Lock. `Vibechat.template.html` carries the updated opening copy, one live refusal outlet, minimal action sizing and current-first builder guide. Full identity tools remain behind the existing disclosure.

`familiar_checks.py` is the new named test source. Its helper lane executes selected exact carried client functions in Chromium DOM with synthetic pins, rooms, policy/link state and navigation collaborators. Those values do not authenticate identities or room objects. The separate `first_run_checks.py --familiar` extension uses original native identities, retained authenticated history and real RTCDataChannels through an owned loopback TURN fixture. `reunion_checks.py` enters an existing disconnected conversation using Open chat and then its Connect action; its original protocol/refusal assertions remain.

`dev.py`, `test.sh` and the mutable current status expose the new lane, revision and inventory. The current status stays below the original 20,000-character bound rather than widening it. C137, letter-0067 and T272–T274 append this turn's design/provenance. Original article, letter, research and lineage objects retain their order and values. Thirty dependency documents change derived current-source byte counts/hashes and inherited-formula digests only; their historical authored content is unchanged. Rebinding is not laboratory execution. The old ratchet memorandum authored-only checksum assertion is deliberately reported separately, not changed into a pass by updating a checksum formula.

### Research used, not certification

The online review used primary W3C/WAI Focus Order and Status Messages guidance and WHATWG HTML focus-management APIs (T272–T274). This informed retaining existing action nodes on asynchronous updates, an explicit local status outlet and focus only for a deliberate action or a removed focused row. Neither guidance nor the DOM checks constitutes assistive-technology certification. No library, permission, service, hosted directory, price, deployment or uptime claim was added or revalidated. Prior research candidates retain their historical dates and limitations.

### Trial history and limits

The received focus regression fails on the exact old function; the same final harness passes on the release. A preliminary helper expectation originally tested removal after a separate synthetic rename had already reordered its fixture. The fixture now explicitly focuses the named row immediately before removal; the product assertion is not waived, and no generic arbitrary-name-reordering focus guarantee is claimed.

The first expanded native cleanup test accidentally returned the stored handler to Playwright, which invoked that function and closed Friends before the following Close click. The test now stores the handler inside a function body without returning it. This was a harness error, not a product failure relabeled as pass. Preliminary selected work was stopped after the correction; interrupted auxiliary work is not counted. The complete final selected run uses one fixed final HTML. The test driver also retains both new helper and native-journey JSON receipts.

Manual live handoffs remain three files for a new friend and two for an exactly verified returning friend. There is no directory, rendezvous, new relay, automatic connection/retry, background upload or closed-tab receiving. Lack of a local connection does not identify the friend's remote presence. DOM focus and geometry are not native keyboard, screen-reader or actual mobile behavior. The native fixture exercises durable native storage, not browser IndexedDB durability. The actual ordinary-navigation gate remains separate from the DOM fixture.

### Next work and repository custody

Prioritize permitted real-device qualification of the sole HTML, including mobile attachment opening and the reading-versus-soft-keyboard experience, actual browser storage, and public-network connectivity. The larger adoption problem remains the reviewed elimination of live manual handoffs; do not turn a developer laboratory or an unreviewed service into the default silently. Keep local reading independent of connection setup, preserve exact identities and original policy guards, and do not solve a failure by weakening a test or declaring an unavailable environment a pass.

The owner's repository starting at `af98b724e9616be52a32566033fc8b9cb679bd25` was not supplied. Preserve its Git/Nix/build/test facilities when integrating. No repository merge, deployment or clean-worktree claim is made here. The ZIP trio is a builder handoff, not a three-file user application or a replacement repository. Section 227 records the actual release bytes and execution, not inventory-as-evidence.


## 227. rev0063 — exact execution, preservation and release receipts

The following receipts bind the final release bytes. Passing selected suites, expected regression failure, unavailable ordinary navigation, and the inherited memorandum failure are separate categories. No incomplete lane or earlier candidate is counted as a final pass. Browser and auxiliary lanes ran at most one each, with inherited inner timeouts. All 31 selected unique suites completed successfully on the same final carrier. The optional bench and the remaining regular lanes were not claimed executed.

The Familiar helper contributes 30 checks using synthetic state collaborators. Its native journey has 70 total checks, including the original 54 first-meeting/cleanup checks and 16 Familiar additions. Native state, real owned TURN and actual encrypted peer traffic are separate from the helper's projection tests. The journey demonstrates local-only opening, one offline submitted message caught up once after explicit exact-room reconnection, a later reply, draft retention, lock fencing and restored offline opening. Its inherited first meeting transfers a multipart file byte-for-byte. No test establishes human reading, independent peer disk retention, remote presence, real IndexedDB durability or public reachability.

### Preliminary and failed work, outside the final passing count

The first preliminary helper failure involved a test starting its removal expectation after a separate synthetic rename had already reordered the focused row. The first expanded native cleanup capture returned a handler to Playwright, which invoked it before the next click; the final test stores without returning. Both are recorded as harness corrections, not ignored failures. The preliminary auxiliary carrier run was stopped after this correction and is not a completed pass. The preparation script initially stopped at an oversized current-status assertion; only its uncompleted tail was rerun after shortening mutable prose, and no duplicate article, source slot or test lane was inserted.

## 228. rev0064 — Waymark: public safety words for exact friend identity

### Product behavior

The ordinary unknown-friend review now opens on **Paste safety words or code**. It accepts exactly twenty-four embedded-list words, optionally preceded by the copied `Vibechat safety words:` heading. Input is normalized only for ASCII letter case, comma/semicolon separators and whitespace; invitation JSON, punctuation, unknown words, too few/many words and oversized input are refused rather than guessed.

The parser reconstructs all 32 fingerprint bytes and checks the appended one-byte SHA-256 checksum before comparing with the exact invitation identity. The result states whether the phrase is incomplete, malformed, checksum-damaged, the local user’s own phrase, a different valid identity, or an exact match. An exact match enables only the separate-source checkbox. The original pin/save/connect guard rechecks the exact current input, packet object, setup object and unlocked generation before accepting.

**Compare together** remains an explicit human-comparison route. It renders all twenty-four words in order and keeps the full 64-character code behind an advanced disclosure. The existing full-code paste parser remains accepted for people and older instructions that already use it. Switching methods clears consent.

**Your safety words & full code** renders only the unlocked local identity. Clipboard writing is optional and never reads clipboard contents. A failed write exposes a selectable complete phrase. Copy state is fenced by a serial and unlocked-generation check. Lock and guide reset clear text, fallback visibility, checked consent and pending comparison state.

### Framing and carried list

- Fingerprint: the existing lowercase 64-hex-character identity ID (256 bits).
- Checksum: first byte of SHA-256 over the 32 fingerprint bytes (8 bits).
- Framing: 264 bits split into twenty-four 11-bit indices.
- List: 2,048 unique lowercase English words, each unique in its first four letters.
- List SHA-256: `2f5eed53a4727b4bf8880d8f3f199efc90e58503646d9ff8eff3a2ed3b24dbda`.
- Reviewed upstream Git blob: `942040ed50f7205cafc465496229128ba4f78e75`.
- Zero-vector check: thirty-two zero bytes encode as twenty-three `abandon` words followed by `art`.

The upstream list is the English word list published with Bitcoin BIP 39. Vibechat does **not** implement BIP39 mnemonic entropy, a wallet, key recovery or seed import. The product deliberately avoids the terms “seed” and “recovery” for its own output except in the prominent warning not to paste such secrets.

## 230. rev0065 — Handback: make copied invitations an ordinary path

### Product behavior

The locked opening screen now places **Open a file** and **Paste copied invitation** beside each other. The unlocked friend guide exposes the same paste action next to creating or opening an invitation. Manual paste remains available under **Paste manually instead**.

Clipboard intake is opt-in. One activation performs at most one `navigator.clipboard.readText()` request. No read occurs during startup, unlock, guide opening, preview rendering or connection preparation. The resulting string is passed to the same strict invitation decoder used by file and manual input, under the inherited 262,144-byte encoded-size bound.

A valid reusable introduction or live connection packet is still only an **unverified preview** until the existing exact identity and separate-channel confirmation completes. Clipboard intake itself performs no trust, room import/creation, provider call, peer construction, storage write, backup restore, fetch or application network request.

When clipboard reading is unavailable, refused or empty, Vibechat expands and focuses manual paste. Oversized or malformed text is refused. In both locked and unlocked flows, a failed candidate is decoded and preflighted before visible state is replaced, so it cannot erase a usable staged invitation, typed login details, an approved exact comparison or a pending crossed-invitation decision. The retained item remains explicitly unverified where applicable.

A serial plus current identity/setup/generation checks fences delayed clipboard promises. Cancel, close, replacement and Lock prevent late adoption, focus changes or status revival. This is cancellation of the result, not a claim that the browser physically aborts its underlying clipboard operation.

For live invitation/reply/ready packets, **Copy invitation text** receives the primary treatment and file sharing becomes quiet secondary UI. Reusable application-carrying introductions retain the existing HTML-first route. Copy success names the recipient action; write refusal selects the complete text and preserves **Save file**. Sharing or copying remains an explicit request and is not represented as delivery.

Safety words and the full-code compatibility route are unchanged. The signed signal, exact recipient, room policy, invitation hash, reply binding, connection lifetime and original cryptographic envelopes are unchanged.
